children.title: Scalar Coordinate Partitions
children.top_down_role: Variable organizations whose selectable units are individual coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Coordinate Partitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate decomposition of a finite-dimensional Euclidean decision space into singleton coordinate subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d\in\mathbb{N}\), let \([d]=\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and let \(e_i\) denote the \(i\)-th standard basis vector of \(\mathbb{R}^d\). The scalar coordinate partition is the indexed family \(\mathcal{S}=\{S_i:i\in[d]\}\), where \(S_i=\operatorname{span}\{e_i\}\). Every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\) has the unique decomposition
\[
x=\sum_{i=1}^d U_i x_i,
\]
where \(U_i:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}^d\) is defined by \(U_i\alpha=\alpha e_i\). Thus \(\mathbb{R}^d=\bigoplus_{i=1}^d S_i\), and a scalar coordinate update has the form \(x^+=x+U_i h\) for some \(i\in[d]\) and \(h\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar partition decomposes the decision space into one-dimensional coordinate subspaces, and each scalar update is supported on at most one component.
assumptions_latex: \(d\in\mathbb{N}\)
\(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\)

notation.meaning: Canonical injection of scalar coordinate \(i\) into \(\mathbb{R}^d\).

children.title: Disjoint-Block Partitions
children.top_down_role: Nonoverlapping groups used as selectable update subspaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjoint-Block Partitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partition of Euclidean coordinates into nonempty, pairwise-disjoint blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal{B}=\{B_1,\ldots,B_m\}\) be nonempty subsets of \([d]\). It is a disjoint-block partition when
\[
B_r\cap B_s=\varnothing\quad(r\ne s),\qquad \bigcup_{r=1}^m B_r=[d].
\]
For each block, let \(U_r:\mathbb{R}^{|B_r|}\to\mathbb{R}^d\) be the canonical coordinate injection and set \(P_r=U_rU_r^{\mathsf T}\). Then \(U_r^{\mathsf T}U_s=0\) for \(r\ne s\), \(\sum_{r=1}^mP_r=I_d\), and every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\) has the unique block decomposition \(x=\sum_{r=1}^mU_rU_r^{\mathsf T}x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A disjoint-block partition groups all coordinates into nonempty, nonoverlapping blocks and yields a unique decomposition into mutually orthogonal block components.
assumptions_latex: \(d,m\in\mathbb{N}\)
\(\varnothing\ne B_r\subseteq[d]\)

notation.meaning: Canonical injection from block coordinates into the full space.
Orthogonal coordinate projector associated with block \(r\).

children.title: Scalar-to-Block Granularity
children.top_down_role: Structural tradeoffs associated with changing the update-unit size.

knowledge_statements.title: Scalar-to-Block Granularity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents each disjoint block as an aggregation of its scalar coordinate components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal{B}=\{B_1,\ldots,B_m\}\) be a disjoint-block partition of \([d]\), with scalar injections \(U_i\) and block injections \(U_r\). For every \(h_r\in\mathbb{R}^{|B_r|}\), indexed by coordinates in \(B_r\),
\[
U_rh_r=\sum_{i\in B_r}U_i(h_r)_i,
\qquad
U_rU_r^{\mathsf T}=\sum_{i\in B_r}U_iU_i^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Consequently, the block subspace is \(\operatorname{range}(U_r)=\bigoplus_{i\in B_r}\operatorname{range}(U_i)\). Scalar granularity is therefore a refinement of block granularity, and a block-supported update is exactly an aggregate of scalar updates whose indices belong to the same block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every disjoint block is the direct sum of its scalar coordinate subspaces, and every block update aggregates scalar updates within that block.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal{B}\) is a disjoint-block partition of \([d]\)
\(h_r\in\mathbb{R}^{|B_r|}\)

children.title: Overlapping Block Collections
children.top_down_role: Block systems permitting repeated membership of a variable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Overlap and Nonunique Additive Block Coordinates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic consequence of shared coordinates for the block synthesis map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(T:\prod_{r=1}^m\mathbb R^{|B_r|}\to\mathbb R^d\) by \(T(h_1,\ldots,h_m)=\sum_{r=1}^mU_rh_r\). Then \(T\) is injective if and only if the blocks are pairwise disjoint. If \(j\in B_r\cap B_s\) for \(r\ne s\), the vector \(e_j\) can be synthesized through either block and \(\ker T\ne\{0\}\), so additive block coordinates are nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overlapping coordinate blocks make additive block coordinates nonunique; the synthesis map is injective exactly for pairwise-disjoint blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(B_r\subseteq[d]\)
\(U_r\) is the canonical injection for \(B_r\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\text{ is injective}\iff B_r\cap B_s=\varnothing\quad\forall r\ne s

notation.meaning: Synthesis map from block coordinates to the ambient space.

children.title: Covering Block Collections
children.top_down_role: Block families organized by coverage of the full variable set.

knowledge_statements.title: Covering Block Collections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete coordinate coverage by a possibly overlapping indexed block collection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal{B}=(B_1,\ldots,B_m)\) be nonempty subsets of \([d]\), and let \(P_r=U_rU_r^{\mathsf T}\) be their coordinate projectors. The collection is covering precisely when
\[
\bigcup_{r=1}^mB_r=[d].
\]
Equivalently, every coordinate belongs to at least one block. If \(c_j=|\{r:j\in B_r\}|\), then
\[
\sum_{r=1}^mP_r=\operatorname{diag}(c_1,\ldots,c_d),
\]
so coverage is also equivalent to \(c_j\ge1\) for all \(j\), or to \(\sum_rP_r\succ0\). The blocks may be disjoint or overlapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block collection covers the space exactly when every coordinate lies in at least one block, equivalently when the sum of block projectors is positive definite.
assumptions_latex: \(\varnothing\ne B_r\subseteq[d]\)
\(P_r=U_rU_r^{\mathsf T}\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary equivalence between set coverage and positivity of diagonal coverage counts

children.title: Overlap Multiplicity
children.top_down_role: The effect of repeated variable membership on block-system organization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp operator characterization of coordinate incidence multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_r\) be the canonical injection for \(B_r\subseteq[d]\), \(c_j=|\{r:j\in B_r\}|\), and \(\omega=\max_jc_j\). Then \(\sum_{r=1}^m\|U_r^{\mathsf T}x\|_2^2=\sum_{j=1}^dc_jx_j^2\le\omega\|x\|_2^2\) for every \(x\), and \(\|\sum_rU_rU_r^{\mathsf T}\|_2=\omega\). If the blocks cover \([d]\) and \(c_{\min}=\min_jc_j\), then \(c_{\min}\|x\|_2^2\le\sum_r\|U_r^{\mathsf T}x\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summed squared block restrictions count each coordinate by its incidence, with sharp upper constant equal to the overlap multiplicity.
assumptions_latex: \(B_r\subseteq[d]\)
\(U_r\) is the canonical coordinate injection
knowledge_statements.title: Energy Bounds from Overlap Multiplicity
Overlap Multiplicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-coordinate and worst-case incidence counts for an indexed block collection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an indexed block collection \(\mathcal{B}=(B_1,\ldots,B_m)\) on \([d]\), define the coordinate multiplicity by
\[
c_j=\sum_{r=1}^m\mathbf{1}_{\{j\in B_r\}},
\qquad j\in[d],
\]
and define the overlap multiplicity by \(\omega(\mathcal{B})=\max_{j\in[d]}c_j\). Thus \(0\le\omega(\mathcal{B})\le m\). If \(\mathcal{B}\) covers \([d]\), then \(1\le c_j\le\omega(\mathcal{B})\) for every \(j\). A covering collection is a disjoint-block partition exactly when \(c_j=1\) for all \(j\), equivalently when \(\omega(\mathcal{B})=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overlap multiplicity is the largest number of blocks containing any single coordinate; a covering collection is disjoint exactly when this number equals one.
assumptions_latex: \(B_r\subseteq[d]\) for \(r\in[m]\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard incidence-count definition for overlapping block systems

children.title: Coverage Gaps
children.top_down_role: Block systems that leave portions of the variable space unreachable.

knowledge_statements.title: Coverage Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure mechanism caused by coordinates absent from every admissible block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal{B}=(B_1,\ldots,B_m)\) be the blocks available to an iterative method and define the coverage gap \(G=[d]\setminus\bigcup_{r=1}^mB_r\). Suppose every update satisfies
\[
x^{k+1}-x^k\in\sum_{r=1}^m\operatorname{range}(U_r).
\]
Then \(x_j^{k+1}=x_j^k=x_j^0\) for every \(j\in G\) and every \(k\ge0\). Consequently, if an optimization problem has a unique solution \(x^\star\) with \(x_j^\star\ne x_j^0\) for some \(j\in G\), no sequence using only these block-supported updates can converge to \(x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An uncovered coordinate never changes under block-supported updates, so convergence fails whenever the solution requires that coordinate to move.
assumptions_latex: \(G=[d]\setminus\bigcup_rB_r\ne\varnothing\)
\(x^{k+1}-x^k\in\sum_r\operatorname{range}(U_r)\)
\(x^\star\) is the unique solution
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists j\in G:\ x_j^\star\ne x_j^0\implies x^k\not\to x^\star\)

notation.meaning: Set of coordinates uncovered by all blocks.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: invariant-coordinate obstruction follows directly from update support

children.title: Multilevel Block Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Nested, coarse-to-fine, and multilevel variable organizations.

children.title: Hierarchical Block Trees
children.top_down_role: Nested block organizations represented through parent-child containment.

knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchical Block Trees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rooted-tree organization of nested coordinate blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A hierarchical block tree on \([d]\) is a finite rooted tree \(T=(V,E)\) with a nonempty block label \(B_v\subseteq[d]\) at each node \(v\). The root \(\rho\) satisfies \(B_\rho=[d]\). For every nonleaf node \(v\), its children \(\operatorname{ch}(v)\) satisfy
\[
B_u\subseteq B_v\quad(u\in\operatorname{ch}(v)),
\qquad
B_v=\bigcup_{u\in\operatorname{ch}(v)}B_u.
\]
In the partition-tree version, siblings are additionally pairwise disjoint. Hence every descendant block is contained in every ancestor block, and each root-to-leaf path specifies a sequence of progressively finer coordinate blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hierarchical block tree labels a rooted tree with nested blocks whose children cover their parent; disjoint siblings give a partition tree.
assumptions_latex: \(T=(V,E)\) is a finite rooted tree
\(\varnothing\ne B_v\subseteq[d]\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conventional rooted laminar block hierarchy formulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement selects a substantive convention in which every parent's children cover it while allowing overlapping siblings outside the partition-tree variant. An authoritative locator is needed to establish that this is the intended hierarchical-block-tree convention.

children.title: Multilevel Block Hierarchies
children.top_down_role: Coarse-to-fine organizations spanning multiple resolution levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Multilevel Block Hierarchies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Level-indexed sequence of coordinate partitions ordered from coarse to fine.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A multilevel block hierarchy of depth \(L\) on \([d]\) is a sequence \((\mathcal{B}_0,\ldots,\mathcal{B}_L)\) in which each \(\mathcal{B}_\ell\) is a disjoint-block partition of \([d]\), \(\mathcal{B}_0=\{[d]\}\), and every block \(C\in\mathcal{B}_{\ell+1}\) is contained in a unique parent \(B\in\mathcal{B}_\ell\). Equivalently, each coarser block satisfies
\[
B=\bigcup\{C\in\mathcal{B}_{\ell+1}:C\subseteq B\}.
\]
Thus the partitions are successively refined, and their parent relation defines a hierarchical block tree whose nodes at depth \(\ell\) are precisely the blocks in \(\mathcal{B}_\ell\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multilevel hierarchy is a sequence of increasingly fine coordinate partitions, with every fine block assigned to a unique containing parent block.
assumptions_latex: \(L\in\mathbb{N}\)
\(\mathcal{B}_\ell\) partitions \([d]\) for \(0\le\ell\le L\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nested-partition definition of a multilevel coordinate hierarchy

children.title: Cross-Level Block Transfer
children.top_down_role: Connections between update subspaces at different resolutions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized-adjoint restriction for an injective prolongation; this is a consistent transfer convention, not a requirement on every multilevel scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(P:X_c\to X_f\) be an injective linear map between finite-dimensional inner-product spaces. Define
\[
R=(P^*P)^{-1}P^*.
\]
Then \(RP=I_{X_c}\), and \(Q=PR\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(P)\):
\[
Q^2=Q,\qquad Q^*=Q,\qquad \operatorname{range}(Q)=\operatorname{range}(P).
\]
The unnormalized adjoint convention \(R=P^*\) is a left inverse exactly when \(P^*P=I_{X_c}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An injective prolongation has a normalized-adjoint left inverse, and prolongation after restriction is the orthogonal projector onto the represented coarse space. The bare adjoint is a left inverse only for an isometric prolongation.
assumptions_latex: \(X_c,X_f\) are finite-dimensional inner-product spaces
\(P:X_c\to X_f\) is linear and injective

notation.meaning: Injective prolongation from the coarse space to the fine space.
Orthogonal projector onto the represented coarse space.
Adjoint under the specified level inner products.

knowledge_statements.title: Left-Inverse Transfer and Coarse-Space Projection
Cross-Level Block Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear restriction and prolongation between adjacent block levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X_\ell\) and \(X_{\ell+1}\) be finite-dimensional inner-product spaces representing adjacent coarse and fine block levels. A cross-level transfer pair consists of a prolongation \(P_\ell:X_\ell\to X_{\ell+1}\) and a restriction \(R_\ell:X_{\ell+1}\to X_\ell\). Under the adjoint-transfer convention,
\[
R_\ell=P_\ell^*,
\qquad
\langle P_\ell z,y\rangle_{\ell+1}=\langle z,R_\ell y\rangle_\ell.
\]
A coarse correction \(s_\ell\in X_\ell\) is represented at the fine level by \(P_\ell s_\ell\), while a fine residual \(r_{\ell+1}\) is transferred to the coarse level as \(R_\ell r_{\ell+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-level transfer prolongs coarse corrections to a finer level and restricts fine residuals to a coarser level, commonly through adjoint operators.
assumptions_latex: \(X_\ell,X_{\ell+1}\) are finite-dimensional inner-product spaces
\(P_\ell:X_\ell\to X_{\ell+1}\) is linear

notation.meaning: Adjoint of the prolongation under the level inner products.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Restriction need not equal the adjoint of prolongation in every multilevel scheme. Because the record adopts that convention as its conclusion, a specific authoritative source is required before the mathematical version can be accepted.

children.title: Active Working-Set Systems
children.top_down_role: Dynamically restricted block systems based on active supports or faces.

children.title: Working-Set Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Temporary candidate subsets used to restrict eligible block updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Working-Set Restrictions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-wise restriction of admissible steps to selected coordinate blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\{B_1,\ldots,B_m\}\) be coordinate blocks with injections \(U_r\), and let \(W_k\subseteq[m]\) be the working set at iteration \(k\). The working-set restriction requires the step \(s^k=x^{k+1}-x^k\) to satisfy
\[
s^k\in\mathcal{S}(W_k):=\sum_{r\in W_k}\operatorname{range}(U_r).
\]
Equivalently, there exist block vectors \(h_r^k\) such that \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\sum_{r\in W_k}U_rh_r^k\). For disjoint blocks this condition is equivalent to \((s^k)_j=0\) for every coordinate \(j\notin\bigcup_{r\in W_k}B_r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A working-set method permits each step to change only coordinates belonging to blocks selected for the current iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(W_k\subseteq[m]\)
\(U_r\) injects block \(B_r\) into \(\mathbb{R}^d\)

children.title: Active Blocks
children.top_down_role: Blocks associated with currently active supports, faces, or constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Active Blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blocks exhibiting nonzero blockwise proximal-gradient stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=f(x)+\sum_{r=1}^m g_r(U_r^{\mathsf T}x)\), where the blocks form a disjoint partition, \(f\) is differentiable, and each \(g_r\) is proper and closed. For \(\alpha>0\), define the block proximal-gradient residual
\[
G_{r,\alpha}(x)=\alpha^{-1}\left(U_r^{\mathsf T}x-\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha g_r}\bigl(U_r^{\mathsf T}x-\alpha U_r^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x)\bigr)\right).
\]
Block \(r\) is active at \(x\) when \(G_{r,\alpha}(x)\ne0\). The active-block set is \(A_\alpha(x)=\{r\in[m]:G_{r,\alpha}(x)\ne0\}\); it is empty exactly when all blockwise proximal-gradient stationarity conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block is active when its blockwise proximal-gradient residual is nonzero; no blocks are active exactly at blockwise stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable
\(g_r\) is proper and closed for each \(r\)
\(\alpha>0\) and the displayed proximal mappings exist

notation.meaning: Set of blocks with nonzero residual.
Proximal mapping of the scaled block function.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: “Active block” is specialized here to a nonzero proximal-gradient residual, but the cited locators concern proximal mappings and coordinate updates rather than this definition. Moreover, proper closed functions do not by themselves ensure a single-valued proximal mapping; convexity or another explicit well-posedness condition is needed. A source supporting the convention and sufficient assumptions is required.

children.title: Working-Set Refresh
children.top_down_role: Policies governing changes to the current candidate subset.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Periodic Full-Inspection Refresh with Sound Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Refresh protocol that separates restricted updates from globally valid termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_i(x)\ge0\) be computable block violations and let \(0=t_0<t_1<\cdots\) be inspection times with \(t_{q+1}-t_q\le H\). At inspection time \(t_q\), evaluate every \(v_i(x^{t_q})\), form \(W_{t_q}^{+}=K_q\cup\{i:v_i(x^{t_q})>\tau_q\}\), where \(K_q\) is any declared retention set, and use only blocks in the current working set between inspections. Termination with tolerance \(\varepsilon\) is permitted only immediately after a full inspection satisfying \(\max_i v_i(x^{t_q})\le\varepsilon\). If \(v_i(x^{t_q})\ge\delta>0\) eventually and \(\tau_q<\delta\) eventually, block \(i\) is inserted at the next inspection, within at most \(H\) iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inspect all blocks at bounded intervals, refresh from the inspected violations, and allow stopping only after a contemporaneous full scan.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many blocks
Every \(v_i(x)\) is computable at inspection times
\(t_{q+1}-t_q\le H<\infty\)
The stopping decision follows the full inspection at the same iterate
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_i v_i(x^{t_q})\le\varepsilon\text{ is required for stopping, and persistent violations above }\tau_q\text{ are inserted within }H\text{ iterations}

notation.meaning: Blocks retained by the declared persistence rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Periodic Full-Inspection Refresh with Sound Stopping
Working-Set Refresh
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic refresh rule for an active subset of coordinate blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an iterate \(x^k\), a current working set \(W_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), violation scores \(v_i(x^k)\geq 0\), a threshold \(\tau_k\geq 0\), and a mandatory refresh set \(R_k\), form \[W_{k+1}=R_k\cup\{i:v_i(x^k)>\tau_k\}\cup K_k,\] where \(K_k\subseteq W_k\) contains blocks retained by the chosen persistence rule. Perform subsequent block updates only on \(W_{k+1}\). A stopping test based on block violations is admissible only when \(\max_i v_i(x^k)\) is evaluated over all blocks, or when the refresh policy guarantees that every block with positive limiting violation is eventually inserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refresh the active blocks using current violations, mandatory inspections, and retained blocks; global termination requires checking all blocks or guaranteeing eventual discovery of every persistently violated block.
assumptions_latex: \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\) has finitely many blocks.
Each \(v_i(x)\) is a computable block-optimality violation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_{k+1}=R_k\cup\{i:v_i(x^k)>\tau_k\}\cup K_k\), with globally valid stopping only under exhaustive or eventually exhaustive inspection.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subsequence Discovery Condition for Full Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precise condition under which blockwise violation decay transfers to a cluster point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_i\ge0\) vanish exactly at block-\(i\) stationarity, and let \(x^{k_\ell}\to\bar x\). If, for every block \(i\), there is a subsequence \(k_{\ell_q}\) with \(i\in W_{k_{\ell_q}}\), \(x^{k_{\ell_q}}\to\bar x\), and \(v_i(x^{k_{\ell_q}})\to0\), and if \(v_i\) is continuous at \(\bar x\), then \(v_i(\bar x)=0\) for every \(i\). Infinite selection without the common-cluster-point and violation-decay conditions is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full stationarity at a cluster point follows when every block is discovered along iterates converging to that same point, its violation decays there, and the violation is continuous.
assumptions_latex: The block set is finite
\(v_i(x)=0\) exactly characterizes block-\(i\) stationarity
Each \(v_i\) is continuous at \(\bar x\)
For each \(i\), selected iterates converging to \(\bar x\) have \(v_i\to0\)
knowledge_statements.title: Subsequence Discovery Condition for Full Stationarity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Permanent Omission Can Preserve a Nonzero Block Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth strongly convex example separating selected-block stationarity from full stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x_1,x_2)=\tfrac12x_1^2+\tfrac12(x_2-1)^2\), \(x^0=(1,0)\), and \(W_k=\{1\}\) for every \(k\). Exact minimization over the selected block followed by retention of the other block gives \(x^k=(0,0)\) for every \(k\ge1\). Thus \(\nabla_1f(x^k)=0\), whereas \(\nabla_2f(x^k)=-1\), and the limit is not the unique minimizer \((0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permanently omitting a block can produce convergence with zero selected-block violation but nonzero violation on the omitted block.
assumptions_latex: The selected block is minimized exactly and the omitted block is retained
knowledge_statements.title: Permanent Omission Can Preserve a Nonzero Block Gradient
Missed-Activity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating safe working-set restriction from permanent omission of a nonstationary block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_i(x)\geq0\) vanish exactly when block \(i\) satisfies its blockwise stationarity condition. A working-set method may fail to reach coordinatewise stationarity if there exist an index \(i\), an iteration \(K\), and a cluster point \(\bar x\) such that \(i\notin W_k\) for every \(k\geq K\) while \(v_i(\bar x)>0\). Thus a sufficient discovery boundary is: for every block \(i\), either \(v_i(x^k)\to0\), or \(i\in W_k\) infinitely often. Without this property, convergence of all updated-block violations does not imply stationarity over the full block partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A method can miss stationarity when a persistently violated block is excluded forever; safety requires its violation to vanish or the block to be selected infinitely often.
assumptions_latex: Every cluster point under consideration lies in the domain of each \(v_i\).
Updated-block convergence alone imposes no condition on blocks omitted permanently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Permanent omission together with \(v_i(\bar x)>0\) invalidates any inference of full coordinatewise stationarity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth objective terms that couple several blocks while retaining blockwise differentiability.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\), where each \(X_i\) is a finite-dimensional Euclidean space. A smooth coupling term is a continuously differentiable function \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) that need not admit a decomposition \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\). Its block gradient \(\nabla_i f(x)\in X_i\) may depend on every component of \(x\). An additional quantitative assumption used in coordinate first-order analysis is the existence of constants \(L_i>0\) such that \[f(x+U_i h_i)\leq f(x)+\langle\nabla_i f(x),h_i\rangle+\frac{L_i}{2}\lVert h_i\rVert_i^2\] whenever \(x\) and \(x+U_i h_i\) belong to the domain. This upper-model condition is not implied by differentiability alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth coupling term can depend jointly on all blocks. Coordinate methods may additionally assume blockwise quadratic upper models, but those models require more than differentiability.
knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Coupling Models

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth Coupling Need Not Admit Uniform Block Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of deriving global block upper models from differentiability or smoothness alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scalar blocks, let \(f(x_1,x_2)=x_1^2x_2^2\) on \(\mathbb R^2\). The function is \(C^\infty\) and genuinely couples the blocks, but \(\nabla_{11}^2f(x)=2x_2^2\) and \(\nabla_{22}^2f(x)=2x_1^2\) are unbounded. Hence no finite global constants \(L_1,L_2\) satisfy the seed's block quadratic upper models on all of \(\mathbb R^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth coupled polynomial can have unbounded block curvature, so differentiability does not provide global coordinate smoothness constants.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No finite global block upper-model constants exist for this \(C^\infty\) coupled function.
knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Coupling Need Not Admit Uniform Block Curvature

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Global Smoothness Implies Block Upper Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient condition for valid coordinate curvature constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient in the product Euclidean norm and each block embedding is isometric, then \[f(x+U_i h_i)\leq f(x)+\langle\nabla_i f(x),h_i\rangle+\frac L2\|h_i\|^2.\] Thus \(L_i=L\) is valid for every block, although sharper block constants may exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global Lipschitz continuity of the gradient supplies every block quadratic upper model.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz.
Each block embedding is isometric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\) is a valid upper-model constant for every block.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Smoothness Implies Block Upper Models

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mixed-Hessian Characterization of Smooth Block Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order criterion for block additivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=\prod_{i=1}^mD_i\) be an open connected product set and let \(f\in C^2(D)\). Then \[f(x)=c+\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\] for suitable functions \(f_i\) if and only if \[\nabla_{ij}^2f(x)=0\quad\text{for every }i\ne j\text{ and }x\in D.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an open connected product domain, a twice-smooth function is block additive exactly when all mixed block Hessians vanish.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is an open connected Cartesian-product domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Separable Composite Terms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real composite terms whose values and proximal subproblems separate across the fixed block partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\), an extended-real function \(g:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is block separable when there exist proper functions \(g_i:X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) such that \[g(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(x_i).\] For positive parameters \(\gamma_i\), the corresponding weighted proximal minimization separates: every minimizer of \[g(z)+\sum_{i=1}^m\frac{1}{2\gamma_i}\lVert z_i-y_i\rVert_i^2\] is obtained by independently solving \[z_i\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{u_i\in X_i}\left\{g_i(u_i)+\frac{1}{2\gamma_i}\lVert u_i-y_i\rVert_i^2\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite term is block separable when it is a sum of one-block functions; its weighted proximal problem then decomposes into independent block proximal problems.
assumptions_latex: The displayed minimizers exist.
Each \(\gamma_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The full weighted proximal minimization is the Cartesian product of the blockwise minimizer sets.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\), where each \(X_i\) is a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, and consider \(F(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(x_i)\), where \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable and each \(g_i:X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper. The model is block-compatible when, for every block \(i\), there is a constant \(L_i>0\) such that \[f(x+U_i h_i)\leq f(x)+\langle\nabla_i f(x),h_i\rangle+\frac{L_i}{2}\lVert h_i\rVert_i^2\] on every admissible block segment, and the one-block proximal subproblem below has a minimizer. Then, for every \(0<\gamma_i\leq L_i^{-1}\), a compatible update is \[x_i^+\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{u_i\in X_i}\left\{g_i(u_i)+\langle\nabla_i f(x),u_i-x_i\rangle+\frac{1}{2\gamma_i}\lVert u_i-x_i\rVert_i^2\right\},\] with every other block unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth-plus-separable model is block-compatible when each smooth partial gradient has a blockwise quadratic upper model and each one-block proximal subproblem is solvable; these conditions yield an independent proximal-gradient update for every selected block.
knowledge_statements.title: Smooth-Composite Compatibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact stationarity test supplied by the compatible block update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume each \(g_i\) is proper, closed, and convex and \(\gamma_i>0\). Define \[T_i(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma_i g_i}(x_i-\gamma_i
abla_i f(x)).\] Then \[T_i(x)=x_i\iff0\in
abla_i f(x)+\partial g_i(x_i).\] Consequently, all block fixed-point equations hold if and only if \(0\in
abla f(x)+\partial g(x)\) for \(g=\sum_i g_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compatible block proximal-gradient map fixes a block exactly when that block's composite first-order inclusion holds.

\(f\) is differentiable.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Compatibility Requires Both Curvature Control and Blockwise Proximal Access
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural boundary of the independent update interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Differentiability of \(f\) and availability of the full proximal map of \(g\) do not by themselves imply the seed's block-compatible interface. Without a valid block upper model, the quadratic block model need not majorize the smooth change. Without block-separable proximal structure, a block of the full proximal map can depend on other output blocks and cannot generally be computed by an independent one-block proximal call.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent block proximal-gradient updates require both controlled block curvature and blockwise proximal structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Neither differentiability alone nor full-proximal accessibility alone guarantees block compatibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Compatibility Requires Both Curvature Control and Blockwise Proximal Access

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective decrease from a compatible block proximal-gradient update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the seed's block upper model, let \(x^+\) update only block \(i\) by minimizing its proximal model with \(0<\gamma_i\leq L_i^{-1}\). Then \[F(x^+)\leq F(x)-\left(\frac{1}{2\gamma_i}-\frac{L_i}{2}\right)\|x_i^+-x_i\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compatible block proximal-gradient update is nonincreasing and gives quantified descent below the curvature threshold.
assumptions_latex: The block upper model holds with constant \(L_i\).
The block proximal model attains a minimizer.
\(0<\gamma_i\leq L_i^{-1}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coupled Proximal Map of an Absolute Difference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit two-block obstruction to independent proximal evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h(x_1,x_2)=|x_1-x_2|\), \(\gamma>0\), \(a=(y_1+y_2)/2\), and \(\delta=(y_1-y_2)/2\). Then \[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h}(y)_1=a+\operatorname{sign}(\delta)(|\delta|-\gamma)_+,\qquad \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h}(y)_2=a-\operatorname{sign}(\delta)(|\delta|-\gamma)_+.\] Thus each output block depends on both input blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map jointly shrinks the block difference while preserving the mean, so it cannot be assembled from independent scalar proximal maps.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each block of \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h}(y)\) depends on both \(y_1\) and \(y_2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Proximal Map of an Absolute Difference

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct obstruction to a block-additive representation of a finite-valued nonsmooth term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix distinct blocks \(i,j\). Let \(x^{ab}\) be four points agreeing outside blocks \(i,j\), with two selected values in each of those blocks. If \(h(x)=\sum_{r=1}^m h_r(x_r)\), then \[h(x^{11})-h(x^{10})-h(x^{01})+h(x^{00})=0.\] Therefore one finite rectangle with a nonzero difference certifies that \(h\) has no block-additive representation relative to the fixed partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero two-block rectangular difference certifies that a finite-valued term is not additive across the chosen blocks.
assumptions_latex: All four displayed function values are finite.
Separability is assessed relative to one fixed block partition.
review_flags: This is a one-way finite-value certificate; extended-real indicators require a product-domain test.
knowledge_statements.title: Rectangular-Difference Certificate of Block Nonseparability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact partition-relative criterion for separability and proximal factorization of a convex-set indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq X_1\oplus\cdots\oplus X_m\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. Its indicator is block additive, \[\delta_C(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\delta_{C_i}(x_i),\] for nonempty closed convex sets \(C_i\subseteq X_i\), if and only if \(C=C_1\times\cdots\times C_m\). Equivalently, in the Euclidean product norm, \[P_C(y)=\bigl(P_{C_1}(y_1),\ldots,P_{C_m}(y_m)\bigr)\qquad\forall y\] if and only if \(C\) is that Cartesian product.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex constraint indicator is block separable, and its projection is independently computable, exactly when the feasible set is a Cartesian product of block sets.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
The ambient norm is the Euclidean product norm.
review_flags: The geometric consequences of coupled nonproduct constraints remain owned by Constraint-Coupling Geometry.
knowledge_statements.title: Product-Domain Criterion for Indicator Separability

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proximal Factorization Characterizes Convex Block Separability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between block-additive convex structure and coordinatewise factorization of the full proximal map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\oplus\cdots\oplus X_m\) be a finite-dimensional Euclidean product and let \(h:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex. The following are equivalent: (i) there exist proper closed convex functions \(h_i:X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(c\in\mathbb R\) such that \(h(x)=c+\sum_i h_i(x_i)\); (ii) for some \(\gamma>0\), there exist maps \(T_i:X_i\to X_i\) satisfying \[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h}(y)=\bigl(T_1(y_1),\ldots,T_m(y_m)\bigr)\qquad\forall y\in X.\] Under (i), one may take \(T_i=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h_i}\), and the factorization holds for every \(\gamma>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper closed convex term, the full proximal map factors blockwise exactly when the term is block additive up to a constant.
assumptions_latex: The block space is a finite-dimensional Euclidean direct sum with the product norm.
\(h\) is proper, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: h=c+\sum_i h_i\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma h}(y)=\bigl(T_i(y_i)\bigr)_{i=1}^m\text{ for some }\gamma>0\text{ and all }y.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematical definition of block separability and nonseparability for proper extended-real terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\oplus\cdots\oplus X_m\) and let \(h:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper. Relative to this fixed partition, \(h\) is block separable when there exist proper functions \(h_i:X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(c\in\mathbb R\) such that \[h(x)=c+\sum_{i=1}^m h_i(x_i)\qquad\forall x\in X.\] It is block nonseparable when no such representation exists. The property is partition-dependent and does not follow merely from a syntactically coupled formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper extended-real term is nonseparable when it has no additive representation across the fixed blocks; this is a mathematical, partition-relative property.
assumptions_latex: \(h\) is proper.
The block partition is fixed.
Every component in a proposed additive representation is proper and the additive constant is finite.

Nonseparable Nonsmooth Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsmooth objectives whose coupling obstructs ordinary independent block proximal updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\). A nonseparable nonsmooth model contains a proper extended-real term \(h:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) for which no representation \(h(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m h_i(x_i)\) is available relative to the chosen partition. Consequently, the proximal problem \[\mathop{\rm minimize}_{z\in X}\;h(z)+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\lVert z-y\rVert^2\] generally couples multiple blocks and cannot be recovered by independently computing one-block proximal maps. Examples include \(h(x)=\lVert Ax-b\rVert_1\) when a row of \(A\) contains nonzero entries from several blocks, and indicators of nonproduct constraint sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonseparable nonsmooth term jointly involves several blocks, so its proximal step generally cannot be assembled from independent one-block proximal calculations.
assumptions_latex: Separability is assessed relative to the fixed block partition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The full proximal subproblem generally requires a coupled solver or an alternative splitting formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinatewise Minimum Need Not Be a Joint Local Minimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by descent directions mixing blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x,y)=x^2+y^2-4xy\), the origin minimizes both one-block restrictions because \(F(x,0)=x^2\geq0\) and \(F(0,y)=y^2\geq0\). Yet \(F(t,t)=-2t^2<0=F(0,0)\) for every \(t\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate minimization in every coordinate can miss a joint descent direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((0,0)\) is coordinatewise globally minimizing but not jointly locally minimizing.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Block Stationarity Does Not Certify a Local Minimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth saddle-point failure of block stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All block gradients can vanish at a saddle point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((0,0)\) is block stationary but not a local minimizer.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinatewise Minimality Implies Limiting Block Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order implication for differentiable-plus-block-separable nonconvex models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(x_i)\), where \(f\) is continuously differentiable near \(\bar x\) and each \(g_i\) is proper and lower semicontinuous near \(\bar x_i\). If \(\bar x\) is a coordinatewise local minimizer, then, for the limiting subdifferential, \[0\in\nabla_i f(\bar x)+\partial g_i(\bar x_i),\qquad i=1,\ldots,m.\] The converse need not hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinatewise local minimality implies every limiting block-stationarity inclusion, but block stationarity alone need not imply minimality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded theorem for problem (11.1); Assumption 11.1(A)–(B) and the problem definition are retained by reference because they are not expanded in the item.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_p\) satisfy Assumption 11.1(A)–(B), and let \(x^*\in\operatorname{dom}g\). Then \(x^*\) is stationary for problem (11.1) if and only if

-\nabla_i f(x^*)\in\partial g_i(x_i^*)\qquad(i=1,\ldots,p).

\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\), where each \(X_i\) is a finite-dimensional Euclidean space. A feasible set \(C\subseteq X\) has product constraint geometry relative to this partition when \[C=C_1\times\cdots\times C_m\] for nonempty sets \(C_i\subseteq X_i\). Hence, if \(x\in C\), replacing a single component \(x_i\) by any \(u_i\in C_i\) preserves feasibility. knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Constraint Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility constraints that link multiple blocks and therefore do not factor as a Cartesian product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible set \(C\subseteq X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) has coupled constraint geometry relative to the chosen partition when it cannot be represented as \(C_1\times\cdots\times C_m\). Equivalently, admissibility of a block value may depend on the remaining blocks. For \(x\in C\), define the conditional block section \[C_i(x_{-i})=\{u_i\in X_i:(x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1},u_i,x_{i+1},\ldots,x_m)\in C\}.\] Coupling is witnessed whenever this section varies with \(x_{-i}\). Thus independent projection or independent block replacement is not generally feasibility preserving, even when \(C\) itself is closed and convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coupled constraints make a block’s admissible values depend on other blocks, so independent block replacement or projection need not preserve feasibility.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tangent Support Does Not Imply Exact One-Block Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates an ambient tangent vector supported on one block from feasible perturbations confined exactly to that block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^2:v\geq u^2\}\) and \(x=(0,0)\). Then \((1,0)\in T_C(x)\), since \((t,t^2)=x+t(1,t)\in C\) and \((1,t)\to(1,0)\). Nevertheless, \(x+t(1,0)=(t,0)\notin C\) for every \(t>0\), and no sequence of feasible perturbations supported only on the first block can converge tangentially to \((1,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ambient tangent vector may be supported on one block even though feasibility requires higher-order motion in another block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((1,0)\in T_C(0,0)\) but no positive perturbation confined to the first block is feasible.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\), let \(x\in C\), and let \(U_i:X_i\to X\) denote the canonical block embedding. The feasible coordinate-direction cone for block \(i\) is \[D_i(C,x)=\{d_i\in X_i:U_i d_i\in T_C(x)\},\] where \(T_C(x)\) is the contingent tangent cone. Equivalently, \(d_i\in D_i(C,x)\) when there exist \(t_n\downarrow0\) and \(d_i^n\to d_i\) such that \(x+t_nU_i d_i^n\in C\) for every \(n\). These are precisely the first-order feasible directions that alter only block \(i\).

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinatewise Feasibility Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A coupled equality where no nonzero one-block direction is feasible although joint feasible motion exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[C=\{(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb R^2:x_1+x_2=0\}\] with scalar blocks and the point \(x=(0,0)\). A perturbation supported only on block one is feasible exactly when \((t d_1,0)\in C\), which forces \(d_1=0\); similarly, every feasible block-two direction has \(d_2=0\). Hence \(D_1(C,x)=D_2(C,x)=\{0\}\). Nevertheless, \((1,-1)\in T_C(x)\) is a nonzero jointly feasible direction. For the objective \(f(x)=-x_1+x_2\), this direction is strictly descending because \(\langle\nabla f(x),(1,-1)\rangle=-2\). Thus coordinatewise immobility need not imply constrained stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the constraint that two blocks sum to zero, neither block can move alone, yet a joint feasible direction can strictly decrease the objective.

Feasibility must be preserved after each individual block update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_1(C,0)=D_2(C,0)=\{0\}\) while \((1,-1)\in T_C(0)\) is a strict descent direction for \(f\).

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Smoothness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lipschitz continuity of each scalar-coordinate partial derivative along its coordinate line.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) be differentiable on an open set containing the relevant coordinate segments. The function is coordinatewise smooth with constants \(L_i>0\) if, for every \(x\), scalar \(t\), and coordinate \(i\) such that the segment from \(x\) to \(x+t e_i\) remains in the domain, \[|
abla_i f(x+t e_i)-
abla_i f(x)|\leq L_i|t|.\] This condition implies the coordinate descent inequality \[f(x+t e_i)\leq f(x)+t
abla_i f(x)+ rac{L_i}{2}t^2.\] It is weaker than requiring the full gradient to be globally Lipschitz with a single constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate smoothness bounds how each partial derivative changes along its own coordinate line and yields a one-dimensional quadratic upper model.

Each \(L_i\) is finite and positive.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinate Constants Do Not Control Cross-Coordinate Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic family separating coordinate curvature from full-gradient smoothness constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M>0\), let \(f_M(x_1,x_2)=Mx_1x_2\). Then each partial derivative is constant along its own coordinate line, so the sharp coordinate constants are \(L_1^*=L_2^*=0\). However, \[\nabla f_M(x_1,x_2)=(Mx_2,Mx_1)\] has Euclidean Lipschitz constant \(M\). Thus coordinate constants alone provide no finite bound on the full-gradient Lipschitz constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrarily large cross-coordinate curvature can coexist with zero coordinate curvature constants.
assumptions_latex: The Euclidean norm is used for the full-gradient Lipschitz constant.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Twice-differentiable characterization along scalar coordinate lines.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be open and convex and let \(f\in C^2(D)\). For each coordinate \(i\), coordinate smoothness with constant \(L_i\) holds on every admissible coordinate segment if and only if \[|\partial_{ii}^2f(x)|\le L_i\qquad(x\in D).\] Consequently, the least coordinate Lipschitz constant is \[L_i^*=\sup_{x\in D}|\partial_{ii}^2f(x)|,\] allowing the value \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a twice continuously differentiable function, coordinate smoothness is equivalent to bounded diagonal Hessian curvature, with the sharp constant given by its supremum.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is open and convex.

knowledge_statements.title: Partition-Dependent Smoothness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smoothness measured in the product metric induced by a specified partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a partition \(\mathcal P=(X_1,\ldots,X_m)\) of \(\mathbb{R}^n\), positive weights \(w_i\), and the product norm \(\lVert h\rVert_{\mathcal P,w}^2=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i\lVert h_i\rVert_i^2\). The partition-dependent smoothness modulus is \[L_{\mathcal P,w}:=\inf\left\{L\ge0:\ f(x+h)\le f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),h\rangle+\frac L2\lVert h\rVert_{\mathcal P,w}^2\ \text{for all }x,h\right\}.\] Because the admissible block decomposition and metric enter this infimum, changing \(\mathcal P\) or \(w\) may change the modulus even though \(f\) is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The smoothness modulus is the least quadratic-model constant in a norm determined by the chosen partition and block weights.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic criterion ensuring that preconditioning preserves the chosen blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m X_i\), let \(Q_i:X\to X\) be the projector onto \(X_i\), and let \(P:X\to X\) be self-adjoint and positive definite. The preconditioner \(P\) is compatible with the partition when \[PQ_i=Q_iP\quad\text{for every }i.\] This condition is equivalent to \(P(X_i)\subseteq X_i\) for every block, and hence to the block-diagonal representation \(P=\sum_i Q_iPQ_i\). Consequently, applying \(P^{-1}\) to a vector supported on one block neither creates components in other blocks nor couples independent block solves.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\operatorname{blkdiag}(P_1,\ldots,P_m)\succ0\), and define the block condition number \(\kappa_i(P)=\lambda_{\max}(P_i)/\lambda_{\min}(P_i)\). For the quadratic \(f_i(x_i)=\tfrac12 x_i^{\mathsf T}P_i x_i\), the Euclidean smoothness and strong-convexity constants are \(\lambda_{\max}(P_i)\) and \(\lambda_{\min}(P_i)\). Gradient descent with the optimal constant stepsize has worst-case Euclidean norm contraction factor \[\rho_i=\frac{\kappa_i(P)-1}{\kappa_i(P)+1}.\] Hence \(\kappa_i(P)\to\infty\) implies \(\rho_i\to1\): block alignment alone does not prevent arbitrarily slow progress when a block metric is ill-conditioned.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) contain the initial point \(x^0\), and suppose a coordinate method produces \(x^{k+1}=x^k+U_{i_k}h_{i_k}^k\). children.title: Localization Breakdown
children.top_down_role: Regimes where restricted or local descriptors fail to control broader behavior.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Endpoint Membership Does Not Replace Segment Containment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of componentwise localization on a disconnected certified set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V=(-2,-1)\cup(1,2)\). For every \(M>0\), there is \(f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R)\) with \(f'=0\) on \((-2,-1)\) and \(f'=M\) on \((1,2)\). Thus the derivative is constant on each component, but for endpoints \(x\in(-2,-1)\), \(y\in(1,2)\), the quantity \[f(y)-f(x)-f'(x)(y-x)\] need not vanish and can grow linearly with \(M\). Componentwise curvature bounds therefore do not certify a step whose joining segment leaves \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Curvature bounds on separate components do not certify a step joining those components.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is disconnected.
Derivative bounds are asserted only within each component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x,y\}\subset V\not\Longrightarrow\text{a local upper model for the step from }x\text{ to }y.
knowledge_statements.title: Endpoint Membership Does Not Replace Segment Containment
Localization Breakdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local coordinate bound fails once another block moves outside its certified region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f(x,y)=\tfrac12 e^y x^2+	frac12 y^2\) on \(\mathbb{R}^2\), with singleton coordinate blocks. On the strip \(R_M=\{(x,y):y\le M\}\), the coordinate curvature in \(x\) is \(\partial_{xx}^2f(x,y)=e^y\le e^M\), so \(L_x(R_M)=e^M\) is valid there. For any fixed \(M\), a permissible update of the \(y\)-block can reach \(y=M+t\) with \(t>0\), where the required \(x\)-block constant is at least \(e^{M+t}>e^M\). Thus the localized model ceases to be valid after the iterate leaves its certified region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block’s curvature can depend unboundedly on another block, so leaving the certified region invalidates the previously valid local constant.
assumptions_latex: Coordinates \(x\) and \(y\) form separate singleton blocks.
The method permits a y-update leaving \(R_M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local constant \(L_x(R_M)=e^M\) does not control subsequent x-updates at points with \(y>M\).

notation.meaning: Strip on which the x-coordinate curvature is locally bounded.

children.title: Partial-Derivative Oracles

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Derivative Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selected-block first-order access for a differentiable objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable under the decomposition \(\mathbb{R}^n=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m X_i\), with block injections \(U_i\). A partial-derivative oracle accepts a query \((x,S)\), where \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and returns \[\mathcal O_{\partial f}(x,S)=\bigl(U_i^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x)\bigr)_{i\in S}.\] It need not return unrequested components, function values, minimizers, or proximal points. A single-block oracle is the special case \(S=\{i\}\); its output lies in the product dual space \(\prod_{i\in S}X_i^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial-derivative oracle returns exactly the requested gradient blocks at a query point, without requiring access to the full gradient.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable at every admissible query point.
The block decomposition and injections are fixed and known to the oracle user.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal O_{\partial f}(x,S)=(\nabla_i f(x))_{i\in S}\) exposes only the selected gradient blocks.

children.title: Coordinate-Minimization Oracles

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimality Certificate for an Exact Coordinate-Minimization Answer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order characterization of an exact convex block minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x\) and block \(i\), and define \(\phi_i(v)=f(x+U_i(v-x_i))\). If \(\phi_i\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and attains its minimum, then \[u_i\in\operatorname*{argmin}_v\phi_i(v)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad0\in\partial\phi_i(u_i).\] For Euclidean blocks, if \(f\) is differentiable at \(x^+=x+U_i(u_i-x_i)\), this condition becomes \[U_i^*\nabla f(x^+)=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact convex coordinate-minimization answer is certified by a zero block subgradient, or by a zero block gradient in the differentiable case.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi_i\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
The block minimum is attained.
The differentiable specialization uses Euclidean product blocks.

notation.meaning: objective restricted to the selected block

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Certificate for an Exact Coordinate-Minimization Answer

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence and Uniqueness Boundary for Coordinate Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonattainment, nonuniqueness, and a sufficient well-posedness regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite block infimum need not be attained: \(\phi(v)=e^v\) on \(\mathbb R\) has infimum zero and no minimizer. An attained minimum need not be unique: every point minimizes \(\phi(v)=0\). By contrast, a proper, lower-semicontinuous, coercive, strongly convex function on a finite-dimensional block has a unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact block minimization may fail through nonattainment or may be set-valued; coercive strong convexity in finite dimensions ensures a unique response.
assumptions_latex: The counterexamples use a one-dimensional selected block.
The sufficient condition is stated for a finite-dimensional block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf\phi> -\infty\not\Rightarrow\operatorname*{argmin}\phi\ne\varnothing;\quad\text{coercive strong convexity implies a singleton argmin}.
knowledge_statements.title: Existence and Uniqueness Boundary for Coordinate Minimization
Coordinate-Minimization Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or additive-error minimization along one selected block subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{j=1}^m X_j\), let \(U_i:X_i\to X\) inject block \(i\), and let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\). Given \(x\in\operatorname{dom}f\), block \(i\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), a coordinate-minimization oracle returns \(u_i\in X_i\) satisfying \[f(x+U_i(u_i-x_i))\le \inf_{v\in X_i}f(x+U_i(v-x_i))+\varepsilon.\] It is exact when \(\varepsilon=0\). The corresponding updated point is \(x^+=x+U_i(u_i-x_i)\), so all blocks other than \(i\) remain unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle exactly or approximately minimizes the objective while varying only the selected block and leaving every other block fixed.
assumptions_latex: \(X_1,\ldots,X_m\) are vector spaces and \(X=\prod_{j=1}^mX_j\).
\(f\) is proper and the displayed block infimum is finite and attained up to \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: canonical injection of block i into the product space

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Proximal Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block proximal access in a Hilbert product space, including additive-error outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{j=1}^m X_j\) be a product of Hilbert spaces and let \(g_i:X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. Given \(z_i\in X_i\), \(\lambda>0\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\), a coordinate-proximal oracle returns \(u_i\in X_i\) such that \[g_i(u_i)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\lVert u_i-z_i\rVert^2\le \inf_{v\in X_i}\left\{g_i(v)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\lVert v-z_i\rVert^2\right\}+\varepsilon.\] For \(\varepsilon=0\), its output is \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda g_i}(z_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle solves, exactly or to additive error, the proximal subproblem restricted to one selected block.
assumptions_latex: \(X_i\) is a Hilbert space.
\(g_i:X_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.
\(\lambda>0\) and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_i=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda g_i}(z_i)\) when \(\varepsilon=0\), with the displayed objective gap at most \(\varepsilon\) otherwise.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact inclusion and the distance consequence of additive proximal-objective error.

Then exact output is characterized by \[0\in\partial g_i(u_i^*)+\lambda^{-1}(u_i^*-z_i),\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad\lambda^{-1}(z_i-u_i^*)\in\partial g_i(u_i^*).\] Every additive-error answer satisfying \(q_i(u_i)\le q_i(u_i^*)+\varepsilon\) obeys \[\|u_i-u_i^*\|\le\sqrt{2\lambda\varepsilon}.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full Fixed-Point Certificate from Coordinate Residual Queries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation of a complete common-point set of block-residual answers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^mX_i\) carry the product norm \(\|x\|^2=\sum_i\|x_i\|_i^2\), let \(T:X\to X\), and let \(R=I-T\). Querying every coordinate residual at the same point gives \[R(x)=(R_1(x),\ldots,R_m(x)),\qquad\|R(x)\|^2=\sum_i\|R_i(x)\|_i^2.\] Hence \(x\in\operatorname{Fix}T\) if and only if every answer is zero. More generally, \(\|R_i(x)\|_i\le\varepsilon_i\) for all \(i\) certifies \[\|R(x)\|\le\left(\sum_i\varepsilon_i^2\right)^{1/2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete common-point collection of coordinate residual answers reconstructs the full residual and yields exact or quantitative fixed-point certificates.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) uses the stated product norm.
\(T:X\to X\) is single-valued.
All residual components are queried at the same point.

Coordinate Residual Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selected-block access to the residual of a fixed-point operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{j=1}^m X_j\) be a product space with coordinate projections \(P_i:X\to X_i\), and let \(T:X\to X\). Define the fixed-point residual by \(R=I-T\). A coordinate residual oracle accepts \((x,i)\in X\times\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and returns exactly \[R_i(x):=P_iR(x)=x_i-P_iT(x).\] Thus the oracle reveals whether block \(i\) satisfies its fixed-point equation, but it need not reveal any component \(R_j(x)\) with \(j\ne i\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reconstruction from a Complete Component Sweep
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assembly of all common-point output-block responses into the full operator value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y=\prod_{i=1}^mY_i\), let \(F:X\to Y\), and let \(F_i=P_i^YF\). Querying every output component at a common point \(x\) reconstructs \[F(x)=(F_1(x),\ldots,F_m(x)).\] If \(Y\) has the product norm \(\|y\|^2=\sum_i\|y_i\|_i^2\), then \[\|F(x)\|^2=\sum_i\|F_i(x)\|_i^2,\] and therefore \(F(x)=0\) if and only if every component answer vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete common-point sweep of output-component queries reconstructs the operator value, its product norm, and its zero test.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{j=1}^mX_j\), let \(T:X\to X\), and write \(T_i=P_iT\). For the residual \(R=I-T\), every point \(x\in X\) and block \(i\) satisfy \[R_i(x)=P_iR(x)=x_i-T_i(x).\] Consequently, access to \(x_i\) and an operator-component oracle for \(T_i(x)\) implements a coordinate residual oracle by subtraction. knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Oracle Incompleteness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One component query cannot generally identify the full operator or its zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=\mathbb R^2\), define \(F(x_1,x_2)=(x_1,x_2)\) and \(G(x_1,x_2)=(x_1,x_2-1)\). Their first-component oracles are indistinguishable at every query because \[F_1(x_1,x_2)=G_1(x_1,x_2)=x_1.\] Nevertheless, \(\operatorname{zer}F=\{(0,0)\}\) whereas \(\operatorname{zer}G=\{(0,1)\}\). Hence unrestricted access to a single component does not determine the remaining components, the full operator, or its zero set without structural assumptions coupling the components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two operators can agree on every query to one component yet have different full zero sets.

No structural relation between the unobserved and observed components is assumed.

knowledge_statements.title: Cyclic Coordinate Orders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Periodic traversal of all coordinates in one fixed order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\ge1\), fix a permutation \(\sigma\) of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\). A coordinate-index sequence \((i_k)_{k\ge0}\) is cyclic with order \(\sigma\) when \[i_k=\sigma\bigl(1+(k\bmod m)\bigr)\qquad(k\ge0).\] Equivalently, each consecutive aligned epoch \((i_{em},\ldots,i_{em+m-1})\) equals \((\sigma(1),\ldots,\sigma(m))\). Thus every coordinate is selected exactly once per epoch and the same order repeats indefinitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cyclic order repeats one fixed permutation of all coordinates, selecting each coordinate exactly once per epoch.
assumptions_latex: \(m\) is a positive integer.
\(\sigma\) is a permutation of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\).

children.title: Essentially Cyclic Orders
children.top_down_role: Variable orders providing recurring block coverage within bounded windows.

knowledge_statements.title: Essentially Cyclic Orders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniformly bounded-delay coverage without requiring a fixed repeated permutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((i_k)_{k\ge0}\) take values in \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\). The order is essentially cyclic if there exists an integer \(q\ge m\) such that, for every \(k\ge0\), \[\{i_k,i_{k+1},\ldots,i_{k+q-1}\}=\{1,\ldots,m\}.\] Repetitions and changing within-window orders are permitted. Equivalently, every coordinate is selected at least once during every \(q\) consecutive iterations, so the delay between consecutive selections of any fixed coordinate is at most \(q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order is essentially cyclic when every coordinate appears within every window of some fixed finite length.
assumptions_latex: \(m\ge1\) and \(i_k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) for all \(k\ge0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded-window condition correctly expresses an essentially cyclic order and uses the appropriate content kind, but no authoritative block-coordinate source is cited.

children.title: Cyclic Coverage Windows
children.top_down_role: Window structure used to compare recurring coverage policies.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structure of the valid consecutive-window coverage lengths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sequence \((i_k)_{k\ge0}\) on \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), define \[Q=\left\{q\in\mathbb N:\forall k\ge0,\ \{i_k,\ldots,i_{k+q-1}\}=I\right\}.\] If \(Q\neq\varnothing\), then \(q_\star=\min Q\) exists and \[Q=\{q\in\mathbb N:q\ge q_\star\}.\] Thus every enlargement of a valid window remains valid, and \(q_\star\) is the sharp coverage-window length.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Whenever bounded-window coverage holds, the valid window lengths form an upper ray and have a unique minimal length.
assumptions_latex: \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) is finite.
\(i_k\in I\) for every \(k\ge0\).
\(Q\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Coverage Window and Monotonicity
Cyclic Coverage Windows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-window certificate for recurrent coverage of every coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an index sequence \((i_k)_{k\ge0}\) in \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\), an integer \(q\ge m\) is a cyclic coverage-window certificate if \[\forall k\ge0,\qquad \{i_k,i_{k+1},\ldots,i_{k+q-1}\}=\{1,\ldots,m\}.\] Verification of this predicate certifies that no coordinate is omitted for \(q\) consecutive iterations. A purely cyclic order generated by a fixed permutation has the sharp certificate \(q=m\); a general essentially cyclic order may require \(q>m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A window length certifies recurrent coverage when every consecutive window of that length contains all coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(i_k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) for every \(k\ge0\).
\(q\ge m\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\) certifies a uniform selection delay of at most \(q\), and fixed-permutation cyclic orders admit \(q=m\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-window formulation of recurrent coordinate coverage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-window predicate is a suitable coverage certificate and is mathematically consistent, but it lacks an inspectable source locator.

children.title: Permutation Sweep Family
children.top_down_role: Epoch-style randomized orders with within-sweep coverage.

children.title: Random Reshuffling
children.top_down_role: Randomized recurring orders formed by reshuffling the available blocks.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marginal and joint laws induced by a uniform random permutation within one epoch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi\) be uniform on the permutations of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\). For every position \(t\) and coordinate \(i\), \(\mathbb P(\pi(t)=i)=1/m\). For distinct positions \(s\ne t\) and distinct coordinates \(i\ne j\), \(\mathbb P(\pi(s)=i,\pi(t)=j)=1/[m(m-1)]\), whereas \(\mathbb P(\pi(s)=i,\pi(t)=i)=0\). Thus positions are marginally uniform but not independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each position in a random reshuffling is uniform, but positions within the epoch are dependent because a coordinate cannot repeat.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi\) is a uniform random permutation.

notation.meaning: coordinate occupying position t in the random permutation

knowledge_statements.title: Within-Epoch Sampling Law
Random Reshuffling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent uniform permutation of all coordinates at each epoch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(m\) coordinate-update maps \(S_1,\ldots,S_m\), initialize \(x^{0,0}=x^0\). For each epoch \(e=0,1,\ldots\), sample a permutation \(\pi_e\) uniformly from all permutations of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\), independently across epochs, and perform \[x^{e,t}=S_{\pi_e(t)}(x^{e,t-1}),\qquad t=1,\ldots,m.\] Set \(x^{e+1,0}=x^{e,m}\). Stop under a prescribed epoch or residual criterion and output the latest iterate. Each epoch uses every coordinate exactly once, without replacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each epoch, sample a fresh uniform permutation and update every coordinate once in that shuffled order.
assumptions_latex: \(S_i:X\to X\) is a specified update map for each coordinate \(i\).
\((\pi_e)_{e\ge0}\) are independent uniform random permutations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{e,m}=S_{\pi_e(m)}\circ\cdots\circ S_{\pi_e(1)}(x^{e,0})\), with every coordinate used once during epoch \(e\).

notation.meaning: uniform random permutation used in epoch e
iterate after t updates in epoch e

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm precisely describes independent uniform reshuffling across epochs and fits the terminal container, but no authoritative random-reshuffling citation is supplied.

children.title: Permutation Sweeps
children.top_down_role: Epoch-style schedules that visit each eligible block through a permutation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial coverage consequences of complete permutation sweeps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a permutation-sweep schedule on \(m\) coordinates, every coordinate is selected exactly \(E\) times during the first \(E\) complete epochs. If \(\tau_r(i)\) and \(\tau_{r+1}(i)\) are consecutive selection times of coordinate \(i\), then \(1\le \tau_{r+1}(i)-\tau_r(i)\le 2m-1\). The upper bound is sharp over arbitrary consecutive permutations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After E complete sweeps every coordinate has been visited E times, and no coordinate waits more than 2m−1 iterations between consecutive visits; this bound is attainable.
assumptions_latex: Every epoch is a permutation of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\).

notation.meaning: number of selections of coordinate i among the first K iterations
iteration of the r-th selection of coordinate i

knowledge_statements.title: Visit Counts and Intervisit Gaps
Permutation Sweeps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epochwise coordinate schedules that visit every coordinate exactly once.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\ge1\). A permutation-sweep schedule is an index sequence partitioned into epochs of length \(m\) for which there exists a permutation \(\pi_e\) of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\) at every epoch \(e\ge0\) such that \[i_{em+t-1}=\pi_e(t),\qquad t=1,\ldots,m.\] The permutations may be deterministic, random, identical, or dependent across epochs. Within each epoch, however, every coordinate occurs exactly once and no coordinate is repeated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A permutation sweep visits every coordinate exactly once per epoch, while the permutation may change between epochs.
assumptions_latex: \(m\) is a positive integer.
\((i_k)_{k\ge0}\) takes values in \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The epochwise permutation-sweep definition is precise and appropriately distinguished from random reshuffling, but it has no authoritative source locator.

children.title: Across-Epoch Dependence
children.top_down_role: Dependence structure induced by successive randomized permutations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Marginals Do Not Imply Independent Epochs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction separating uniform epoch marginals from across-epoch independence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Draw one uniform random permutation \(\Pi\) of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and set \(\pi_e=\Pi\) for every epoch \(e\ge0\). Every \(\pi_e\) is marginally uniform and every epoch is a complete permutation sweep, but \(\pi_e\) is \(\sigma(\pi_0)\)-measurable. For every nontrivial \(A\subset\mathfrak S_m\), \[\mathbb P(\pi_e\in A\mid\pi_0)=\mathbf 1_{\{\pi_0\in A\}},\] which differs from \(\mathbb P(\pi_e\in A)=|A|/m!\) with positive probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeating one initially uniform permutation forever gives uniform marginal orders and complete sweeps but maximal dependence between epochs.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi\) is uniform on \(\mathfrak S_m\).
\(A\) is neither empty nor all of \(\mathfrak S_m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_e\sim\operatorname{Unif}(\mathfrak S_m)\) for every \(e\), but \((\pi_e)_{e\ge0}\) is not independent.

notation.meaning: set of permutations of m indices

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Marginals Do Not Imply Independent Epochs
Across-Epoch Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probabilistic criterion distinguishing dependent permutation sweeps from independent reshuffling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\pi_e)_{e\ge0}\) be random permutations of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \(\mathcal F_e=\sigma(\pi_0,\ldots,\pi_e)\). The sweep orders exhibit across-epoch dependence if there exist \(e\ge1\) and a set \(A\) of permutations such that \[\mathbb P(\pi_e\in A\mid\mathcal F_{e-1})\ne\mathbb P(\pi_e\in A)\] on an event of positive probability. Uniform marginal distributions do not preclude this dependence; independent random reshuffling instead makes the two displayed probabilities equal almost surely for every \(e\) and \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Epoch orders are dependent when a past permutation changes the conditional distribution of a later permutation, even if every marginal is uniform.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi_e\) is a random permutation for every epoch \(e\).
Conditional probabilities are taken with respect to \(\mathcal F_{e-1}=\sigma(\pi_0,\ldots,\pi_{e-1})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\pi_e)\) is across-epoch dependent exactly when the displayed conditional-independence identity fails for some \(e\) and \(A\).

notation.meaning: history generated by permutation orders through epoch e

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conditional-probability definition of temporal dependence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional-probability condition correctly characterizes dependence of an epoch order on its history and fits the leaf, but no optimization-specific source is cited.

children.title: Incomplete Permutation Coverage
children.top_down_role: Interrupted or restricted sweeps that lose full epoch coverage.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Per-Epoch Incompleteness Does Not Determine Recurrent Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates omission inside each epoch from omission across the entire run.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let I=\{1,2\} and let every epoch contain one unrepeated selection. The alternating schedule J_{2r}=\{1\}, J_{2r+1}=\{2\} is incomplete in every epoch because J_e\subsetneq I, yet both blocks are selected infinitely often. Therefore incomplete permutation coverage within individual epochs does not imply run-wide starvation; recurrent coverage must be checked across epochs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Epochs may each omit a block while their combined schedule still visits every block infinitely often.
assumptions_latex: The block set is I=\{1,2\}.
Each epoch contains one selected block and therefore has no within-epoch repetition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: J_e\subsetneq I\ \forall e\quad\centernot\Rightarrow\quad\exists i\in I\text{ selected only finitely often}.

notation.meaning: Set of blocks selected in epoch e.

knowledge_statements.title: Per-Epoch Incompleteness Does Not Determine Recurrent Coverage
Incomplete Permutation Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a permutation sweep when an epoch omits one or more blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the block set be \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and partition a serial schedule into finite epochs \(E_e\). An epoch has incomplete permutation coverage when its ordered selection list contains no repeated block but its selected set \(J_e\) is a strict subset of \(I\). Such coverage does not guarantee coordinate-wise progress: for \(m=2\), the schedule \(J_e=\{1\}\) for every epoch is incomplete and never updates block \(2\), so any convergence result requiring recurrent coverage of every block is inapplicable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An epoch that visits a proper subset without repetition is an incomplete sweep; repeated omission of the same block permits permanent starvation.
assumptions_latex: \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) is finite.
Each epoch is finite and contains no repeated selected block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_e\subsetneq I\) does not imply recurrent coverage, and \(J_e=\{1\}\) for all \(e\) starves block \(2\).

notation.meaning: iteration indices belonging to epoch e

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample and failure boundary are mathematically coherent, but no source supports the specific incomplete-permutation terminology or its intended taxonomy sense.

children.title: Flexible Coverage Schedules
children.top_down_role: Schedules permitting variable order and grouped recurring coverage.
