children.title: Almost-Cyclic Schedules
children.top_down_role: Flexible recurring orders with bounded coverage requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Almost-Cyclic Schedules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-gap coverage condition for serial block-coordinate schedules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((i_k)_{k\geq 0}\) be a serial schedule with \(i_k\in I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\). The schedule is almost cyclic if there exists an integer \(T\geq m\) such that every consecutive window of \(T\) iterations contains every block: \[\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+T-1}\{i_t\}=I\qquad\text{for every }k\geq0.\] Equivalently, the gap between consecutive selections of any fixed block is uniformly bounded by \(T\). The ordering and multiplicities inside each window may vary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A serial schedule is almost cyclic when every block occurs within every window of some fixed finite length.
assumptions_latex: \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) is finite.
Exactly one index \(i_k\in I\) is selected at each iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists T\geq m\) such that \(\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+T-1}\{i_t\}=I\) for all \(k\geq0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bounded-window condition is precise, but the almost-cyclic terminology and the claimed gap equivalence require a source clarifying treatment of initial and terminal gaps.

children.title: Block-Iterative Coverage
children.top_down_role: Schedules organized around recurring coverage by selected block groups.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Iterative Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-window coverage allowing simultaneous selection of multiple blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \(S_k\subseteq I\) be the set of blocks activated at iteration \(k\). The schedule is block-iterative with coverage bound \(T\in\mathbb N\) if \[\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+T-1}S_t=I\qquad\text{for every }k\geq0.\] Thus every block is activated at least once in each consecutive \(T\)-iteration window. The sets \(S_k\) may contain several blocks, overlap across iterations, or be empty, provided the displayed coverage condition holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-iterative schedule activates every block at least once within each window of a fixed finite length.
assumptions_latex: \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) is finite.
Each activation set satisfies \(S_k\subseteq I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists T\in\mathbb N\) such that \(\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+T-1}S_t=I\) for every \(k\geq0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed coverage condition is coherent and fits a condition container, but the block-iterative terminology and allowance of empty activation sets are unsupported.

children.title: Grouped Coverage Windows
children.top_down_role: Window structures used to track recurring group participation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduction to a Global Coverage Window
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between finitely many group-specific bounds and one global coverage bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=G_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}G_r\) be a finite partition. If each group has a finite bound \(T_j\) satisfying \[G_j\subseteq\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+T_j-1}S_t\qquad\text{for every }k\ge0,\] then \(T=\max_{1\le j\le r}T_j\) satisfies \[I=\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+T-1}S_t\qquad\text{for every }k\ge0.\] Conversely, any global bound \(T\) is a valid bound for every group. Thus grouped and global coverage are equivalent as existence conditions for a finite partition, while \((T_1,\ldots,T_r)\) retains group-specific recurrence information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finitely many groups, group-specific finite windows exist exactly when a global finite coverage window exists, although the group bounds retain finer timing information.
assumptions_latex: \(I=G_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}G_r\) is a finite partition into nonempty groups.
\(S_k\subseteq I\) for every \(k\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T=\max_jT_j\) is a global coverage bound, and every global bound is valid for each \(G_j\).
knowledge_statements.title: Reduction to a Global Coverage Window
Grouped Coverage Windows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage condition organized by a fixed partition of the block set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be partitioned into nonempty groups \(G_1,\ldots,G_r\), and let \(S_k\subseteq I\) denote the blocks activated at iteration \(k\). The schedule has grouped coverage windows if, for each group \(G_j\), there exists \(T_j\in\mathbb N\) such that \[G_j\subseteq\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+T_j-1}S_t\qquad\text{for every }k\geq0.\] Hence all members of each group recur with a group-specific bounded gap, while different groups may have different window lengths and activation patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each block group has its own finite window length within which every member of that group must be activated.
assumptions_latex: \(I=G_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}G_r\) with every \(G_j\neq\varnothing\).
Each activation set satisfies \(S_k\subseteq I\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition is internally consistent, but grouped coverage windows appear to be a specialized convention with no cited authority confirming this exact meaning.

children.title: Coverage-Starvation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Schedules permitting persistent exclusion of required blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Coverage-Starvation Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of bounded recurrent coverage through unbounded selection gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For activation sets \(S_k\subseteq I\), a block \(i\in I\) is starved if its selection times \(K_i=\{k\geq0:i\in S_k\}\) are finite or have unbounded consecutive gaps. Equivalently, for every \(T\in\mathbb N\), some window \(\{k,\ldots,k+T-1\}\) contains no activation of \(i\). Consequently, no finite block-iterative coverage bound exists, and convergence arguments requiring each block to be updated within uniformly bounded windows cannot be invoked.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starvation occurs when some block is selected only finitely often or with unbounded gaps, destroying every bounded-window coverage guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is a finite block-index set.
Each activation set satisfies \(S_k\subseteq I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists i\in I\,\forall T\in\mathbb N\,\exists k\geq0:\ i\notin\bigcup_{t=k}^{k+T-1}S_t\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quantified failure of bounded-window coverage is mathematically sound and fits a failure-boundary leaf, but the starvation terminology and convergence-use claim lack evidence.

children.title: Randomized Block Sampling
children.top_down_role: Probability distributions over individual blocks and block subsets.

children.title: Serial Sampling Probability Regimes
children.top_down_role: One-block random sampling with uniform or heterogeneous probabilities.

children.title: Uniform Serial Sampling
children.top_down_role: One-block sampling using equal selection probabilities.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Serial Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-block randomized sampling with equal conditional probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \(\mathcal F_k\) contain all randomness revealed before iteration \(k\). Uniform serial sampling selects exactly one random block \(I_k\in I\) and satisfies \[\mathbb P(I_k=i\mid\mathcal F_k)=\frac1m\qquad\text{for every }i\in I\text{ and }k\geq0.\] Because the conditional distribution is constant, each block has the same marginal inclusion probability and the sequence \((I_k)\) is independent of its past selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every iteration, exactly one of the m blocks is selected, each with conditional probability 1/m.
assumptions_latex: \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) is finite.
\(I_k\) is measurable after the iteration-k draw, while \(\mathcal F_k\) records the prior history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(I_k=i\mid\mathcal F_k)=1/m\) for every \(i\in I\) and \(k\geq0\).

notation.meaning: single block sampled at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupon-collector coverage time intrinsic to independent uniform serial sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_{\mathrm{all}}\) be the first draw by which every block has been selected. Then \[\mathbb E[T_{\mathrm{all}}]=mH_m=m\sum_{r=1}^m\frac1r.\] For integer \(k\ge0\), \[\mathbb P(T_{\mathrm{all}}\le k)=\sum_{j=0}^m(-1)^j\binom mj\left(1-\frac jm\right)^k,\] and \(\mathbb P(T_{\mathrm{all}}>k)\le m(1-1/m)^k\le me^{-k/m}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform serial sampling needs m times the m-th harmonic number of draws on average to visit every block, with an exact inclusion-exclusion distribution.
assumptions_latex: Successive serial selections are independent and uniform over \(m\) blocks.

notation.meaning: Number of draws required to visit every block.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Coupon-Collector Coverage

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon occupancy representation for independent uniform serial block sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(N_i(k)=\sum_{t=1}^k\mathbf 1_{\{I_t=i\}}\), \[(N_1(k),\ldots,N_m(k))\sim\operatorname{Multinomial}\!\left(k;\frac1m,\ldots,\frac1m\right).\] Hence \(\mathbb E[N_i(k)]=k/m\), \(\operatorname{Var}(N_i(k))=k(m-1)/m^2\), and \(\operatorname{Cov}(N_i(k),N_j(k))=-k/m^2\) for \(i\ne j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform serial visit counts have the symmetric multinomial distribution, equal means, and negative cross-count covariance.
assumptions_latex: \(I_1,\ldots,I_k\) are independent and uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\).

notation.meaning: Number of selections of block \(i\) among the first \(k\) draws.

children.title: Nonuniform Serial Sampling
children.top_down_role: One-block sampling using heterogeneous selection probabilities.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonuniform Serial Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-block randomized sampling with prescribed unequal positive probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(p\in(0,1]^m\) satisfy \(\sum_{i=1}^m p_i=1\), and let \(\mathcal F_k\) denote the history before iteration \(k\). Nonuniform serial sampling selects exactly one block \(I_k\in I\) according to \[\mathbb P(I_k=i\mid\mathcal F_k)=p_i\qquad\text{for every }i\in I\text{ and }k\geq0,\] where the probabilities are not all equal. Positivity ensures that every block has a nonzero chance of selection at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exactly one block is drawn per iteration from a fixed, positive, unequal probability distribution.
assumptions_latex: \(p_i>0\) for every \(i\in I\), and \(\sum_{i=1}^m p_i=1\).
The vector \(p\) is fixed independently of the prior history \(\mathcal F_k\).

notation.meaning: single block sampled at iteration k

children.title: Probability-Imbalance Effects
children.top_down_role: Coverage and cost consequences of highly unequal serial probabilities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rare-block waiting time and finite-horizon coverage under fixed serial sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For independent categorical draws with fixed \(p_i>0\), let \(T_i\) be the first draw on which block \(i\) is selected. Then \[\mathbb P(T_i>k)=(1-p_i)^k,\qquad \mathbb E[T_i]=\frac1{p_i}.\] Consequently, after \(k\) draws, \[\mathbb P(\text{some block is unselected})\le\sum_i(1-p_i)^k\le me^{-kp_{\min}}.\] Thus \(k\ge p_{\min}^{-1}\log(m/\delta)\) suffices for all-block coverage with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rare block waits an average of 1/p_i draws, and a generic all-block coverage guarantee scales as 1/p_min times a logarithmic confidence factor.
assumptions_latex: Successive serial selections are independent categorical draws with fixed probabilities \(p_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(T_i>k)=(1-p_i)^k\), \(\mathbb E[T_i]=1/p_i\), and \(\mathbb P(\exists i:T_i>k)\le me^{-kp_{\min}}\).

notation.meaning: First draw number on which block \(i\) is selected.

review_flags: the all-block bound is sufficient and need not be tight for a specified nonuniform probability vector
knowledge_statements.title: Rare-Block Coverage Delay

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp benchmark for the worst-block coverage parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every serial probability vector satisfies \[p_{\min}=\min_i p_i\le\frac1m,\] with equality if and only if \(p_1=\cdots=p_m=1/m\). Hence uniform serial sampling uniquely minimizes \(\max_i1/p_i=1/p_{\min}\) and any generic upper bound depending monotonically only on \(p_{\min}^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform probabilities uniquely optimize the worst-block coverage parameter; imbalance lowers p_min and worsens reciprocal-p_min bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_{\min}\le1/m\), with equality exactly for the uniform distribution.
knowledge_statements.title: Worst-Block Imbalance Benchmark
Probability-Imbalance Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-moment inflation caused by inverse-probability correction in serial sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_m)\) be block-decomposed, sample \(I\) with positive probabilities \(p_i\), and form the unbiased estimator \(\widehat g=p_I^{-1}U_Ig_I\), where \(U_i\) embeds block \(i\) into the product space. Then \[\mathbb E[\widehat g]=g,\qquad \mathbb E\|\widehat g\|^2=\sum_{i=1}^m\frac{\|g_i\|^2}{p_i}\leq\frac{\|g\|^2}{p_{\min}}.\] Thus a small sampling probability can inflate the estimator's second moment and any bound controlled by it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse-probability correction is unbiased, but rare blocks inflate the estimator’s second moment by factors proportional to reciprocal sampling probabilities.
assumptions_latex: The product-space norm satisfies \(\|g\|^2=\sum_{i=1}^m\|g_i\|^2\).

children.title: Zero-Probability Blocks
children.top_down_role: Sampling designs that exclude blocks required for global progress.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reachability restriction induced by blocks that are never selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=\{i:p_i>0\}\) and \(Z=I\setminus A\). Any method that modifies only its sampled block satisfies \[x_Z^k=x_Z^0\quad\text{almost surely for every }k,\] so all iterates lie in \(\mathcal R(x^0)=\{x:x_Z=x_Z^0\}\). Therefore \(X^\star\cap\mathcal R(x^0)\ne\varnothing\) is necessary for convergence to a solution. Its satisfaction is not sufficient without separate assumptions ensuring convergence of the active-block method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero-probability coordinates remain frozen, so a solution is reachable only if one lies in the affine slice fixed by their initial values.
assumptions_latex: Serial sampling uses probabilities \(p_i\ge0\) with active support \(A=\{i:p_i>0\}\).
Each iteration modifies only the sampled block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_Z^k=x_Z^0\) almost surely for every \(k\), and \(X^\star\cap\mathcal R(x^0)\ne\varnothing\) is necessary for convergence to a solution.

notation.meaning: Set of blocks with positive sampling probability.
Affine slice reachable from the initialization.

review_flags: reachable-slice intersection is necessary but not sufficient for algorithmic convergence
knowledge_statements.title: Support-Restricted Reachability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp coverage boundary at zero selection probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(p_j=0\), then the first-selection time \(T_j=\inf\{k\ge1:I_k=j\}\) satisfies \[\mathbb P(T_j=\infty)=1,\qquad \mathbb E[T_j]=\infty.\] Thus no iteration budget restores coverage of block \(j\), and inverse-probability correction for that block is undefined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-probability block has infinite hitting time almost surely, so more iterations cannot restore coverage or define inverse-probability correction.
assumptions_latex: Serial draws assign fixed probability \(p_j=0\) to block \(j\).
knowledge_statements.title: Infinite Excluded-Block Hitting Time
Zero-Probability Blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A coordinate objective showing failure when a required block is never sampled.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\geq2\), choose \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and suppose serial sampling assigns \(p_j=0\). Consider \(f:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) defined by \(f(x)=\tfrac12(x_j-1)^2\), initialized at \(x^0=0\), with iterations that modify only the sampled coordinate. Since block \(j\) is sampled with probability zero, \(x_j^k=0\) almost surely for every \(k\), whereas every minimizer satisfies \(x_j=1\). Hence the iterates cannot converge to a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a necessary coordinate has zero sampling probability, a coordinate-only method can leave it unchanged forever and fail on a simple convex quadratic.
assumptions_latex: \(p_j=0\) for some block \(j\).
Each iteration changes only the sampled coordinate.

notation.meaning: j-th coordinate of the k-th iterate

children.title: Minibatch Sampling Pair
children.top_down_role: Standard multiple-block sampling constructions.

children.title: Fixed-Size Minibatches
children.top_down_role: Multiple-block samples constrained to a prescribed cardinality.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order inclusion structure of uniform sampling without replacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be uniform over the \(b\)-subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and set \(X_i=\mathbf 1_{\{i\in S\}}\). For distinct \(i,j\), \[\mathbb P(i,j\in S)=\frac{b(b-1)}{m(m-1)},\qquad \operatorname{Cov}(X_i,X_j)=-\frac{b(m-b)}{m^2(m-1)}.\] Also \(\sum_iX_i=b\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform fixed-size sampling has negatively correlated inclusion indicators except at degenerate endpoint sizes.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is uniform over all \(b\)-subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
\(m\ge2\) and \(1\le b\le m\).
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Size Inclusion Dependence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact permutation construction of a uniform fixed-size minibatch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\Pi=(\Pi_1,\ldots,\Pi_m)\) is a uniform random permutation and \(1\le b\le m\), then \(S=\{\Pi_1,\ldots,\Pi_b\}\) is uniform over all \(b\)-subsets. Conversely, a uniform \(b\)-subset followed by independent uniform orderings of the subset and its complement produces a uniform permutation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform fixed-size minibatch is the unordered set in the first b positions of a uniform random permutation.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi\) is a uniformly random permutation of \(\{1,�ldots,m\}\).
\(1\le b\le m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{\Pi_1,\ldots,\Pi_b\}\) is uniform over the \(\binom mb\) subsets of size \(b\).

notation.meaning: Set of the first \(b\) permuted indices.

knowledge_statements.title: Permutation Representation
Fixed-Size Minibatches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Without-replacement block sampling with deterministic minibatch cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and fix \(b\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). A uniform fixed-size minibatch is a random subset \(S_k\subseteq I\) drawn uniformly from the \(\binom mb\) subsets of cardinality \(b\), conditionally on the history before iteration \(k\). Thus \[|S_k|=b\quad\text{almost surely},\qquad \mathbb P(i\in S_k)=\frac bm\quad\text{for every }i\in I.\] Distinct blocks within one minibatch are sampled without replacement and their inclusion indicators are dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-size minibatch uniformly selects exactly b distinct blocks, giving every block inclusion probability b/m.
assumptions_latex: \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) is finite.
\(1\leq b\leq m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(S_k=S)=1/\binom mb\) for every \(S\subseteq I\) with \(|S|=b\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The uniform without-replacement definition and inclusion probability are correct, but no source establishes that this is the intended fixed-size minibatch convention.

children.title: Independent Minibatches
children.top_down_role: Multiple-block samples formed through independent inclusion events.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary-event probabilities and the change of law caused by rejecting empty Bernoulli minibatches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For independent inclusion \(S=\{i:B_i=1\}\), \[\mathbb P(S=\varnothing)=\prod_{i=1}^m(1-q_i),\qquad \mathbb P(S=I)=\prod_{i=1}^m q_i.\] If \(a=\prod_i(1-q_i)<1\), then \(\mathbb P(i\in S\mid S\ne\varnothing)=q_i/(1-a)\). Conditioning on nonemptiness generally destroys independence, so rejection of empty batches defines a different sampling law.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent inclusion permits empty and full batches; rejecting empty batches changes the marginals and generally destroys independence.
assumptions_latex: \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\) are mutually independent with \(B_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_i)\).
For the conditional formula, \(\mathbb P(S\ne\varnothing)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(S=\varnothing)=\prod_i(1-q_i)\), \(\mathbb P(S=I)=\prod_iq_i\), and \(\mathbb P(i\in S\mid S\ne\varnothing)=q_i/(1-a)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Empty-Batch Conditioning Boundary
Independent Minibatches
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bernoulli block sampling with independent inclusion decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and choose probabilities \(q_i\in[0,1]\). An independent minibatch is the random set \(S_k=\{i:B_{k,i}=1\}\), where, conditionally on the pre-iteration history, the variables \(B_{k,1},\ldots,B_{k,m}\) are independent Bernoulli variables satisfying \(\mathbb P(B_{k,i}=1)=q_i\). Consequently, for every \(S\subseteq I\), \[\mathbb P(S_k=S)=\prod_{i\in S}q_i\prod_{i\notin S}(1-q_i).\] Empty and full minibatches are permitted unless separately excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each block enters the minibatch through an independent Bernoulli draw, so minibatch size is generally random and may be zero.
assumptions_latex: \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) is finite.
\(q_i\in[0,1]\) for every \(i\in I\).

notation.meaning: marginal inclusion probability of block i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional Bernoulli construction and subset probability are coherent, but the exact independent-minibatch convention lacks a cited source.

children.title: Minibatch Cardinality Variability
children.top_down_role: Structural differences between fixed and random sample sizes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Poisson-binomial distribution of independent-minibatch cardinality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(N=\sum_{i=1}^mB_i\) with mutually independent \(B_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_i)\), \[G_N(z)=\mathbb E[z^N]=\prod_{i=1}^m(1-q_i+q_i z),\qquad \mathbb P(N=r)=[z^r]G_N(z).\] If all \(q_i=q\), then \(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(m,q)\). Moreover, \(0\le\operatorname{Var}(N)\le\mathbb E[N]\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(N)\le m/4\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent minibatch size has a product generating function, specializes to a binomial law for equal probabilities, and has variance bounded by its mean and by m/4.
assumptions_latex: \(N=\sum_{i=1}^mB_i\) with mutually independent \(B_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_i)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Cardinality Distribution Representation
Minibatch Cardinality Variability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mean and variance of minibatch size under independent and fixed-size sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an independent minibatch \(S=\{i:B_i=1\}\) with mutually independent \(B_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_i)\), its cardinality \(N=|S|=\sum_{i=1}^m B_i\) is Poisson-binomial and satisfies \[\mathbb E[N]=\sum_{i=1}^m q_i,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(N)=\sum_{i=1}^m q_i(1-q_i).\] Its variance is positive if and only if \(q_i\in(0,1)\) for at least one \(i\). In contrast, a fixed-size minibatch with \(|S|=b\) almost surely has \(\mathbb E[N]=b\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(N)=0\). Therefore, when \(\sum_i q_i=b\) and at least one inclusion probability is nondegenerate, the two schemes have equal expected cardinality but different cardinality variability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent inclusion gives a Poisson-binomial minibatch size whose variance is positive exactly when at least one inclusion probability lies strictly between zero and one; fixed-size sampling always has zero cardinality variance.
assumptions_latex: The inclusion indicators \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\) are mutually independent.
Each \(B_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(q_i)\), where \(q_i\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E|S|=\sum_i q_i\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(|S|)=\sum_i q_i(1-q_i)\); the latter is positive exactly when \(q_i\in(0,1)\) for some \(i\), whereas fixed-size sampling has zero cardinality variance.

children.title: Duplicate-Work Exposure
children.top_down_role: Redundant computation arising from interactions within selected minibatches.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact collision-free probability for independent with-replacement block selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be the number of distinct values among independent draws \(I_1,\ldots,I_\tau\) with \(\mathbb P(I_s=i)=p_i\). For \(\tau\le n\), \[\mathbb P(D=\tau)=\tau!e_\tau(p_1,\ldots,p_n),\] and for \(\tau>n\) this probability is zero. Under uniform sampling it equals \((n)_\tau/n^\tau\), so the probability of at least one duplicate is \(1-(n)_\tau/n^\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The probability of no repeated block is an elementary symmetric polynomial; for uniform draws it is the standard birthday-collision probability.
assumptions_latex: \(I_1,\ldots,I_\tau\) are independent draws from a distribution \(p\) on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: No-Duplicate Probability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise collision count for independent with-replacement selections; it differs from the number of redundant selections when multiplicities exceed two.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(C=\sum_{1\le r<s\le\tau}\mathbf 1_{\{I_r=I_s\}}\). Then \[\mathbb E[C]=\binom{\tau}{2}\sum_{i=1}^n p_i^2.\] Among distributions on \(n\) blocks, uniform sampling minimizes this expectation and gives \(\mathbb E[C]=\binom{\tau}{2}/n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected colliding draw pairs equal the number of draw pairs times the one-pair collision probability; uniform sampling minimizes this measure.
assumptions_latex: \(I_1,\ldots,I_\tau\) are independent and \(\mathbb P(I_s=i)=p_i\).
\(p_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_i p_i=1\).

notation.meaning: Number of unordered pairs of equal selections.

review_flags: pair-collision count is not identical to tau minus the number of distinct blocks when a block is selected three or more times
knowledge_statements.title: Expected Pair Collisions
Duplicate-Work Exposure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies repeated block selections under independent sampling with replacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_1,\ldots,I_\tau\) be independent samples from \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with \(\mathbb P(I_s=i)=p_i\), and let \(S=\{I_1,\ldots,I_\tau\}\). The number of executed selections is \(\tau\), whereas the number of distinct block updates is \(D=|S|\). Then \[\mathbb E[D]=\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl(1-(1-p_i)^\tau\bigr),\qquad \mathbb E[\tau-D]=\tau-\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl(1-(1-p_i)^\tau\bigr).\] Thus \(\mathbb E[\tau-D]\) measures duplicate-work exposure. Under uniform sampling, \(\mathbb E[D]=n(1-(1-1/n)^\tau)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For independent draws with replacement, expected duplicate work equals the batch size minus the expected number of distinct selected blocks.
assumptions_latex: Selections within the minibatch are independent and made with replacement.

notation.meaning: Number of selections in the minibatch.
Marginal probability of selecting block i on one draw.

children.title: Interaction-Aware Joint Sampling

children.title: Correlated Block Sampling
children.top_down_role: Joint block selection with dependent inclusion events.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that pairwise inclusion probabilities do not detect all dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n=3\) and draw \(S\) uniformly from \(\{\varnothing,\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{2,3\}\}\). Then \(p_i=1/2\) and \(p_{ij}=1/4=p_ip_j\) for every \(i\ne j\), but \(\mathbb P(1,2,3\in S)=0\ne1/8=p_1p_2p_3\). Thus the inclusion indicators are pairwise independent but not mutually independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform sampling of the even-cardinality subsets of three blocks is pairwise independent but has higher-order dependence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_{ij}=p_ip_j\ \forall i\ne j,\qquad (Z_1,Z_2,Z_3)\text{ are not mutually independent}.

notation.meaning: Joint inclusion probability of blocks i and j.

knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise-Independent but Dependent Block Sampling

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mutual Independence Criterion for a Random Subset
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes general subset dependence from pairwise inclusion correlation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a random subset \(S\subseteq[n]\), let \(Z_i=\mathbf1_{\{i\in S\}}\), \(p_i=\mathbb P(i\in S)\), and \(q_A=\mathbb P(S=A)\). The inclusion indicators are mutually independent if and only if \(q_A=\prod_{i\in A}p_i\prod_{i\notin A}(1-p_i)\) for every \(A\subseteq[n]\). The sampling is dependent, or correlated in the general sense, whenever this product-law identity fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subset sampling is fully independent exactly when its complete law is the product Bernoulli law; correlation may therefore be higher-order and invisible to pairwise moments.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a random subset of finite \([n]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (Z_1,\ldots,Z_n)\text{ are mutually independent}\iff q_A=\prod_{i\in A}p_i\prod_{i\notin A}(1-p_i)\ \forall A.

notation.meaning: Indicator that block i is selected.
Probability of selecting exactly subset A.

knowledge_statements.title: Mutual Independence Criterion for a Random Subset
Correlated Block Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines joint block sampling without an independence requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A correlated block sampling on \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is a random subset \(S\subseteq[n]\) whose law is specified by joint inclusion probabilities \(p_i=\mathbb P(i\in S)\) and \(p_{ij}=\mathbb P(i,j\in S)\). Its dependence matrix is \(C\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), where \(C_{ij}=p_{ij}-p_ip_j\). The sampling is correlated when \(C_{ij}\ne0\) for at least one distinct pair \(i,j\); positive and negative values respectively encode enhanced and suppressed co-selection relative to independent Bernoulli inclusion with the same marginals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correlated sampling is a random block subset whose pairwise inclusion probabilities do not all factor into products of marginal probabilities.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a random subset of the finite block index set \([n]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sampling is correlated exactly when \(p_{ij}\ne p_ip_j\) for some \(i\ne j\).

notation.meaning: Marginal inclusion probability of block i.
Joint inclusion probability of blocks i and j.

children.title: Conflict-Aware Sampling
children.top_down_role: Joint selection shaped by interaction, interference, or placement conflicts.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates pairwise conflict avoidance from static full-block support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be the declared conflicting pairs and \(S\) the sampled update set. Strict pairwise conflict avoidance together with full marginal support is expressed by \(\mathbb P(i,j\in S)=0\) for every \(\{i,j\}\in\mathcal C\) and \(p_i:=\mathbb P(i\in S)>0\) for every required block \(i\). Conflict avoidance alone does not imply marginal coverage: a law supported on conflict-free subsets of a proper vertex subset satisfies every avoidance constraint while assigning zero probability to omitted blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conflict avoidance and individual-block coverage are separate requirements; a conflict-free law can still starve blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) is the declared pairwise conflict set.
The sampling law is fixed and every indexed block is required.

notation.meaning: Marginal inclusion probability of block i.
Joint inclusion probability of blocks i and j.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Avoidance and Marginal Coverage
Conflict-Aware Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalizes sampling laws that suppress jointly incompatible block updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\subseteq\{\{i,j\}:i,j\in[n],\ i\ne j\}\) be a set of conflicting block pairs, and let \(S\subseteq[n]\) be a random update set. The sampling is strictly conflict-aware when \[\mathbb P(\{i,j\}\subseteq S)=0\quad\text{for every }\{i,j\}\in\mathcal C.\] More generally, for prescribed tolerances \(\varepsilon_{ij}\ge0\), it is tolerance-based conflict-aware when \(\mathbb P(\{i,j\}\subseteq S)\le\varepsilon_{ij}\) for all conflicting pairs. Positive marginal inclusion probabilities may still be assigned to every individual block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conflict-aware law forbids, or explicitly limits, simultaneous selection of every declared conflicting block pair.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) is fixed before the random subset is drawn.
Each conflict is represented by an unordered pair of distinct blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(\{i,j\}\subseteq S)\le\varepsilon_{ij}\) for every \(\{i,j\}\in\mathcal C\), with strict avoidance given by \(\varepsilon_{ij}=0\).

notation.meaning: Random set of blocks selected together.
Permitted co-selection probability for a conflicting pair.

children.title: Conflict Graph Sampling
children.top_down_role: Sampling structure expressed through pairwise or grouped incompatibilities.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stable-Set Polytope Characterization of Feasible Marginals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact marginal realizability under independent-set support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite conflict graph \(G=([n],E)\), a vector \(p\in[0,1]^n\) is the marginal vector of a probability law supported on independent sets if and only if \(p\in\operatorname{STAB}(G):=\operatorname{conv}\{\mathbf1_I:I\in\mathcal I(G)\}\). Equivalently, there are \(q_I\ge0\) with \(\sum_Iq_I=1\) and \(p=\sum_Iq_I\mathbf1_I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The achievable marginal vectors of conflict-graph samplings are exactly the stable-set polytope.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p\text{ is realizable by independent-set sampling}\iff p\in\operatorname{STAB}(G).

notation.meaning: Convex hull of independent-set incidence vectors.
Probability assigned to independent set I.

knowledge_statements.title: Stable-Set Polytope Characterization of Feasible Marginals
Conflict Graph Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents conflict-free minibatches as independent sets of a graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=([n],E)\) be an undirected conflict graph, where \(\{i,j\}\in E\) means that blocks \(i\) and \(j\) must not be updated together. A conflict-graph sampling is a probability law \(q\) supported on the independent sets \(\mathcal I(G)\): \[q(S)\ge0,\qquad \sum_{S\in\mathcal I(G)}q(S)=1,\qquad q(S)=0\ \text{for }S\notin\mathcal I(G).\] Consequently, every edge has zero joint inclusion probability. Conversely, any random subset that almost surely contains no edge induces such a law on \(\mathcal I(G)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conflict-graph sampling draws only independent vertex sets, so no graph edge has both endpoints selected together.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite undirected graph whose vertices index update blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\in\mathcal I(G)\) almost surely if and only if \(\mathbb P(i,j\in S)=0\) for every \(\{i,j\}\in E\).

notation.meaning: Family of independent vertex sets of G.
Probability mass function on block subsets.

children.title: Unmodeled Selection Conflicts
children.top_down_role: Interference patterns omitted from the sampling design.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marginal correction does not generally repair analyses depending on joint inclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be the modeled set and \(\widehat S\) the set executed after resolving undeclared conflicts. Reweighting with \(\widehat p_i=\mathbb P(i\in\widehat S)>0\) restores the first-moment identity \(\mathbb E[\sum_{i\in\widehat S}g_i/\widehat p_i]=\sum_i g_i\). It does not in general justify a second-moment or minibatch argument written using \(P_{ij}=\mathbb P(i,j\in S)\), because execution uses \(\widehat P_{ij}=\mathbb P(i,j\in\widehat S)\). Exact joint-moment identities transfer when \(\widehat P=P\); otherwise any required bound must be reverified for \(\widehat P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Executed-marginal weighting can restore unbiasedness, but joint-law-dependent guarantees must be checked again using the executed inclusion matrix.
assumptions_latex: The implementation may suppress updates after the modeled draw.
The claimed analysis depends on joint inclusion probabilities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat p_i\text{-reweighting restores the first moment, while joint-moment claims must use or validly bound }\widehat P.

notation.meaning: Executed joint inclusion probability after conflict resolution.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint-Law Distortion Despite Marginal Recalibration
Unmodeled Selection Conflicts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies bias or invalid updates caused by undeclared incompatibilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be sampled from a modeled law \(q\), but suppose an undeclared conflicting pair \(\{i,j\}\) satisfies \(q(\{S:\{i,j\}\subseteq S\})>0\). If the implementation discards one member whenever both are selected, then the executed set \(\widehat S\) has marginal probabilities \(\widehat p_k=\mathbb P(k\in\widehat S)\) that need not equal the modeled probabilities \(p_k=\mathbb P(k\in S)\). Hence an estimator weighted by \(1/p_k\) need not remain unbiased: generally \(\mathbb E[\mathbf1_{\{k\in\widehat S\}}g_k/p_k]=(\widehat p_k/p_k)g_k\ne g_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An undeclared conflict can alter executed inclusion probabilities, invalidating unbiasedness or convergence claims based on the intended sampling law.
assumptions_latex: At least one conflicting pair is selected with positive probability.
The implementation resolves that conflict by suppressing at least one selected update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Modeled importance weights \(1/p_k\) are invalid whenever conflict resolution yields \(\widehat p_k\ne p_k\).

notation.meaning: Block set actually executed after conflict resolution.
Modeled and executed marginal inclusion probabilities.

requires source distinguishing selected and executed sampling laws

knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrary-Sampling Frameworks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a general random-subset law encompassing serial and structured minibatch sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An arbitrary sampling of \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is a random subset \(S\subseteq[n]\), equivalently specified by probabilities \(q_A=\mathbb P(S=A)\) for every \(A\subseteq[n]\), where \(q_A\ge 0\) and \(\sum_{A\subseteq[n]}q_A=1\). Its marginal and joint inclusion probabilities are \(p_i=\mathbb P(i\in S)=\sum_{A\ni i}q_A\) and \(P_{ij}=\mathbb P(i,j\in S)=\sum_{A\supseteq\{i,j\}}q_A\). Serial, fixed-size, independent Bernoulli, and structured subset samplings are special cases obtained by restricting or factorizing the law \((q_A)_{A\subseteq[n]}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arbitrary sampling is any probability law on subsets of a finite block index set; subset probabilities determine its marginal and joint inclusion probabilities, and standard serial, minibatch, Bernoulli, and structured samplings are special cases.
assumptions_latex: The block index set \([n]\) is finite.
At least one block has positive inclusion probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Serial, fixed-size, independent Bernoulli, and structured subset samplings are instances of the same random-subset model.

notation.meaning: Probability of drawing exactly subset A.
Marginal inclusion probability of block i.
Joint inclusion probability of blocks i and j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical unbiased aggregate for an arbitrary subset sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_1,\ldots,g_n\) be vectors measurable before drawing \(S\), and suppose \(p_i=\mathbb P(i\in S)>0\) for every required index. Then \(\widehat g(S)=\sum_{i\in S}g_i/p_i\) satisfies \(\mathbb E[\widehat g(S)]=\sum_{i=1}^n g_i\), irrespective of dependence among inclusion events.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse-marginal weighting makes the sampled aggregate unbiased under arbitrary dependence, provided every required marginal is positive.
assumptions_latex: \(p_i>0\) for every required block.
Each \(g_i\) is deterministic or measurable before the subset draw.
knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Marginal Unbiased Aggregate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: First- and second-order moments induced by an arbitrary random subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z=\mathbf1_S\in\{0,1\}^n\), define \(p=\mathbb Ez\) and \(P=\mathbb E[zz^\top]\). Then \(P\succeq0\), \(P-pp^\top\succeq0\), \(P_{ii}=p_i\), \(\mathbb E|S|=\sum_i p_i\), and \(\mathbb E|S|^2=\sum_{i,j}P_{ij}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every arbitrary subset law induces a positive-semidefinite inclusion-moment matrix whose diagonal contains the marginals and whose sums give batch-size moments.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a random subset of finite \([n]\).
knowledge_statements.title: Inclusion-Moment Representation

children.title: Adaptive Importance-Sampling Policies
children.top_down_role: Nonuniform policies derived from geometry, residuals, cost, or observed progress.

children.title: Curvature-Based Importance Sampling
children.top_down_role: Probabilities calibrated to coordinate or block geometry.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact criterion-dependent characterizations of linear and square-root curvature sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(L_i>0\) and probabilities \(p_i>0\), \(\sum_i p_i=1\),
\[
\min_p\max_i\frac{L_i}{p_i}=\sum_iL_i,
\qquad
p_i^{\mathrm{mm}}=\frac{L_i}{\sum_jL_j}.
\]
For the aggregate inverse-probability criterion,
\[
\min_p\sum_i\frac{L_i}{p_i}=
\left(\sum_i\sqrt{L_i}\right)^2,
\qquad
p_i^{\mathrm{agg}}= rac{\sqrt{L_i}}{\sum_j\sqrt{L_j}}.
\]
Thus there is no universally optimal curvature exponent: linear curvature weighting minimizes worst normalized curvature, whereas square-root weighting minimizes the aggregate criterion. The policies coincide only when all \(L_i\) are equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear and square-root curvature probabilities are optimal for different convergence surrogates, so no curvature exponent is universally canonical.
assumptions_latex: \(L_i>0\) are fixed coordinate or block curvature constants.
\(p\) lies in the open probability simplex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_i\propto L_i\) uniquely solves the minimax criterion, while \(p_i\propto\sqrt{L_i}\) uniquely solves the aggregate criterion.

notation.meaning: Serial probability of selecting coordinate i.

knowledge_statements.title: Variational Characterization of Curvature Sampling
Curvature-Based Importance Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses block smoothness constants to set serial coordinate probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given differentiable \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) with blocks \(x_i\) and positive block smoothness constants \(L_i\), choose an exponent \(\alpha\ge0\) and set \[p_i=\frac{L_i^\alpha}{\sum_{j=1}^nL_j^\alpha}.\] At iteration \(k\), draw \(i_k\) from \((p_i)_{i=1}^n\), compute the block gradient \(\nabla_i f(x^k)\), and update \(x_{i_k}^{k+1}=x_{i_k}^k-L_{i_k}^{-1}\nabla_{i_k}f(x^k)\), leaving other blocks unchanged. Stop under a prescribed stationarity or iteration criterion and return the last iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample blocks with probabilities proportional to powers of their curvature constants, then take the corresponding block-gradient step.
assumptions_latex: For every block \(i\), \(\nabla_i f\) is block-Lipschitz with known constant \(L_i>0\).
The selected block gradient can be evaluated at the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sampling distribution is \(p_i=L_i^\alpha/\sum_jL_j^\alpha\), with \(\alpha=0\) giving uniform sampling and \(\alpha=1\) giving linear curvature weighting.

children.title: State-Dependent Priority Sampling
children.top_down_role: State-dependent probabilities using current optimality or improvement indicators.

children.title: Residual-Based Sampling
children.top_down_role: State-dependent probabilities derived from current coordinate residuals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Calibration boundary for residual-derived priority scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_i=w_i\lVert r_i(x)\rVert\), with \(w_i>0\). If an equivalent residual is expressed as \(\widetilde r_i=c_i r_i\), \(c_i>0\), then choosing \(\widetilde w_i=w_i/c_i\) preserves every score and hence the normalized sampling distribution. Without this compensation, rankings and probabilities can change even though the residual zero sets are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual priorities depend on block units unless their weights compensate for residual rescaling.
assumptions_latex: \(w_i>0\) and \(c_i>0\) for every block.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Priority Scaling Dependence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected Selected Residual under Proportional Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step score comparison for current residual-proportional sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_i=\lVert r_i(x)\rVert\ge0\), \(S=\sum_i a_i>0\), and \(\Pr(I=i)=a_i/S\). Then \[\mathbb E[a_I]=\frac{\sum_i a_i^2}{S}\ge\frac{S}{n},\] with equality if and only if all residual scores are equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual-proportional sampling selects an expected residual score at least as large as uniform sampling.
assumptions_latex: The residual scores are current, nonnegative, and not all zero.
Scores are fixed before the draw.
review_flags: This compares selected residual scores, not realized objective decrease.
knowledge_statements.title: Expected Selected Residual under Proportional Sampling
Residual-Based Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Samples blocks according to current fixed-point or optimality residual magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_i(x^k)\) be a computable residual for block \(i\), let \(w_i>0\), and choose an exploration floor \(\epsilon>0\). At iteration \(k\), form \(a_i^k=w_i\lVert r_i(x^k)\rVert+\epsilon\) and \[p_i^k=\frac{a_i^k}{\sum_{j=1}^na_j^k}.\] Draw \(i_k\sim p^k\), apply the prescribed coordinate or block update to \(i_k\), and leave other blocks unchanged. Recompute affected residual scores before the next draw. Stop when a global residual tolerance or iteration limit is reached, and return the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute block residual scores, normalize them into positive probabilities, and preferentially update blocks with larger current residuals.
assumptions_latex: Each \(r_i(x)\) is computable and vanishes when block i satisfies its target condition.
The exploration floor \(\epsilon\) is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every block has \(p_i^k>0\), while larger weighted residuals receive larger selection probabilities.

residual definition and refresh convention are method-dependent

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the procedural record, but no source supports this particular residual score, additive exploration floor, normalization, or refresh rule. These choices are method-dependent rather than a canonical definition of residual-based sampling.

children.title: Progress-Based Sampling
children.top_down_role: State-dependent probabilities derived from observed or predicted improvement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected Selected Score under Proportional Progress Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step comparison for sampling proportional to nonnegative predicted-progress scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Delta_i\ge0\), \(S=\sum_{i=1}^n\Delta_i>0\), and \(\Pr(I=i)=\Delta_i/S\). Then \[\mathbb E[\Delta_I]=\frac{\sum_i\Delta_i^2}{S}\ge\frac{S}{n}.\] Equality holds if and only if all \(\Delta_i\) are equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Progress-proportional sampling selects an expected score at least as large as uniform sampling, with equality exactly for equal scores.
assumptions_latex: \(\Delta_i\ge0\) for every block.
\(\sum_i\Delta_i>0\).
Scores are fixed before the draw.
knowledge_statements.title: Expected Selected Score under Proportional Progress Sampling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent parameterizations of positive exploration in progress-priority sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Delta_i\ge0\), \(S=\sum_i\Delta_i>0\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1]\), define \[p_i=(1-\alpha)\frac{\Delta_i}{S}+\frac{\alpha}{n}.\] Then \(p_i\ge\alpha/n\). Moreover, \(p_i=(\Delta_i+\epsilon)/(S+n\epsilon)\) is the same distribution when \(\alpha=n\epsilon/(S+n\epsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding a common positive score floor is equivalent to mixing proportional-progress sampling with uniform exploration.
assumptions_latex: \(\Delta_i\ge0\), \(S>0\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1]\).
For the additive-floor form, \(\epsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_i\ge\alpha/n\), and the two parameterizations coincide for \(\alpha=n\epsilon/(S+n\epsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform-Exploration Mixture and Additive-Floor Equivalence
Progress-Based Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses predicted per-block objective decrease as the sampling priority.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each block \(i\) at iterate \(x^k\), let \(\Delta_i^k\ge0\) be a computable prediction of objective decrease from its candidate update. Given \(\epsilon>0\), define \[p_i^k=\frac{\Delta_i^k+\epsilon}{\sum_{j=1}^n(\Delta_j^k+\epsilon)}.\] Draw \(i_k\sim p^k\), execute the candidate update for block \(i_k\), and update all progress estimates affected by the new iterate. Continue until a prescribed stationarity, objective-gap, or iteration criterion is met; output the final iterate. The floor prevents permanent exclusion when a predicted decrease is zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimate each block's prospective decrease and sample in proportion to that estimate plus a positive exploration floor.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\Delta_i^k\) is nonnegative and available before sampling.
The exploration floor \(\epsilon\) is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Blocks with greater predicted progress receive greater probability, and \(p_i^k>0\) for every block.

notation.meaning: Predicted decrease from updating block i at iteration k.

review_flags: no supplied locator supports the stated progress-priority rule

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the procedural record, but no source supports the stated predicted-decrease normalization or exploration mechanism. The meaning and validity of the progress surrogate depend on the underlying block method.

children.title: Stale Priority Indicators
children.top_down_role: Sampling distortion caused by outdated residual or progress information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguard against permanent exclusion caused by stale scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For arbitrary delayed nonnegative scores \(b_i^k\), define \[p_i^k=(1-\alpha)\frac{b_i^k}{\sum_j b_j^k}+\frac{\alpha}{n},\qquad \alpha\in(0,1],\] when the score sum is positive, and use the uniform distribution otherwise. Then \(p_i^k\ge\alpha/n\) for all \(i,k\). On an infinite run whose draws follow these conditional probabilities, every block is selected infinitely often almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform exploration prevents stale priorities from permanently excluding a block and ensures infinite visitation on an infinite run.
assumptions_latex: Each draw follows the declared conditional probability vector.
The visitation conclusion concerns an infinite sequence of draws.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_i^k\ge\alpha/n\) for every \(i,k\), and each block is sampled infinitely often almost surely.

notation.meaning: Delayed priority score used at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Exploration Prevents Priority Starvation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Probability Distortion from Relative Score Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative distortion bound for normalized stale priorities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_i>0\), \((1-\rho)a_i\le b_i\le(1+\rho)a_i\) for \(0\le\rho<1\), and define \(q_i=a_i/\sum_j a_j\) and \(p_i=b_i/\sum_j b_j\). Then \[\frac{1-\rho}{1+\rho}q_i\le p_i\le\frac{1+\rho}{1-\rho}q_i\quad\text{for every }i.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform relative error in stale scores yields an explicit multiplicative distortion bound for the normalized probabilities.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i>0\) for every block.
\((1-\rho)a_i\le b_i\le(1+\rho)a_i\).
knowledge_statements.title: Probability Distortion from Relative Score Error
Stale Priority Indicators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows how delayed scores can suppress currently important blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose block probabilities at iteration \(k\) are formed from delayed scores \(a_i^{k-d_i^k}\ge0\) by \(p_i^k=a_i^{k-d_i^k}/\sum_j a_j^{k-d_j^k}\), with no positive exploration floor. If some block \(i\) has stale score \(a_i^{k-d_i^k}=0\) while its current score satisfies \(a_i^k>0\), then \(p_i^k=0\) despite current priority. If this condition persists, block \(i\) is never selected, so convergence arguments requiring infinitely frequent block selection or a uniform lower bound \(p_i^k\ge p_{\min}>0\) do not apply.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without exploration, a stale zero score can permanently exclude a block whose current residual or predicted progress is positive.
assumptions_latex: Probabilities are obtained by normalizing delayed nonnegative priority scores.
No exploration floor or forced refresh guarantees positive sampling probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistent stale zero scores can violate both \(p_i^k\ge p_{\min}>0\) and infinite-selection requirements.

notation.meaning: Current priority score for block i.
Age of the score used at iteration k.
Required uniform positive probability lower bound.

children.title: Cost-Aware Sampling
children.top_down_role: Probabilities balancing predicted progress against heterogeneous update cost.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact cost-aware probability optimizer for a cost-times-inverse-probability surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(a_i>0\) be coordinate contribution weights and \(c_i>0\) their update costs. For probabilities \(p_i>0\), \(\sum_i p_i=1\), define
\[
\Phi(p)=\left(\sum_i p_ic_i\right)\left(\sum_i\frac{a_i}{p_i}\right).
\]
Then
\[
\Phi(p)\ge\left(\sum_i\sqrt{a_ic_i}\right)^2,
\]
with equality exactly when
\[
p_i=\frac{\sqrt{a_i/c_i}}{\sum_j\sqrt{a_j/c_j}}.
\]
Thus the cost-optimal law depends on the analyzed surrogate; probabilities proportional linearly to \(a_i/c_i\) are not generally optimal for this product objective. If some \(a_i=0\) but persistent exploration is required, the optimum is replaced by the corresponding constrained or floored problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For expected cost times an inverse-probability quality bound, the optimal sampling probability is proportional to the square root of contribution divided by cost.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i>0\) for every coordinate.
\(c_i>0\) for every coordinate.
\(p\) lies in the open probability simplex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unique optimizer is \(p_i\propto\sqrt{a_i/c_i}\), and the minimum equals \((\sum_i\sqrt{a_ic_i})^2\).

notation.meaning: Coordinate contribution to the inverse-probability quality bound.
Cost of selecting and updating coordinate i.

knowledge_statements.title: Cost-Weighted Sampling Variational Characterization
Cost-Aware Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Balances predicted block progress against heterogeneous evaluation or update costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), assign each block a nonnegative predicted gain \(g_i^k\), a positive execution cost \(c_i^k\), and an exploration parameter \(\epsilon>0\). Form the efficiency score \(e_i^k=g_i^k/c_i^k\) and probability \[p_i^k=\frac{e_i^k+\epsilon}{\sum_{j=1}^n(e_j^k+\epsilon)}.\] Draw \(i_k\sim p^k\), execute its block update, record the realized cost and gain, and refresh affected estimates. Stop under the optimization budget or stationarity rule and return the current iterate. Thus selection favors predicted progress per unit cost while retaining positive exploration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample blocks according to predicted improvement per unit update cost, with an exploration floor ensuring every block remains selectable.
assumptions_latex: Predicted gains satisfy \(g_i^k\ge0\).
Estimated update costs satisfy \(c_i^k>0\).
The exploration parameter satisfies \(\epsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule assigns higher probability to greater predicted gain-to-cost ratios and guarantees \(p_i^k>0\).

notation.meaning: Predicted gain from updating block i.
Predicted cost of updating block i.

review_flags: no supplied locator supports this particular cost-aware normalization
alternative cost-optimal probability formulas exist under different convergence models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the explicit procedure, but no source supports sampling linearly by predicted gain divided by cost with an additive floor. Cost-optimal probabilities depend on the convergence objective and cost model, so this formula cannot be treated as canonical without evidence.

children.title: Adaptive Sampling Refresh
children.top_down_role: Policies for revising sampling information during optimization.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact incremental alternative to recomputing every adaptive score.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Maintain current scores \(a_i^k\ge0\) and \(A^k=\sum_i a_i^k\). After an update, let \(D_k\) contain every score whose value may have changed. Recompute \(a_j^{k+1}\) for \(j\in D_k\), retain the remaining scores, and set
\[
A^{k+1}=A^k+\sum_{j\in D_k}(a_j^{k+1}-a_j^k).
\]
Normalization from these maintained values gives exactly the same score distribution as a full refresh. If \(D_k\) omits a changed score, exactness is lost and the resulting distribution is stale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recomputing exactly the scores invalidated by an update and adjusting their normalizer reproduces a full refresh; an incomplete dependency set creates staleness.
assumptions_latex: The score dependency set contains every score changed by the last update.
Invalidated scores are recomputed exactly before the next draw.
A fallback is used when the maintained total score vanishes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incrementally maintained score vector and normalizer equal those obtained by full recomputation.

notation.meaning: Set of scores invalidated by the last update.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Incremental Sampling Refresh

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General scheduled or history-triggered recomputation of adaptive scores with an explicit fallback and exploration mixture.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Before the draw at iteration \(k\), let the history determine whether a refresh occurs. On refresh, compute nonnegative scores \(a_i^k\). If \(A^k=\sum_j a_j^k>0\), define \(q_i^k=a_i^k/A^k\); otherwise use a prescribed fallback distribution \(q^k\). For an exploration parameter \(\eta\in(0,1]\), set
\[
p_i^k=(1-\eta)q_i^k+\frac{\eta}{n}.
\]
Between refreshes retain the previous probability vector. Draw the next coordinate conditionally from \(p^k\). Then \(p^k\) is history-measurable, sums to one, and satisfies \(p_i^k\ge\eta/n\). The score definition belongs to the curvature-, priority-, or cost-based policy leaf that supplies it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At predictable refresh times, normalize current scores, use a declared fallback if they vanish, and mix with uniform exploration; otherwise reuse the previous probabilities.
assumptions_latex: The refresh decision and scores are measurable before the current draw.
Scores are nonnegative.
The all-zero fallback is a probability vector and \(\eta\in(0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every refreshed or retained distribution is valid and satisfies \(p_i^k\ge\eta/n\).

notation.meaning: Adaptive score available at a refresh.

knowledge_statements.title: Predictable Full Sampling Refresh

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure coordinate coverage ensured by the refresh policy's uniform probability floor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal F_k\) be the history before the draw and suppose
\[
\mathbb P(i_k=i\mid\mathcal F_k)=p_i^k\ge\delta>0
\]
almost surely for every coordinate and iteration. Then each coordinate is selected infinitely often almost surely. If a refresh policy can instead assign one coordinate probability zero forever, this coverage conclusion can fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A history-measurable adaptive policy with a uniform positive probability floor selects every coordinate infinitely often almost surely.
assumptions_latex: \(p^k\) is measurable with respect to the pre-draw history.
There is a uniform constant \(\delta>0\) with \(p_i^k\ge\delta\) almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every coordinate is sampled infinitely often almost surely.

notation.meaning: Information available before iteration k's draw.

knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Exploration Under Adaptive Refresh
Adaptive Sampling Refresh
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Periodically recomputes state-dependent block probabilities while preserving exploration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an initial probability vector \(p^0\), a refresh set \(\mathcal R\subseteq\mathbb N\), and a floor \(p_{\min}\in(0,1/n]\). At iteration \(k\), if \(k\in\mathcal R\), compute nonnegative block scores \(a_i^k\) and set \[p_i^k=p_{\min}+(1-np_{\min})\frac{a_i^k}{\sum_j a_j^k},\] using \(p_i^k=1/n\) when all scores vanish; otherwise set \(p^k=p^{k-1}\). Draw a block from \(p^k\), update it, and stop under the prescribed optimization criterion. The floor guarantees persistent exploration between refreshes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At scheduled iterations, recompute probabilities from current scores; between refreshes, reuse them while maintaining a positive probability floor.
assumptions_latex: The refresh set and score rule are specified before each draw.
Scores are nonnegative and the probability floor satisfies \(0<p_{\min}\le1/n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every iteration and block, \(p_i^k\ge p_{\min}\) and \(\sum_i p_i^k=1\).

notation.meaning: Iterations at which sampling scores are refreshed.
Current priority score for block i.

children.top_down_role: Classical greedy rankings based on gradient or composite residual information.

children.title: Gradient-Magnitude Rules
children.top_down_role: Greedy rankings based on partial-gradient magnitude.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Rate under Block-One Strong Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rate for exact Euclidean block gradient-magnitude selection with a common curvature majorant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume Euclidean blocks, coordinate quadratic upper bounds with \(L_i\le L\), and \(\mu_1\)-strong convexity with respect to \(\lVert d\rVert_{1,\mathrm{blk}}=\sum_i\lVert d_i\rVert_2\). At iteration \(k\), choose \(i_k\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_i\lVert\nabla_i f(x^k)\rVert_2\) and set \(x^{k+1}=x^k-U_{i_k}\nabla_{i_k}f(x^k)/L\). Then \[f(x^{k+1})-f^*\le\left(1-\frac{\mu_1}{L}\right)(f(x^k)-f^*),\] and \(k\ge(L/\mu_1)\log((f(x^0)-f^*)/\varepsilon)\) suffices for gap at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under common coordinate smoothness and block-one strong convexity, exact gradient-magnitude Gauss–Southwell descent converges linearly.
assumptions_latex: The blocks are Euclidean.
\(f\) is \(\mu_1\)-strongly convex in \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_{1,\mathrm{blk}}\).
Every coordinate quadratic upper-bound constant satisfies \(L_i\le L\).
Selection is exact and the stated reciprocal-\(L\) update is applied.

notation.meaning: Strong-convexity modulus in the block-one norm.

review_flags: The rate applies to the stated coordinate-descent update, not to the selection rule in isolation.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Rate under Block-One Strong Convexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm representation of exact gradient-magnitude selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a fixed block partition, define \(\lVert gVert_{\infty,\mathrm{blk}}=\max_i\lVert U_i^{\mathsf T}gVert_{i,*}\). A gradient-magnitude Gauss–Southwell choice \(i(x)\) satisfies \[\lVert U_{i(x)}^{\mathsf T}
abla f(x)Vert_{i(x),*}=\lVert
abla f(x)Vert_{\infty,\mathrm{blk}}.\] For scalar Euclidean coordinates this is \(\lVert
abla f(x)Vert_\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient-magnitude selection chooses a block attaining the block-infinity norm of the gradient.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gauss–Southwell selection for differentiable block-coordinate optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, and let \(U_i\) embed block \(i\) into \(\mathbb{R}^n\). At iterate \(x\), assign each eligible block the score \(s_i(x)=\|U_i^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x)\|_{i,*}\), where \(\|\cdot\|_{i,*}\) is the dual norm on block \(i\). For scalar Euclidean coordinates, this reduces to selecting a coordinate having maximal \(|\nabla_i f(x)|\).

children.title: Maximum-Improvement Selection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Meaning of vanishing exact one-block improvements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be finite at \(x\in X=\prod_iX_i\), and define \[\Delta_i(x)=F(x)-\inf_{z_i\in X_i}F(x_1,\ldots,z_i,\ldots,x_m).\] Then \(\Delta_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\) if and only if \(x\) is a coordinatewise minimum. If additionally \(F+\iota_X\) is proper convex and the blockwise optimality conditions validly assemble into \(0\in\partial(F+\iota_X)(x)\), then \(x\) is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero exact improvement in every block characterizes coordinatewise minimality and, with an assembling convex optimality condition, certifies global optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(F(x)\) is finite and each block infimum is well-defined.
For global optimality, \(F+\iota_X\) is proper convex and the block conditions assemble into its full subdifferential condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_i(x)=0\ \forall i\iff x\) is coordinatewise minimal, with global optimality under the additional convex condition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Predicted Ranking Need Not Maximize Actual Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between predicted and evaluated maximum-improvement selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat\Delta_i\ge0\) be predicted improvements and \(\Delta_i\ge0\) the corresponding actual improvements. Maximizing \(\widehat\Delta_i\) need not maximize \(\Delta_i\). If, however, \(0<c\le C<\infty\) and \(c\Delta_i\le\widehat\Delta_i\le C\Delta_i\) for every eligible block, then any \(i^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_i\widehat\Delta_i\) satisfies \[\Delta_{i^*}\ge\frac{c}{C}\max_j\Delta_j.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Predicted and actual improvement rankings may differ; two-sided model accuracy transfers a quantitative approximation factor.
assumptions_latex: For the quantitative conclusion, \(0<c\le C<\infty\).
\(c\Delta_i\le\widehat\Delta_i\le C\Delta_i\) for every eligible block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_{i^*}\ge(c/C)\max_j\Delta_j\) under two-sided accuracy, while nonnegativity alone gives no ordering guarantee.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison with uniform selection over the same eligible blocks.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact maximum-improvement selection achieves at least the average improvement of a uniformly chosen eligible block.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal E(x)\) is finite and nonempty.
All improvements are measured on the same objective or model scale.

children.title: Approximate Greedy Selection
children.top_down_role: Greedy choice based on inexact candidate scores or partial searches.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A posteriori certification without exact exhaustive score evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\ell_i\le s_i(x)\le u_i\) for every eligible block. A chosen block \(\widehat i\) is certified multiplicatively \(\eta\)-greedy if \[\ell_{\widehat i}\ge\eta\max_j u_j,\qquad \eta\in(0,1],\] and is certified additive-\(\delta\) greedy if \(\ell_{\widehat i}\ge\max_j u_j-\delta\), where \(\delta\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified lower and upper score bounds can verify approximate greediness without evaluating every exact score.
assumptions_latex: \(\ell_i\le s_i(x)\le u_i\) for every eligible block.
\(\eta\in(0,1]\) and \(\delta\ge0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Additive Accuracy Is Not Scale Invariant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale boundary separating additive and multiplicative approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(\widetilde s_i=c s_i\), \(c>0\), the multiplicative condition \(s_{\widehat i}\ge\eta\max_j s_j\) is unchanged. The additive condition \(s_{\widehat i}\ge\max_j s_j-\delta\) is preserved only when \(\widetilde\delta=c\delta\). With fixed \(\delta\), the additive condition is satisfied by every block whenever \(\max_j s_j\le\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplicative accuracy is invariant to score units, whereas additive accuracy requires a scaled tolerance and can become vacuous near zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Additive scale covariance requires \(\widetilde\delta=c\delta\); fixed \(\delta\) is vacuous when \(\max_j s_j\le\delta\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-independent transfer into a score-proportional progress bound.

assumptions_latex: \(s_i(x)\ge0\) for every eligible block.
\(\Phi(x)-\Phi(T_i x)\ge c s_i(x)\) with the same \(c>0\) for every candidate.

Approximate Greedy Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative approximation condition for a greedy block choice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_i(x)\ge 0\) be the exact greedy score of eligible block \(i\) at iterate \(x\), and fix \(\eta\in(0,1]\). A selected block \(\widehat i\in\mathcal E(x)\) satisfies the multiplicative approximate-greedy condition when \(s_{\widehat i}(x)\ge\eta\max_{j\in\mathcal E(x)}s_j(x)\). The case \(\eta=1\) is exact greedy selection. An additive version with tolerance \(\delta\ge0\) instead requires \(s_{\widehat i}(x)\ge\max_{j\in\mathcal E(x)}s_j(x)-\delta\). The multiplicative condition is informative only when the scores are nonnegative and share a common scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A choice is multiplicatively approximate greedy if its score is at least a fixed fraction of the largest eligible score.

\(s_i(x)\ge0\) for every \(i\in\mathcal E(x)\).

Screened Greedy Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy ranking restricted to a screened candidate subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an iterate \(x\), first construct a nonempty candidate set \(S(x)\subseteq\mathcal E(x)\) using a screening predicate that is cheaper than evaluating every exact score. Compute \(s_i(x)\) for each \(i\in S(x)\), choose \(i^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{i\in S(x)}s_i(x)\), and output block \(i^*\). If the screen guarantees \(\max_{i\in S(x)}s_i(x)\ge\eta\max_{j\in\mathcal E(x)}s_j(x)\), then the output is \(\eta\)-approximately greedy over the full eligible set. Without that guarantee, the algorithm is greedy only relative to \(S(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Screen blocks to a candidate subset, evaluate exact scores within it, and select its maximizer; a coverage guarantee transfers approximation quality to the full set.
assumptions_latex: \(S(x)\) is a nonempty subset of the finite eligible set \(\mathcal E(x)\).

children.title: Screening–Ranking Tradeoffs

knowledge_statements.title: Screening–Ranking Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Progress-versus-cost criterion for screened greedy policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose evaluating a full greedy ranking costs \(C_{\mathrm{full}}(x)\), while screening to \(S(x)\) and ranking its members costs \(C_{\mathrm{scr}}(x)+C_{\mathrm{rank}}(S(x))\). If a block with score \(s\) guarantees progress at least \(c s\), and the screen has coverage factor \(\eta\), then screened selection guarantees progress at least \(c\eta s_{\max}(x)\), where \(s_{\max}(x)=\max_{i\in\mathcal E(x)}s_i(x)\). Thus its guaranteed progress per unit selection cost is at least \(c\eta s_{\max}(x)/(C_{\mathrm{scr}}(x)+C_{\mathrm{rank}}(S(x)))\); screening is preferable by this criterion only when this ratio exceeds the corresponding full-ranking ratio.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Screening trades a reduced selection cost against a weaker greedy factor; compare policies by guaranteed objective progress per unit selection cost.
assumptions_latex: Selecting a block of score \(s\) guarantees progress at least \(c s\) for some \(c>0\).
The screen satisfies a full-set coverage factor \(\eta\in(0,1]\).

children.title: Unsafe Candidate Screening

knowledge_statements.title: Unsafe Candidate Screening
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent exclusion of an improving block can destroy convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f(x_1,x_2)=\tfrac12(x_1-1)^2+\tfrac12x_2^2\) with initial point \(x^0=(0,0)\). Its unique minimizer is \(x^*=(1,0)\), and block \(1\) has score \(|\nabla_1 f(x^0)|=1\). If an unsafe screen returns \(S(x^k)=\{2\}\) at every iteration, any method updating only screened coordinates keeps \(x_1^k=0\). Exact minimization of block \(2\) also leaves \(x_2^k=0\), so \(x^k=x^0\) and \(f(x^k)-f(x^*)=1/2\) for all \(k\). Thus screening without eventual inclusion or a valid coverage guarantee can prevent convergence even for a strongly convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A screen that permanently removes an improving coordinate can make a block method stagnate away from the unique minimizer, even on a strongly convex quadratic.
assumptions_latex: Only coordinates in the screened set \(S(x^k)\) may be updated.
The screen persistently returns \(S(x^k)=\{2\}\).

children.title: Sampling-Distribution Maintenance
children.top_down_role: Storage and refresh mechanisms for nonuniform probabilities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-time exact sampling for a nonuniform distribution whose probabilities remain fixed between rebuilds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed probabilities \(p_1,\ldots,p_m\) with \(p_i\ge0\) and \(\sum_i p_i=1\), an alias table can be built in \(O(m)\) time and stored in \(O(m)\) space. Each subsequent exact categorical draw uses one uniform table-index draw, one uniform threshold draw, and \(O(1)\) table accesses. For the standard static alias representation, reflecting arbitrary probability changes by rebuilding the table costs \(O(m)\); hence it favors many samples per rebuild rather than frequent adaptive refreshes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A static alias table gives O(1) exact samples after O(m) preprocessing, while rebuilding it after arbitrary distribution changes costs O(m).
assumptions_latex: The probabilities are nonnegative and normalized.
The table remains unchanged between rebuilds.
Constant-time uniform random variates and table access are available.

notation.meaning: fixed categorical probability of block i

knowledge_statements.title: Static Alias-Table Sampling
Sampling-Distribution Maintenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic storage, sampling, and refresh of nonuniform block probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given nonnegative block weights \(w_1,\ldots,w_m\) with \(W=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i>0\), store their partial sums in a balanced cumulative-sum tree. To sample, draw \(u\) uniformly from \([0,W)\) and return the least index \(i\) whose cumulative weight exceeds \(u\); then \(\mathbb P(i=j)=w_j/W\). When a weight changes from \(w_j\) to \(w_j'\), add \(w_j'-w_j\) to the affected tree nodes and update \(W\). A Fenwick or segment-tree implementation uses \(O(m)\) storage, \(O(\log m)\) time per weight update, and \(O(\log m)\) time per sample.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain nonuniform sampling weights in a cumulative-sum tree, enabling logarithmic-time updates and exact logarithmic-time sampling with linear storage.
assumptions_latex: \(w_i\ge0\) for all blocks and \(W>0\).
Uniform random numbers on \([0,W)\) are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(i=j)=w_j/W\), with \(O(m)\) storage and \(O(\log m)\) update and sampling time.

notation.meaning: Current nonnegative sampling weight of block i.
Sum of all current block weights.

children.title: Greedy Candidate Search
