knowledge_statements.title: Greedy Candidate Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison cost of exact search over an explicit candidate set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) contain \(q\ge1\) candidate blocks, and suppose each exact score \(s_i\) is available in \(O(1)\) time. A sequential scan that retains the largest score seen returns an index in \(\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{i\in S}s_i\) after exactly \(q-1\) score comparisons, using \(O(1)\) auxiliary storage. Moreover, in the comparison model with arbitrary unordered scores, every deterministic algorithm that always identifies a maximum requires at least \(q-1\) comparisons in the worst case. If computing score \(i\) costs \(c_i\), the scan additionally incurs \(\sum_{i\in S}c_i\) score-evaluation work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact search among q explicit candidates needs q−1 comparisons in the worst case, plus the cost of evaluating their scores.
assumptions_latex: Candidate scores are arbitrary and accessed only through evaluation and comparison.
The candidate set has finite cardinality \(q\ge1\).

notation.meaning: Cost of evaluating candidate i's score.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound content kind is appropriate and the comparison count is standard, but the upper and lower bounds lack a cited comparison-model source.

children.title: Priority Maintenance
children.top_down_role: Data structures used to retain or refresh coordinate rankings.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse score-dependency structure determining which exact priorities require updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a directed dependency graph contain an edge \(j\to i\) whenever updating block \(j\) can change score \(s_i\). After updating block \(j\), refreshing \(A(j)=\{i:j\to i\}\cup\{j\}\) preserves exact keys for every block. If \(|A(j)|\le d+1\), a binary heap incurs \(O((d+1)\log m)\) key-maintenance work, excluding score computation; for dense dependence, \(d=m-1\) and the bound becomes \(O(m\log m)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complete score-dependency graph localizes exact priority refreshes to affected neighbors; sparse dependence makes maintenance cheap, while dense dependence can require every key.
assumptions_latex: The dependency graph contains every possible score dependence.
All keys are exact immediately before the block update.

knowledge_statements.title: Dependency-Localized Priority Refresh
Priority Maintenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact greedy priorities maintained in a dynamic max-priority queue.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain one key \(p_i=s_i(x)\) for every eligible block in a max-priority queue. After a block update changes the iterate from \(x\) to \(x^+\), identify a set \(A\) containing every block whose score may have changed, recompute \(s_i(x^+)\) for \(i\in A\), and replace their keys. Leave all other keys unchanged only when their scores are invariant under the update. Return a block at the maximum key, stopping when that key satisfies the method's termination threshold. With a binary heap, initialization costs \(O(m)\), maximum lookup costs \(O(1)\), and refreshing \(|A|\) arbitrary keys costs \(O(|A|\log m)\), excluding score computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store exact block scores in a max-priority queue and refresh every score affected by an update; heap maintenance then costs logarithmic time per changed key.
assumptions_latex: The affected set \(A\) contains every block whose exact score changes.
The priority queue contains one current key for each eligible block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned block maximizes the current exact score, and heap refresh costs \(O(|A|\log m)\).

notation.meaning: Set of blocks whose scores may change after an update.

children.title: Lazy Priority Refresh
children.top_down_role: Deferred score maintenance intended to reduce selection overhead.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection cost expressed through the number of distinct priorities refreshed at a fixed state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: During one lazy selection at a fixed state \(x\), mark each exact score after it is refreshed so that it is not recomputed while \(x\) remains fixed. If the certification loop refreshes \(r\) distinct scores and each evaluation costs at most \(c_s\), then a binary max-heap implementation uses \(O(r(c_s+\log m))\) work and \(O(m)\) priority storage. Since \(1\le r\le m\), the worst case refreshes every score and has no better score-evaluation order than a full scan; the advantage occurs when \(r\ll m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With refreshed scores cached during a fixed-state selection, refreshing r distinct priorities costs O(r(c_s+log m)); the worst case refreshes all m scores.
assumptions_latex: The iterate remains fixed throughout the certification loop.
Every unrefreshed key remains a valid upper bound.
A refreshed exact score is cached and not recomputed during the same selection.
One exact score evaluation costs at most \(c_s\).

knowledge_statements.title: Output-Sensitive Lazy-Refresh Cost
Lazy Priority Refresh
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deferred score recomputation using certified upper-bound priorities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each eligible block maintain a key \(u_i\) satisfying \(u_i\ge s_i(x)\). Repeatedly remove a block \(i\) with maximal key, compute its current exact score \(s_i(x)\), and set \(u_i\leftarrow s_i(x)\). If the refreshed value is at least the largest remaining key, output \(i\); otherwise reinsert it and continue. Stop according to the method's threshold after a certified maximal block is found. Because every unrefreshed score is bounded by its key, termination of the inner loop certifies \(s_i(x)\ge s_j(x)\) for every eligible \(j\). With a binary heap, each pop or reinsertion costs \(O(\log m)\), excluding score evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refresh only the largest upper-bound priority; accept it once its exact score dominates every remaining bound, thereby certifying an exact greedy choice.
assumptions_latex: Every maintained key remains a valid upper bound \(u_i\ge s_i(x)\).
The eligible set is finite and the heap operations are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Upon acceptance, \(i\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_j s_j(x)\); each heap pop or reinsertion costs \(O(\log m)\).

notation.meaning: Maintained upper bound on the current score of block i.
Current exact greedy score of block i.

children.title: Priority-Staleness Failure
children.top_down_role: Selection degradation caused by rankings that no longer reflect the current state.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp additive selection guarantee when every cached priority has bounded error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let current scores be \(p_i\), cached scores be \(\widehat p_i\), and suppose \(|\widehat p_i-p_i|\le\varepsilon\) for every eligible block. If \(\widehat i\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_i\widehat p_i\), then \[p_{\widehat i}\ge \max_i p_i-2\varepsilon.\] The factor \(2\) is sharp without further assumptions. If no uniform error bound is available, cached-score maximization supplies no nontrivial additive greedy certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform priority error ε makes a stale maximizer 2ε-approximately greedy; without an error bound, no nontrivial additive guarantee follows.
assumptions_latex: The eligible set is finite and nonempty.
\(|\widehat p_i-p_i|\le\varepsilon\) for every eligible block \(i\).
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate-Greedy Certificate Under Bounded Staleness
Priority-Staleness Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of greedy coordinate selection when stored priorities are not refreshed after coupled updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx\), where \(Q=\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\ \rho&1\end{pmatrix}\) and \(0<\rho<1\). Define the current greedy priority by \(p_i(x)=|\nabla_i f(x)|\). If a coordinate update changes \(x_1\) while the stored priority \(\widehat p_2\) is not refreshed, then \(p_2(x)=|\rho x_1+x_2|\) may differ arbitrarily from \(\widehat p_2\) relative to competing priorities. Consequently, selection by \(\arg\max_i\widehat p_i\) need not select a coordinate maximizing the current priority and provides no current greedy-progress guarantee without an error bound or refresh rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-coordinate coupling can invalidate cached priorities after an update, so a stale priority queue may choose a non-greedy coordinate and lose greedy progress guarantees.
assumptions_latex: \(p_i(x)=|\nabla_i f(x)|\)
\(\widehat p_2\) is retained across an update of \(x_1\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\arg\max_i\widehat p_i\) need not belong to \(\arg\max_i p_i(x)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure phenomenon and content kind fit the leaf, but the concrete quadratic family and claimed loss of a greedy-progress guarantee have no cited source.

children.title: Progress-per-Unit-Cost Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Policy comparisons incorporating both update progress and selection work.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-aware policy comparison when policies require different update counts to reach the same accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For policy \(\pi\), let \(N_\pi(\varepsilon)\) be the first update count attaining a common target criterion \(R(x)\le\varepsilon\), and let \(C_\pi(\varepsilon)=\sum_{t=0}^{N_\pi(\varepsilon)-1}(c^{\pi}_{\mathrm{sel},t}+c^{\pi}_{\mathrm{upd},t})\). Policy \(\pi_1\) is cheaper to the target exactly when \(C_{\pi_1}(\varepsilon)<C_{\pi_2}(\varepsilon)\). Under constant per-update costs \(\bar c_1,\bar c_2>0\), this is equivalent to \[\frac{N_{\pi_1}(\varepsilon)}{N_{\pi_2}(\varepsilon)}<\frac{\bar c_2}{\bar c_1}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A policy wins at a target accuracy only when its reduction in required updates outweighs its selection-plus-update cost ratio.
assumptions_latex: Both policies use the same instance, initialization, target criterion, and cost unit.
Each policy reaches \(R(x)\le\varepsilon\) in finitely many updates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_{\pi_1}(\varepsilon)<C_{\pi_2}(\varepsilon),\quad\text{or, for constant costs,}\quad N_1/N_2<\bar c_2/\bar c_1.

notation.meaning: updates required by policy π to attain target ε
total modeled work to attain target ε

knowledge_statements.title: Target-Accuracy Work Crossover
Progress-per-Unit-Cost Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-aware comparison of coordinate-selection policies over a common iteration horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a coordinate policy \(\pi\), let \(F_0-F_T^{\pi}\ge 0\) be its objective decrease over \(T\) updates, let \(c_{\mathrm{sel},t}^{\pi}\ge0\) be selection cost, and let \(c_{\mathrm{upd},t}^{\pi}>0\) be update cost. Its realized progress per unit cost is \[\eta_T(\pi)=\frac{F_0-F_T^{\pi}}{\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}(c_{\mathrm{sel},t}^{\pi}+c_{\mathrm{upd},t}^{\pi})}.\] Thus a policy with larger per-update decrease is preferable on a cost basis only when its additional selection and maintenance work does not reverse the ordering of \(\eta_T\). Comparisons must use the same objective, initialization, stopping horizon, and cost model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare policies by total objective decrease divided by total selection-plus-update work, rather than by decrease per iteration alone.
assumptions_latex: \(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}(c_{\mathrm{sel},t}^{\pi}+c_{\mathrm{upd},t}^{\pi})>0\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_1\) is more cost-efficient than \(\pi_2\) over the horizon precisely when \(\eta_T(\pi_1)>\eta_T(\pi_2)\).

notation.meaning: realized objective progress per unit computational cost
selection and policy-maintenance cost at update t
selected-coordinate update cost at update t

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Limit-Point Stationarity of Cyclic Block Coordinate Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit-point stationarity for cyclic exact block minimization on a Cartesian product of closed convex sets, under continuous differentiability and unique attainment of every one-block minimum. The result does not assert that a limit point exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m, where each X_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i} is closed and convex, and suppose f is continuously differentiable on X. Assume that for every x\in X and every i\in\{1,\ldots,m\},
\[
\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\xi\in X_i}f(x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1},\xi,x_{i+1},\ldots,x_m)
\]
is a singleton. If \{x^k\} is generated by cyclic exact block coordinate descent, then every limit point of \{x^k\} is stationary for minimizing f over X.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Suppose the objective is continuously differentiable on a Cartesian product of closed convex block sets and every one-block subproblem has a unique minimizer at every feasible point. Then every limit point of the cyclic exact block coordinate descent sequence is stationary. The proposition does not guarantee that the sequence has a limit point.
assumptions_latex: X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m,\quad X_i\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\text{ is closed and convex for }i=1,\ldots,m
f\text{ is continuously differentiable on }X
\forall x\in X,\ \forall i\in\{1,\ldots,m\},\quad \operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\xi\in X_i}f(x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1},\xi,x_{i+1},\ldots,x_m)\text{ is a singleton}
\{x^k\}\text{ is generated by cyclic exact block coordinate descent}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every limit point }\bar x\text{ of }\{x^k\}\text{ is stationary for }\min_{x\in X}f(x).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix the complementary blocks and write \(h_i(u)=F(x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1},u,x_{i+1},\ldots,x_m)\). If \(X_i\) is nonempty, closed, and convex and \(h_i\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, then \[u^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in X_i}h_i(u)\iff0\in\partial h_i(u^*)+N_{X_i}(u^*).\] If \(h_i\) is differentiable at \(u^*\), this is equivalent to \(\langle\nabla h_i(u^*),u-u^*\rangle\ge0\) for every \(u\in X_i\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi_k\) be the selected-block objective, \(v_k=\phi_k(x_{i_k}^k)\), and \(\phi_k^*=\inf_{u\in X_{i_k}}\phi_k(u)>-\infty\). For \(\eta_k\in(0,1]\), an update \(z_k\in X_{i_k}\) achieves relative block improvement \(\eta_k\) when \[v_k-\phi_k(z_k)\ge\eta_k(v_k-\phi_k^*).\] It follows that \(\phi_k(z_k)\le v_k\); if the infimum is attained, \(\eta_k=1\) requires an exact block minimum.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uncontrolled Block Error Can Destroy Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing why an explicit inexactness requirement is necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=\tfrac12x^2\), the exact one-block minimum is attained at \(0\). An unrestricted approximate solver may return \(x^{k+1}=2x^k\), in which case \(F(x^{k+1})=4F(x^k)\). Thus an update called approximate but subject to no gap, improvement, residual, or descent condition need not decrease even a convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without quantitative accuracy control, an approximate block update can increase a convex quadratic fourfold.
assumptions_latex: No quantitative accuracy or descent condition is imposed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Product-space and intermediate-iterate notation for alternating minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the canonical block embeddings and intermediate points used to describe a cyclic alternating-minimization sweep.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $p\geq 1$, let $E_i$ be Euclidean spaces, and equip $E=\prod_{i=1}^pE_i$ with
\[
\|(u_1,\ldots,u_p)\|_E=\left(\sum_{i=1}^p\|u_i\|_{E_i}^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
For a proper function $F:E\to(-\infty,\infty]$, consider $\min_{x\in E}F(x)$. For each $i$, define the canonical block embedding $\mathcal U_i:E_i\to E$ by
\[
\mathcal U_i(d)=(0,\ldots,0,\underset{i\text{th block}}{d},0,\ldots,0).
\]
If $x^k=(x_1^k,\ldots,x_p^k)$ and the blocks are updated cyclically, define
\[
x^{k,0}=x^k,\qquad x^{k,i}=(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_i^{k+1},x_{i+1}^k,\ldots,x_p^k),\quad i=1,\ldots,p,
\]
so that $x^{k,p}=x^{k+1}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The variable space is a finite product of Euclidean block spaces with the product norm. The canonical embedding inserts a displacement into one selected block. During a cyclic sweep, the intermediate point after block i contains the new values of the first i blocks and the old values of all remaining blocks; the zeroth and final intermediate points are the current and next iterates.
assumptions_latex: p\geq 1
E_i\text{ is a Euclidean space for }i=1,\ldots,p
E=E_1\times\cdots\times E_p
F:E\to(-\infty,\infty]\text{ is proper}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence of global and exact block minimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite-dimensional attainment result ensuring that the exact alternating-minimization block updates are well defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $E=E_1\times\cdots\times E_p$ be a finite product of Euclidean spaces. Suppose $F:E\to(-\infty,\infty]$ is proper and closed, and suppose every real sublevel set
\[
\operatorname{Lev}(F,\alpha)=\{x\in E:F(x)\leq\alpha\},\qquad \alpha\in\mathbb R,
\]
is bounded. Then $F$ attains its global minimum. Moreover, for every $\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}F$ and every $i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}$, the block subproblem
\[
\min_{y\in E_i}F\bigl(\bar x+\mathcal U_i(y-\bar x_i)\bigr)
\]
attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper closed extended-real function on a finite product of Euclidean spaces whose real sublevel sets are all bounded has a global minimizer. At every point in its effective domain, exact minimization over any one block while holding the other blocks fixed also has a solution.
assumptions_latex: E=E_1\times\cdots\times E_p\text{ with each }E_i\text{ Euclidean}
F:E\to(-\infty,\infty]\text{ is proper and closed}
\operatorname{Lev}(F,\alpha)=\{x\in E:F(x)\leq\alpha\}\text{ is bounded for every }\alpha\in\mathbb R
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in E}F(x)\neq\varnothing,\qquad \operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in E_i}F\bigl(\bar x+\mathcal U_i(y-\bar x_i)\bigr)\neq\varnothing\quad\text{for every }\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}F\text{ and }i=1,\ldots,p.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composite Alternating-Minimization Update and Blockwise Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents the Gauss–Seidel block update for the separable composite model and the equivalent blockwise form of its stationarity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=f+g\) on \(\mathbb E=\prod_{i=1}^p\mathbb E_i\), where \(g(\mathbf x)=\sum_{i=1}^p g_i(x_i)\). Suppose every \(g_i:\mathbb E_i\to(-\infty,\infty]\) is proper, closed, convex, and continuous on its domain; \(f:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,\infty]\) is closed; \(\operatorname{dom}f\) is convex; \(f\) is differentiable on \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\); and \(\operatorname{dom}g\subseteq\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\). The \(i\)-th alternating-minimization update can be written as
\[
x_i^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{y\in\mathbb E_i}\left\{f(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_{i-1}^{k+1},y,x_{i+1}^k,\ldots,x_p^k)+g_i(y)\right\},
\]
because the terms \(g_j(x_j)\), \(j\ne i\), are constant in this block subproblem. For every \(\mathbf x^*\in\operatorname{dom}g\), the stationarity condition has the equivalent blockwise representation
\[
-\nabla f(\mathbf x^*)\in\partial g(\mathbf x^*)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
-\nabla_i f(\mathbf x^*)\in\partial g_i(x_i^*)\quad\text{for all }i=1,\ldots,p.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated composite-model assumptions, alternating minimization updates one block by minimizing f plus that block's separable term, using new values for preceding blocks and old values for following blocks. Full composite stationarity is equivalent to stationarity in every block.
assumptions_latex: g_i:\mathbb E_i\to(-\infty,\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, convex, and continuous on }\operatorname{dom}g_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,p)
f:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,\infty]\text{ is closed}
\operatorname{dom}f\text{ is convex}
f\text{ is differentiable on }\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)
\operatorname{dom}g\subseteq\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)
g(\mathbf x)=\sum_{i=1}^p g_i(x_i)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_i^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{y\in\mathbb E_i}\{f(x_{<i}^{k+1},y,x_{>i}^{k})+g_i(y)\},\qquad -\nabla f(\mathbf x^*)\in\partial g(\mathbf x^*)\Longleftrightarrow \forall i,\ -\nabla_i f(\mathbf x^*)\in\partial g_i(x_i^*).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundedness and Cluster-Point Stationarity of Alternating Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Establishes boundedness of the generated sequence and stationarity of every cluster point under unique block minimizers and bounded level sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=f+g\), where \(g(\mathbf x)=\sum_{i=1}^p g_i(x_i)\). Suppose every \(g_i:\mathbb E_i\to(-\infty,\infty]\) is proper, closed, convex, and continuous on its domain; \(f:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,\infty]\) is closed; \(\operatorname{dom}f\) is convex; \(f\) is differentiable on \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\); and \(\operatorname{dom}g\subseteq\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\). Assume further that, for every \(\bar x\in\operatorname{dom}F\) and every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\), the problem
\[
\min_{y\in\mathbb E_i}F\bigl(\bar x+U_i(y-\bar x_i)\bigr)
\]
has a unique minimizer, and that for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), the level set
\[
\{x\in\mathbb E:F(x)\le\alpha\}
\]
is bounded. If \(\{x^k\}_{k\ge0}\) is generated by alternating minimization, then the sequence is bounded. Moreover, whenever a subsequence satisfies \(x^{k_j}\to x^*\), the limit is stationary:
\[
-\nabla f(x^*)\in\partial g(x^*).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the composite-model assumptions, if every one-block subproblem has a unique minimizer and every objective level set is bounded, then the alternating-minimization sequence is bounded and each of its cluster points is stationary.

\operatorname{dom}f\text{ is convex}
f\text{ is differentiable on }\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)
\operatorname{dom}g\subseteq\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)
\forall \bar x\in\operatorname{dom}F\ \forall i\in\{1,\ldots,p\},\ \arg\min_{y\in\mathbb E_i}F(\bar x+U_i(y-\bar x_i))\text{ is a singleton}
\forall\alpha\in\mathbb R,\ \{x\in\mathbb E:F(x)\le\alpha\}\text{ is bounded}
\{x^k\}_{k\ge0}\text{ is generated by alternating minimization}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cyclic Alternating Minimization for a Block-Separable Composite Objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States one ordered Gauss–Seidel sweep of exact block minimization under the composite-model assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
F(\mathbf x)=f(\mathbf x)+g(\mathbf x),\qquad g(\mathbf x)=\sum_{i=1}^p g_i(x_i).
\]
Assume that every \(g_i:\mathbb E_i\to(-\infty,\infty]\) is proper, closed, convex, and continuous on its domain; \(f:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,\infty]\) is closed with convex domain and is differentiable on \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\); and \(\operatorname{dom}g\subseteq\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\). During iteration \(k\), update the blocks in the order \(i=1,\ldots,p\) by
\[
x_i^{k+1}\in\arg\min_{y\in\mathbb E_i}\left\{f(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_{i-1}^{k+1},y,x_{i+1}^k,\ldots,x_p^k)+g_i(y)\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, visit the blocks in order and exactly minimize with respect to the current block, using already updated values for preceding blocks and previous-iteration values for following blocks.

\operatorname{dom}f\text{ is convex}
f\text{ is differentiable on }\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)
\operatorname{dom}g\subseteq\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)
g(\mathbf x)=\sum_{i=1}^p g_i(x_i)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A coordinate-wise minimum need not be a global minimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: For the convex absolute-value objective introduced immediately before this proposition, coordinate-wise minimality is strictly weaker than global minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[F(x_1,x_2)=|3x_1+4x_2|+|x_1-2x_2|.\] The unique global minimizer of \(F\) is \((0,0)\). Nevertheless, for every \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), the point \((-4\alpha,3\alpha)\) is a coordinate-wise minimum of \(F\). Hence, for every \(\alpha\neq0\), \((-4\alpha,3\alpha)\) is coordinate-wise minimal but is not a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the specified convex absolute-value objective, the origin is the unique global minimizer, while every point (-4α,3α) is coordinate-wise minimal. Nonzero α therefore gives a coordinate-wise minimum that is not globally minimizing.
assumptions_latex: \alpha\in\mathbb R
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{(x_1,x_2)\in\mathbb R^2}F=\{(0,0)\},\qquad (-4\alpha,3\alpha)\text{ is a coordinate-wise minimum of }F\quad\forall\alpha\in\mathbb R.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Block-embedding form of cyclic alternating minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An equivalent full-product-space implementation of one cyclic exact alternating-minimization sweep, conditional on solvability of each block subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $x^{k,0}=x^k$. For $i=1,\ldots,p$, the $i$th block of $x^{k,i-1}$ is still $x_i^k$. Select
\[
\widetilde y_i\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in E_i}F\bigl(x^{k,i-1}+\mathcal U_i(y-x_i^k)\bigr)
\]
and set
\[
x^{k,i}=x^{k,i-1}+\mathcal U_i(\widetilde y_i-x_i^k).
\]
After all blocks have been visited, set $x^{k+1}=x^{k,p}$. If a required argmin is empty, this exact update is not defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from the current iterate, express each block replacement as a displacement in the full product space through the canonical block embedding. Minimize over the next block, apply the resulting displacement, and continue through all blocks. The final intermediate point is the next iterate, provided every required block minimizer exists.
assumptions_latex: E=E_1\times\cdots\times E_p\text{ with each }E_i\text{ Euclidean}
F:E\to(-\infty,\infty]\text{ is an extended-real objective}
\mathcal U_i:E_i\to E\text{ is the canonical embedding of block }i
(x^{k,i-1})_i=x_i^k\text{ before block }i\text{ is updated}
\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in E_i}F\bigl(x^{k,i-1}+\mathcal U_i(y-x_i^k)\bigr)\neq\varnothing\text{ for each executed update}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widetilde y_i\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in E_i}F\bigl(x^{k,i-1}+\mathcal U_i(y-x_i^k)\bigr),\qquad x^{k,i}=x^{k,i-1}+\mathcal U_i(\widetilde y_i-x_i^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=x^{k,p}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cyclically minimizes the objective exactly over one variable block at a time; the method is defined only when every required block argmin is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $E=E_1\times\cdots\times E_p$ and $F:E\to(-\infty,\infty]$. Choose $x^0=(x_1^0,\ldots,x_p^0)\in\operatorname{dom}F$. For $k=0,1,2,\ldots$, visit $i=1,\ldots,p$ in order and select
\[
x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in E_i}F(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_{i-1}^{k+1},y,x_{i+1}^k,\ldots,x_p^k).
\]
Earlier blocks therefore use their new values, while later blocks retain their values from iteration $k$. If any displayed argmin is empty, the exact alternating-minimization update is not defined at that stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from a point in the effective domain and visit the blocks cyclically. At each visit, replace the selected block by an exact minimizer with previously visited blocks fixed at their new values and unvisited blocks fixed at their old values. The exact method is not well defined if a required block subproblem has no minimizer.
assumptions_latex: E=E_1\times\cdots\times E_p\text{ with each }E_i\text{ Euclidean}
F:E\to(-\infty,\infty]\text{ is an extended-real objective}
x^0\in\operatorname{dom}F
\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in E_i}F(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_{i-1}^{k+1},y,x_{i+1}^k,\ldots,x_p^k)\neq\varnothing\text{ whenever the corresponding update is executed}

Thus \(\|R(x)\|\) is the canonical full-sweep residual, although a small residual is only an approximate fixed-point certificate unless additional error-bound assumptions are available.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Block Gauss–Seidel Can Diverge Without Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear counterexample showing that well-defined block solves do not imply convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1&a\\a&1\end{pmatrix}\), \(b=0\), and scalar blocks, Gauss–Seidel gives \(x_1^{k+1}=-a x_2^k\) and \(x_2^{k+1}=a^2x_2^k\). Hence the iteration diverges for generic \(x_2^0\ne0\) whenever \(|a|>1\), although both diagonal block solves are uniquely defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unique block solves alone do not ensure nonlinear or linear Gauss–Seidel convergence.

Sequentially solving the block equations of \(Ax=b\) with newest available values gives \[(D+L)x^{k+1}=b-Ux^k,\qquad x^{k+1}=-(D+L)^{-1}Ux^k+(D+L)^{-1}b.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Contraction of a Nonlinear Gauss–Seidel Sweep
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local convergence criterion for a differentiable single-valued sweep map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\) be a single-valued nonlinear block Gauss–Seidel sweep with \(G(x^*)=x^*\). If \(G\) is continuously differentiable near \(x^*\) and \(\rho(G'(x^*))<1\), then an equivalent norm, a neighborhood \(V\) of \(x^*\), and \(q<1\) exist such that iterations starting sufficiently near \(x^*\) remain in \(V\) and satisfy \(\|x^{k+1}-x^*\|\le q\|x^k-x^*\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A differentiable nonlinear Gauss–Seidel fixed point is locally linearly attracting when the full-sweep Jacobian has spectral radius below one.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is single-valued and continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\). For each block, let \(S_i\) map fixed complementary variables to a solution of the corresponding nonlinear block problem; in optimization, \(S_i(x_{-i})\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in X_i}F(u,x_{-i})\). Starting from \(x^0\), perform the ordered sweep \[x_i^{k+1}=S_i(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_{i-1}^{k+1},x_{i+1}^{k},\ldots,x_m^k),\qquad i=1,\ldots,m.\] The composed sweep map is \(G=S_m\circ\cdots\circ S_1\), with block embeddings understood, and the iteration is \(x^{k+1}=G(x^k)\). Return an iterate satisfying the prescribed residual or change tolerance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected objective-gap bound for randomized coordinate descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An extraction-grounded sublinear expected bound under the referenced coordinatewise Lipschitz condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and differentiable everywhere, satisfy the referenced coordinatewise Lipschitz condition with constants \(\beta_i>0\), and attain its minimum at \(x^*\). If \(x_k\) is generated by uniform randomized coordinate descent, then for every \(k\ge1\), \[\mathbb{E}_{\xi_{k-1}}[f(x_k)]-f(x^*)\le \frac{n}{n+k}\left(\frac12\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert_\beta^2+f(x_0)-f(x^*)\right),\qquad \lVert x\rVert_\beta=\left(\sum_{i=1}^n\beta_i x_i^2\right)^{1/2},\] where \(\xi_{k-1}\) denotes the coordinate-selection history through iteration \(k-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an everywhere-differentiable convex objective satisfying the stated coordinatewise Lipschitz condition and having a minimizer, uniform randomized coordinate descent has an expected objective gap bounded by n/(n+k) times the sum of half the initial squared beta-weighted distance to a minimizer and the initial objective gap, for every k at least one.

f\text{ satisfies the referenced coordinatewise Lipschitz condition with constants }\beta_i>0
x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}f(x)
x_k\text{ is generated by uniform randomized coordinate descent}
k\ge1

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinate descent and classical coordinate-selection rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines scalar and block coordinate minimization and its principal deterministic and randomized selection variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R} have continuous first partial derivatives. A descent step with respect to coordinate i replaces x_i by a solution of \(\min_{t\in\mathbb{R}} f(x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1},t,x_{i+1},\ldots,x_n)\), leaving all other components fixed; the analogous block-coordinate step minimizes over one block. Cyclic coordinate descent visits \(1,\ldots,n\) repeatedly, an Aitken double sweep visits \(1,\ldots,n,n-1,\ldots,1\), Gauss--Southwell selects an index attaining \(\max_i |\nabla_i f(x)|\), and randomized coordinate descent selects a coordinate randomly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuously partially differentiable objective, coordinate descent improves the point by minimizing over one coordinate while holding the others fixed; the same construction applies to blocks. Coordinates may be visited cyclically, by a forward-and-backward double sweep, by choosing a largest-magnitude gradient component, or randomly.

abla_i f(\mathbf y)-
abla_i f(\mathbf y+\mathcal U_i(\mathbf d))\|\le L_i\|\mathbf d\|\) whenever \(\mathbf y,\mathbf y+\mathcal U_i(\mathbf d)\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Raw Block Progress Can Reverse After Work Normalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic family showing that larger raw decrease need not mean greater work efficiency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|x\|_2^2\), and suppose a candidate block of size \(b\) contains unit-valued coordinates. Exact minimization over the block gives decrease \(\Delta_b=b/2\). Under a declared dense local-solve cost \(C_b=b^2\), \[\frac{\Delta_b}{C_b}=\frac1{2b}.\] Thus raw decrease increases with \(b\), whereas decrease per unit work decreases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A larger block can give more raw decrease but less decrease per work when its local solve has quadratic cost.
assumptions_latex: The selected block contains \(b\) unit-valued coordinates.
The block is minimized exactly and has declared cost \(C_b=b^2\).

notation.meaning: Declared work of the block update.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of block granularities by guaranteed or predicted decrease per declared computational cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For candidate block \(i\), let \(\Delta_i(x)\ge0\) be a certified lower bound on the objective decrease produced by its proposed update, and let \(C_i(x)>0\) include the declared costs of selection, derivative access, local-model solution, and update application. Define \[\eta_i(x)= rac{\Delta_i(x)}{C_i(x)}.\] If the block quadratic upper model holds with \(L_i>0\), then the step \(d_i=-L_i^{-1}
abla_i f(x)\) permits \(\Delta_i(x)=\|
abla_i f(x)\|^2/(2L_i)\), so \[\eta_i(x)= rac{\|
abla_i f(x)\|^2}{2L_iC_i(x)}.\] Comparisons require a common cost convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare block sizes using certified decrease divided by the complete cost of selecting, computing, solving, and applying the update.
assumptions_latex: \(\Delta_i(x)\) is a valid nonnegative decrease lower bound.
\(C_i(x)>0\) follows one fixed accounting convention.
For the specialization, the block quadratic upper model holds with \(L_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta_i(x)=\Delta_i(x)/C_i(x)\), with \(\eta_i(x)=\|\nabla_i f(x)\|^2/(2L_iC_i(x))\) for the displayed block-gradient step.

knowledge_statements.title: Work-Normalized Block Progress
Block-Size Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descent benefit and computational cost induced by the chosen block granularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose differentiable \(f\) satisfies the block descent inequality \[f(x+U_id)\le f(x)+\langle
abla_i f(x),dangle+ rac{L_i}{2}\|d\|^2\] for every block step \(d\). The block-gradient choice \(d=-L_i^{-1}
abla_i f(x)\) then gives \[f(x)-f(x+U_id)\ge rac{\|
abla_i f(x)\|^2}{2L_i}.\] Enlarging a block can increase the captured gradient norm and hence potential one-step progress, but it can also increase \(L_i\), derivative-access cost, and the cost of solving the local model. Therefore block sizes are comparable only after normalizing predicted progress by their actual update and selection costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Larger blocks may capture more gradient energy but also have different smoothness constants and higher update costs; iteration counts alone are not comparable.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) obeys the displayed block descent inequality
\(d=-L_i^{-1}\nabla_i f(x)\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Termination of Block Armijo Backtracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-definedness of Armijo backtracking along a fixed selected-block descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be continuously differentiable near \(x\), let \(s=U_i d\) satisfy \(\langle\nabla f(x),s\rangle<0\), and fix \(\bar\alpha>0\), \(0<\beta<1\), and \(0<\sigma<1\). Then some finite \(j\ge0\) satisfies \[f(x+\bar\alpha\beta^j s)\le f(x)+\sigma\bar\alpha\beta^j\langle\nabla f(x),s\rangle.\] Consequently, block Armijo backtracking accepts a positive step after finitely many contractions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous differentiability and a strict selected-block descent direction guarantee finite termination of Armijo backtracking.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable near \(x\).
\(s=U_i d\) and \(\langle\nabla f(x),s\rangle<0\).
\(\bar\alpha>0\), \(0<\beta<1\), and \(0<\sigma<1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Armijo Backtracking Can Fail Without Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of finite acceptance for a selected-block ascent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(t)=t\), \(x=0\), and \(s=1\). For any \(0<\sigma<1\) and every \(\alpha>0\), Armijo acceptance would require \(\alpha\le\sigma\alpha\), which is false. Thus geometric backtracking rejects every positive trial step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ascent direction can make every positive Armijo trial unacceptable.
knowledge_statements.title: Armijo Backtracking Can Fail Without Descent

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationarity of Essentially Cyclic Block-Gradient Armijo Iterates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global stationarity for block-gradient directions controlled by Armijo backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the initial level set be compact, let \(f\) be continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of it with Lipschitz gradient there, and let blocks be selected essentially cyclically. Set \(s_k=-U_{i_k}
abla_{i_k}f(x^k)\), and perform Armijo backtracking from trial scales lying in a fixed interval \([\underline\alpha,\overline\alpha]\subset(0,\infty)\). Then accepted step lengths are bounded away from zero, \(\sum_k\|
abla_{i_k}f(x^k)\|^2<\infty\), and \(\|
abla f(x^k)\|	o0\). Consequently every accumulation point is stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under compact-level-set smoothness and nonstarving block selection, block-gradient Armijo iterates approach stationarity.
assumptions_latex: The initial level set is compact.
\(f\) has a Lipschitz-continuous gradient on a neighborhood of that level set.
Block selection is essentially cyclic.
Armijo trial scales lie in \([\underline\alpha,\overline\alpha]\subset(0,\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity of Essentially Cyclic Block-Gradient Armijo Iterates

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accepted-step and decrease bounds for selected-block Armijo backtracking under directional smoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s=U_i d\) satisfy \(g=\langle\nabla f(x),s\rangle<0\). Suppose the descent lemma with constant \(L>0\) holds along every tested segment. Armijo backtracking from \(\bar\alpha>0\), with \(0<\beta,\sigma<1\), accepts \(\alpha\) satisfying \[\alpha\ge \min\!\left\{\bar\alpha,\frac{2\beta(1-\sigma)(-g)}{L\|s\|^2}\right\},\qquad f(x)-f(x+\alpha s)\ge\sigma\alpha(-g).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directional smoothness gives an explicit lower bound on the accepted block Armijo step and its guaranteed decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(\langle\nabla f(x),s\rangle<0\).
The \(L\)-smooth descent inequality holds along all tested trial segments.
\(\bar\alpha>0\) and \(0<\beta,\sigma<1\).

notation.meaning: Directional derivative along the selected-block direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Quantitative Armijo Step Lower Bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-iterate gradient bound for Armijo backtracking along the largest block-gradient direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Partition \(
abla f(x)\) into \(p\) disjoint blocks. Assume \(f\) is bounded below by \(f_{\inf}\) and has \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient on the iterates and tested segments. At iteration \(k\), choose \(i_k\in\arg\max_i\|
abla_i f(x^k)\|\), set \(s_k=-U_{i_k}
abla_{i_k}f(x^k)\), and use Armijo backtracking with fixed initial trial \( ar\alpha>0\) and parameters \(0< eta,\sigma<1\). Define \[a=\min\{ ar\alpha,2 eta(1-\sigma)/L\}.\] Then, for every \(K\ge1\), \[\min_{0\le k<K}\|
abla f(x^k)\|^2\le rac{p\,[f(x^0)-f_{\inf}]}{\sigma aK}.\] Thus at most \(\lceil p[f(x^0)-f_{\inf}]/(\sigma a\varepsilon^2)ceil\) iterations suffice to produce \(\|
abla f\|\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedy block selection plus Armijo backtracking reaches an epsilon-stationary point in order p divided by epsilon squared iterations.
assumptions_latex: The blocks form a disjoint partition.
\(f\) is bounded below.
The gradient is \(L\)-Lipschitz along all iterates and tested segments.
The block with largest gradient norm is selected.
Armijo backtracking uses fixed parameters and a fixed initial trial scale.

notation.meaning: Uniform lower bound on accepted Armijo step lengths

Coordinate Line-Search Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Line search along a selected coordinate or block-supported descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuously differentiable. At iteration \(k\), select a block injection \(U_{i_k}\) and a direction \(d_k\) satisfying \(\langle\nabla f(x^k),U_{i_k}d_k\rangle<0\). Starting from \(\bar\alpha_k>0\), choose the first \(\alpha_k=\bar\alpha_k\beta^j\), with \(j\in\{0,1,\ldots\}\), satisfying \[f(x^k+\alpha_kU_{i_k}d_k)\le f(x^k)+\sigma\alpha_k\langle\nabla f(x^k),U_{i_k}d_k\rangle,\] where \(0<\beta<1\) and \(0<\sigma<1\). Set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\alpha_kU_{i_k}d_k\), and stop by a prescribed criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtrack along a selected block-supported descent direction until the Armijo sufficient-decrease condition holds.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable
\(\langle\nabla f(x^k),U_{i_k}d_k\rangle<0\)
\(0<\beta,\sigma<1\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x^{k+1})<f(x^k)\) whenever \(d_k\ne0\) and the accepted Armijo step exists.

children.title: Coordinate Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Selected-coordinate or selected-block updates using local second-order curvature.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicted reduction and stationarity test for a positive-curvature scalar coordinate Newton model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the scalar coordinate model \(m_i(d)=g_i d+\tfrac12 h_i d^2\) with \(h_i>0\), its unique minimizer is \(d_i^N=-g_i/h_i\), and its predicted reduction is \[m_i(0)-m_i(d_i^N)=\frac{g_i^2}{2h_i}.\] Hence this coordinate Newton decrement is nonnegative and vanishes if and only if \(g_i=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive coordinate curvature gives a computable Newton-model reduction equal to the squared partial gradient divided by twice the curvature; it vanishes exactly at coordinate stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Newton Predicted-Decrease Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinate Newton Need Not Have Full-Newton Finite Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled SPD quadratic on which cyclic scalar Newton updates converge only linearly by sweeps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f(x,y)=\tfrac12(x^2+2\rho xy+y^2) with 0<|\rho|<1. Updating x and then y by their exact scalar Newton steps gives x^+=-\rho y and y^+=\rho^2y. After the first sweep, each subsequent sweep scales the iterate by \rho^2 and the objective by \rho^4.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a coupled positive-definite quadratic, cyclic scalar Newton steps are Gauss–Seidel steps and need not terminate after one sweep.
assumptions_latex: Coordinates are updated in the order x then y.
Each scalar model uses its exact second derivative.
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Newton Need Not Have Full-Newton Finite Termination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized scalar coordinate-Newton variant with a bounded step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For selected coordinate \(i\), let \(g_i=\nabla_i f(x)\), \(h_i=\nabla_{ii}^2f(x)\), \(\Delta>0\), and \(\lambda\ge\max\{0,-h_i+\gamma\}\) with \(\gamma>0\). Compute \[d_i=\arg\min_{|d|\le\Delta}\left\{g_id+\tfrac12(h_i+\lambda)d^2\right\}=\operatorname{clip}\!\left(-\frac{g_i}{h_i+\lambda},-\Delta,\Delta\right),\] and update only coordinate \(i\). A global method must additionally specify an acceptance or damping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive regularization and a scalar trust region produce a well-posed bounded coordinate Newton trial step.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice differentiable at \(x\).
\(\Delta>0\) and \(\gamma>0\).
\(\lambda\ge\max\{0,-h_i+\gamma\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Coordinate Newton Step

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Local Rate for Separable Coordinate Newton Sweeps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local convergence of cyclic scalar Newton updates for a separable smooth objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_i(x_i)\), where \(\phi_i'(x_i^*)=0\). Suppose in neighborhoods of \(x_i^*\), \(\phi_i''(t)\ge m>0\) and \(|\phi_i''(s)-\phi_i''(t)|\le H|s-t|\). A full sweep of undamped scalar Newton updates satisfies \[\|x^{r+1}-x^*\|_\infty\le\frac{H}{2m}\|x^r-x^*\|_\infty^2\] whenever the sweep remains in those neighborhoods.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a separable objective with uniformly positive Lipschitz coordinate curvature, complete coordinate-Newton sweeps converge locally quadratically.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\sum_i\phi_i(x_i)\).
\(\phi_i''\ge m>0\) locally.
Each \(\phi_i''\) is locally \(H\)-Lipschitz.
The sweep remains in the stated neighborhoods.

notation.meaning: local Lipschitz constant of coordinate second derivatives

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Gauss–Seidel Rate of Coupled Coordinate Newton Sweeps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local convergence characterization for cyclic scalar Newton updates on a coupled objective near a nondegenerate minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\in C^2\) near a strict local minimizer \(x^*\), and suppose \(H^*=
abla^2f(x^*)\succ0\). Fix a coordinate order and decompose \(H^*=D+L+U\) into diagonal, strictly lower, and strictly upper parts. Let one sweep sequentially apply the undamped scalar Newton update \(x_i\leftarrow x_i-
abla_i f(x)/
abla_{ii}^2f(x)\). The derivative of the sweep map at \(x^*\) is \[G=-(D+L)^{-1}U.\] Since \(H^*\succ0\), \(ho(G)<1\). Consequently, for every \(q\in(ho(G),1)\), there is a neighborhood and an equivalent norm in which complete sweeps satisfy \(\|x^{r+1}-x^*\|\le q\|x^r-x^*\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near a nondegenerate minimizer, a coupled coordinate-Newton sweep has the Gauss–Seidel linearization and converges locally linearly.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
\(\nabla f(x^*)=0\) and \(\nabla^2f(x^*)\succ0\).
Every scalar Newton update is undamped and follows the fixed order.
The initial point is sufficiently close to \(x^*\).

notation.meaning: Order-dependent splitting of the limiting Hessian

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global first-order stationarity bound for positive-curvature coordinate Newton directions accepted by Armijo backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be bounded below by \(f_{\inf}\) and have \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient on all iterates and tested segments. Suppose \(m\le h_i(x)=
abla_{ii}^2f(x)\le M\) for every selectable coordinate. At iteration \(k\), choose \(i_k\in\arg\max_i|
abla_i f(x^k)|\), set \(d_k=-
abla_{i_k}f(x^k)/h_{i_k}(x^k)\), and apply Armijo backtracking from unit trial step with parameters \(0< eta, \sigma<1\). Define \(a=\min\{1,2 eta(1-\sigma)m/L\}\). Then \[\min_{0\le k<K}\|
abla f(x^k)\|_2^2\le rac{nM[f(x^0)-f_{\inf}]}{\sigma aK}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedy positive-curvature coordinate Newton steps with Armijo damping reach epsilon stationarity in order n divided by epsilon squared iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is bounded below.
The gradient is L-Lipschitz along all iterates and tested segments.
\(0<m\le\nabla_{ii}^2f(x)\le M\) for selectable coordinates.
The largest-magnitude partial gradient is selected.
Armijo backtracking starts from one.

children.title: Diagonal-Newton Methods
children.top_down_role: Second-order coordinate updates using diagonal curvature approximations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-posedness and bounded-scaling condition for selected diagonal-Newton directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_k=\operatorname{Diag}(d_{k,1},\ldots,d_{k,n})\). A uniformly safeguarded diagonal curvature sequence satisfies constants \(0<m\le M<\infty\) such that \(m\le d_{k,i}\le M\) for every iteration and coordinate that may be selected. Then every selected inverse scaling is well defined and obeys \(M^{-1}\le d_{k,i}^{-1}\le m^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clipping diagonal curvature between fixed positive bounds prevents division by zero and unbounded or vanishing inverse scaling.
assumptions_latex: \(0<m\le M<\infty\).
\(m\le d_{k,i}\le M\) for all selectable \((k,i)\).

notation.meaning: Uniform lower and upper curvature safeguards

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Diagonal-Curvature Safeguard

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Smooth-Objective Descent for a Safeguarded Diagonal Step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient-decrease guarantee for a selected diagonally scaled gradient direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f\) has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, \(d_{k,i}\ge m>0\), and \(p=-P_SD_k^{-1}\nabla f(x)\). For \(0<\alpha<2m/L\), \[f(x+\alpha p)\le f(x)-\alpha\left(1-\frac{L\alpha}{2m}\right)\sum_{i\in S}\frac{(\nabla_i f(x))^2}{d_{k,i}}.\] Thus the step strictly decreases \(f\) whenever the selected gradient is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive lower curvature safeguard and sufficiently small step size make the selected diagonal-Newton direction a strict descent step for a smooth objective.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz.
\(d_{k,i}\ge m>0\) on selected coordinates.
knowledge_statements.title: Smooth-Objective Descent for a Safeguarded Diagonal Step

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform-Coordinate Rate for Safeguarded Diagonal Steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected objective-error rate for uniform singleton selection with a bounded diagonal metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the assumptions of smoothness, strong convexity, and mI\preceq D_k\preceq MI, independently select i_k uniformly from \{1,\ldots,n\} and set x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha e_{i_k}\nabla_{i_k}f(x^k)/d_{k,i_k}, where 0<\alpha<2m/L. With c_\alpha=1-L\alpha/(2m), \mathbb E[f(x^{k+1})-f^*\mid x^k]\le(1-2\mu\alpha c_\alpha/(nM))(f(x^k)-f^*).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform singleton diagonal steps have a geometric expected rate weakened by the coordinate count.
assumptions_latex: f is \mu-strongly convex.
\nabla f is L-Lipschitz.
m\le d_{k,i}\le M for all k,i.
i_k is conditionally uniform.
0<\alpha<2m/L.
0\le1-2\mu\alpha c_\alpha/(nM)<1.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose f is \mu-strongly convex with L-Lipschitz gradient, mI\preceq D_k\preceq MI, and x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha D_k^{-1}\nabla f(x^k), where 0<\alpha<2m/L. With c_\alpha=1-L\alpha/(2m), f(x^{k+1})-f^*\le(1-2\mu\alpha c_\alpha/M)(f(x^k)-f^*).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly safeguarded full diagonal steps converge linearly on smooth strongly convex objectives.
assumptions_latex: f is \mu-strongly convex.
\nabla f is L-Lipschitz.
mI\preceq D_k\preceq MI.
Every coordinate is selected.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing Positive Curvature Can Destabilize a Diagonal Step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional failure when positive diagonal curvature has no adequate lower safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For f(x)=\tfrac12x^2, choose \alpha=1 and the positive diagonal approximation d\in(0,1/2). The diagonal step is x^+=(1-1/d)x, so |1-1/d|>1 and every nonzero iterate grows geometrically in magnitude and objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positivity alone does not stabilize diagonal Newton scaling; an excessively small positive curvature estimate can make the iteration diverge.
assumptions_latex: \alpha=1.
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Positive Curvature Can Destabilize a Diagonal Step

Diagonal-Newton Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Newton-like update on selected coordinates using a positive diagonal curvature approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, let \(D_k=\operatorname{diag}(d_{k,1},\ldots,d_{k,n})\) with \(d_{k,i}>0\), and let \(S_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be the selected coordinate set. Define \(P_{S_k}\) as the diagonal projector onto \(S_k\), compute \[p^k=-P_{S_k}D_k^{-1}\nabla f(x^k),\] choose \(\alpha_k>0\), and update \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\alpha_kp^k\). Common curvature choices use positive diagonal Hessian entries or safeguarded positive approximations. Stop using a prescribed stationarity, change, or iteration criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale each selected gradient component by a positive diagonal curvature approximation and leave every unselected component unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable
\(d_{k,i}>0\) for every \(i\)
\(S_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\)
\(\alpha_k>0\)

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature Approximation Fidelity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral fidelity of a positive-definite block curvature model and its effect on the block Newton direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_i\succ0\) be the exact Hessian restricted to block \(i\), let \(B_i\succ0\) be an approximation, and suppose \(0\leq\varepsilon<1\) satisfies \((1-\varepsilon)H_i\preceq B_i\preceq(1+\varepsilon)H_i\). For a block gradient \(g_i\), define \(d_i^*=-H_i^{-1}g_i\) and \(d_i=-B_i^{-1}g_i\). Then the approximation is uniformly faithful in the local curvature norm and obeys \[\lVert d_i-d_i^*\rVert_{H_i}\leq\frac{\varepsilon}{1-\varepsilon}\lVert d_i^*\rVert_{H_i}.\] Thus decreasing \(\varepsilon\) continuously recovers the exact block Newton direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectrally accurate positive-definite curvature approximation produces a block direction whose relative local-norm error is controlled by the spectral approximation error.
assumptions_latex: \(H_i\succ0\) and \(B_i\succ0\).
\(0\leq\varepsilon<1\).
\((1-\varepsilon)H_i\preceq B_i\preceq(1+\varepsilon)H_i\).

knowledge_statements.title: Indefinite Coordinate Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of an unconstrained quadratic block model when its curvature matrix has a negative direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the block model \(m_i(d)=g_i^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}B_i d\) on \(\mathbb R^{n_i}\), where \(g_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i}\) and \(B_i=B_i^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n_i\times n_i}\). If there exists \(v\neq0\) such that \(v^{\mathsf T}B_i v<0\), then \(m_i(tv)\to-\infty\) as \(|t|\to\infty\). Hence the unrestricted coordinate-curvature subproblem has no minimizer. Boundedness and attainment can instead be restored, for example, by minimizing over a nonempty compact trust region or feasible block, or by choosing \(\lambda\) such that \(B_i+\lambda I\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A negative-curvature direction makes an unrestricted quadratic coordinate model unbounded below. A compact restriction or positive-definite curvature regularization provides a well-posed replacement subproblem.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i}\).
\(B_i=B_i^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{n_i\times n_i}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_i(d)=g_i^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}B_i d\) with \(B_i=B_i^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\). Then \(m_i\) is bounded below on \(\mathbb R^{n_i}\) if and only if \(g_i\in\operatorname{Range}(B_i)\), equivalently \(g_i\perp\ker(B_i)\). In that case \[\operatorname*{argmin}_d m_i(d)=-B_i^{\dagger}g_i+\ker(B_i),\] and the minimizer is unique if and only if \(B_i\succ0\). If \(g_i\notin\operatorname{Range}(B_i)\), then \(\inf_d m_i(d)=-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With singular positive-semidefinite coordinate curvature, the quadratic model is bounded exactly when the gradient has no component in the curvature nullspace; its minimizers then form an affine nullspace.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Block Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive positive-definite quadratic models for selected finite-dimensional blocks of a composite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in\mathbb R^{n_1}\times\cdots\times\mathbb R^{n_m}\) and \(F(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m r_i(x_i)\), where \(f\) is differentiable and each \(r_i\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. At iteration \(k\), select \(i_k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), choose a symmetric matrix \(B_{i_k}^k\succ0\), and compute \[d_{i_k}^k=\operatorname*{argmin}_{d\in\mathbb R^{n_{i_k}}}\left\{\langle\nabla_{i_k}f(x^k),d\rangle+\tfrac12\langle d,B_{i_k}^k d\rangle+r_{i_k}(x_{i_k}^k+d)\right\}.\] Set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+U_{i_k}d_{i_k}^k\), so every unselected block remains unchanged. The strong convexity supplied by \(B_{i_k}^k\succ0\) makes the displayed block minimizer unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, the selected finite-dimensional block uniquely minimizes a convex composite quadratic model in an iteration-dependent positive-definite metric, while all other blocks remain fixed.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i}\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
\(F(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m r_i(x_i)\), with \(f\) differentiable.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent proximal-map form of the accepted variable-metric block subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a selected block \(i\), let \(B_i\succ0\), \(g_i=\nabla_i f(x)\), and define \[\operatorname{prox}_{r_i}^{B_i}(z)=\operatorname*{argmin}_y\left\{r_i(y)+\tfrac12\lVert y-z\rVert_{B_i}^2\right\}.\] The unique minimizer of \[\min_d\ \langle g_i,d\rangle+\tfrac12\lVert d\rVert_{B_i}^2+r_i(x_i+d)\] is \[d_i=\operatorname{prox}_{r_i}^{B_i}(x_i-B_i^{-1}g_i)-x_i.\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step descent safeguard for an exact selected-block variable-metric composite update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=f(x)+\sum_j r_j(x_j)\), and suppose that for the computed selected-block step \(d_i\), \[f(x+U_i d_i)\le f(x)+\langle\nabla_i f(x),d_i\rangle+\tfrac12\langle d_i,H_i d_i\rangle,\qquad H_i\succeq0.\] If \(d_i\) exactly minimizes the variable-metric model with \(B_i\succ0\), then \[F(x+U_i d_i)-F(x)\le-\tfrac12\langle d_i,(B_i-H_i)d_i\rangle.\] Hence \(B_i-H_i\succeq\mu_i I\) with \(\mu_i>0\) implies \[F(x+U_i d_i)\le F(x)-\frac{\mu_i}{2}\lVert d_i\rVert^2.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationarity of Exact BSUM Accumulation Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualitative convergence of exact essentially-cyclic block upper-bound minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^mX_i\) have closed convex blocks, and let \(F\) be continuous on the compact initial sublevel set. Suppose every block surrogate is continuous, touches and majorizes the corresponding one-block objective, agrees with its block directional derivatives at the base point, and has a unique attained minimizer. If block selection is essentially cyclic, every accumulation point is coordinatewise stationary. If every such point is regular in the sense that coordinatewise stationarity implies stationarity, then every accumulation point \(\bar x\) satisfies \(F'(\bar x;d)\ge0\) for every feasible direction \(d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under compactness, compatible upper models, unique block solutions, and recurring selection, exact BSUM has stationary accumulation points at regular points.
assumptions_latex: Every block is selected at least once in each bounded number of iterations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact cyclic minimization of blockwise majorants that touch and first-order match the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be defined on \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\). knowledge_statements.title: Strictly Convex Block Approximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong convexity as a sufficient condition for a unique and stable selected-block minimizer in finite dimensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) be nonempty, closed, and convex. For a fixed base point \(x\), suppose the block approximation \(u_i(\cdot;x)\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, coercive on \(X_i\), and \(\mu_i\)-strongly convex for some \(\mu_i>0\), meaning that \[u_i(\theta z+(1-\theta)y;x)\leq\theta u_i(z;x)+(1-\theta)u_i(y;x)-\tfrac{\mu_i}{2}\theta(1-\theta)\lVert z-y\rVert^2\] for all \(z,y\in X_i\) and \(\theta\in[0,1]\). Then \(u_i(\cdot;x)\) has exactly one minimizer on \(X_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a closed convex finite-dimensional block set, a proper lower-semicontinuous coercive model with positive strong-convexity modulus has exactly one minimizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearized Block Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order block surrogate obtained by freezing all other blocks at the current iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a differentiable function \(f\) and base point \(x\), the linearized model for a displacement \(d_i\) in block \(i\) is \[\ell_i(d_i;x)=f(x)+\langle\nabla_i f(x),d_i\rangle.\] If the objective is composite, \(F(x)=f(x)+\sum_j r_j(x_j)\), the corresponding block model, up to terms independent of \(d_i\), is \[q_i(d_i;x)=\langle\nabla_i f(x),d_i\rangle+r_i(x_i+d_i).\] This model is first-order exact at \(d_i=0\), but it need not majorize \(F\) or possess a minimizer without stabilization or bounded feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linearized block model retains the selected partial gradient and exact block regularizer, but may require stabilization to be bounded or majorizing.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the block partial gradient obeys \(\lVert
abla_i f(x+U_i d)-
abla_i f(x)Vert\leq L_i\lVert dVert\) along every feasible block segment. Then \[f(x+U_i d)\leq f(x)+\langle
abla_i f(x),dangle+ rac{L_i}{2}\lVert dVert^2.\] Consequently, a stabilized linear model with quadratic coefficient \(	au_i\) majorizes the one-block restriction whenever \(	au_i\geq L_i\). Choosing \(	au_i\) close to \(L_i\) preserves a larger step, whereas a substantially larger coefficient yields a more conservative block displacement.

If \(\tau_i\ge L_i\), then \[F(x+U_id_i)\le F(x)-\frac{\tau_i-L_i}{2}\|d_i\|^2.\] Thus \(\tau_i>L_i\) gives a positive displacement-based descent margin, whereas equality guarantees only nonincrease through this estimate.

children.title: Understabilized Block Models

knowledge_statements.title: Understabilized Block Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of block majorization and possible objective increase below the smoothness-determined stabilization threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(t)=\tfrac{L}{2}t^2\) with \(L>0\), and at \(x\neq0\) use the stabilized linear model \(q(d;x)=f(x)+f'(x)d+\tfrac{\tau}{2}d^2\). If \(0<\tau<L\), then \[f(x+d)-q(d;x)=\frac{L-\tau}{2}d^2>0\qquad(d\neq0),\] so the model is not an upper bound. Its minimizer is \(d=-Lx/\tau\). Moreover, if \(0<\tau<L/2\), the full update increases the objective because \(f(x+d)>f(x)\). Thus insufficient stabilization invalidates unconditional descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Below the block curvature threshold, the stabilized linear model ceases to majorize; for sufficiently small stabilization, its minimizing update can increase the objective.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual Certificate for Strongly Convex Surrogate Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of a block-surrogate first-order residual into an objective-gap bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u\) be proper, closed, and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with respect to a norm on a closed convex set \(X_i\), and let \(z^*\) minimize \(u\) over \(X_i\). If \(z\in X_i\) and \(r\in\partial u(z)+N_{X_i}(z)\), then \[u(z)-u(z^*)\le\frac{\|r\|_*^2}{2\sigma}.\] Consequently, \(\|r\|_*\le\sqrt{2\sigma\varepsilon}\) certifies additive surrogate gap at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a strongly convex surrogate, a small constrained optimality residual certifies a small surrogate objective gap.
assumptions_latex: \(u\) is proper, closed, and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with \(\sigma>0\).
\(X_i\) is closed and convex.
A constrained minimizer \(z^*\) exists.
The dual norm corresponds to the norm used for strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Certificate for Strongly Convex Surrogate Solves

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent Surrogate Error Can Prevent Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-block exact-surrogate example showing failure under a nonvanishing additive solve tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=\tfrac12x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\), and at every iteration use the exact surrogate \(u(z;x^k)=F(z)\). Its minimum is zero at \(z=0\). If the inexact solver is allowed the constant additive tolerance \(\varepsilon_k=\tfrac12\), it may return \(x^{k+1}=1\) for every \(k\), since \(u(1;x^k)=\inf_z u(z;x^k)+\tfrac12\). Starting from \(x^0=1\), the iterates remain at the nonstationary point \(1\), where \(F'(1)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed positive surrogate-gap tolerance permits an admissible inexact solver to remain forever at a nonstationary point, even when the surrogate is the objective itself.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon_k=1/2\) for every k.
The solver may choose any point satisfying the additive-gap test.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Surrogate Error Can Prevent Stationarity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Additive Surrogate Gap Certifies Solution Distance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance guarantee for a strongly convex block surrogate solved to additive accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let u be \sigma-strongly convex on a convex set X_i, with \sigma>0, and let z^* minimize u over X_i. If z\in X_i satisfies u(z)-u(z^*)\le\varepsilon, then \|z-z^*\|\le\sqrt{2\varepsilon/\sigma}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a strongly convex block surrogate, an additive objective-gap tolerance bounds distance to its unique exact minimizer.
assumptions_latex: X_i is convex.
u is \sigma-strongly convex on X_i.
A minimizer z^* exists.
u(z)-u(z^*)\le\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive Surrogate Gap Certifies Solution Distance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact surrogate-block variant using a relative constrained first-order residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), select block \(i_k\) and let \(u_{i_k}(\cdot;x^k)\) be a strongly convex surrogate on a closed convex set \(X_{i_k}\). Choose \(z^k\in X_{i_k}\) and \(r_k\in\partial u_{i_k}(z^k;x^k)+N_{X_{i_k}}(z^k)\) satisfying \[\|r_k\|_*\le\eta_k\|z^k-x_{i_k}^k\|,\qquad \eta_k\ge0.\] Set \(x_{i_k}^{k+1}=z^k\) and leave all other blocks unchanged. Any convergence theorem must separately control \(\eta_k\) and the block-selection rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate surrogate solve may be accepted when its constrained first-order residual is small relative to the proposed block displacement.
assumptions_latex: \(X_{i_k}\) is closed and convex.
\(u_{i_k}(\cdot;x^k)\) is proper, closed, and strongly convex.
A residual satisfying the displayed inclusion is available.

notation.meaning: normal-cone mapping of the block constraint set

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotone Acceptance for an Inexact Upper-Surrogate Solve
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal descent condition for an approximate block solve when the surrogate majorizes the updated objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u_i(z;x)\) satisfy \[F(x_{-i},z)\le u_i(z;x)\quad\text{for every feasible }z,\qquad u_i(x_i;x)=F(x).\] If an inexact block solver returns feasible \(z\) with \(u_i(z;x)\le u_i(x_i;x)\), then the block update \(x^+=(x_{-i},z)\) satisfies \(F(x^+)\le F(x)\). Strict surrogate decrease implies strict objective decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate upper-surrogate solve preserves descent whenever it improves the surrogate relative to the unchanged block.
assumptions_latex: The block surrogate majorizes the objective along the selected block.
The surrogate is tight at the current block.
The returned block is feasible and does not increase the surrogate.

notation.meaning: All blocks other than selected block i

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Acceptance for an Inexact Upper-Surrogate Solve

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective Descent with Additive Error in an Upper-Surrogate Solve
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-change bound for an additive-gap approximate minimizer of a tight block upper surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let u_i(z;x) satisfy F(x_{-i},z)\le u_i(z;x) for every feasible z and u_i(x_i;x)=F(x). If z_\varepsilon is feasible and u_i(z_\varepsilon;x)\le\inf_z u_i(z;x)+\varepsilon, define \Delta_i(x)=u_i(x_i;x)-\inf_z u_i(z;x). Then, for x^+=(x_{-i},z_\varepsilon), \[F(x^+)\le F(x)-\Delta_i(x)+\varepsilon.\] In particular, objective descent is guaranteed when \varepsilon<\Delta_i(x).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Additive surrogate-solve error reduces the best predicted block-surrogate decrease by at most the error.
assumptions_latex: The selected block surrogate majorizes the objective along that block.
The surrogate is tight at the current block.
The returned feasible point has additive surrogate gap at most \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Best decrease available in the selected block surrogate

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Descent with Additive Error in an Upper-Surrogate Solve

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inner Gradient Complexity for a Smooth Strongly Convex Block Surrogate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work required to realize an additive-gap inexact block-surrogate solve by gradient descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u:\mathbb R^{d_i}\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, \(L\)-smooth, and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex, with minimizer \(z^*\), where \(0<\sigma<L\). Starting from \(z^0\), apply \(z^{t+1}=z^t-L^{-1}\nabla u(z^t)\). Then \[u(z^t)-u(z^*)\le\left(1-\frac\sigma L\right)^t\bigl(u(z^0)-u(z^*)\bigr).\] Therefore, when the initial gap exceeds \(\varepsilon>0\), an additive surrogate gap at most \(\varepsilon\) is obtained after \[t\ge\left\lceil\frac{\log((u(z^0)-u(z^*))/\varepsilon)}{-\log(1-\sigma/L)}\right\rceil\] inner gradient steps; no step is required when the initial gap is already at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient descent solves a smooth strongly convex block surrogate to additive accuracy in logarithmically many inner iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(u\) is differentiable, \(L\)-smooth, and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with \(0<\sigma<L\).
A minimizer \(z^*\) exists.
The inner method uses stepsize \(1/L\).
knowledge_statements.title: Inner Gradient Complexity for a Smooth Strongly Convex Block Surrogate
Inexact Surrogate Block Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate block-surrogate minimization controlled by a summable sequence of objective-gap errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u_i(\cdot;x^k)\) be a proper lower-semicontinuous block surrogate with finite infimum on \(X_i\). Select block \(i_k\), choose \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\), and compute \(z_{i_k}^k\in X_{i_k}\) satisfying \[u_{i_k}(z_{i_k}^k;x^k)\leq\inf_{z\in X_{i_k}}u_{i_k}(z;x^k)+\varepsilon_k.\] Set \(x_{i_k}^{k+1}=z_{i_k}^k\) and leave other blocks fixed. Require \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty\), or enforce an explicitly stated vanishing relative residual. Stop when the block-surrogate optimality residual is below tolerance and return \(x^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each block subproblem may be solved approximately, provided its certified error is controlled, commonly by a summable error sequence or vanishing relative residual.
assumptions_latex: \(u_i(\cdot;x^k)\) is proper and lower semicontinuous with finite infimum on \(X_i\).
\(\varepsilon_k\geq0\).
\(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty\).

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Separable Upper Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic additive quadratic majorant for simultaneous updates on a prescribed block set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be differentiable on a finite-dimensional product space, fix \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and define \(h_{[S]}=\sum_{i\in S}U_i h_i\). Positive weights \(v_i\) define a deterministic separable quadratic upper model on \(S\) if, for every feasible block displacement, \[f(x+h_{[S]})\leq f(x)+\sum_{i\in S}\left(\langle\nabla_i f(x),h_i\rangle+\frac{v_i}{2}\lVert h_i\rVert^2\right).\] Because the right-hand side separates over \(i\in S\), its block-dependent terms can be minimized independently after \(x\), \(S\), and the valid weights are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed deterministic update set, weights define a separable upper model when the objective change is bounded by the sum of the corresponding independent blockwise linear-quadratic terms.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable on every relevant update segment.
\(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) is fixed deterministically.
\(v_i>0\) for every \(i\in S\).
The displayed upper-model inequality holds for every feasible displacement supported on \(S\).

notation.meaning: Prescribed set of simultaneously updated blocks.
Full-space displacement supported on blocks in S.
Canonical embedding of block i into the product space.
Block curvature weight in the separable majorant.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Separate Coordinate Bounds Need Not Majorize a Joint Update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-coordinate example showing that individual coordinate smoothness does not imply a simultaneous separable upper model with unchanged weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x_1,x_2)=\tfrac12(x_1+x_2)^2\). Along either coordinate alone the curvature is one, so \(v_1=v_2=1\) gives valid one-coordinate quadratic upper models. For \(S=\{1,2\}\), however, at \(x=0\) and \(h=(t,t)\), \[f(h)=2t^2>t^2=\tfrac12(h_1^2+h_2^2)\qquad(t\ne0).\] Thus the two individual curvature bounds do not form a valid deterministic separable upper model for the joint update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-block curvature can invalidate the simultaneous sum of otherwise valid one-coordinate upper models.
assumptions_latex: Both coordinates are updated simultaneously.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_1=v_2=1\text{ is valid for either singleton set but invalid for }S=\{1,2\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Separate Coordinate Bounds Need Not Majorize a Joint Update

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order equivalence for deterministic separable quadratic upper models on a fixed block set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in C^2(D)\) on an open convex set \(D\), fix a block set \(S\), let \(U_S\) embed its product subspace, and put \(V_S=\operatorname{blkdiag}(v_i I)_{i\in S}\). The upper model \[f(x+U_Sh)\le f(x)+\langle U_S^{\mathsf T}\nabla f(x),h\rangle+\tfrac12\langle h,V_Sh\rangle\] holds whenever \(x,x+U_Sh\in D\) if and only if \[U_S^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(z)U_S\preceq V_S\qquad\text{for every }z\in D.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic separable quadratic majorant is equivalent to uniform domination of the Hessian restricted to the simultaneously updated blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is open and convex.
\(S\) and the positive block weights \(v_i\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ has the displayed upper model on }S\ \Longleftrightarrow\ U_S^{\mathsf T}\nabla^2f(z)U_S\preceq V_S\ \forall z\in D.

notation.meaning: The embedding of the product of blocks in S into the full space.
The block-diagonal curvature matrix formed from the separable weights.

knowledge_statements.title: Serial Overapproximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-block specialization of a separable quadratic upper model under blockwise gradient smoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume that for block \(i\), the partial gradient is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz along feasible block segments. Then for every feasible displacement \(h_i\), \[f(x+U_i h_i)\leq f(x)+\langle\nabla_i f(x),h_i\rangle+\frac{L_i}{2}\lVert h_i\rVert^2.\] This is the serial overapproximation corresponding to the singleton update set \(S=\{i\}\). Because no other block moves, no simultaneous-update interaction inflation is required; any coefficient \(v_i\geq L_i\) also defines a valid, possibly more conservative, serial upper model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A serial update needs only the selected block's Lipschitz curvature; simultaneous-block interaction inflation is absent because exactly one block moves.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable on the relevant block segment.
\(\lVert\nabla_i f(x+U_i h)-\nabla_i f(x)\rVert\leq L_i\lVert h\rVert\).

notation.meaning: Lipschitz constant for the selected partial gradient.
Update set, here the singleton containing block \(i\).

children.title: Minibatch Overapproximations
