knowledge_statements.title: Minibatch Overapproximations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected separable quadratic upper model for a randomly selected minibatch of blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), let \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be a random minibatch with \(p_i=\mathbb P(i\in S)>0\), and let \(h_{[S]}\) retain blocks \(h_i\) only for \(i\in S\). A minibatch overapproximation with parameters \(v_i>0\) is the inequality
\[\mathbb E[f(x+h_{[S]})]\leq f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\left(\langle\nabla_i f(x),h_i\rangle+\frac{v_i}{2}\lVert h_i\rVert_i^2\right)\]
for every admissible \(x\) and block displacement \(h\). For \(F=f+\sum_i\psi_i\), the corresponding expected composite model adds \(\sum_i p_i(\psi_i(x_i+h_i)-\psi_i(x_i))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minibatch overapproximation bounds the expected objective after simultaneous sampled-block changes by a sum of independent blockwise linear-quadratic models, with separable nonsmooth terms added exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable on an open set containing all considered updates.
\(\psi_i\) are proper lower-semicontinuous block functions when the composite model is used.
\(S\) is sampled independently of the displacement used in the displayed conditional model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[f(x+h_{[S]})]\) admits the displayed separable upper bound.

notation.meaning: Block vector equal to h on sampled blocks and zero elsewhere.
Marginal probability that block i is sampled.

review_flags: Exact expected-separable-overapproximation source and locator are absent from the supplied inventory.
standard_field_rationale: This is the standard ESO predicate for block sampling.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation matches the minibatch ESO leaf and is mathematically coherent, including the exact expected contribution of separable nonsmooth terms for a displacement independent of the sampling. However, no source or inspectable locator supports the defining inequality and its assumptions, so the record remains needs_source.

children.title: Batch-Interaction Inflation
children.top_down_role: Additional conservatism caused by interactions among simultaneously selected blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Batch-Interaction Inflation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Curvature inflation caused by simultaneous updates of interacting blocks under uniform fixed-size sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(f=\sum_J f_J\), each component \(f_J\) depends on at most \(\omega\) blocks, and \(S\) is sampled uniformly among all subsets of size \(\tau\). If \(L_i>0\) are valid serial block-curvature constants, then the standard partial-separability minibatch model uses
\[v_i=\gamma_{\tau,\omega}L_i,\qquad \gamma_{\tau,\omega}=1+\frac{(\tau-1)(\omega-1)}{\max\{1,n-1\}}.\]
Thus \(1\leq\gamma_{\tau,\omega}\leq\min\{\tau,\omega\}\) for \(n>1\), with no inflation when \(\tau=1\) or \(\omega=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneous block updates inflate serial curvature according to batch size and interaction degree; the factor is one for serial updates or fully separable objectives.
assumptions_latex: \(n>1\), \(1\leq\tau\leq n\), and \(1\leq\omega\leq n\).
The serial constants \(L_i\) upper-bound the relevant blockwise component curvature.
The sampling is uniform without replacement with fixed cardinality \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_i=\gamma_{\tau,\omega}L_i\) accounts for minibatch interaction in the separable quadratic model.

notation.meaning: Number of blocks selected per iteration.
Maximum number of blocks on which one component function depends.

review_flags: The sharp partial-separability inflation formula requires a dedicated ESO source.
standard_field_rationale: The formula is standard for tau-nice sampling and degree-omega partial separability.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property belongs in the batch-interaction leaf, and the stated factor is the standard tau-nice partial-separability expression. Its exact normalization depends on the smoothness and ESO conventions, however, and no cited source verifies those conventions or the formula.

children.title: Arbitrary-Sampling Overapproximations

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic Matrix Characterization of an Arbitrary-Sampling ESO
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact semidefinite characterization for scalar blocks and a convex quadratic objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Ax+b^{\mathsf T}x+c\), where \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\). Let \(S\) be any random subset of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), set \(p_i=\mathbb P(i\in S)>0\), and let \(P_{ij}=\mathbb P(i,j\in S)\). For scalar blocks, weights \(v_i>0\) satisfy \[\mathbb E[f(x+h_{[S]})]\le f(x)+\sum_i p_i\nabla_i f(x)h_i+\tfrac12\sum_i p_i v_i h_i^2\quad\text{for all }x,h\] if and only if \[P\circ A\preceq\operatorname{Diag}(p_1v_1,\ldots,p_nv_n).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a quadratic objective, arbitrary-sampling ESO validity is exactly a semidefinite domination condition involving pairwise inclusion probabilities.
assumptions_latex: \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).
\(S\) is an arbitrary random subset with \(p_i>0\).
\(P_{ij}=\mathbb P(i,j\in S)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\circ A\preceq\operatorname{Diag}(p_i v_i)\ \Longleftrightarrow\ v\text{ satisfies the displayed ESO for all }x,h.

notation.meaning: The Hadamard product of inclusion probabilities and quadratic curvature.
The vector h masked to sampled coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Matrix Characterization of an Arbitrary-Sampling ESO

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equal Marginals Do Not Determine ESO Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identical marginal inclusion probabilities with different joint interactions require different ESO weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<\rho<1\) and \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Ax\), where \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\ \rho&1\end{pmatrix}\). Let \(S_{\rm ser}\) equal \(\{1\}\) or \(\{2\}\), each with probability \(1/2\), and let \(S_{\rm all}\) equal \(\varnothing\) or \(\{1,2\}\), each with probability \(1/2\). Both laws have \(p_1=p_2=1/2\). For \(S_{\rm ser}\), \(v=(1,1)\) satisfies the quadratic ESO. For \(S_{\rm all}\), these weights fail because \(\tfrac12A\npreceq\tfrac12I\), while \(v_1=v_2=1+\rho\) is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subset laws with identical marginals can require different curvature weights because their pairwise inclusion probabilities differ.
assumptions_latex: \(A=\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}\).
The two subset laws are as displayed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_i^{\rm ser}=p_i^{\rm all}=1/2\), but \(v=(1,1)\) is valid only for \(S_{\rm ser}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Equal Marginals Do Not Determine ESO Curvature

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Upward Closure and Convexity of Valid ESO Weights
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order and convexity structure of curvature vectors valid for a fixed arbitrary sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(f\), the block norms, and a sampling \(S\) with marginals \(p_i>0\). If \(v\) satisfies the expected separable overapproximation, every \(w\ge v\) componentwise also satisfies it. If \(v\) and \(w\) are valid, then \(\theta v+(1-\theta)w\) is valid for every \(\theta\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed arbitrary sampling, the valid ESO curvature vectors form a convex upward-closed set.
assumptions_latex: The objective, sampling law, marginals, and block norms are fixed.
All displayed expectations are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v,w\in\mathcal V,\ \theta\in[0,1]\Longrightarrow\{u:u\ge v\}\subseteq\mathcal V\text{ and }\theta v+(1-\theta)w\in\mathcal V.

notation.meaning: Set of valid ESO curvature vectors.

knowledge_statements.title: Upward Closure and Convexity of Valid ESO Weights

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matrix-Majorant Construction for Arbitrary-Sampling ESO Weights
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient scalar-block ESO construction from a global quadratic upper model and joint inclusion probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) satisfies \[f(x+h)\le f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),h\rangle+\tfrac12h^{\mathsf T}Mh\quad\text{for all }x,h,\] where \(M=M^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\). For an arbitrary subset sampling \(S\), let \(p_i=\mathbb P(i\in S)>0\) and \(P_{ij}=\mathbb P(i,j\in S)\). If \[P\circ M\preceq\operatorname{Diag}(p_1v_1,\ldots,p_nv_n),\] then \(v\) satisfies the arbitrary-sampling expected separable overapproximation for \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For scalar blocks, semidefinite domination involving the curvature majorant and joint inclusion probabilities supplies valid arbitrary-sampling ESO weights.
assumptions_latex: The blocks are scalar.
\(f\) admits the displayed global quadratic upper model with \(M\succeq0\).
\(p_i>0\) for every coordinate.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Majorant Construction for Arbitrary-Sampling ESO Weights

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Diagonal-Dominance Construction of Arbitrary-Sampling ESO Weights
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit scalar-block weights obtained from a global quadratic majorant and pairwise inclusion probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose f admits a global quadratic upper model with symmetric M\succeq0. Let P_{ij}=\mathbb P(i,j\in S) and p_i=P_{ii}>0. Define \[v_i=\frac{1}{p_i}\sum_{j=1}^n|P_{ij}M_{ij}|.\] Then \[P\circ M\preceq\operatorname{Diag}(p_1v_1,\ldots,p_nv_n),\] so v is valid for the scalar-block arbitrary-sampling expected separable overapproximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Absolute row sums of the sampling-weighted curvature matrix provide explicit valid ESO weights.
assumptions_latex: The blocks are scalar.
The objective admits a global quadratic upper model with symmetric \(M\succeq0\).
Every marginal inclusion probability \(p_i\) is positive.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Block-Operator Characterization of Quadratic Arbitrary-Sampling ESO
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact validity test for non-scalar blocks with declared quadratic block norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=\mathcal X_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal X_n\), let \(A:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\) be self-adjoint and positive semidefinite with block operators \(A_{ij}:\mathcal X_j\to\mathcal X_i\), and let \(f(x)=\tfrac12\langle x,Ax\rangle+\langle b,x\rangle+c\). Let \(P_{ij}=\mathbb P(i,j\in S)\), \(p_i=P_{ii}>0\), and let \(B_i\succ0\) define \(\|h_i\|_{B_i}^2=\langle h_i,B_i h_i\rangle\). Define the self-adjoint block operator \(C\) by \(C_{ij}=P_{ij}A_{ij}\). Then positive weights \(v_i\) satisfy \[\mathbb E f(x+h_{[S]})\le f(x)+\sum_i p_i\langle\nabla_i f(x),h_i\rangle+\frac12\sum_i p_iv_i\|h_i\|_{B_i}^2\quad\text{for all }x,h\] if and only if \[C\preceq\operatorname{BlkDiag}(p_1v_1B_1,\ldots,p_nv_nB_n).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a block quadratic, ESO validity is exactly positive-semidefinite domination of the sampling-weighted curvature operator by the separable block metric.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\mathcal X_i\) is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space.
\(A\) is self-adjoint and positive semidefinite.
Every \(B_i\) is self-adjoint and positive definite.
Every marginal probability satisfies \(p_i>0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected separable upper-model condition for an unrestricted distribution over block subsets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal X=\mathcal X_1\times\cdots\times\mathcal X_n\), let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\mathcal X\), and let \(S\) have any probability distribution on subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with marginals \(p_i=\mathbb P(i\in S)>0\). For \(h=(h_1,\ldots,h_n)\in\mathcal X\), let \(h_{[S]}\) equal \(h_i\) on blocks \(i\in S\) and zero elsewhere. A vector \(v\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) is valid for an arbitrary-sampling overapproximation of differentiable \(f\) if, for every admissible \(x\) and \(h\),
\[\mathbb E\!\bigl[f(x+h_{[S]})\bigr]\leq f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\langle\nabla_i f(x),h_i\rangle+\frac12\sum_{i=1}^n p_i v_i\lVert h_i\rVert_i^2.\]
The joint law of \(S\), not merely its marginals, determines which vectors \(v\) satisfy this condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any block-subset distribution, valid curvature weights make the expected sampled update no larger than a separable linear-quadratic model; correlations may affect those weights.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse component decomposition used by partial-separability overapproximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A block function \(f\) is partially separable with interaction family \(\mathcal J\) if \[f(x)=\sum_{J\in\mathcal J}f_J(x_J),\] where each component \(f_J\) depends only on blocks indexed by \(J\). Its degree of partial separability is \[\omega=\max_{J\in\mathcal J}|J|.\] Blocks \(i\) and \(j\) interact in this representation only if some \(J\in\mathcal J\) contains both.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partially separable objective is a sum of components involving small block subsets; the largest component support is its interaction degree.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal J\) is a finite family of nonempty block-index sets.
Each \(f_J\) is defined on the product of blocks indexed by \(J\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \omega=\max_{J\in\mathcal J}|J|\text{ bounds the number of blocks coupled within any component.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sampling-aware upper model obtained by summing sparse component interactions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=\sum_{J\in\mathcal J}f_J(x_J)\), where each \(f_J\) depends only on blocks in \(J\). Assume constants \(L_{J,i}\geq0\) satisfy
\[f_J(x_J+u_J)\leq f_J(x_J)+\sum_{i\in J}\langle\nabla_i f_J(x),u_i\rangle+\frac{|J|}{2}\sum_{i\in J}L_{J,i}\lVert u_i\rVert_i^2.\]
For a random subset \(S\) with \(p_i>0\), a valid conservative separable expected model is obtained with
\[v_i=\sum_{J\ni i}L_{J,i}\,\mathbb E[|J\cap S|\mid i\in S].\]
Hence sparse interaction sets reduce curvature relative to bounds based on all \(n\) blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decomposing the objective into sparsely interacting components yields curvature weights governed by the expected number of simultaneously sampled neighbors in each component.

A dedicated source is required to determine the correct normalization rather than weakening the claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Serial Proximal Coordinate Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-block proximal-gradient update for a block-separable composite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(F(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_i(x_i)\), an iterate \(x^k\), positive block curvature \(L_i\), and a selected block \(i_k\), compute
\[d_{i_k}^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{d}\left\{\langle\nabla_{i_k}f(x^k),d\rangle+\frac{L_{i_k}}2\lVert d\rVert_{i_k}^2+\psi_{i_k}(x_{i_k}^k+d)\right\}.\]
Set \(x_{i_k}^{k+1}=x_{i_k}^k+d_{i_k}^k\) and \(x_j^{k+1}=x_j^k\) for \(j\neq i_k\). Stop when a prescribed coordinate-stationarity residual is below tolerance; otherwise select the next block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, minimize a proximal quadratic model on one block and leave every other block unchanged, stopping when coordinate stationarity is sufficiently small.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and has blockwise Lipschitz gradients with valid constants \(L_i>0\).
Each \(\psi_i\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, and each displayed block subproblem has a minimizer.
The block-selection rule visits every block infinitely often for convergence use.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is the last iterate after the one-block proximal updates satisfy the prescribed stopping test.

notation.meaning: Proximal displacement on the selected block.

\[F(x^k+U_id)\le F(x^k)+Q_i^k(d),\]
one has
\[F(x^k+U_id_i^k)\le F(x^k)-\frac{L_i}{2}\|d_i^k\|_i^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a convex strongly convex block model, an exact serial proximal coordinate step decreases the objective by at least half the block-model modulus times the squared displacement.

knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Proximal Block Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random blockwise proximal-gradient descent for separable composite regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(x)=f(x)+\sum_i\psi_i(x_i)\), choose probabilities \(p_i>0\) with \(\sum_i p_i=1\). At iteration \(k\), draw \(i_k\) conditionally independently with \(\mathbb P(i_k=i)=p_i\), compute
\[d_i^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{d}\left\{\langle\nabla_i f(x^k),d\rangle+\frac{v_i}{2}\lVert d\rVert_i^2+\psi_i(x_i^k+d)\right\},\]
for \(i=i_k\), and set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+U_i d_i^k\). Stop at a fixed budget or when an estimated stationarity measure meets tolerance; output the last iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Draw a block with positive probability, solve its proximal quadratic model, and update only that block until a budget or stationarity test is met.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable with valid block upper-model constants \(v_i>0\).
Each \(\psi_i\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, and the sampled subproblem is solvable.
Every block has positive sampling probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}=x^k+U_{i_k}d_{i_k}^k\) is the randomized proximal block update.

notation.meaning: Canonical embedding of block i into the full space.
Block curvature used in the proximal model.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q_i^k(0)=0\), suppose \(Q_i^k\) is \(v_i\)-strongly convex, and let \(d_i^k\in\arg\min_dQ_i^k(d)\). If
\[F(x^k+U_id)\le F(x^k)+Q_i^k(d),\]
then
\[F(x^k+U_id_i^k)\le F(x^k)-\frac{v_i}{2}\|d_i^k\|_i^2.\]
Thus
\[\mathbb E_k[F(x^{k+1})]\le F(x^k)-\frac12\sum_i p_iv_i\|d_i^k\|_i^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With convex strongly convex block models, exact randomized block-proximal updates decrease the objective in conditional expectation by a probability-weighted sum of squared block displacements.
assumptions_latex: Each normalized block model \(Q_i^k\) is \(v_i\)-strongly convex with \(v_i>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected O(1/k) objective rate for randomized block proximal gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit expected suboptimality bound for convex RBPG with uniform block sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose Assumption 11.21 holds, \(f\) is convex, and \(\{x^k\}_{k\ge0}\) is generated by RBPG for the stated problem. For any \(x^*\in X^*\) and every \(k\ge0\), \[\mathbb E_{\xi_k}\bigl[F(x^{k+1})\bigr]-F_{\mathrm{opt}}\le\frac{p}{p+k+1}\left(\frac12\|x^0-x^*\|_L^2+F(x^0)-F_{\mathrm{opt}}\right).\] In particular, the expected objective residual is \(O(1/k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any optimizer, the expected objective gap after the next RBPG update is at most p divided by p+k+1 times the sum of half the initial weighted squared distance and the initial objective gap. Hence the expected objective residual decreases at order 1/k.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Notation used in the convergence analysis of randomized block proximal gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(k\ge1\), define the sampling history \(\xi_{k-1}=\{i_0,i_1,\ldots,i_{k-1}\}\). For \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_p)\) and \(L_i>0\), define \[\|x\|_L=\left(\sum_{i=1}^p L_i\|x_i\|^2\right)^{1/2},\qquad \|x\|_{L,*}=\left(\sum_{i=1}^p\frac{1}{L_i}\|x_i\|^2\right)^{1/2}.\] At an iterate \(x^k\), define \[\widetilde G(x^k)=\bigl(G_{L_1}^1(x^k),G_{L_2}^2(x^k),\ldots,G_{L_p}^p(x^k)\bigr).\] If \(L_1=\cdots=L_p=L\), then \(\widetilde G(x^k)=G_L(x^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The RBPG analysis records the sampled-block history, uses a block-Lipschitz-weighted norm and its dual, and stacks all block gradient mappings into one aggregate mapping. When all block constants are equal, the aggregate mapping is the usual proximal-gradient mapping.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relative accuracy for an approximate proximal block solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Normalize the selected block model by \(Q_i^k(0)=0\), and let \(q_i^{k,*}=\inf_dQ_i^k(d)>-\infty\). For \(\eta_k\in[0,1)\), an approximate displacement \(d_i^k\) has relative model accuracy when
\[Q_i^k(d_i^k)-q_i^{k,*}\le\eta_k(-q_i^{k,*}),\]
equivalently,
\[Q_i^k(d_i^k)\le(1-\eta_k)q_i^{k,*}\le0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative-accuracy rule requires an approximate block step to realize at least a prescribed fraction of the best model decrease.

notation.meaning: Infimum of the selected block model.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure without decay or relative control of block-solver errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(x)=\tfrac12x^2\), use \(Q^k(d)=x^kd+\tfrac12d^2\). Its minimizer is \(d_*^k=-x^k\), with \(\inf_dQ^k(d)=-\tfrac12(x^k)^2\). If \(\varepsilon_k\ge\tfrac12(x^k)^2\), then \(d^k=0\) satisfies
\[Q^k(0)\le\inf_dQ^k(d)+\varepsilon_k.\]
Selecting this admissible displacement forever leaves every nonzero initial point unchanged and nonstationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An uncontrolled additive tolerance can admit the zero step forever, even for a scalar strongly convex quadratic.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon_k\ge\tfrac12(x^k)^2\).

notation.meaning: Scalar proximal quadratic model at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Additive Model Error Controls Distance to the Exact Block Step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric meaning of additive inexactness for a strongly convex proximal block model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_i^k\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(v_i\)-strongly convex, with \(v_i>0\), and let \(d_i^{k,*}=\arg\min_dQ_i^k(d)\). If \[Q_i^k(d_i^k)\le Q_i^k(d_i^{k,*})+\varepsilon_k,\] then \[\|d_i^k-d_i^{k,*}\|_i\le\sqrt{\frac{2\varepsilon_k}{v_i}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity converts additive block-model error into distance from the exact proximal coordinate step.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_i^k\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(v_i\)-strongly convex.
The approximate solve has additive error \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aggregate Block-Model Decrease Rate under Relative Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer iteration rate for uniform randomized inexact proximal-coordinate updates, measured by exact block-model decreases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_i(x_i), and suppose each block model Q_i^k satisfies \[F(x^k+U_id)\le F(x^k)+Q_i^k(d),\qquad Q_i^k(0)=0.\] Define \(\Delta_i(x^k)=-\inf_dQ_i^k(d)\ge0\). At iteration k, sample i_k uniformly and return d^k satisfying relative model accuracy with \(\eta_k\le\bar\eta<1\). If F is bounded below by F_{\inf}, then for every K\ge1, \[\min_{0\le k<K}\mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{i=1}^n\Delta_i(x^k)\right]\le\frac{n\,[F(x^0)-F_{\inf}]}{(1-\bar\eta)K}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform relative-accuracy block solves retain an inverse-linear outer rate in aggregate exact block-model decrease, slowed by the factor 1/(1−η).
assumptions_latex: The objective has smooth-plus-block-separable composite form.
Every block model majorizes its corresponding one-block objective change.
Blocks are sampled uniformly.
The relative model-error factors satisfy \(\eta_k\le\bar\eta<1\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete outer iteration using one fixed relative block-model convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_i(x_i)\), sample block \(i_k\) with \(\mathbb P(i_k=i\mid\mathcal F_k)\ge p_{\min}>0\) and form \[Q_{i_k}^k(d)=\langle\nabla_{i_k}f(x^k),d\rangle+\frac{v_{i_k}}2\|d\|^2+\psi_{i_k}(x_{i_k}^k+d)-\psi_{i_k}(x_{i_k}^k),\qquad Q_{i_k}^k(0)=0.\] With \(q_k^*=\inf_dQ_{i_k}^k(d)\), compute \(d^k\) satisfying \[Q_{i_k}^k(d^k)-q_k^*\le\eta_k(-q_k^*),\qquad0\le\eta_k\le\bar\eta<1,\] and set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+U_{i_k}d^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each selected proximal block model is solved to a fixed relative fraction of its best possible decrease before the coordinate update is committed.
assumptions_latex: Every block model has finite attained infimum and \(v_i>0\).
Each block model majorizes the corresponding one-block objective change.
\(\mathbb P(i_k=i\mid\mathcal F_k)\ge p_{\min}>0\) for every block and iteration.
\(0\le\eta_k\le\bar\eta<1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Aggregate Model-Decrease Bound with Additive Errors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer convergence estimate for uniform randomized additive-error block solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(i_k\) is conditionally uniform, \(F(x^k+U_id)\le F(x^k)+Q_i^k(d)\), and \[Q_{i_k}^k(d^k)\le\inf_dQ_{i_k}^k(d)+\varepsilon_k.\] Define \(\Delta_i(x^k)=-\inf_dQ_i^k(d)\ge0\). If \(F\ge F_{\inf}\), then \[\min_{0\le k<K}\mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{i=1}^n\Delta_i(x^k)\right]\le\frac{n}{K}\left(F(x^0)-F_{\inf}+\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\mathbb E[\varepsilon_k]\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform randomized inexact coordinate updates retain inverse-linear outer progress when cumulative expected additive model error is finite.
assumptions_latex: Blocks are sampled uniformly conditionally on the past.
Each block model majorizes its one-block objective change and satisfies \(Q_i^k(0)=0\).
The objective is bounded below.

Inexact Proximal Coordinate Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate proximal-gradient update whose block subproblem is solved to certified additive accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For selected block \(i_k\), define
\[Q_i^k(d)=\langle\nabla_i f(x^k),d\rangle+\frac{v_i}{2}\lVert d\rVert_i^2+\psi_i(x_i^k+d)-\psi_i(x_i^k).\]
Given \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\), choose \(d_{i_k}^k\) satisfying
\[Q_{i_k}^k(d_{i_k}^k)\leq\inf_d Q_{i_k}^k(d)+\varepsilon_k,\]
and set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+U_{i_k}d_{i_k}^k\). Continue until the prescribed global stationarity or iteration test holds. Convergence guarantees normally require a stated control such as \(\sum_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\) or accuracy proportional to the model decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The selected block model need only be solved within an explicit error tolerance; convergence requires a compatible rule controlling accumulated or relative errors.
assumptions_latex: \(v_i>0\), and each block model has finite infimum.
The block-selection rule provides persistent coverage of all blocks.
The error sequence satisfies the convergence theorem's specified summability or relative-accuracy condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each update is an \(\varepsilon_k\)-accurate proximal coordinate step for the selected block model.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Summable Proximal Time Can Converge Nonstationarily
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of stationarity when positive proximal parameters have no nonsummability or lower-bound condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x_1,x_2)=\tfrac12(x_1^2+x_2^2)\), start with \(x_1^0x_2^0\ne0\), and use the same \(\lambda_k>0\) for both exact block updates in sweep \(k\), where \(\sum_k\lambda_k<\infty\). Each update is
\[x_i^{k+1}=\frac{x_i^k}{1+\lambda_k}.\]
Hence
\[x_i^k=x_i^0\prod_{j<k}(1+\lambda_j)^{-1}\longrightarrow x_i^\infty\ne0.\]
The objective decreases and successive displacements vanish, but \(\nabla F(x^\infty)=x^\infty\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive but summable proximal parameters can make exact alternating proximal minimization stop short of stationarity, despite descent and vanishing steps.
assumptions_latex: \(\lambda_k>0\) and \(\sum_k\lambda_k<\infty\).

notation.meaning: Common proximal parameter used during sweep k.

knowledge_statements.title: Summable Proximal Time Can Converge Nonstationarily

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descent produced by exact cyclic proximal block minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^{k,0}=x^k\) and let \(x^{k,i}\) be the mixed iterate after block \(i\) is updated. Then
\[F(x^{k,i})+\frac{1}{2\lambda_i^k}\|x_i^{k,i}-x_i^{k,i-1}\|_i^2\le F(x^{k,i-1}).\]
Consequently,
\[F(x^{k+1})+\sum_{i=1}^m\frac{1}{2\lambda_i^k}\|x_i^{k+1}-x_i^k\|_i^2\le F(x^k).\]
If \(F\) is bounded below and \(\lambda_i^k\le\bar\lambda<\infty\), then \(\sum_k\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2<\infty\) for the product norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each exact proximal block minimization decreases the objective by its proximal movement penalty; a lower objective bound and uniformly bounded proximal parameters make squared sweep displacements summable.
assumptions_latex: Every displayed block subproblem is solved exactly.
\(F\) is bounded below for the summability conclusion.
\(0<\lambda_i^k\le\bar\lambda<\infty\).

notation.meaning: Mixed iterate after block i in sweep k.
Uniform upper bound on proximal parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Sweepwise Sufficient Decrease

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criticality estimate derived from exact smooth unconstrained proximal block optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be differentiable with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, and let an exact cyclic proximal sweep use \(\lambda_i^k\ge\underline\lambda>0\). If \(x^{k,i}\) is the mixed iterate after updating block \(i\), then \[\nabla_iF(x^{k,i})+\frac{x_i^{k+1}-x_i^k}{\lambda_i^k}=0.\] Consequently there is a constant \(C\), depending only on \(L\), the block decomposition, and \(\underline\lambda\), such that \[\|\nabla F(x^{k+1})\|\le C\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For smooth unconstrained blocks, exact proximal block optimality bounds the final gradient by the sweep displacement.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is differentiable with Lipschitz gradient.
Blocks are unconstrained.
Each block subproblem is solved exactly.
\(\lambda_i^k\ge\underline\lambda>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KL Convergence of Smooth Alternating Proximal Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Whole-sequence convergence for exact cyclic proximal block minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be continuously differentiable with Lipschitz gradient on a neighborhood of a bounded level set containing the iterates. Suppose exact cyclic proximal block minimization is used with \(0<\underline\lambda\le\lambda_i^k\le\overline\lambda<\infty\), and suppose \(F\) has the Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz property on the cluster set. Then the sweepwise sufficient-decrease and stationarity-residual bounds hold uniformly, \(\sum_k\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|<\infty\), and the whole sequence converges to a stationary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded exact alternating proximal minimization converges as a whole under uniform parameter bounds and KL geometry.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is continuously differentiable with Lipschitz gradient near the relevant bounded level set.
Every block subproblem is solved exactly.
\(0<\underline\lambda\le\lambda_i^k\le\overline\lambda<\infty\).
\(F\) has the KL property on the cluster set.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_i\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and suppose \(u\mapsto F(x_{<i}^{k+1},u,x_{>i}^k)\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. If \(x_i^{k+1}\) exactly minimizes this block slice plus \(\|u-x_i^k\|^2/(2\lambda_i^k)\) over \(X_i\), where \(\lambda_i^k>0\), then \[0\in \partial_iF(x^{k,i})+\frac{x_i^{k+1}-x_i^k}{\lambda_i^k}+N_{X_i}(x_i^{k+1}).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every exact convex alternating proximal block solve yields a blockwise subgradient-plus-normal-cone optimality certificate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity implication when an exact alternating proximal sweep makes no block changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every block slice is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on its closed convex block set. If an exact alternating proximal sweep from x returns x unchanged, then for every block i, \[0\in\partial_iF(x)+N_{X_i}(x_i).\] Thus x is coordinatewise stationary. If the chosen subdifferential is block-regular so that these block inclusions combine into \(0\in\partial F(x)+N_X(x)\), then x is stationary for the full product-constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unchanged exact proximal sweep certifies coordinatewise stationarity; full stationarity additionally requires block regularity.
assumptions_latex: Every block slice is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonquadratic proximal variant of cyclic mixed-iterate block minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\prod_{i=1}^mX_i\), and let each differentiable generator \(h_i\) be strongly convex on \(X_i\), with \(D_{h_i}(u,v)=h_i(u)-h_i(v)-\langle\nabla h_i(v),u-v\rangle\). Update cyclically by \[x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in X_i}\left\{F(x_{<i}^{k+1},u,x_{>i}^k)+\frac{1}{\lambda_i^k}D_{h_i}(u,x_i^k)\right\},\qquad\lambda_i^k>0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Bregman variant alternates exact block minimizations regularized by a block-adapted nonquadratic proximity measure.
assumptions_latex: Each \(X_i\) is nonempty and each displayed block subproblem attains a minimizer.
Each \(h_i\) is differentiable and strongly convex on its block domain.
\(\lambda_i^k>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KL-Exponent Rate Alternatives for Alternating Proximal Sweeps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rate classification once an alternating proximal sequence satisfies uniform descent and relative error near its limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an alternating proximal sequence \((x^k)\) converges to \(x^*\), and eventually satisfies \[F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\ge a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x^{k+1}))\le b\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|,\] where \(a,b>0\). Assume that near \(x^*\), \(F\) has a KL inequality with \(\varphi(s)=cs^{1-\theta}\), where \(c>0\) and \(\theta\in[0,1)\). For \(r_k=F(x^k)-F(x^*)\), finite termination occurs when \(\theta=0\); for \(0<\theta\le1/2\), \(r_k\le Cq^k\) for some \(q\in(0,1)\); and for \(1/2<\theta<1\), \(r_k=O(k^{-1/(2\theta-1)})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform descent, relative error, and a KL exponent yield finite, geometric, or polynomial objective convergence for alternating proximal sweeps.
assumptions_latex: The sequence converges to \(x^*\) and eventually remains in a KL neighborhood.
The displayed descent and limiting-subdifferential relative-error bounds hold with uniform positive constants.
\(F(x^k)\downarrow F(x^*)\).

notation.meaning: Objective residual relative to the limiting critical value.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonsmooth Separable KL Convergence of Alternating Proximal Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Whole-sequence convergence for exact cyclic proximal minimization of a smooth coupling plus block-separable nonsmooth terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Psi(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m r_i(x_i)\), where \(f\) is continuously differentiable with Lipschitz gradient on a neighborhood of the bounded iterate sequence and each \(r_i\) is proper and lower semicontinuous. Perform exact cyclic mixed-iterate block minimization with quadratic terms \(\|u-x_i^k\|^2/(2\lambda_i^k)\), where \(0<\underline\lambda\le\lambda_i^k\le\overline\lambda<\infty\). Assume \(\Psi\) is bounded below, has the Kurdyka--Łojasiewicz property on the cluster set, and is value-continuous along iterate subsequences converging to that set. Then constants \(a,b>0\) exist such that \[\Psi(x^k)-\Psi(x^{k+1})\ge a\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|^2,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\Psi(x^{k+1}))\le b\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|.\] Consequently \(\sum_k\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|<\infty\), and \(x^k\) converges to a limiting-critical point \(x^*\) with \(0\in\partial\Psi(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded exact alternating proximal iterates for a smooth coupling plus separable lower-semicontinuous terms converge to one critical point under uniform parameter bounds, KL geometry, and cluster-value continuity.
assumptions_latex: \(\Psi=f+\sum_i r_i\) is proper and bounded below, and every \(r_i\) is proper and lower semicontinuous.
\(f\) has a Lipschitz-continuous gradient near the bounded iterate sequence.
Every cyclic block subproblem is solved exactly.
\(0<\underline\lambda\le\lambda_i^k\le\overline\lambda<\infty\).
\(\Psi\) has the KL property on the cluster set.
Whenever an iterate subsequence converges to a cluster point \(\bar x\), its objective values converge to \(\Psi(\bar x)\).

notation.meaning: Possibly nonsmooth block-separable term, including a block-constraint indicator.

Alternating Proximal Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cyclic exact block minimization stabilized by proximal quadratic terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\) be proper and bounded below on \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\), and choose \(\lambda_i^k>0\). Starting from \(x^0\in X\), update blocks cyclically. With
\[z_i^k=(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_{i-1}^{k+1},x_i^k,x_{i+1}^k,\ldots,x_m^k),\]
choose
\[x_i^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in X_i}\left\{F(x_1^{k+1},\ldots,x_{i-1}^{k+1},u,x_{i+1}^k,\ldots,x_m^k)+\frac{1}{2\lambda_i^k}\lVert u-x_i^k\rVert_i^2\right\}.\]
After a full sweep, stop when successive iterates or a stationarity residual meet tolerance; otherwise repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cycle through the blocks, exactly minimizing the objective in each current block plus a proximal term that penalizes movement from its previous value.
assumptions_latex: Each displayed proximal block subproblem attains a minimizer.
The feasible set has product form \(X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\).
The proximal parameters \(\lambda_i^k\) are positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: One sweep produces \(x^{k+1}\) by sequential proximal minimization over all blocks.

notation.meaning: Mixed iterate immediately before block i is updated.
Positive proximal parameter for block i.

abla f(x)+N_X(x)\); for convex \(f\), this is equivalent to global optimality over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The displacement of a block projected-gradient step is an exact block stationarity residual on a product constraint set.
assumptions_latex: Each \(X_i\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(f\) is differentiable.
\(\alpha_i>0\).

notation.meaning: Convex normal cone of the block feasible set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Single-Block Projection Does Not Handle Coupled Equalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary of the product-constraint assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{x\in\mathbb R^2:x_1+x_2=1\}\) and \(x=(1/2,1/2)\). If only coordinate \(1\) changes, feasibility forces its displacement to be zero. The coordinate projection of \(X\) onto the first axis is all of \(\mathbb R\), so independently projecting a nonzero scalar gradient step generally changes \(x_1\) and violates \(x_1+x_2=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globally coupled equality cannot generally be preserved by independently projecting one coordinate.
assumptions_latex: Only coordinate 1 is updated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x+te_1\in X\iff t=0\), whereas projection onto the first-coordinate image \(\mathbb R\) permits \(t\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Single-Block Projection Does Not Handle Coupled Equalities

children.title: Pairwise Coordinate Updates
children.top_down_role: Coupled two-coordinate moves preserving global constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Singleton Updates Can Be Frozen by a Coupled Equality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why two-coordinate moves are minimally necessary for a simplex-type equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=1\}\), every feasible direction supported on one coordinate is zero, because \(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}(te_i)=t\). In contrast, \(e_i-e_j\) is a nonzero feasible pairwise direction. Thus a method restricted to feasible singleton moves stagnates at every feasible point even when a feasible pairwise descent direction exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sum constraint eliminates nonzero singleton moves but permits mass transfer between two coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\{x:\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=1\}\).
Feasible directions must preserve the equality.
knowledge_statements.title: Singleton Updates Can Be Frozen by a Coupled Equality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical representation of pairwise moves preserving one linear equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a^{\mathsf T}x=b\) and distinct indices \(i,j\), a direction supported on \(\{i,j\}\) preserves the equality exactly when \(a_id_i+a_jd_j=0\). If \((a_i,a_j)\ne(0,0)\), this one-dimensional nullspace is spanned by \[d^{ij}=a_je_i-a_ie_j.\] Every equality-preserving pairwise update therefore has the form \(x^+=x+td^{ij}\), with \(t\) restricted further by any remaining constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pairwise move preserves one linear equality precisely when it lies in the selected pair's nullspace.
assumptions_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x=b\).

notation.meaning: Canonical equality-preserving direction supported on coordinates i and j.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Coordinate Nullspace Direction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pairwise Stationarity Test on the Simplex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order stationarity test using all feasible mass-transfer pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Delta=\{x\ge0:\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=1\}\) and let \(f\) be differentiable. A point \(x\in\Delta\) is first-order stationary if and only if \[
abla_j f(x)-
abla_i f(x)\ge0\quad	ext{for every }i	ext{ with }x_i>0	ext{ and every }j.\] Equivalently, all positive coordinates have gradient equal to \(\min_j
abla_j f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simplex point is stationary exactly when no feasible transfer from a positive donor coordinate to any recipient coordinate is descending.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\Delta\).
\(f\) is differentiable at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Stationarity Test on the Simplex

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasible Pairwise Step Interval under Box Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact bound truncation for a two-coordinate equality-preserving direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in[\ell,u]\) and let \(d\) be supported on \(\{i,j\}\). The scales preserving the box form the closed interval \[I(x,d)=\bigcap_{r\in\{i,j\}:d_r>0}\left[\frac{\ell_r-x_r}{d_r},\frac{u_r-x_r}{d_r}\right]\cap\bigcap_{r\in\{i,j\}:d_r<0}\left[\frac{u_r-x_r}{d_r},\frac{\ell_r-x_r}{d_r}\right].\] If \(a^{\mathsf T}x=b\) and \(a^{\mathsf T}d=0\), then \(x+td\in[\ell,u]\cap\{z:a^{\mathsf T}z=b\}\) exactly when \(t\in I(x,d)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Box feasibility truncates an equality-preserving pairwise move to an explicitly computable interval.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in[\ell,u]\).
\(d\) is supported on two coordinates.
\(a^{\mathsf T}x=b\) and \(a^{\mathsf T}d=0\) for the equality conclusion.

notation.meaning: Maximal feasible scale interval along the pairwise direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible Pairwise Step Interval under Box Bounds

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sufficient Decrease from a Bound-Truncated Pairwise Quadratic Step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step descent for an equality-preserving pair direction under a directional quadratic upper model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let d be an equality-preserving pairwise direction, let I be its feasible scale interval with 0\in I, and suppose \[f(x+td)\le f(x)+tg+\frac{H}{2}t^2\quad(t\in I),\qquad g=\langle\nabla f(x),d\rangle,\ H>0.\] If t^*=\operatorname{proj}_I(-g/H), then \[f(x+t^*d)\le f(x)-\frac{H}{2}|t^*|^2\le f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projecting the unconstrained minimizer of a valid pairwise quadratic model onto the feasible interval gives quantified descent.
assumptions_latex: The direction \(d\) preserves the coupled equality.
The interval \(I\) is the feasible scale interval and contains zero.
The displayed directional quadratic upper model holds with \(H>0\).

notation.meaning: Directional derivative along the pairwise direction

knowledge_statements.title: Sufficient Decrease from a Bound-Truncated Pairwise Quadratic Step

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximal-Violation Pairwise Quadratic Step on the Simplex
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete donor–recipient iteration specialized to simplex feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Delta=\{x\ge0:\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=1\}\). At \(x^k\in\Delta\), choose \[i_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{i:x_i^k>0}
abla_i f(x^k),\qquad j_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_j
abla_j f(x^k),\] set \(d^k=e_{j_k}-e_{i_k}\), and choose \(H_k>0\) such that \[f(x^k+td^k)\le f(x^k)+t\langle
abla f(x^k),d^kangle+ rac{H_k}{2}t^2\quad(0\le t\le x_{i_k}^k).\] Set \[t_k=\min\!\left\{x_{i_k}^k, rac{
abla_{i_k}f(x^k)-
abla_{j_k}f(x^k)}{H_k}ight\},\qquad x^{k+1}=x^k+t_kd^k.\] Stop when \(
abla_{i_k}f(x^k)-
abla_{j_k}f(x^k)\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transfer mass from the positive coordinate with largest gradient to the coordinate with smallest gradient, using the feasible minimizer of a quadratic upper model.
assumptions_latex: \(x^0\in\Delta\) and \(f\) is differentiable on a neighborhood of \(\Delta\).
Each \(H_k>0\) is a valid curvature bound on the selected feasible segment.
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Positive donor coordinate with maximal gradient.

knowledge_statements.title: Maximal-Violation Pairwise Quadratic Step on the Simplex

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional complexity for nontruncated maximal-violation simplex transfers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\Delta=\{x\ge0:\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x=1\}\), define \(G(x)=\max_{i:x_i>0}\nabla_i f(x)-\min_j\nabla_j f(x)\). Suppose \(0<H_k\le\overline H\), and call iteration \(k\) productive when \(t_k=G(x^k)/H_k\) is not truncated. If \(f(x^k)-f(x^{k+1})\ge H_kt_k^2/2\) and \(f\ge f_{\inf}\), then for the productive iterations \(\mathcal P_K\) before \(K\), \[\min_{k\in\mathcal P_K}G(x^k)^2\le\frac{2\overline H[f(x^0)-f_{\inf}]}{|\mathcal P_K|}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Non-drop pairwise steps attain an inverse-linear best squared-violation bound; a total iteration rate additionally requires control of donor-exhausting steps.
assumptions_latex: The maximal-violation donor and recipient are selected.
\(0<H_k\le\overline H\).
Every counted iteration is untruncated.
\(f\) is bounded below by \(f_{\inf}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Pairwise Line Minimization under One Coupled Equality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact pair update for a box intersected with one linear equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[\ell,u]\cap\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x=b\}\) and \(x^k\in X\). Choose distinct \(i_k,j_k\) with \((a_{i_k},a_{j_k})\ne(0,0)\), set \(d^k=a_{j_k}e_{i_k}-a_{i_k}e_{j_k}\), and let \(I_k=\{t:x^k+td^k\in[\ell,u]\}\). Choose \[t_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{t\in I_k}f(x^k+td^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=x^k+t_kd^k.\] Then \(x^{k+1}\in X\) and \(f(x^{k+1})\le f(x^k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exactly minimize over the box-feasible segment of a two-coordinate direction that preserves the coupled equality.
assumptions_latex: \(x^k\in X\).
The restricted one-dimensional problem attains a minimizer.

Equality-preserving direction supported on the selected coordinates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Connectivity of an Allowed Pair Graph Characterizes Tangent-Space Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear reachability of simplex-preserving pair directions under restrictions on eligible coordinate pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=([n],E)\) be an undirected graph and \(\mathcal D_E=\{e_i-e_j:\{i,j\}\in E\}\). If \(C_1,\ldots,C_c\) are its connected components, then \[\operatorname{span}\mathcal D_E=\left\{d\in\mathbb R^n:\sum_{i\in C_r}d_i=0\text{ for }r=1,\ldots,c\right\},\qquad \dim\operatorname{span}\mathcal D_E=n-c.\] Consequently, the allowed pair directions span \(\{d:\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}d=0\}\) exactly when \(G\) is connected. If \(G\) is disconnected, every sequence of allowed pairwise updates preserves \(\sum_{i\in C_r}x_i\) separately for each component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allowed mass-transfer pairs generate every sum-preserving direction exactly when their pair graph is connected; disconnected eligibility preserves additional componentwise masses.
assumptions_latex: \(G=([n],E)\) is undirected.
Allowed directions are scalar multiples of \(e_i-e_j\) for \(\{i,j\}\in E\).

notation.meaning: Equality-preserving directions associated with allowed pairs.
Connected components of the allowed-pair graph.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global stopping test supplementing optimality of the restricted subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_i(x)\ge0\) be block residuals such that \(r_i(x)=0\) for every \(i\) if and only if \(x\) is stationary for the full problem. For working set \(W\), a global tolerance certificate is \[\max_{i\in W}r_i(x)\le\varepsilon\quad\text{and}\quad\max_{i\notin W}r_i(x)\le\varepsilon,\] equivalently \(\max_i r_i(x)\le\varepsilon\). Restricted optimality alone tests only active blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solving the active subproblem is not a global stopping certificate; excluded blocks must also pass the stationarity test.
assumptions_latex: The residual family jointly detects full stationarity.
\(W\) is the current working set.
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Stationarity violation associated with block i.

knowledge_statements.title: Working-Set Exclusion Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal nonstarvation condition for working-set stationarity arguments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A working-set rule has persistent-violation admission if, for every block \(i\) and every \(\delta>0\), \[r_i(x^k)\ge\delta\ \text{for all sufficiently large }k\quad\Longrightarrow\quad i\in W_k\ \text{for infinitely many }k.\] This excludes convergence arguments based only on restricted optimality while a uniformly nonzero excluded-block violation persists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any block whose stationarity violation remains bounded away from zero must re-enter the working set infinitely often.
assumptions_latex: \(r_i(x^k)\) is a declared block stationarity residual.
\(W_k\) is the iteration-k working set.

notation.meaning: Working set selected at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Permanent Exclusion Can Produce False Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary for working-set selection rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=\tfrac12(x_1-1)^2+\tfrac12(x_2-1)^2\), start from \(x^0=(0,0)\), and take \(W_k=\{1\}\) for every \(k\). Exact minimization over the working set reaches \(x=(1,0)\), after which every restricted step is zero, but \(\nabla_2F(1,0)=-1\). Thus restricted optimality and a zero active-set step do not imply full stationarity when a persistently violating block is permanently excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A working-set method can stop at a nonstationary point if it permanently excludes a violating block.
assumptions_latex: \(W_k=\{1\}\) for every k.
Each restricted subproblem is solved exactly.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract convergence result coupling working-set selection with restricted-step decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x^k)\) be nonincreasing and bounded below, set \(R_k=\max_i r_i(x^k)\), and suppose the working set contains an index \(i_k\) satisfying \(r_{i_k}(x^k)\ge\theta R_k\) for some \(\theta>0\). If the accepted restricted update satisfies \[F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\ge c\,r_{i_k}(x^k)^2\] for a constant \(c>0\), then \(R_k\to0\). If \(R_k=0\) exactly characterizes stationarity, every accumulation point at which the residuals are continuous is stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Admitting a fixed fraction of the largest violation and obtaining quadratic sufficient decrease forces the full working-set residual to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(F(x^k)\) is bounded below.
\(r_{i_k}(x^k)\ge\theta\max_i r_i(x^k)\).
The aggregate residual detects stationarity and is continuous at accumulation points.

Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be closed and convex, let \(F\) be differentiable, and let \(r_i(x)\ge0\) jointly characterize stationarity. Choose \(W_k\) containing \(i_k\) with \[r_{i_k}(x^k)\ge	heta\max_i r_i(x^k),\qquad	heta\in(0,1].\] For \(B_k\succeq mI\), compute \[d^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}\left\{\langle
abla F(x^k),dangle+	frac12\langle d,B_kdangle:x^k+d\in X,\ d_i=0\ (i
otin W_k)ight\}.\] Backtrack over \(t_k\in\{1,\gamma,\gamma^2,\ldots\}\) until \[F(x^k+t_kd^k)\le F(x^k)+\sigma t_k\langle
abla F(x^k),d^kangle,\] then set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+t_kd^k\). Stop only when \(\max_i r_i(x^k)\le\varepsilon\).

If \(W_k\) contains \(i_k\) with \(r_{i_k}(x^k)\ge\theta R(x^k)\), and \(d^k\) exactly minimizes the displayed model over displacements supported on \(W_k\), with \(x^{k+1}=x^k+d^k\), then \[F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\ge\tfrac12r_{i_k}(x^k)\ge\tfrac\theta2R(x^k),\] and \[\min_{0\le k<K}R(x^k)\le\frac{2[F(x^0)-F_{\inf}]}{\theta K},\qquad R(x^k)\to0.\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible model minimization restricted to a selected subset of variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_{x\in X}F(x)\), where \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) and \(\mathbb R^d\) is partitioned into \(n\) coordinate blocks. At iteration \(k\), choose a working set \(W_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), a model vector \(g^k\in\mathbb R^d\), a self-adjoint model operator \(B_k:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\), and a proper model term \(R_k:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). Define
\[M_k(d)\coloneqq F(x^k)+\langle g^k,d\rangle+\frac12\langle d,B_kd\rangle+R_k(d).\]
Compute
\[d^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{M_k(d):x^k+d\in X,\ d_i=0\text{ for }i\notin W_k\},\]
possibly followed by a feasibility-preserving line search, and set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+t_kd^k\) with \(t_k\in(0,1]\). Stop when the working-set optimality test also certifies that no excluded block violates the prescribed stationarity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select active blocks, minimize a local model over feasible displacements supported there, and stop only when both active and excluded blocks pass stationarity tests.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global-optimality test for a differentiable concave dual objective on a Cartesian feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A=\prod_{i=1}^n\mathcal A_i\) be a nonempty convex Cartesian product, let \(D:\mathcal A\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable and concave, and define \[\Delta_i(\alpha)=\sup\{D(\alpha+t e_i)-D(\alpha):\alpha_i+t\in\mathcal A_i\}.\] Then \(\alpha\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\beta\in\mathcal A}D(\beta)\) if and only if \(\Delta_i(\alpha)=0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a convex product domain, a differentiable concave dual objective is globally maximized exactly when no feasible coordinate change improves it.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is differentiable and concave on \(\mathcal A\).
\(\mathcal A\) is a nonempty convex Cartesian product.
The coordinate suprema are well defined in \([0,+\infty]\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Randomized Exact Coordinate-Ascent Linear Rate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected linear convergence for unconstrained strongly concave smooth dual coordinate ascent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable and \(\mu\)-strongly concave, and suppose \(|\nabla_iD(\alpha+t e_i)-\nabla_iD(\alpha)|\le L_i|t|\) with \(L_i>0\). If \(i_k\) is sampled uniformly and \(\alpha^{k+1}\) exactly maximizes \(D\) along coordinate \(i_k\), then, for \(L_{\max}=\max_iL_i\), \[\mathbb E[D^*-D(\alpha^k)]\le\left(1-\frac{\mu}{nL_{\max}}\right)^k[D^*-D(\alpha^0)].\] Consequently, expected dual error at most \(\varepsilon\) is reached after at most \(\left\lceil\frac{nL_{\max}}{\mu}\log\frac{D^*-D(\alpha^0)}{\varepsilon}\right\rceil\) updates whenever \(0<\varepsilon<D^*-D(\alpha^0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform randomized exact dual coordinate ascent converges linearly under strong concavity and coordinate smoothness, with condition factor n times the largest coordinate curvature divided by the strong-concavity modulus.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is differentiable and \(\mu\)-strongly concave on \(\mathbb R^n\), with \(\mu>0\).
Each coordinate derivative is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz along its coordinate line.
Coordinates are sampled independently and uniformly, and each selected coordinate is maximized exactly.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A=\{(a,b)\in[0,1]^2:a=b\}\) and \(D(a,b)=-(a-1)^2\). From every \((t,t)\in\mathcal A\), no nonzero change of only one coordinate is feasible. Exact one-coordinate ascent therefore stalls at every feasible point, although only \((1,1)\) maximizes \(D\) over \(\mathcal A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coupled feasibility can prohibit every single-coordinate move, so coordinatewise stalling need not imply dual optimality.
assumptions_latex: Each update must change only one coordinate while remaining in \(\mathcal A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((t,t)\) is coordinatewise immovable for every \(t\in[0,1]\), but is globally optimal only for \(t=1\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence in value and cluster-point optimality for cyclic exact coordinate maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A=\prod_{i=1}^n\mathcal A_i\) be compact and convex, and let \(D\) be continuously differentiable and concave on a neighborhood of \(\mathcal A\). Suppose coordinates are visited cyclically, each coordinate restriction is maximized exactly, and every coordinate subproblem has a unique maximizer. Then \(D(\alpha^k)\) is nondecreasing and converges to \(\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A}D(\alpha)\); every cluster point of \((\alpha^k)\) is a global maximizer. If the global maximizer is unique, then \(\alpha^k\) converges to it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a compact product domain, cyclic exact coordinate ascent with unique coordinate solutions converges in value, and all of its cluster points are dual optima.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is a compact convex Cartesian product.
\(D\) is continuously differentiable and concave on a neighborhood of \(\mathcal A\).
Coordinates are updated cyclically by exact maximization.
Every coordinate subproblem has a unique maximizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D(\alpha^k)\uparrow\max_{\alpha\in\mathcal A}D(\alpha)\) and every cluster point belongs to \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{\mathcal A}D\).

knowledge_statements.title: Cyclic Exact Dual Coordinate-Ascent Convergence
Dual Coordinate Ascent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Serial or randomized ascent obtained by maximizing a concave dual objective along one coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D:\mathcal A\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) be a proper concave dual objective on a convex feasible set \(\mathcal A\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). Starting from \(\alpha^0\in\mathcal A\), select \(i_k\) cyclically or with positive probabilities and compute
\[t_k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{t:\,\alpha^k+t e_{i_k}\in\mathcal A}D(\alpha^k+t e_{i_k}).\]
Set \(\alpha^{k+1}=\alpha^k+t_ke_{i_k}\). A model-based variant may maximize a certified coordinatewise concave lower model instead. Stop when the dual coordinate-improvement residual is below tolerance; output \(\alpha^k\) and any associated primal reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose one dual coordinate, maximize the feasible one-dimensional dual restriction exactly or through a certified ascent model, and repeat until coordinate improvement is negligible.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is proper and concave, and \(\alpha^0\in\operatorname{dom}D\cap\mathcal A\).
Every selected one-dimensional subproblem attains a maximizer.
The selection rule visits every nonfixed coordinate infinitely often for convergence use.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha^{k+1}\in\mathcal A\) and \(D(\alpha^{k+1})\geq D(\alpha^k)\) for the exact coordinate maximization step.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Attainment Requirement for an SDCA Coordinate Subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-definedness condition omitted by bare proper closed convex loss assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[D(\alpha)=-\frac1n\sum_j\phi_j^*(-\alpha_j)-\frac{\lambda}{2}\left\|\frac1{\lambda n}\sum_j\alpha_ja_j\right\|^2,\] an exact update on coordinate \(i\) requires \(t\mapsto D(\alpha+te_i)\) to attain its supremum. It suffices that this function be upper semicontinuous and that, for some \(t_0\), its upper level set \(\{t:D(\alpha+te_i)\ge D(\alpha+t_0e_i)\}\) be compact. Equivalently, it suffices that the negative coordinate objective be proper, lower semicontinuous, and coercive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact SDCA requires attainment of every selected one-dimensional dual maximum; proper closed convex losses alone do not state this requirement.
assumptions_latex: \(\lambda>0\).
The displayed dual objective is proper at the current iterate.
Coordinate \(i\) is selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under the displayed compact-level-set condition, \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{t\in\mathbb R}D(\alpha+te_i)\ne\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Convex Loss Assumptions Need Not Ensure Coordinate Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-definedness counterexample for exact SDCA.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take \(n=1\), \(a_1=0\), and let \(\phi^*(u)=e^u\), with \(\phi=(\phi^*)^*\). Then \(\phi\) is proper, closed, and convex, while the dual coordinate objective is \[D(\alpha)=-e^{-\alpha}\] up to an additive constant. Its supremum is \(0\), approached as \(\alpha\to+\infty\), but no finite maximizer exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper closed convex loss can yield a dual coordinate objective whose finite supremum is unattained.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume every \(\phi_i\) is convex and \(1/\gamma\)-smooth, \(\|a_i\|\le R\), and each iteration uniformly selects one coordinate and exactly maximizes the displayed regularized-ERM dual along it. If a dual maximizer \(\alpha^*\) exists, then, under the stated \(1/n\) primal normalization, \[\mathbb E[D(\alpha^*)-D(\alpha^k)]\le\left(1-\frac1{n+R^2/(\lambda\gamma)}\right)^k[D(\alpha^*)-D(\alpha^0)].\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-dimensional Fenchel optimality condition for a selected example-wise dual update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the regularized-ERM dual \[D(\alpha)=-\frac1n\sum_j\phi_j^*(-\alpha_j)-\frac\lambda2\|w(\alpha)\|^2,\qquad w(\alpha)=\frac1{\lambda n}\sum_j\alpha_ja_j,\] suppose the maximum of \(t\mapsto D(\alpha+te_i)\) is attained at \(\Delta\). Then \(\Delta\) is an exact coordinate maximizer if and only if \[0\in-\partial\phi_i^*(-\alpha_i-\Delta)+a_i^{\mathsf T}w(\alpha)+\frac{\Delta\|a_i\|^2}{\lambda n}.\] When \(\phi_i^*\) is differentiable, the inclusion reduces to a scalar root equation.

Stochastic Dual Coordinate Ascent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Serial SDCA for quadratic-regularized finite-sum empirical risk minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the primal problem \(\min_{w\in\mathbb R^d} P(w)=\frac{\lambda}{2}\lVert w\rVert^2+\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_i(a_i^{\mathsf T}w)\), initialize \(\alpha^0\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(w^0=(\lambda n)^{-1}\sum_i\alpha_i^0a_i\). At iteration \(k\), sample \(i_k\) with positive probability and choose \(\Delta_k\) maximizing the concave dual objective \[D(\alpha)=-\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_i^*(-\alpha_i)-\frac{\lambda}{2}\left\lVert\frac1{\lambda n}\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i a_i\right\rVert^2\] along coordinate \(i_k\). Set \(\alpha^{k+1}=\alpha^k+\Delta_k e_{i_k}\), \(w^{k+1}=w^k+\Delta_k a_{i_k}/(\lambda n)\), and stop when a prescribed duality-gap tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SDCA randomly selects one example, exactly or approximately maximizes the dual along its coordinate, and incrementally maintains the associated primal vector until the duality gap is small.
assumptions_latex: \(\lambda>0\) and \(a_i\in\mathbb R^d\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\).
Each \(\phi_i:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex.
Every coordinate is sampled with strictly positive probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha^{k+1}\) differs from \(\alpha^k\) in one coordinate and satisfies \(D(\alpha^{k+1})\ge D(\alpha^k)\) when the coordinate subproblem is solved exactly.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,Y_1,\ldots,Y_m\) be finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, let \(A_i:X\to Y_i\) be linear, and consider \(\min_{x\in X} g(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(A_i x)\). Write the dual minimization objective on \(Y_1\oplus\cdots\oplus Y_m\) as \(F(y)=g^*(-\sum_iA_i^*y_i)+\sum_i f_i^*(y_i)\). Initialize \(y^0\) and define \(x^k=\nabla g^*(-\sum_iA_i^*y_i^k)\). At iteration \(k\), select block \(i_k\), choose \(\tau_{i_k}>0\), and update \[y_{i_k}^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\tau_{i_k}f_{i_k}^*}\!\left(y_{i_k}^k+\tau_{i_k}A_{i_k}x^k\right),\qquad y_j^{k+1}=y_j^k\quad(j\ne i_k).\] Output \(y^k\) and recover \(x^k\); stopping may use the primal-dual gap or a block-residual tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method updates one dual block by a proximal step on its nonsmooth conjugate while holding all other dual blocks fixed and recovering a coupled primal point.

For \(y=(y_1,\ldots,y_m)\in Y_1\oplus\cdots\oplus Y_m\), set \(s(y)=-\sum_{i=1}^m A_i^*y_i\). If \(g\) is strongly convex, then \(g^*\) is differentiable and the canonical recovered primal point is \[x(y)=\nabla g^*(s(y)).\] Equivalently, \(s(y)\in\partial g(x(y))\). If \((x^*,y^*)\) satisfies the primal-dual optimality conditions, then \(x(y^*)=x^*\).

Thus a change in one dual coordinate changes both its local Fenchel relation and, through the adjoint sum, the global stationarity relation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X,Y_1,\ldots,Y_m\) be finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, let \(A_i:X\to Y_i\) be linear, let \(x\in X\), and let \(y=(y_1,\ldots,y_m)\in Y_1\oplus\cdots\oplus Y_m\). Define \[\mathcal G(x,y)=g(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(A_i x)+g^*\!\left(-\sum_{i=1}^mA_i^*y_i\right)+\sum_{i=1}^m f_i^*(y_i).\] Whenever every displayed value is finite, Fenchel inequalities imply \(\mathcal G(x,y)\ge0\). Moreover, \(\mathcal G(x,y)=0\) exactly when \(-\sum_iA_i^*y_i\in\partial g(x)\) and \(y_i\in\partial f_i(A_i x)\) for all \(i\). Hence \(\mathcal G(x,y)\le\varepsilon\) is a directly checkable \(\varepsilon\)-duality-gap certificate for every \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate the primal objective and conjugate dual terms. Their nonnegative sum certifies optimality at zero and an epsilon primal-dual gap when at most epsilon.

knowledge_statements.title: Recovery Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of stable single-valued recovery without curvature in the primal regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The recovery relation \(x\in\partial g^*(s)\), with \(s=-\sum_iA_i^*y_i\), need not define a unique or Lipschitz primal point when \(g\) lacks strong convexity. For example, on \(\mathbb R\), \(g(x)=0\) gives \(g^*=\delta_{\{0\}}\) and \(\partial g^*(0)=\mathbb R\), so the same aggregate dual value \(s=0\) admits every primal point. Quantitatively, for \(g_\mu(x)=\mu x^2/2\), recovery is \(x_\mu(s)=s/\mu\); its Lipschitz constant \(1/\mu\) diverges as \(\mu\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without strong convexity, dual-to-primal recovery can be multivalued; as curvature vanishes, even unique recovery can become arbitrarily sensitive to dual perturbations.
assumptions_latex: Recovery is defined through the Fenchel relation \(s\in\partial g(x)\).
The examples use the Euclidean space \(\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Removing a positive strong-convexity modulus destroys any uniform single-valued Lipschitz guarantee for the recovery map.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonexpansive Operator Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric definition of the nonexpansive fixed-point regime on a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and \(T:H\to H\). The operator \(T\) is nonexpansive precisely when \[\lVert Tx-Ty\rVert\le \lVert x-y\rVert\qquad\text{for all }x,y\in H.\] Thus its global Lipschitz constant is at most one. This condition permits equality and therefore does not itself impose strict distance decrease, asymptotic regularity, or convergence of the unrelaxed Picard iteration \(x^{k+1}=Tx^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonexpansive operator never increases pairwise distances, although equality may occur and its direct fixed-point iteration need not converge.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(T\) is defined on all of \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) is nonexpansive if and only if \(\operatorname{Lip}(T)\le1\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic geometry of the fixed-point set of a nonexpansive self-map on a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a real Hilbert space and let \(T:C\to C\) be nonexpansive. Then \(\operatorname{Fix}T=\{x\in C:Tx=x\}\) is closed and convex, possibly empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The fixed-point set of a nonexpansive self-map of a closed convex Hilbert-space set is closed and convex, although existence is not guaranteed.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty closed convex subset of a real Hilbert space.
\(T:C\to C\) is nonexpansive.
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Convex Fixed-Point Set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-limit identification for residuals of nonexpansive maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a closed convex subset of a real Hilbert space and let \(T:C\to C\) be nonexpansive. If \(x^k\rightharpoonup x\in C\) and \(x^k-Tx^k\to0\) strongly, then \(Tx=x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonexpansive map, a weak limit whose residual converges strongly to zero must be a fixed point.
assumptions_latex: \(T:C\to C\) is nonexpansive.
\(x^k\rightharpoonup x\) and \((I-T)x^k\to0\).

children.title: Averaged-Operator Regimes
children.top_down_role: Coordinate fixed-point settings governed by averaged map structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Averaged-Operator Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard alpha-averaged representation for fixed-point operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). An operator \(T:H\to H\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged when there exists a nonexpansive operator \(R:H\to H\) such that \[T=(1-\alpha)I+\alpha R.\] Equivalently, \(I-T=\alpha(I-R)\). The parameter range excludes the endpoint \(\alpha=1\), where the representation reduces to mere nonexpansiveness rather than proper averagedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An alpha-averaged operator is a strict convex combination of the identity and a nonexpansive operator, with alpha strictly between zero and one.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged exactly when \(T=(1-\alpha)I+\alpha R\) for some nonexpansive \(R\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A valid averagedness parameter for finite compositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_j:H\to H\) be \(\alpha_j\)-averaged with \(0<\alpha_j<1\) for \(j=1,\ldots,r\), and set \(s=\sum_{j=1}^r\alpha_j/(1-\alpha_j)\). Then \(T_1\circ\cdots\circ T_r\) is \(s/(1+s)\)-averaged. For two operators this parameter equals \[(\alpha_1+\alpha_2-2\alpha_1\alpha_2)/(1-\alpha_1\alpha_2).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite compositions of averaged operators remain averaged, with an explicit valid parameter.
assumptions_latex: All operators act on the same real Hilbert space.
\(0<\alpha_j<1\) for every \(j\).
review_flags: The displayed parameter is a valid general composition parameter and need not be minimal.
knowledge_statements.title: Composition of Averaged Operators

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure of averaged operators under finite convex mixtures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_j:H\to H\) be \(\alpha_j\)-averaged with \(0<\alpha_j<1\), let \(\omega_j\ge0\) satisfy \(\sum_{j=1}^r\omega_j=1\), and define \(T=\sum_{j=1}^r\omega_jT_j\) and \(\alpha=\sum_{j=1}^r\omega_j\alpha_j\). Then \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite convex mixture of proper averaged operators remains averaged, with the weighted-average parameter.
assumptions_latex: Each \(T_j\) is \(\alpha_j\)-averaged with \(0<\alpha_j<1\).
\(\omega_j\ge0\) and \(\sum_j\omega_j=1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Combinations of Averaged Operators

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nesting of proper averaged classes as the averaging parameter increases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(T:H\to H\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged and \(0<\alpha\le\beta<1\), then \(T\) is \(\beta\)-averaged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An alpha-averaged operator is also beta-averaged for every larger proper parameter beta.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\alpha\le\beta<1\).
\(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity of Averagedness Parameters

children.title: Averagedness Within Nonexpansiveness
children.top_down_role: Structural distinction between general nonexpansive maps and their averaged subclass.

assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a nonzero real Hilbert space.
\(T:H\to H\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged with \(0<\alpha<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\) is nonexpansive and obeys the displayed strengthened inequality; on a nonzero Hilbert space, proper averagedness is strictly stronger than nonexpansiveness.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict inclusion and residual inequality for averaged operators on a nonzero Hilbert space.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a nonzero real Hilbert space. If \(T:H\to H\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged for some \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), then for every \(x,y\in H\), \[\lVert Tx-Ty\rVert^2\le \lVert x-y\rVert^2-\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}\lVert (I-T)x-(I-T)y\rVert^2.\] Consequently, every averaged operator is nonexpansive. The converse fails in general: nonexpansiveness alone supplies no positive coefficient multiplying the residual-difference term. Hence, on a nonzero Hilbert space, the class of properly averaged operators is a strict subclass of the nonexpansive operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a nonzero Hilbert space, averaged operators are nonexpansive and satisfy an additional residual decrease inequality, while some nonexpansive operators are not averaged for any alpha below one.
knowledge_statements.title: Averagedness Within Nonexpansiveness

source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent residual formulation of proper averagedness within the nonexpansive hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) and \(0<\alpha<1\). The following are equivalent: \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged; for all \(x,y\in H\), \[\lVert Tx-Ty\rVert^2\le\lVert x-y\rVert^2-\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}\lVert(I-T)x-(I-T)y\rVert^2;\] and \(I-T\) is \(1/(2\alpha)\)-cocoercive, meaning \[\langle(I-T)x-(I-T)y,x-y\rangle\ge\frac{1}{2\alpha}\lVert(I-T)x-(I-T)y\rVert^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alpha-averagedness is equivalent to the strengthened nonexpansive inequality and to cocoercivity of the residual.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Cocoercivity Characterization

children.title: Nonaveraged Boundary Cases
children.top_down_role: Nonexpansive coordinate maps lacking the stronger averaged structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonaveraged Boundary Cases
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A nonexpansive isometry lying outside every proper averaged class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On any nonzero real Hilbert space \(H\), let \(T=-I\). Then \(\lVert Tx-Ty\rVert=\lVert x-y\rVert\), so \(T\) is nonexpansive. If \(T=(1-\alpha)I+\alpha R\) for \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), then \(R=(1-\alpha^{-1})I+\alpha^{-1}T=(1-2/\alpha)I\). Its Lipschitz constant is \(\lvert1-2/\alpha\rvert>1\), contradicting nonexpansiveness of \(R\). Therefore \(-I\) is not \(\alpha\)-averaged for any \(\alpha<1\); moreover, \(x^{k+1}=Tx^k\) oscillates whenever \(x^0\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negation is nonexpansive but not properly averaged. Its unrelaxed fixed-point iteration alternates between a nonzero point and its negative.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a nonzero real Hilbert space.
\(I\) denotes the identity on \(H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(-I\) is nonexpansive, belongs to no \(\alpha\)-averaged class with \(0<\alpha<1\), and its Picard iterates can fail to converge.

knowledge_statements.title: Contractive Coordinate-Operator Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected linear contraction under uniform single-coordinate updates of a contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=H_1\oplus\cdots\oplus H_m\), let \(T:H\to H\) satisfy \(\lVert Tx-Ty\rVert\le q\lVert x-y\rVert\) with \(0\le q<1\), and let \(x^*\) be its unique fixed point. From \(x^k\), sample \(i_k\) uniformly and set \(x_{i_k}^{k+1}=T_{i_k}x^k\), leaving all other blocks unchanged. Then \[\mathbb E\!\left[\lVert x^{k+1}-x^*\rVert^2\mid x^k\right]\le\left(1-\frac{1-q^2}{m}\right)\lVert x^k-x^*\rVert^2.\] Consequently, the expected squared error decreases geometrically under repeated independent sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly updating one component of a contraction yields geometric expected squared-error decay, slowed by the number of coordinate blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is the orthogonal direct sum of \(m<\infty\) Hilbert blocks.
\(T\) is a global contraction with modulus \(q<1\).
Coordinates are sampled independently and uniformly.
