knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided conversion between fixed-point residual and distance to the unique fixed point of a contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be a contraction with modulus \(q\in[0,1)\), and let \(x^*\) be its unique fixed point. Then, for every \(x\in H\), \[(1-q)\lVert x-x^*\rVert\le \lVert x-Tx\rVert\le(1+q)\lVert x-x^*\rVert.\] Consequently, \(\lVert x-Tx\rVert\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(\lVert x-x^*\rVert\le\varepsilon/(1-q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a contraction, residual and fixed-point error are equivalent, yielding an explicit residual stopping certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a Hilbert space.
\(\lVert Tx-Ty\rVert\le q\lVert x-y\rVert\) for some \(q<1\).

notation.meaning: Unique fixed point of the contraction.

knowledge_statements.title: Contractive Residual Error Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tail and iteration bounds for uniform single-coordinate iteration of a contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the uniform single-coordinate iteration of the seed theorem, set \(r=1-(1-q^2)/m\). For every \(k\ge0\) and \(\varepsilon,\delta>0\), \[\mathbb P\bigl(\lVert x^k-x^*\rVert>\varepsilon\bigr)\le \frac{r^k\lVert x^0-x^*\rVert^2}{\varepsilon^2}.\] Thus probability at least \(1-\delta\) of \(\varepsilon\)-accuracy is guaranteed whenever \[k\ge \frac{\bigl[\log(\lVert x^0-x^*\rVert^2/(\delta\varepsilon^2))\bigr]_+}{-\log r}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The expected coordinate-contraction rate gives an explicit high-probability iteration bound.
assumptions_latex: The global operator is a \(q\)-contraction with \(q<1\).
One block is sampled independently and uniformly at each iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed iteration bound implies \(\mathbb P(\lVert x^k-x^*\rVert\le\varepsilon)\ge1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.title: High-Probability Coordinate Contraction Bound

children.title: Block-Iterative Fixed-Point Updates
children.top_down_role: Fixed-point schedules updating selected operator components over recurring windows.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Iterative Fixed-Point Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic block schedule with an essentially cyclic coverage condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=H_1\oplus\cdots\oplus H_m\) and \(T=(T_1,\ldots,T_m):H\to H\). Choose \(x^0\in H\), relaxation parameters \(\lambda_k>0\), and nonempty active sets \(I_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), update \[x_i^{k+1}=\begin{cases}x_i^k+\lambda_k(T_i x^k-x_i^k),&i\in I_k,\\x_i^k,&i\notin I_k.\end{cases}\] Require an integer \(M\ge1\) such that \(\bigcup_{j=k}^{k+M-1}I_j=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) for every \(k\). Stop when \(\lVert Tx^k-x^k\rVert\) is below tolerance, and output \(x^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, relax selected fixed-point components and retain inactive components; every block must be activated within each bounded window.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a finite product of Hilbert spaces.
Every component \(T_i x\) is evaluable for the current iterate.
The active-set schedule satisfies bounded-window coverage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration produces blockwise relaxed fixed-point updates while ensuring that no coordinate remains inactive for more than \(M-1\) consecutive iterations.

notation.meaning: Set of blocks activated at iteration \(k\).

children.title: Direct Coordinate-Friendly Operators
children.top_down_role: Operators admitting inexpensive direct component evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct Coordinate-Friendly Operators
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-based definition for direct evaluation of one output block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H=\mathcal H_1\oplus\cdots\oplus\mathcal H_m\), let \(P_i:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H_i\) be the coordinate projections, and let \(T:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\). Write \(T_i=P_iT\). Relative to a fixed computational model, \(T\) is directly coordinate-friendly if every \(T_i(x)\) can be evaluated from \(x\) without first evaluating all of \(T(x)\), and its worst-case cost \(c_i\) satisfies \(c_i\leq Cc/m\), where \(c\) is the cost of evaluating \(T(x)\) and \(C\) is independent of \(m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An operator is directly coordinate-friendly when any output block can be computed from the current point at roughly one block’s share of the full evaluation cost.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m\mathcal H_i\) is a finite product Hilbert space.
Evaluation costs are measured in one fixed computational model.

notation.meaning: Costs of one block evaluation and a full operator evaluation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical structural sufficient condition for direct coordinate evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:\bigoplus_{i=1}^m\mathcal H_i\to\bigoplus_{i=1}^m\mathcal H_i\) have product form \(T(x)=(T_1x_1,\ldots,T_mx_m)\). If block evaluation costs are balanced and full evaluation costs \(\Theta(\sum_i c_i)\), then each output block can be evaluated without other blocks and has cost \(O(c/m)\), where \(c\) is the full evaluation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A balanced block-product operator is directly coordinate-friendly because each output block depends only on its matching input block.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is block local in the declared decomposition.
Block evaluation costs are balanced.
Full and block costs use the same computational model.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m\mathcal H_i\), let \(P_i:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H_i\) be the coordinate projections, and let \(T:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\). The operator \(T\) is extended coordinate-friendly if there exist a state space \(\mathcal Z\), a consistency map \(S:\mathcal H\to\mathcal Z\), block evaluators \(E_i:\mathcal H_i\times\mathcal Z\to\mathcal H_i\), and state updates \(U_i:\mathcal Z\times\mathcal H_i\times\mathcal H_i\to\mathcal Z\) such that, whenever \(z=S(x)\), one has \(E_i(x_i,z)=P_iT(x)\), and, after replacing \(x_i\) by \(x_i^+\), one has \(U_i(z,x_i,x_i^+)=S(x+P_i^*(x_i^+-x_i))\). Relative to a fixed computational model, both \(E_i\) and \(U_i\) must cost \(O(c/m)\), where \(c\) is the cost of evaluating the full operator and constructing its consistent state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended coordinate-friendly operator exposes cheap block evaluations through auxiliary information that can itself be updated cheaply and consistently after each block change.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stale Auxiliary State Invalidates Extended Coordinate Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness boundary for cache-based block evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the maintained-linear-image representation, suppose the authoritative iterate changes from \(x\) to \(x+P_j^*\Delta_j\), but the state remains \(z=Ax\) rather than \(z^+=z+A_j\Delta_j\). A subsequent query returns \(A_i^*\phi(z)\), whereas the required block is \(A_i^*\phi(z+A_j\Delta_j)\). Unless these coincide, the query evaluates the operator at an obsolete point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a committed block change is omitted from the cache, later cheap block queries generally evaluate the wrong point.
assumptions_latex: A block change is committed without its required state update.
The queried block is sensitive to the omitted state increment.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale Auxiliary State Invalidates Extended Coordinate Evaluation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical extended coordinate-friendly representation for linearly coupled operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[A_1\ \cdots\ A_m]\) act on \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\), and let \(T_i(x)=A_i^*\phi(Ax)\). Maintain \(z=Ax\). Then \(T_i(x)=A_i^*\phi(z)\), and after changing block \(x_i\) to \(x_i^+\), exact consistency is restored by \(z^+=z+A_i(x_i^+-x_i)\). Thus \(T\) is extended coordinate-friendly whenever the block query and state update each cost \(O(c/m)\) relative to full evaluation with state construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintaining a shared linear image converts a globally coupled output into a cheap block query and exact incremental state update.
assumptions_latex: Initially \(z=Ax\).
Only one block changes per committed update.
The block query and state update satisfy the declared \(O(c/m)\) cost bound.

notation.meaning: Column block associated with input block i.

knowledge_statements.title: Maintained Linear-Image State

children.title: Coordinate-Friendly Operator Compositions
children.top_down_role: Coordinate evaluation and state maintenance for composed operators.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A composition whose single output block costs as much as the full output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R^m\), let \(G=I\) and let \(F(y)=(s(y),\ldots,s(y))\), where \(s(y)=\sum_{j=1}^m y_j\). Under the arithmetic model counting scalar reads and additions, evaluating one coordinate of \(F\circ G\) from an uncached input costs \(\Theta(m)\), while evaluating the full vector also costs \(\Theta(m)\). Hence the composition is not directly coordinate-friendly because one coordinate does not cost \(O(c/m)=O(1)\). Maintaining \(s(x)\) as auxiliary state restores constant-cost queries and updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global reduction can make one output coordinate as expensive as the full output, although a maintained sum restores extended coordinate friendliness.
assumptions_latex: No cached global sum is available for direct evaluation.
Scalar input access and addition have unit cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Global-Reduction Composition Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient condition for extended coordinate friendliness of a composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=F\circ G:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\), where \(\mathcal H=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m\mathcal H_i\). Suppose there are a state space \(\mathcal Z\), a consistency map \(S:\mathcal H\to\mathcal Z\), block evaluators \(E_i\), and block-change updates \(U_j\) such that \(E_i(x_i,S(x))=P_iF(G(x))\) and \(U_j(S(x),x_j,x_j^+)=S(x+P_j^*(x_j^+-x_j))\). If every required evaluation and state update costs \(O(c_T/m)\), where \(c_T\) is the cost of full composition evaluation with consistent-state construction, then \(T\) is extended coordinate-friendly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composition is extended coordinate-friendly when exact maintained intermediate state supports cheap output-block queries and cheap updates after every block change.
assumptions_latex: The state initially equals \(S(x)\).
Every committed block change applies its exact state update.
Evaluation and maintenance costs use the same model as \(c_T\).

notation.meaning: Consistent intermediate state for the composition.
Output-block evaluator and block-change state updater.

knowledge_statements.title: Maintained-State Closure for Composed Operators

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct coordinate friendliness under partition-preserving composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m\mathcal H_i\), \(\mathcal Y=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m\mathcal Y_i\), \(G(x)=(G_1x_1,\ldots,G_mx_m)\), and \(F(y)=(F_1y_1,\ldots,F_my_m)\). Then \(P_i(F\circ G)(x)=F_i(G_i(x_i))\). If the block costs of \(G_i\) and \(F_i\) are at most \(C_Gc_G/m\) and \(C_Fc_F/m\), and the full-composition cost is comparable to \(c_G+c_F\), then \(F\circ G\) is directly coordinate-friendly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two maps preserving the same block partition remain directly coordinate-friendly under composition, with their block costs adding.
assumptions_latex: Both maps preserve the same block partition.
Costs use one computational model.
Full-composition cost is comparable to \(c_G+c_F\).

notation.meaning: Aligned inner and outer block maps.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient closure rule for coordinate evaluation through a composition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=F\circ G\), where \(G:\mathcal H\to\mathcal Y\), \(F:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal H\), and \(\mathcal H=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m\mathcal H_i\). Suppose a maintained state \(z_G\) determines exactly the data \(q_i(G(x))\) required to evaluate \(P_iF(G(x))\). If a change of block \(x_j\) permits updating \(z_G\) and all affected \(q_i\) incrementally, then \(T_i(x)=P_iF(G(x))\) is evaluable from \((x_i,z_G)\). Consequently, the composition is extended coordinate-friendly whenever the combined block-evaluation and state-update costs are \(O(c_T/m)\), with \(c_T\) the full-composition cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composition remains coordinate-friendly when maintained intermediate data suffices for each requested output block and can be updated cheaply after a block change.
assumptions_latex: The maintained intermediate state is exact for the current iterate.
Every affected intermediate quantity has an incremental update rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\circ G\) is extended coordinate-friendly if its per-block evaluation and maintenance cost is \(O(c_T/m)\).

notation.meaning: Intermediate information required by output block i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Almost-Sure Convergence Under IID Random Block Activation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical convergence result for randomized activation of the accepted coordinate iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the finite-dimensional product setting, \(\operatorname{zer}(A+B)\ne\varnothing\), \(B\) is \(\beta\)-cocoercive, and \(0<\gamma<2\beta\). Let \(T=J_{\gamma A}(I-\gamma B)\) and \(\alpha=2\beta/(4\beta-\gamma)\). Suppose the nonempty activation masks are independent and identically distributed, independent of the initial iterate, and every block is activated with positive probability. If \[0<\underline\lambda\leq\lambda_k\leq\overline\lambda<1/\alpha,\] then the accepted relaxed coordinate iteration converges almost surely to a random point in \(\operatorname{zer}(A+B)\), and every block residual \(P_i(Tx^k-x^k)\) converges almost surely to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With cocoercivity, a solution, IID positive-probability block coverage, and admissible relaxation, randomized coordinate forward–backward iterates converge almost surely to an inclusion zero.

\(A\) is maximally monotone and \(B\) is \(\beta\)-cocoercive.
\(\operatorname{zer}(A+B)\ne\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Primal–Dual Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selected-block updates for a convex primal–dual saddle system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For proper lower-semicontinuous convex \(f:\mathcal X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), \(g:\mathcal Y\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and bounded linear \(K:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y\), initialize \((x^0,y^0)\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathcal H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(\gamma>0\). For every \(x\in\mathcal H\), \[J_{\gamma\partial f}(x)=(I+\gamma\partial f)^{-1}(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)=\mathop{\arg\min}_{u\in\mathcal H}\left\{f(u)+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\lVert u-x\rVert^2\right\}.\] Equivalently, \(u=J_{\gamma\partial f}(x)\) if and only if \((x-u)/\gamma\in\partial f(u)\). If, additionally, \(\mathcal H=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m\mathcal H_i\), \(P_i:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H_i\) are the coordinate projections, and \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\) with each \(f_i:\mathcal H_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex, then \(P_iJ_{\gamma\partial f}(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f_i}(x_i)\) for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The resolvent of a convex subdifferential is exactly the proximal map; when the Hilbert space, objective, and squared norm separate by blocks, the identity holds independently on each block.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A maximally monotone resolvent whose coordinates are coupled.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R^2\), let \(A(x_1,x_2)=(-x_2,x_1)\). This continuous skew-symmetric linear operator is maximally monotone. For \(\gamma>0\), \[J_{\gamma A}(x_1,x_2)=\frac{1}{1+\gamma^2}(x_1+\gamma x_2,\,x_2-\gamma x_1).\] Thus neither output coordinate is determined by its matching input coordinate alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A skew coupling is maximally monotone, but both coordinates of its resolvent depend on both input coordinates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact structural boundary for independent block evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:\mathcal H\rightrightarrows\mathcal H\) be maximally monotone on \(\mathcal H=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m\mathcal H_i\), and let \(\gamma>0\). The resolvent has the product form \(J_{\gamma A}(x)=(J_1x_1,\ldots,J_mx_m)\), with firmly nonexpansive \(J_i\), if and only if \(A=A_1\times\cdots\times A_m\) for maximally monotone \(A_i\); then \(J_i=J_{\gamma A_i}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximal monotone resolvent separates by blocks exactly when its operator is a Cartesian product of block operators.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is maximally monotone.
The decomposition is an orthogonal finite product.

notation.meaning: Firmly nonexpansive block component of the product resolvent.

knowledge_statements.title: Cartesian-Product Criterion for Block-Separable Resolvents
Nonseparable Resolvent Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A coupled quadratic showing failure of independent coordinate resolvent evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R^m\) with \(m\geq2\), define \(f(x)=\tfrac12(\sum_{j=1}^m x_j)^2\) and let \(A=\partial f\). Writing \(\mathbf 1=(1,\ldots,1)\), the resolvent is \[J_{\gamma A}(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)=x-\frac{\gamma}{1+\gamma m}(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}x)\mathbf 1.\] Hence \(P_iJ_{\gamma A}(x)=x_i-\frac{\gamma}{1+\gamma m}\sum_jx_j\), which depends on every input coordinate. Therefore nonseparability prevents evaluation from \(x_i\) alone; a coordinate implementation must either access all blocks or maintain the global sum as auxiliary state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rank-one coupled quadratic has proximal coordinates depending on the sum of every input block, so direct local resolvent evaluation fails without global or maintained state.
assumptions_latex: \(m\geq2\) and \(\gamma>0\).
Direct coordinate evaluation is restricted to the local input block without auxiliary state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resolvent of this nonseparable subdifferential is not directly block-separable.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m\mathcal H_i\), let \(P_i:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H_i\) be the coordinate projections, and let \(T:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\). Initialize \(x^0\in\mathcal H\). At iteration \(k\), choose a nonempty block set \(S_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), freeze the snapshot \(\bar x=x^k\), and evaluate every requested \(P_iT(\bar x)\) without incorporating any same-round update. With relaxations \(\lambda_{k,i}>0\), form in parallel \[d_i^k=\lambda_{k,i}\bigl(P_iT(\bar x)-P_i\bar x\bigr),\qquad i\in S_k.\] After all selected computations finish, commit simultaneously: \[x^{k+1}=x^k+\sum_{i\in S_k}P_i^*d_i^k.\] Stop under a prescribed residual or iteration rule.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m\mathcal H_i\), let \(P_i:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H_i\) be the coordinate projections, let \(T:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\), let \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \(\lambda_i\geq0\) for every \(i\in S\). A Jacobi round based on the common snapshot \(x\in\mathcal H\) applies the coupled map \[U_S(x)=x+\sum_{i\in S}\lambda_iP_i^*\bigl(P_iT(x)-P_ix\bigr).\] Although its block increments can be computed concurrently, they are coupled through the shared argument \(x\): for distinct \(i,j\in S\), the value \(P_iT(x)\) may depend on \(P_jx\). Thus parallel execution does not imply separability; it realizes the single simultaneous map \(U_S\), rather than a composition of successively refreshed block maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel block increments may remain mathematically coupled because each reads the same full iterate; together they implement one simultaneous map rather than sequentially refreshed updates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact factorization boundary between coupled and block-local residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(T:\bigoplus_i\mathcal H_i\to\bigoplus_i\mathcal H_i\), define \(R_i(x)=P_iT(x)-P_ix\). The residual blocks are mutually block-local exactly when, for every \(i\), \[P_ix=P_iy\implies R_i(x)=R_i(y).\] Equivalently, maps \(r_i:\mathcal H_i\to\mathcal H_i\) exist with \(R_i=r_i\circ P_i\). In that case the simultaneous map decomposes into commuting single-block maps; failure of this invariance means that at least one residual block depends on coordinates outside its own block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shared-iterate updates decouple exactly when each residual block depends only on its own input block.
assumptions_latex: T\text{ is defined on the stated direct-sum block space}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\forall i,\ P_ix=P_iy\Rightarrow R_i(x)=R_i(y)\bigr]\iff\bigl[\exists r_i,\ R_i=r_i\circ P_i\bigr].

notation.meaning: factorized residual map on block i

knowledge_statements.title: Separability Criterion for Shared-Iterate Decoupling

children.title: Common-Snapshot Validity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Execution regimes where a common block snapshot remains an appropriate coordination model.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regime in which simultaneous common-snapshot updates equal sequential block execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every full-space block map \(\widehat B_i\) changes only block \(i\), and its new value depends only on \(x_i\). Then distinct maps commute, and for every selected set \(S\), \[x+\sum_{i\in S}P_i^*\bigl(B_i(x_i)-x_i\bigr)=\Bigl(\prod_{i\in S}\widehat B_i\Bigr)x,\] independently of the order of the product. Thus simultaneous common-snapshot execution is exact for block-separable update maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If each update depends only on its own disjoint block, simultaneous execution equals every sequential ordering of the selected block maps.
assumptions_latex: Each \(B_i\) depends only on \(x_i\).
The block subspaces are disjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat B_i\widehat B_j=\widehat B_j\widehat B_i\quad(i\ne j),\qquad U_S=\prod_{i\in S}\widehat B_i.

notation.meaning: full-space map changing only block i

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Separable Validity Regime

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Common Snapshot Is Not a Descent Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled quadratic showing that coherent reads alone do not validate a simultaneous round.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[F(x_1,x_2)=\tfrac12(x_1+x_2)^2+\tfrac\varepsilon2(x_1^2+x_2^2),\qquad 0<\varepsilon<1.\] Simultaneous unit coordinate-gradient steps computed at \(x=(1,1)\) produce \(x^+=(-1-\varepsilon,-1-\varepsilon)\), and \[F(x^+)=(1+\varepsilon)^2F(x)>F(x).\] Hence common-snapshot coherence alone does not certify descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfectly coherent same-snapshot coordinate steps can increase a coupled strongly convex objective.
assumptions_latex: 0<\varepsilon<1.
Both coordinate-gradient steps use the common snapshot \((1,1)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Common Snapshot Is Not a Descent Certificate
Common-Snapshot Validity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A block quadratic-majorization condition validating simultaneous gradient steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable on \(\mathcal H=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m\mathcal H_i\). For a selected set \(S\), a common-snapshot Jacobi gradient update is covered by a valid quadratic model when there exist \(L_i>0\) such that, for every \(x\) and every block-supported \(h=\sum_{i\in S}P_i^*h_i\), \[F(x+h)\leq F(x)+\sum_{i\in S}\langle\nabla_iF(x),h_i\rangle+\frac12\sum_{i\in S}L_i\lVert h_i\rVert^2.\] Under this condition, choosing \(h_i=-\gamma_i\nabla_iF(x)\) with \(0<\gamma_i<2/L_i\) makes the displayed upper bound strictly smaller unless every selected block gradient vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneous gradient blocks are valid when one separable quadratic upper model controls their combined change; steps below twice the reciprocal block curvature then decrease that model.
assumptions_latex: The displayed block-supported quadratic upper bound holds for the selected set.
Each selected step size satisfies \(0<\gamma_i<2/L_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quadratic model decreases by \(\sum_{i\in S}\gamma_i(1-L_i\gamma_i/2)\lVert\nabla_iF(x)\rVert^2\), unless all selected gradients vanish.

notation.meaning: Block gradient evaluated at the common snapshot.
Curvature coefficient in the simultaneous block upper model.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated majorization condition and model-decrease calculation are mathematically coherent, and condition is the appropriate content kind for this validity-regime leaf. The record nevertheless supplies neither a source locator nor explicit standard-field rationale, so the claimed regime requires sourcing.

children.title: Parallel Randomized Block Updates
children.top_down_role: Synchronous random subsets of concurrently updated blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Randomized Block Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous randomized block fixed-point iteration using a common iterate snapshot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\ge 1\), let each \(X_i\) be a real vector space, set \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\), and let \(T:X\to X\) have block components \(T_i:X\to X_i\). Choose \(x^0\in X\). At iteration \(k\), sample a nonempty subset \(S_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) from a prescribed distribution, evaluate every selected component from the common snapshot \(x^k\), and commit simultaneously according to
\[
x_i^{k+1}=\begin{cases}x_i^k+\lambda_k\bigl(T_i(x^k)-x_i^k\bigr),&i\in S_k,\\x_i^k,&i\notin S_k.\end{cases}
\]
Here \(\lambda_k>0\) is the relaxation parameter. Stop under a specified residual or iteration-budget rule and return the latest iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each synchronized round, sample a nonempty set of blocks, compute all selected updates from the same iterate, commit them simultaneously, and leave unselected blocks unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(m\ge1\), each \(X_i\) is a real vector space, and \(T:X\to X\) is block-decomposed.
Each \(S_k\) is nonempty and sampled from a prescribed distribution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update produces a synchronous randomized block iteration whose selected components all use the shared snapshot \(x^k\).

notation.meaning: random set of blocks selected at iteration k
i-th block component of the update operator

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient sampling condition for almost-sure repeated activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((S_k)_{k\geq0}\) be independent random subsets. If, for every block \(i\), \(\inf_k\mathbb P(i\in S_k)\geq p_i>0\), then \[\mathbb P(i\in S_k\ \mathrm{i.o.})=1.\] If a block has zero selection probability from some time onward, a generic randomized block method cannot enforce that block's fixed-point equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent rounds with uniformly positive marginals activate every block infinitely often; an eventually excluded block cannot generally be solved.
assumptions_latex: (S_k)_{k\geq0}\text{ are independent across rounds}.
\inf_k\mathbb P(i\in S_k)\geq p_i>0\text{ for every }i.

notation.meaning: uniform positive lower bound on block i's activation probability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expectation identity for an inverse-probability random residual mask.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For block residuals \(R_i(x)\), subset marginals \(p_i>0\), and \((M_SR(x))_i=\mathbf1_{\{i\in S\}}R_i(x)/p_i\), one has \(\mathbb E[M_SR(x)\mid x]=R(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse marginal-probability scaling makes a sampled residual mask unbiased.
assumptions_latex: p_i>0\text{ for every block}.
R(x)\text{ is fixed conditional on }x.

children.title: Conflict-Aware Parallel Coordinate Updates
children.top_down_role: Concurrent updates organized around sparse block interactions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic synchronous schedule formed from a proper coloring.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c:V\to\{1,\ldots,q\}\) be a proper coloring of \(G\), and set \(C_\ell=\{i\in V:c(i)=\ell\}\). Process the color classes sequentially; within stage \(\ell\), compute and commit the updates for all blocks in \(C_\ell\) concurrently. Every block is scheduled once per sweep, and every stage is an independent set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper coloring partitions the blocks into conflict-free parallel stages.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is a proper coloring of \(G\).
The conflict graph conservatively represents the relevant pairwise incompatibilities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V=\bigsqcup_{\ell=1}^{q}C_\ell,\qquad C_\ell\text{ is independent for every }\ell.

notation.meaning: color class executed at stage ell
number of stages in the schedule

knowledge_statements.title: Color-Class Conflict Schedule

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum synchronization depth of a complete graph-conflict-free sweep.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Among schedules that partition all vertices of \(G\) into independent concurrent stages, the minimum number of stages is the chromatic number \(\chi(G)\). A greedy coloring supplies a schedule with at most \(\Delta(G)+1\) stages, where \(\Delta(G)\) is the maximum degree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimal number of conflict-free stages is the graph's chromatic number, while greedy coloring needs at most maximum degree plus one stages.
assumptions_latex: Every block is scheduled exactly once in the sweep.
Each stage must be an independent set of \(G\).

notation.meaning: chromatic number of the conflict graph

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Schedule Stage Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise incompatibility model for concurrent block updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A block-conflict graph is an undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\), with \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), in which every pair of block updates incompatible under the declared execution and update model is joined by an edge. A batch \(S\subseteq V\) is graph-conflict-free exactly when it is an independent set: \[\forall i\ne j\in S,\quad \{i,j\}\notin E.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conflict graph connects incompatible block updates; its independent sets are the admissible concurrent batches.
assumptions_latex: All incompatibilities relevant to the declared model are pairwise representable.
Every genuine pairwise incompatibility is included in \(E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ is graph-conflict-free}\iff S\text{ is independent in }G.
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Conflict Graph

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of the independent-set safety certificate when conflicts are omitted or are not pairwise representable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If incompatible blocks \(i\ne j\) satisfy \(\{i,j\}\notin E\), then the declared graph admits the unsafe independent set \(\{i,j\}\). More generally, an ordinary graph cannot certify a genuinely higher-order incompatibility whose every pair is admissible. Thus graph independence certifies safety only for a conservative and adequate pairwise conflict model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An omitted edge or a genuinely higher-order conflict can make an unsafe batch appear graph-admissible.
assumptions_latex: The declared graph omits a genuine pairwise conflict, or the execution model contains a non-pairwise conflict.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ independent in }G\centernot\implies S\text{ safe without an adequate conservative conflict model}.
knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Conflict Model Boundary
Conflict-Aware Parallel Coordinate Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous block updates restricted by a sparse interaction graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a block-conflict graph with \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), where an edge marks two blocks whose concurrent writes or required data overlap. Given \(x^k\), choose a set \(S_k\subseteq V\) that is independent in \(G\). Every \(i\in S_k\) computes \(d_i^k\) from the common snapshot \(x^k\), after which the disjoint block updates are committed simultaneously:
\[
x^{k+1}=x^k+\sum_{i\in S_k}U_i d_i^k.
\]
Blocks outside \(S_k\) remain unchanged. Stop by a prescribed residual or iteration budget and return the latest iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a graph of interfering blocks, select a conflict-free set each round, compute its updates from one snapshot, and commit those updates concurrently.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) correctly contains every pair of blocks that cannot safely be updated concurrently.
\(S_k\) is an independent set of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No two updates committed in round \(k\) correspond to an edge of the declared conflict graph.

notation.meaning: canonical embedding of block i into the product space

children.title: Distributed Block-Coordinate Updates
children.top_down_role: Block sampling and aggregation across distributed workers.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Block-Coordinate Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous distributed sampling, local block computation, and coordinator aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m,p\ge1\), let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) be a product of real vector spaces, and let \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) be partitioned into disjoint worker-owned sets \(V_1,\ldots,V_p\). Let \(U_i:X_i\to X\) be the canonical block embedding. At round \(k\), a coordinator supplies the snapshot \(x^k\in X\). Worker \(r\in\{1,ldots,p\}\) samples \(S_{k,r}\subseteq V_r\), computes \(d_i^k\in X_i\) for every \(i\in S_{k,r}\), and returns \(\sum_{i\in S_{k,r}}U_i d_i^k\). After receiving the designated round messages, the coordinator performs
\[
x^{k+1}=x^k+\sum_{r=1}^{p}\sum_{i\in S_{k,r}}U_i d_i^k,
\]
broadcasts the new state, and repeats. A prescribed residual or round budget determines termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers sample owned blocks and compute sparse updates from a shared round snapshot; a coordinator sums the designated round updates and broadcasts the next iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(V_1,\ldots,V_p\) form a disjoint partition of \(V=\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
All messages aggregated in round \(k\) were computed from the same snapshot \(x^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregate is a well-defined synchronous block-coordinate update over \(\bigcup_{r=1}^{p}S_{k,r}\).

notation.meaning: blocks sampled by worker r in round k
canonical embedding of block i into the global product space

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If synchronous round \(k\) commits only after every designated worker responds, worker \(r\) has response time \(T_{k,r}\), and aggregation takes \(A_k\), then \[T_k\geq\max_r T_{k,r}+A_k.\] An indefinitely delayed required response therefore prevents completion of the round.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A synchronous distributed round waits for its slowest required worker, and an indefinitely delayed worker stalls the round.
assumptions_latex: Every designated worker response is required before commitment.
Communication delay is included in \(T_{k,r}\).

children.title: Totally Asynchronous Models
children.top_down_role: Classical asynchronous models without a uniform synchronization window.

knowledge_statements.title: Totally Asynchronous Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical componentwise iteration with unbounded but eventually vanishing information age.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a product state \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\), a totally asynchronous execution of a map \(T\) consists of update-time sets \(K_i\subseteq\mathbb N\) and read indices \(\tau_{ij}(k)\le k\). For \(k\in K_i\), component \(i\) is assigned \(T_i(x_1^{\tau_{i1}(k)},\ldots,x_m^{\tau_{im}(k)})\); otherwise it is unchanged. The execution is totally asynchronous when every \(K_i\) is infinite and, for every \(i,j\),
\[
\lim_{\substack{k\to\infty\\k\in K_i}}\tau_{ij}(k)=\infty.
\]
No finite uniform bound on update gaps or delays is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every component updates infinitely often, and information used by sufficiently late updates is eventually arbitrarily recent, although delays and update gaps need not be uniformly bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(T:X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\to X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\).
Each read index satisfies \(0\le\tau_{ij}(k)\le k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The schedule is totally asynchronous precisely when all components update infinitely often and every read index tends to infinity along the corresponding component's updates.

notation.meaning: times at which component i is updated
version index of component j read for update i at time k
i-th component of the iteration map

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp failure when infinite activation is retained but read freshness is removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T(x)=x/2\), \(x^0=1\), and update the sole component at every event using the permanently frozen index \(\tau(k)=0\). Then \(x^{k+1}=T(x^{\tau(k)})=1/2\) for every \(k\ge0\). Thus the component is activated infinitely often, but \(x^k\not\to0\), the unique fixed point of \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infinite activation does not ensure convergence if reads remain permanently frozen, even for the contraction x mapped to x/2.
assumptions_latex: There is one scalar component and it is updated at every event.

notation.meaning: version index read at event k

knowledge_statements.title: Failure Without Asymptotic Freshness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical convergence of totally asynchronous component iteration for a block-maximum-norm contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) be complete under \(\|x\|_{\infty,w}=\max_i\|x_i\|_i/w_i\), where \(w_i>0\), and suppose \(T:X\to X\) satisfies \(\|T(x)-T(y)\|_{\infty,w}\le q\|x-y\|_{\infty,w}\) for some \(q<1\). Every totally asynchronous component execution of \(T\), with each component activated infinitely often and every componentwise read index tending to infinity along the relevant activations, converges to the unique fixed point \(x^\star\) of \(T\). Without uniform bounds on activation gaps or delays, the model alone yields no uniform rate in the global event counter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A totally asynchronous component iteration of a contraction converges to its unique fixed point, but total asynchronism alone supplies no uniform event-count rate.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is complete in the weighted block-maximum norm.
\(T\) is a contraction with factor \(0\le q<1\).
Every component is activated infinitely often and all read indices are asymptotically fresh.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k\to x^\star\), where \(T(x^\star)=x^\star\); no schedule-independent rate in \(k\) follows without stronger timing bounds.

children.title: Partially Asynchronous Models
children.top_down_role: Asynchronous models with controlled update and communication timing.

knowledge_statements.title: Partially Asynchronous Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical asynchronous iteration with uniformly bounded update gaps and information delays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\ge1\), let global events be indexed by \(k\in\mathbb N\), let \(K_i\subseteq\mathbb N\) be the update times of component \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), and let \(\tau_{ij}(k)\in\{0,\ldots,k\}\) be the version of component \(j\) used when component \(i\) updates at \(k\in K_i\). An execution is partially asynchronous with bound \(B\in\mathbb N\), \(B\ge1\), if, for every \(k\in\mathbb N\) and every component \(i\),
\[
K_i\cap\{k,k+1,\ldots,k+B-1\}\ne\varnothing,
\]
and, for every \(i,j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(k\in K_i\),
\[
0\le k-\tau_{ij}(k)\le B.
\]
Thus every component is updated at least once in each window of \(B\) consecutive global events, and every value used by an update is at most \(B\) versions old.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform finite bound controls both how long any component can go without updating and how stale any value used by an update can be.
assumptions_latex: \(m\ge1\) and global update events are indexed by \(k\in\mathbb N\).
For \(k\in K_i\), each read index satisfies \(0\le\tau_{ij}(k)\le k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both component-update gaps and componentwise information delays are uniformly bounded by the finite constant \(B\).

notation.meaning: version of component j used by update i at time k

children.top_down_role: Coherent delayed snapshots versus mixed-age coordinate views.

children.title: Consistent Read Snapshots
children.top_down_role: Coherent delayed views whose coordinates originate from a single historical state.

knowledge_statements.title: Consistent Read Snapshots
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Read coherence represented by one previously realized global iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^0,x^1,\ldots\in X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) be the committed global states. A worker read \(\widehat x^k\) used for update \(k\) is a consistent snapshot if there exists an index \(s_k\le k\) such that
\[
\widehat x^k=x^{s_k}.
\]
Equivalently, every block of \(\widehat x^k\) has the form \(\widehat x_i^k=x_i^{s_k}\) with the same version index \(s_k\). The snapshot may be stale, but it must equal a global state that existed in the serialized history.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A read is consistent when all of its blocks come from one common historical global iterate, even if that iterate is stale.
assumptions_latex: Committed states \(x^k\) are indexed by a serialized global history.
The read \(\widehat x^k\) is assembled before computing update \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Read consistency holds exactly when one index \(s_k\le k\) represents every block of \(\widehat x^k\).

notation.meaning: committed global state at serialized index s

children.title: Inconsistent Mixed-Age Reads

knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistent Mixed-Age Reads
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise reads whose versions need not form one historical global state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^0,x^1,\ldots\) be committed global states. A worker's read at update \(k\) has mixed ages when
\[
\widehat x^k=\bigl(x_1^{\tau_1(k)},\ldots,x_m^{\tau_m(k)}\bigr),\qquad 0\le\tau_i(k)\le k,
\]
with component-dependent version indices. It is an inconsistent mixed-age read when no \(s\le k\) satisfies \(\widehat x^k=x^s\). Thus each block value may individually have existed, while their assembled vector never occurred as a committed global state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed-age read combines blocks from different versions and is inconsistent when the assembled vector never appeared as any committed global iterate.
assumptions_latex: Committed global states are \(x^0,x^1,\ldots\).
Each component read uses some historical version \(\tau_i(k)\le k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The read is inconsistent exactly when \(\widehat x^k\notin\{x^0,\ldots,x^k\}\).

notation.meaning: version index used for component i
committed global state at index s

children.title: Read-Coherence Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions separating coherent snapshot interpretations from mixed-age execution.

knowledge_statements.title: Read-Coherence Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise historical validity does not imply global snapshot consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider serialized states in \(\mathbb R^2\): \(x^0=(0,0)\), \(x^1=(1,0)\), and \(x^2=(1,1)\), produced by committing the first and then the second coordinate. A concurrent reader may obtain the first coordinate before the first commit and the second coordinate after the second commit, yielding
\[
\widehat x=(0,1).
\]
Both read values occurred individually, but \(\widehat x\notin\{x^0,x^1,x^2\}\). Therefore per-coordinate historical validity, even with bounded ages, does not ensure that a read equals a consistent global snapshot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reading each coordinate from a valid historical version does not guarantee coherence: concurrent commits can produce an assembled vector that never existed globally.
assumptions_latex: Coordinate reads and coordinate commits may interleave without a snapshot mechanism.
The serialized committed states are \(x^0=(0,0)\), \(x^1=(1,0)\), and \(x^2=(1,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The mixed read \(\widehat x=(0,1)\) is componentwise valid but is not any committed global state.

notation.meaning: vector assembled by the concurrent reader

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Delay Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform deterministic bound on the staleness of every component read.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m\ge1\), index serialized committed updates by \(k\in\mathbb N\), and let \(I_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) be the components read by update \(k\). For each \(i\in I_k\), let \(\tau_i(k)\in\{0,\ldots,k\}\) be the version read and define \(d_i(k)=k-\tau_i(k)\). The execution satisfies a bounded-delay model when there exists a deterministic finite integer \(D\ge0\) such that
\[
0\le d_i(k)\le D
\]
for every \(k\in\mathbb N\) and every \(i\in I_k\). The bound controls information staleness only; it does not by itself impose consistent snapshots or bounded component-update gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every component used by every update is at most a fixed finite number of committed updates old; this alone does not guarantee coherent reads or bounded update gaps.
assumptions_latex: \(m\ge1\) and global commits have serialized indices \(k\in\mathbb N\).
For every \(i\in I_k\), the read version satisfies \(0\le\tau_i(k)\le k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A single finite constant \(D\) uniformly bounds every realized delay \(k-\tau_i(k)\) for \(k\in\mathbb N\) and \(i\in I_k\).

notation.meaning: version of component i read by update k

children.title: Stochastic Delay Models
children.top_down_role: Asynchronous regimes characterized through probabilistic delay behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Delay Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Random read delays controlled conditionally by a prescribed distributional envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(d_i(k)=k-\tau_i(k)\) be the nonnegative random delay of component \(i\) used by update \(k\), and let \(\mathcal F_{k-1}\) contain the execution history before that update. A stochastic-delay model is specified by a nonincreasing envelope \(q:\mathbb N\to[0,1]\) with \(q(t)\to0\) such that
\[
\mathbb P\bigl(d_i(k)\ge t\mid\mathcal F_{k-1}\bigr)\le q(t)
\]
almost surely for every relevant \(i,k,t\). Unlike deterministic bounded delay, arbitrarily large delays may occur, but their conditional probabilities are uniformly controlled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delays may be unbounded random variables, but every update and component obeys a common conditional tail-probability envelope that vanishes with age.
assumptions_latex: Each \(d_i(k)\) is a nonnegative integer-valued random variable adapted at update \(k\).
\(q\) is nonincreasing and satisfies \(\lim_{t\to\infty}q(t)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All conditional delay tails are uniformly dominated by \(q(t)\), while no finite almost-sure delay bound is required.

notation.meaning: random delay of component i at update k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but no source is supplied for this particular uniform conditional-tail formulation. Different stochastic-delay models use materially different dependence and conditioning assumptions.

children.title: Delay-Tail Regimes
children.top_down_role: Qualitative distinctions arising from light, heavy, or truncated delay tails.

knowledge_statements.title: Delay-Tail Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moment and exponential regimes classified through a uniform delay-tail envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose nonnegative delays satisfy \(\mathbb P(d_i(k)\ge t\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\le q(t)\). A polynomial-tail regime of order \(p>0\) holds when \(q(t)\le C(1+t)^{-p}\); an exponential-tail regime holds when \(q(t)\le Ce^{-ct}\) for constants \(C,c>0\). More generally, the weighted-tail condition
\[
\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}w(t)q(t)<\infty
\]
identifies the summability available for an analysis, where \(w(t)\ge0\) is prescribed. These regimes permit unbounded realized delays while quantitatively restricting rare large delays.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delay regimes are distinguished by how quickly a uniform tail envelope decays, such as polynomial, exponential, or a weighted summability condition.
assumptions_latex: The conditional delay tails share an envelope \(q(t)\).
The weight sequence satisfies \(w(t)\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Polynomial, exponential, and weighted-summable delay regimes are determined by the corresponding displayed bounds on \(q\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the leaf, but no source supports the proposed polynomial, exponential, and arbitrary weighted-tail taxonomy or the claimed analytical interpretation.

children.title: Shared-Memory Lock-Free Architectures
children.top_down_role: Concurrent workers updating shared parameter storage.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct shared-array coordinate updates with linearizable atomic commits, mixed-age reads, and system-wide lock-free progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A shared-memory lock-free coordinate architecture maintains one authoritative block array \(x=(x_i)_{i=1}^m\). Each worker repeatedly performs an operation that reads blocks of \(x\), possibly at different commit times, computes an increment \(d_i\), and invokes a linearizable atomic read-modify-write primitive to commit \(x_i\leftarrow x_i+d_i\). Each successful commit therefore has one linearization point, although a multi-block read need not equal the array at any single linearization point. The architecture is lock-free when, in every infinite execution in which workers continue taking steps, infinitely many worker operations complete; this is a system-wide progress condition and does not require every individual worker operation to complete.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers directly update a shared block array through linearizable atomic commits; reads may mix ages, and lock freedom requires continuing system-wide completion rather than merely the absence of a global lock.
assumptions_latex: The authoritative parameter is a shared block array.
Each block read used by the model is atomic at its declared granularity.
Each committed block update uses a linearizable atomic read-modify-write primitive.
The underlying atomic-update implementation satisfies system-wide lock-free progress.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Committed block modifications admit a linearized order, multi-block reads may be inconsistent snapshots, and continued execution guarantees system-wide operation completion without guaranteeing per-worker completion.
knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Memory Lock-Free Coordinate Architecture
Shared-Memory Lock-Free Architectures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational model for atomic coordinate commits without global worker locking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A shared-memory lock-free coordinate architecture maintains one global array \(x\) accessed by workers. Worker \(r\) repeatedly reads a possibly mixed-age vector \(\widehat x^{k_r}\), selects a block \(i_r\), computes an increment \(d_{i_r}^{k_r}\), and atomically commits
\[
x_{i_r}\leftarrow x_{i_r}+d_{i_r}^{k_r}.
\]
No global lock serializes the read-compute-commit cycles. Atomicity guarantees that each committed block modification has a position in a serialized commit history, but the preceding multi-block read need not equal any state in that history. Termination is imposed externally by a residual, budget, or coordination flag.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers independently read shared parameters, compute block increments, and atomically commit them without a global lock; commits serialize, but multi-block reads may be inconsistent.
assumptions_latex: The shared parameter is partitioned into blocks.
Each block commit is atomic, while a multi-block read need not be atomic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Committed block writes admit a serialized order, whereas worker read vectors may contain components from different points of that order.

notation.meaning: possibly inconsistent state read by worker r

children.title: Server–Worker Coordinate Architectures
children.top_down_role: Workers communicating partial information through centralized state.

knowledge_statements.title: Server–Worker Coordinate Architectures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Centralized authoritative state with asynchronously computed block updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A server–worker coordinate architecture for a product space \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) consists of one server storing the authoritative iterate \(x\in X\) and workers that do not write \(x\) directly. A worker reads a possibly delayed snapshot \(\hat x\), selects a block \(i\), computes a message \(u_i\in X_i\), and sends \((i,u_i)\) to the server. Upon receipt, the server commits the message as an indivisible update \(x\leftarrow x+P_i u_i\), in some server-defined order, and may return updated state to the workers. Thus all changes to the authoritative iterate are serialized at the server, although reads and computations may overlap asynchronously.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers compute block updates from possibly stale snapshots, while a central server serializes all commits to the authoritative iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) is a block product space.
Each worker message identifies its target block and proposed increment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{+}=x+P_i u_i\) is committed only by the server.

notation.meaning: canonical embedding of block i into the product space

children.title: Partitioned-Memory Placement
children.top_down_role: Distribution of coordinate data across distinct worker-local memory regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Partitioned-Memory Placement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Physical placement of disjoint coordinate blocks across distributed owners.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) and let \(W\) be a finite set of workers. A partitioned-memory placement is a map \(p:\{1,\ldots,m\}\to W\) such that the storage containing the authoritative value of block \(x_i\) resides at worker \(p(i)\). Each block has exactly one authoritative location, while replicas, if present, are read-only or are governed by a separate consistency protocol. An update of block \(i\) must therefore be executed at \(p(i)\) or transmitted to \(p(i)\) for commitment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each coordinate block has one authoritative worker location; updates execute there or are routed there for commitment.
assumptions_latex: \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) has a fixed finite block decomposition.
\(W\) is a finite nonempty worker set.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) be a block index set, let \(W\) be a finite nonempty worker set, and let \(\mathcal T\) be a set of logical times. A block ownership policy is a family of nonempty sets \(O_i(t)\subseteq W\), indexed by \(i\in I\) and \(t\in\mathcal T\), where \(O_i(t)\) is precisely the set of workers authorized to commit an authoritative write to block \(i\) at time \(t\). The policy is exclusive when \(|O_i(t)|=1\) for every \(i\in I\) and \(t\in\mathcal T\); otherwise it is a shared-ownership policy whose write-serialization or conflict-resolution semantics must be specified separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block ownership policy specifies the workers authorized to commit each block at each logical time; it is exclusive when exactly one worker is authorized for every block and time.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\) be a finite nonempty worker set and let the auxiliary state be \(z=(z_j)_{j\in J}\), where \(J\) is finite and nonempty. knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be the block index set, let \(W\) be the worker set, and let \(\mathcal T\) be physical time. For each \(i\in I\) and \(t\in\mathcal T\), let \(A_i(t)\subseteq W\) be the workers authorized to modify the authoritative value of block \(x_i\) at time \(t\). Exclusive update ownership is the condition \[\forall i\in I\;\forall t\in\mathcal T,\qquad |A_i(t)|\leq 1.\] If every executing writer is authorized throughout its commit interval, then commits \(k\) and \(\ell\) with the same target block and distinct writers satisfy \(C_k\cap C_\ell=\varnothing\). Reads may overlap a commit only under the separately specified read-consistency semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every physical time, at most one worker is authorized to modify any authoritative block; consequently, authorized commit intervals of distinct writers targeting that block cannot overlap.

children.title: Coordinate Locking Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Lock-based protection scopes for coordinate or block modifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Locking Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mutual-exclusion protocol for committing block-coordinate updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an authoritative iterate \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\), one mutex \(L_i\) per block, and a proposed block update \(U_i\). A worker repeatedly attempts to acquire \(L_i\); after acquisition, it reads the current \(x_i\), computes or validates \(U_i(x_i)\), writes \(x_i\leftarrow U_i(x_i)\), and releases \(L_i\). No other worker may read-modify-write block \(i\) while \(L_i\) is held. With multi-block updates on \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), all locks \(\{L_i:i\in S\}\) are acquired in a fixed global order and released after the commit. The output is the iterate after the successfully locked update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A worker locks every target block, commits its update exclusively, then releases the locks; multi-block locks follow a global order.
assumptions_latex: Each mutex grants mutual exclusion.
Every multi-block update uses the same global lock order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i^{+}=U_i(x_i)\) is committed while \(L_i\) is held exclusively.

notation.meaning: set of blocks targeted by a multi-block update

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lock Safety Does Not Ensure Progress
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Liveness boundary for an otherwise mutually exclusive, deadlock-avoiding block-lock protocol.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Mutual exclusion guarantees that at most one worker occupies a protected block's critical section, and a common strict order for acquiring multiple locks prevents circular wait. These safety conditions do not imply starvation freedom: without a fair acquisition or eventual-grant condition, a worker may be postponed indefinitely while other workers repeatedly acquire the same lock. Consequently, optimization convergence assumptions requiring every block to update infinitely often must be imposed separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mutex safety and ordered acquisition prevent simultaneous commits and circular wait, but they do not guarantee that every waiting worker or block eventually progresses.
assumptions_latex: Each lock enforces mutual exclusion.
Every multi-lock acquisition follows one common strict order.
No fairness or eventual-grant property is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{mutual exclusion plus ordered acquisition}\not\Rightarrow\text{starvation freedom or infinite block activation}.
knowledge_statements.title: Lock Safety Does Not Ensure Progress

children.title: Atomic Write Semantics
children.top_down_role: Write-level atomicity guarantees relevant to concurrent coordinate updates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct operation-history formulation of atomic access to one authoritative block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a concurrent history contain invocations and responses of reads, writes, and any declared read-modify-write operations on authoritative blocks. It has atomic block-operation semantics when every completed operation can be assigned a linearization point within its invocation-response interval so that the resulting total order respects real-time precedence and is a legal sequential history for each block. In that order, a read returns the value of the latest preceding write or read-modify-write operation on its block, and a read-modify-write operation reads and replaces one block as one indivisible action. Atomicity applies only to the declared operation and block unit; it does not make a multi-block update atomic unless that entire update is one declared operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reads, writes, and declared read-modify-write operations must admit a legal real-time-consistent sequential order, with each operation taking effect indivisibly at its own linearization point.
assumptions_latex: Every operation has a well-defined invocation and response interval.
The block and operation serving as the unit of atomicity are declared.
Sequential read, write, and read-modify-write behavior is specified for each block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\) a legal total order of all completed operations that respects real-time precedence and places each operation within its invocation-response interval.
knowledge_statements.title: Linearizable Block-Operation Semantics

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between indivisible replacement and an indivisible update derived from the current value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Atomic loads and atomic stores prevent torn values but do not make their composition an atomic read-modify-write. If two workers both read \(x\), compute \(x+a\) and \(x+b\), and then perform separate atomic stores, the final value may be only \(x+a\) or \(x+b\). If instead each commit is a linearizable atomic addition to the same block, both increments are retained and the final value is \(x+a+b\), up to the declared arithmetic semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Indivisible stores can still lose a concurrently computed increment; preserving both increments requires an atomic read-modify-write or accumulation operation.
assumptions_latex: Two updates are computed from the same initial block value \(x\).
Loads and stores are individually atomic, but the load-compute-store sequence is not one atomic operation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{atomicStore}(x+a),\operatorname{atomicStore}(x+b)\not\Rightarrow x^+=x+a+b\), whereas two legal atomic additions do.
knowledge_statements.title: Atomic Stores Versus Atomic Accumulation
Atomic Write Semantics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linearizable semantics for individual coordinate-block writes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family of concurrent block writes has atomic write semantics if every completed write \(W_k:x_{i_k}\leftarrow v_k\) has a linearization point inside its invocation–response interval and there exists a total order of these points that respects real-time precedence. Every read of block \(i\) returns the value produced by the latest preceding write to \(i\) in that order, or the initial value if none exists. Consequently, a block write is observed either entirely before or entirely after another operation; no operation observes a partially written block. This condition does not require a multi-block update to be atomic unless that stronger guarantee is stated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every block write appears to occur at one instant in a real-time-consistent serial order, and partial block values are never observable.
assumptions_latex: Each write has a well-defined invocation and response interval.
The stored block value is the unit of atomicity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\prec\text{ such that }\prec\text{ is total, respects real time, and each read returns the latest preceding write value}.\)

children.title: Overlapping-Block Write Conflicts
children.top_down_role: Concurrent interference caused by shared block components.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational certificate for absence of direct unsafe write-write interference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A concurrent execution is pairwise write-conflict-free if, for every pair of updates whose commit intervals overlap, either their write sets are disjoint or every shared-location effect is protected by a declared mechanism that yields a legal serial history or the specified atomic combined result. This test certifies only direct write-write safety; it does not certify read coherence, auxiliary-state consistency, deadlock freedom, or optimization convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every concurrently committing pair must either write disjoint locations or use a declared serialization or atomic-combination mechanism on all shared locations.
assumptions_latex: Commit intervals and write sets are available for every update.
The legal sequential or combined semantics of each protection mechanism is specified.

notation.meaning: all common writes have declared serializing or atomic-combination semantics

knowledge_statements.title: Pairwise Write-Conflict-Freedom Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal shared-coordinate execution exhibiting a lost update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an authoritative scalar initially satisfy \(x=0\). Two workers concurrently read \(0\), each computes the valid incremented value \(1\), and each later stores \(1\) without an atomic read-modify-write or mutual exclusion. After both commits, \(x=1\), whereas either serial execution of the two increments gives \(x=2\). Thus individually valid and even commuting update intentions can lose one effect under overlapping replacement writes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two concurrent increments from the same read can leave a shared scalar at one instead of two when their read-modify-write sequences are not serialized.
assumptions_latex: \(x=0\) initially.
Both workers intend the update \(x\leftarrow x+1\).
The two load-compute-store sequences overlap and are not atomic as compound operations.
knowledge_statements.title: Lost Increment Under Overlapping Read-Modify-Write

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of potential shared-location collisions from safely serialized or atomically combined commits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let concurrent updates \(a\) and \(b\) have commit intervals \(C_a,C_b\) and write sets \(W_a,W_b\). They have a potential overlapping-block write collision when \(C_a\cap C_b\ne\varnothing\) and \(W_a\cap W_b\ne\varnothing\). The collision becomes an unsafe write conflict when the declared commit semantics do not guarantee a legal serial result or a specified atomic combination of both effects. Noncommutativity is not required: even commuting increments can be lost under separate non-atomic read-modify-write sequences. If the write sets are disjoint, there is no direct write-write conflict, although shared reads or auxiliary state may create a different dependency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Concurrent blocks potentially collide when they write a common location; the collision is unsafe only when the commit protocol neither serializes nor atomically combines the effects.
assumptions_latex: Each update has a declared write set and commit interval.
The semantics of replacement, read-modify-write, or accumulation commits is declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_a\cap C_b\ne\varnothing\ \land\ W_a\cap W_b\ne\varnothing\text{ identifies a potential collision; safety additionally requires serialization or a specified atomic combination.}

Overlapping-Block Write Conflicts

Represent update \(a\) by a write set \(S_a\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), an execution interval \(C_a\), and an update map \(U_a\). Two updates \(a\) and \(b\) have an overlapping-block write conflict when \(S_a\cap S_b

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A write-write conflict can exist whenever concurrent operations write a shared location without adequate serialization; noncommutativity is a possible order-dependence consequence, not a necessary defining condition. knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-State Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant coupling cached state to the authoritative coordinate vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the authoritative iterate be \(x\in X\), and let cached or extended state \(z\in Z\) be defined by \(z=\Phi(x)\). Strong auxiliary-state consistency holds at every visible commit boundary when this invariant is satisfied. If a committed block increment changes \(x\) to \(x^{+}=x+P_i d\), the protocol must also apply an auxiliary update \(z^{+}=V_i(z,d)\) satisfying \[V_i(\Phi(x),d)=\Phi(x+P_i d).\] The primal and auxiliary changes must be jointly visible or serialized so that no subsequent operation declared consistent reads a pair \((x,z)\) violating \(z=\Phi(x)\). A bounded-staleness interface may relax the invariant only by explicitly bounding the omitted committed updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cached residuals, products, or operator state must remain equal to their defining function of the authoritative iterate at visible commit boundaries.
assumptions_latex: \(z=\Phi(x)\) uniquely defines the maintained auxiliary state.
A block commit changes \(x\) by \(P_i d\).

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Coordinate Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Delayed partial-gradient descent with atomic block commits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a differentiable objective \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), a block decomposition, stepsizes \(\gamma_i>0\), and \(x^0\), commit counter \(k\) proceeds as follows. A worker selects block \(i_k\), reads a possibly inconsistent delayed vector \(\hat x^k\) whose components come from commits no later than \(k\), computes \(d_k=-\gamma_{i_k}\nabla_{i_k}f(\hat x^k)\), and atomically commits \[x^{k+1}=x^k+P_{i_k}d_k.\] Other blocks remain unchanged. Workers repeat without a global computation barrier. The method stops under a prescribed budget or when a chosen stationarity measure, evaluated on a consistent snapshot, meets its tolerance, and returns the latest committed iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers compute partial-gradient steps from delayed reads and atomically add them to selected blocks without a global barrier.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable.
The iterate has a fixed block decomposition.
Each block commit is atomic.

notation.meaning: delayed vector read by the worker producing commit k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asynchronous exact coordinate minimization with explicit exclusion and replacement semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For commit \(k\), a worker acquires the exclusive lock for block \(i_k\), reads a possibly delayed vector \(\widehat x^k\) with \(\widehat x_{i_k}^k=x_{i_k}^k\), chooses \[u^k\in\arg\min_u f(\widehat x_1^k,\ldots,\widehat x_{i_k-1}^k,u,\widehat x_{i_k+1}^k,\ldots,\widehat x_m^k),\] atomically replaces the selected block by \(u^k\), and releases the lock. Other blocks may be committed concurrently, but no other worker may write block \(i_k\) while the lock is held.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A worker locks its block, exactly minimizes its delayed coordinate subproblem using a current self-coordinate, replaces that block, and unlocks it.

If block \(i\) satisfies a quadratic upper model with constant \(L_i\), then \[f(x^{k+1})\le f(x^k)-\gamma_i\langle g_i^k,g_i^k+e_i^k\rangle+\frac{L_i\gamma_i^2}{2}\|g_i^k+e_i^k\|_i^2.\]

A worker selecting i_k reads \widehat x^k, computes \delta_{i_k}^k=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma_{i_k}g_{i_k}}(\widehat x_{i_k}^k-\gamma_{i_k}\nabla_{i_k}f(\widehat x^k))-\widehat x_{i_k}^k, and atomically commits x^{k+1}=x^k+P_{i_k}\delta_{i_k}^k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Delayed Proximal Corrections Are Not Current Stationarity Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates executable stale proximal corrections from valid composite stopping tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let R_i(x)=\gamma_i^{-1}[x_i-\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma_i g_i}(x_i-\gamma_i\nabla_i f(x))]. The correction computed from a delayed read is \delta_i(\hat x)=-\gamma_iR_i(\hat x). Even if \delta_i(\hat x)=0, one cannot conclude R_i(x^k)=0 unless the read is current or a bound controls \|R_i(x^k)-R_i(\hat x)\|. Likewise, one delayed sampled block residual cannot certify full composite stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero stale proximal correction certifies stationarity only at the stale snapshot, not necessarily at the latest shared iterate.
assumptions_latex: The block proximal-gradient residuals are well defined.
The worker may use \hat x\ne x^k.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \delta_i(\hat x)=0\centernot\Rightarrow R_i(x^k)=0\quad\text{without a current-read or residual-error bound}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Two-Commit Delay Can Destabilize Additive Proximal Corrections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite convex instability of the accepted additive-correction model under an excessive delay-relative proximal parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=g(x)=\tfrac12x^2\), set \(f\equiv0\), choose \(\gamma=3\), and let every commit after initialization use \(\widehat x^k=x^{k-2}\). Since \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(z)=z/(1+\gamma)=z/4\), the additive correction is \(-\tfrac34\widehat x^k\), so \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\tfrac34x^{k-2}\). The characteristic polynomial \(r^3-r^2+\tfrac34\) has roots outside the closed unit disk; hence some nonzero initialized histories do not converge to the unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-commit-old additive proximal corrections can be unstable even for a one-dimensional strongly convex composite objective.
assumptions_latex: \(f\equiv0\) and \(g(x)=\tfrac12x^2\).
Commit \(k\) uses the correction computed from \(x^{k-2}\).
The initialized history has a nonzero component in an unstable characteristic mode.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometric Convergence for Self-Current Separable Proximal Blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Delay-insensitive convergence when the objective is block separable and selected blocks are read currently.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(x_i)\), where each \(g_i\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and \(\mu_i\)-strongly convex with \(\mu_i>0\). On selecting block \(i_k\), suppose the additive-correction method reads its own block currently and commits \[x_{i_k}^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma_{i_k}g_{i_k}}(x_{i_k}^k),\qquad \gamma_i>0.\] If every block is selected in each \(B\)-commit window, then, for the unique minimizer \(x^\star\), \[\|x^k-x^\star\|_\infty\le q^{\lfloor k/B\rfloor}\|x^0-x^\star\|_\infty,\qquad q=\max_i(1+\gamma_i\mu_i)^{-1}<1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For strongly convex separable blocks, current-self-block proximal replacements converge geometrically under bounded block starvation.
assumptions_latex: \(F(x)=\sum_i g_i(x_i)\) is block separable.
Each \(g_i\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, convex, and \(\mu_i\)-strongly convex.
The selected block's read is current and its commit is atomic.
Every block is selected within each \(B\)-commit window.
\(\gamma_i>0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The worker reads a delayed vector but the proximal formula uses the current committed block value \(x_{i_k}^k\), without specifying how that value is obtained atomically with computation or protected from intervening writes. An atomic replacement can therefore overwrite a later commit unless the model uses locking, recomputation at commit, or an additive stale correction. Moreover, properness and computability alone do not establish a single-valued proximal map without an explicit convention or additional assumptions. The cited asynchronous and synchronous sections must be inspected to determine the intended update.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Coordinate Fixed-Point Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Delayed relaxed component updates for solving a fixed-point equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\), let \(T:X\to X\), and seek \(x^\star=T(x^\star)\). Starting from \(x^0\), the worker producing commit \(k\) selects block \(i_k\), reads a delayed vector \(\hat x^k\), evaluates the residual component \(r_{i_k}^k=T_{i_k}(\hat x^k)-\hat x_{i_k}^k\), and atomically commits \[x^{k+1}=x^k+\eta_k P_{i_k}r_{i_k}^k,\] where \(\eta_k>0\) is a relaxation parameter. Other blocks retain their latest committed values. The method stops under a prescribed budget or when a consistently evaluated fixed-point residual meets tolerance, returning the latest committed iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers evaluate one component of a fixed-point residual on delayed state and atomically add a relaxed correction to that block.
assumptions_latex: \(T:X\to X\) is defined on a block product space.
Each selected-block commit is atomic.
\(\eta_k>0\) is prescribed.

Thus \|R(\widehat x)\|\le\varepsilon_r and \|x-\widehat x\|\le\varepsilon_d imply \|x-Tx\|\le\varepsilon_r+(1+L)\varepsilon_d.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-delay failure outside a compatible relaxation regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=\mathbb R\), let \(T(x)=-x\), with \(\operatorname{Fix}T=\{0\}\), use \(\eta=1\), and set \(\widehat x^k=x^{k-1}\). Then \(x^{k+1}=x^k-2x^{k-1}\). Its characteristic polynomial \(r^2-r+2\) has roots of modulus \(\sqrt2>1\), so every nonzero initialized trajectory fails to converge to the fixed point.
