knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let T be a q-contraction, 0\le q<1, in the block maximum norm, with fixed point x^\star. Use \eta_k=1 and require the activated block's own read to be current, \widehat x_{i_k}^k=x_{i_k}^k, so the commit replaces x_{i_k}^k by T_{i_k}(\widehat x^k). Suppose every other read component is a committed value at most \tau commits old and every block is selected at least once in each B consecutive commits. Then x^k\to x^\star. With E_0 denoting the maximum error over the initialized delay history, \|x^k-x^\star\|_\infty\le q^{\lfloor k/(B+\tau)\rfloor}E_0 after aligning epoch zero with that history.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A contractive fixed-point map converges geometrically under bounded delays and bounded block starvation when each full-relaxation commit is an actual block replacement.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the bounded-delay asynchronous contraction theorem, let \(0<q<1\), let \(E_0\) bound the initialized-history error, and let \(B\) and \(\tau\) be the coverage and delay bounds. For \(0<\varepsilon<E_0\), \[k\ge (B+\tau)\left\lceil\frac{\log(E_0/\varepsilon)}{-\log q}\right\rceil\] implies \(\|x^k-x^\star\|_\infty\le\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be a \(q\)-contraction, \(0\le q<1\), in the block maximum norm. For \[x^{k+1}=x^k+\eta P_{i_k}(T_{i_k}(\widehat x^k)-x_{i_k}^k),\] define \(q_\eta=1-\eta(1-q)\). After aligning epoch zero with the initialized delay history, \[\|x^k-x^\star\|_\infty\le q_\eta^{\lfloor k/(B+\tau)\rfloor}E_0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A self-current underrelaxed asynchronous coordinate iteration of a strict contraction converges geometrically under bounded delay and bounded block starvation.

The activated block's own read is current.
All other component delays are bounded by \(\tau\).
Every block is selected within each \(B\)-commit window.
\(0<\eta\le1\), and selected-block commits are atomic.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Accelerated Coordinate Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract delayed-gradient acceleration interface with bounded asynchronous reads.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the objective be differentiable and block-coordinate smooth. Initialize \(x^0=z^0\), choose positive weights \(v_i\), probabilities \(p_i>0\), and acceleration parameters \(\theta_k>0\). At update \(k\), form \(y^k=(1-\theta_k)x^k+\theta_k z^k\), read a delayed state \(\widehat y^k=y^{k-d_k}\), sample block \(i_k\), and set
\[
z^{k+1}=z^k-\frac{p_{i_k}}{\theta_k v_{i_k}}e_{i_k}\nabla_{i_k}f(\widehat y^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=y^k+\theta_kP^{-1}(z^{k+1}-z^k).
\]
The family is delay-compatible only when the chosen weights and acceleration schedule admit a Lyapunov decrease uniformly for \(0\le d_k\le\tau\). Stop under a prescribed residual or iteration budget and return the latest consistent state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An asynchronous accelerated coordinate scheme couples momentum states while using delayed block gradients; admissibility requires a delay-uniform Lyapunov decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable and block-coordinate smooth.
\(0\le d_k\le\tau<\infty\) and every \(p_i>0\).
The weights \(v_i\) and schedule \(\theta_k\) satisfy a delay-aware stability condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}=y^k+\theta_kP^{-1}(z^{k+1}-z^k)\) defines a compatible asynchronous accelerated update whenever the stated Lyapunov condition holds.

knowledge_statements.title: Serial Accelerated Coordinate Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-state acceleration with one randomized coordinate update per iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be convex and coordinate-smooth with constants \(L_i>0\). Initialize \(x^0=z^0\), choose probabilities \(p_i>0\), and select an estimate-sequence schedule \(\theta_k\in(0,1]\). At iteration \(k\), set \(y^k=(1-\theta_k)x^k+\theta_kz^k\), sample \(i_k\) with probability \(p_{i_k}\), and update
\[
z^{k+1}=z^k-\frac{p_{i_k}}{\theta_kL_{i_k}}e_{i_k}\nabla_{i_k}f(y^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=y^k+\theta_kP^{-1}(z^{k+1}-z^k).
\]
Only coordinate \(i_k\) changes in the correction. Stop under a prescribed accuracy or iteration budget and output \(x^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A serial accelerated coordinate method mixes two states, samples one coordinate, and applies a probability-scaled coordinate correction.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex, differentiable, and coordinate-smooth with constants \(L_i>0\).
\(\theta_k\) is chosen by a valid accelerated estimate-sequence construction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed recurrence specifies a one-block-at-a-time accelerated coordinate method.

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Parallel Coordinate Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous accelerated updates of a randomly sampled coordinate subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(x^0=z^0\), choose subset samples \(S_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), marginal probabilities \(p_i=\mathbb P(i\in S_k)>0\), safe curvature weights \(v_i>0\), and acceleration parameters \(\theta_k\). Form \(y^k=(1-\theta_k)x^k+\theta_kz^k\). In parallel for every \(i\in S_k\), compute
\[
(z^{k+1}-z^k)_i=-\frac{p_i}{\theta_kv_i}\nabla_i f(y^k),
\]
leaving unsampled coordinates unchanged, and synchronize
\[
x^{k+1}=y^k+\theta_kP^{-1}(z^{k+1}-z^k).
\]
The weights must satisfy an expected separable overapproximation for the joint sample. Stop at the chosen accuracy or budget and return \(x^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampled coordinates compute accelerated corrections concurrently, followed by a synchronized state update governed by joint-sampling curvature weights.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is convex and differentiable.
Each marginal probability satisfies \(p_i>0\).
The pair \((S_k,v)\) satisfies an expected separable overapproximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recurrence performs one synchronized accelerated parallel coordinate iteration.

notation.meaning: Coordinate subset selected at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Arbitrary-Sampling Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Probability-corrected acceleration for general proper coordinate-subset distributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S_k\) be independent samples from any proper distribution on coordinate subsets, with marginals \(p_i=\mathbb P(i\in S_k)>0\). Given safe weights \(v_i>0\), initialize \(x^0=z^0\) and form \(y^k=(1-\theta_k)x^k+\theta_kz^k\). Define the sampled correction by
\[
(z^{k+1}-z^k)_i=-\mathbf 1_{\{i\in S_k\}}\frac{p_i}{\theta_kv_i}\nabla_i f(y^k),
\]
and set
\[
x^{k+1}=y^k+\theta_kP^{-1}(z^{k+1}-z^k).
\]
Thus inverse marginal scaling removes first-moment sampling bias, while the weights encode higher-order inclusion dependence. Stop under the prescribed accuracy or iteration budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrary-sampling acceleration corrects each selected coordinate by its marginal probability while curvature weights account for joint inclusion dependence.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is convex and differentiable.
The sampling is proper: \(p_i>0\) for every coordinate.
The weights \(v_i\) satisfy a valid sampling-dependent overapproximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[P^{-1}(z^{k+1}-z^k)\mid y^k]\) includes every coordinate correction without marginal sampling bias.

notation.meaning: Indicator that coordinate i is sampled.

children.top_down_role: Structural effects arising when general subset sampling is executed concurrently.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling–Parallelism Interaction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected separable overapproximation condition coupling subset sampling and safe parallel curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a random subset \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), define \(h_{[S]}=\sum_{i\in S}e_i h_i\) and \(p_i=\mathbb P(i\in S)\). A vector \(v\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) is sampling-compatible for differentiable \(f\) if, for every \(x,h\in\mathbb R^n\),
\[
\mathbb E[f(x+h_{[S]})]\le f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\nabla_i f(x)h_i+\frac12\sum_{i=1}^n p_i v_i h_i^2.
\]
This condition determines safe simultaneous coordinate steps. Enlarging the subset or increasing positive inclusion dependence may require larger \(v_i\), so nominal parallelism and permitted step sizes cannot generally be chosen independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel sample size and dependence determine the curvature weights—and hence safe step sizes—through an expected separable overapproximation.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable.
\(S\) is a random coordinate subset with marginals \(p_i\).
\(v_i>0\) for every coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequality is the sampling–parallelism compatibility condition for simultaneous coordinate corrections.

notation.meaning: Vector h restricted to sampled coordinates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feasibility test for sampling-compatible curvature weights on a quadratic objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx+b^{\mathsf T}x+c\), where \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\), and define \(P_{ij}=\mathbb P(i,j\in S)\) and \(p_i=P_{ii}>0\). Then
\[
\mathbb E[f(x+h_{[S]})]=f(x)+\sum_i p_i\nabla_i f(x)h_i+\tfrac12h^{\mathsf T}(P\circ Q)h.
\]
Consequently, the ESO inequality with weights \(v\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) holds for every \(x,h\) if and only if
\[
\operatorname{Diag}(p\circ v)-P\circ Q\succeq0.
\]
A vector with negative quadratic form for this difference matrix is an explicit violation witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For quadratic objectives, ESO compatibility is equivalent to a positive-semidefinite matrix inequality involving joint inclusion probabilities; any negative direction witnesses failure.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric.
\(p_i=\mathbb P(i\in S)>0\) and \(P_{ij}=\mathbb P(i,j\in S)\).
\(v_i>0\) for every coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Diag}(p\circ v)-P\circ Q\succeq0\) is necessary and sufficient for the quadratic ESO inequality.

children.title: Restarted Coordinate Acceleration
children.top_down_role: Restart families for strongly curved, growth, or locally sharp regimes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistent epoch wrapper that resets every acceleration state at a common accepted point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal A_m(u)\) be the output of \(m\) iterations of a specified accelerated coordinate method initialized with all coupled acceleration states at \(u\). Set \(u^0=x^0\) and repeat
\[
\widetilde u^{r+1}=\mathcal A_m(u^r),\qquad
u^{r+1}=\begin{cases}
\widetilde u^{r+1},&F(\widetilde u^{r+1})\le F(u^r),\\
u^r,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
with the consistent identification \(u^{r+1}=\nu^{r+1}\) and \(\nu^0=u^0\). Equivalently, one may write the second branch directly as \(u^r\). Every new epoch reinitializes all acceleration states at \(u^{r+1}\). The acceptance safeguard ensures nonincreasing objective values at restart points but, by itself, does not imply a rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run a specified accelerated coordinate routine for fixed-length epochs, accept only a nonworsening endpoint, and reset all momentum states at the accepted point.
assumptions_latex: The base accelerated coordinate routine and epoch length \(m\) are specified.
The objective can be evaluated at restart points.
Each epoch initializes all coupled acceleration states consistently.

notation.meaning: Base accelerated coordinate routine run for one epoch.

knowledge_statements.title: Periodic Coordinate-Acceleration Restart

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric convergence obtained by restarting an inverse-square accelerated coordinate routine under quadratic growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume
\[
F(u)-F^*\ge\frac\mu2\operatorname{dist}(u,X^*)^2
\]
at restart points and
\[
\mathbb E[F(\mathcal A_m(u))-F^*\mid u]\le\frac{C}{m^2}\operatorname{dist}(u,X^*)^2.
\]
For \(u^{r+1}=\mathcal A_m(u^r)\),
\[
\mathbb E[F(u^{r+1})-F^*\mid u^r]\le
\rho\,[F(u^r)-F^*],\qquad \rho=\frac{2C}{\mu m^2}.
\]
Thus \(m^2>2C/\mu\) gives strict geometric contraction, and \(m=\Theta(\sqrt{C/\mu})\) gives
\[
O\!\left(\sqrt{C/\mu}\log\frac{F(u^0)-F^*}{\varepsilon}\right)
\]
base iterations. When \(m^2\le2C/\mu\), these assumptions alone do not certify contraction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic growth converts an inverse-square accelerated coordinate epoch bound into geometric convergence when the restart epoch is sufficiently long.
assumptions_latex: Quadratic growth with constant \(\mu>0\) holds at all restart points.
The reset accelerated coordinate routine has the displayed conditional inverse-square guarantee.
All acceleration states are restarted from the epoch input.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(m^2>2C/\mu\), restart epochs contract expected objective error by \(2C/(\mu m^2)<1\).

notation.meaning: Constant in the base routine's inverse-square guarantee.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Periodic or adaptive restart of an accelerated coordinate base routine.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal A_m(u)\) denote the output after \(m\) iterations of a fixed accelerated coordinate method initialized with coincident momentum states at \(u\). Choose an epoch length \(m\ge1\), set \(u^0=x^0\), and for epochs \(r=0,1,\ldots\) compute
\[
\widetilde u^{r+1}=\mathcal A_m(u^r),\qquad
u^{r+1}=\begin{cases}
\widetilde u^{r+1},&f(\widetilde u^{r+1})\le f(u^r),\\
u^r,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\]
where the accepted point reinitializes all momentum states. A fixed restart uses predetermined \(m\); an adaptive restart terminates an epoch when a stated growth, residual, or momentum test fires. Return the last accepted restart point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run coordinate acceleration in epochs, accept a nonworsening endpoint, and reset momentum periodically or when a specified trigger fires.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is bounded below and evaluable at restart points.
\(\mathcal A_m\) is a specified accelerated coordinate routine.
The restart length or adaptive trigger is fixed before each epoch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(u^{r+1})\le f(u^r)\) for every accepted restart epoch.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact factorization that implements dense mixing and sparse coordinate corrections without scanning all coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Represent \(r\) dense algorithm states by
\[
X^k=U^kM_k,
\]
where \(U^k\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) and \(M_k\in\mathbb R^{r\times r}\) is nonsingular. A global state mixing \(X^{k+1/2}=X^kB_k\) is implemented by \(M_{k+1}=M_kB_k\) while retaining \(U^k\). If a correction \(e_iq_k^{\mathsf T}\) is then added to the represented states, set
\[
U^{k+1}=U^k+e_iq_k^{\mathsf T}M_{k+1}^{-1}.
\]
Then \(U^{k+1}M_{k+1}=X^{k+1/2}+e_iq_k^{\mathsf T}\) exactly. For fixed \(r\), mixing and one coordinate-supported correction require constant scalar work plus access to one row of \(U\). The representation requires nonsingular \(M_{k+1}\); applying \(M_{k+1}^{-1}\) becomes numerically sensitive as its smallest singular value approaches zero, so stable implementations must reconstruct or refactor before that boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small coefficient matrix can carry dense acceleration mixing while a sampled correction changes only one stored basis row; singular or nearly singular mixing matrices mark the representation's failure boundary.
assumptions_latex: The accelerated state consists of a fixed number \(r\) of dense vectors.
Each iteration applies an \(r\)-state linear mixing followed by a coordinate-supported correction.
\(M_{k+1}\) is nonsingular, and coordinate-row access to \(U\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The factorized update exactly reproduces the dense-state update using coordinate-scale work for fixed \(r\).
knowledge_statements.title: Lazy Low-Dimensional Acceleration-State Representation
Efficient Acceleration Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lazy two-vector representation of dense acceleration mixing and sparse coordinate corrections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Represent two dense acceleration states by
\[
[\,x^k\ z^k\,]=[\,u^k\ v^k\,]M_k,
\]
where \(M_k\in\mathbb R^{2\times2}\) is nonsingular. Any global linear mixing \([\,x^{k+1}\ z^{k+1}\,]=[\,x^k\ z^k\,]B_k\) is implemented by \(M_{k+1}=M_kB_k\), without scanning coordinates. If the algorithm then adds \(e_iq_k^{\mathsf T}\) to the state pair, update only row \(i\) of the basis pair by
\[
[\,u_i^{k+1}\ v_i^{k+1}\,]=[\,u_i^k\ v_i^k\,]+q_k^{\mathsf T}M_{k+1}^{-1}.
\]
Thus mixing costs constant scalar work and a coordinate correction touches one stored row; occasional refactorization is required if conditioning deteriorates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two dense momentum states can be stored as a small coefficient matrix over two basis vectors, making global mixing constant-cost and corrections coordinate-local.
assumptions_latex: \(M_k\in\mathbb R^{2\times2}\) is nonsingular.
Each iteration consists of a two-state linear mixing and one coordinate-supported correction.
Basis-vector coordinate access has constant cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The represented state pair is updated exactly using \(O(1)\) scalar work plus one coordinate-row modification.

notation.meaning: Small coefficient matrix mapping basis vectors to algorithm states.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact work-model boundary between an accelerated coordinate implementation and its nonaccelerated baseline.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an accuracy target \(\varepsilon\). Let a baseline coordinate method require at most \(N_b(\varepsilon)\) iterations at cost \(c_b>0\) coordinate-equivalent operations per iteration. Let an accelerated implementation require at most \(N_a(\varepsilon)\) iterations, with per-iteration coordinate work \(c_a>0\), additional per-iteration mixing or synchronization work \(q\ge0\), and setup cost \(s\ge0\). Under this declared additive upper-bound model, the accelerated guarantee improves total work exactly when
\[
s+(c_a+q)N_a(\varepsilon)<c_bN_b(\varepsilon).
\]
If \(N_b=C\kappa\log(1/\varepsilon)\), \(N_a=C_a\sqrt\kappa\log(1/\varepsilon)\), and \(s=0\), this becomes
\[
c_a+q<\frac{C}{C_a}c_b\sqrt\kappa.
\]
The conclusion is conditional on the stated cost and iteration bounds and is not an implementation-independent acceleration theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate acceleration reduces modeled work only when its setup, coordinate work, mixing, and synchronization costs remain below the work saved by its smaller iteration bound.
assumptions_latex: The compared iteration quantities are valid upper bounds for the same accuracy criterion.
All costs use the same coordinate-equivalent work convention.
The additive cost model accounts for the implementation overhead being compared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequality is necessary and sufficient for improvement within the declared upper-bound work model.

notation.meaning: Per-iteration accelerated mixing or synchronization overhead.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Work Acceleration Crossover
Acceleration Applicability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work-complexity boundary where acceleration overhead cancels its iteration advantage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a strongly convex regime with condition parameter \(\kappa\ge1\). Suppose a nonaccelerated coordinate method needs at most \(C\kappa\log(1/\varepsilon)\) coordinate-equivalent operations, while an accelerated implementation needs \(C_a q\sqrt\kappa\log(1/\varepsilon)\), where \(q\ge1\) measures dense mixing, synchronization, or delay-control overhead per accelerated iteration. Acceleration improves this work model only if
\[
q<\frac{C}{C_a}\sqrt\kappa.
\]
If the execution model forces \(q\ge(C/C_a)\sqrt\kappa\), its nominal square-root iteration gain does not reduce total coordinate-equivalent work. This boundary compares work, not merely iteration counts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceleration loses its work advantage when per-iteration mixing, synchronization, or delay overhead reaches the square root of the condition parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(\kappa\ge1\) is the relevant strong-convexity condition parameter.
Both methods target objective accuracy \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\).
Costs are measured in coordinate-equivalent operations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\ge(C/C_a)\sqrt\kappa\) eliminates the accelerated method's advantage in the stated work model.

notation.meaning: Accelerated per-iteration overhead in coordinate-equivalent units.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the leaf, and the threshold follows algebraically from the two assumed work bounds. Those bounds and the interpretation of q as dense-mixing, synchronization, or delay overhead have no cited support, so the proposed applicability boundary remains a model-dependent unsourced claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Realized Descent Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise decrease from minimizing a coordinate-smooth upper model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume coordinate smoothness:
\[
f(x+he_i)\le f(x)+h\nabla_i f(x)+\frac{L_i}{2}h^2
\]
for every point \(x\), scalar \(h\), and coordinate \(i\). For the realized coordinate \(i_k\), choose \(h_k=-\nabla_{i_k}f(x^k)/L_{i_k}\) and set \(x^{k+1}=x^k+h_ke_{i_k}\). Substitution into the upper model gives the pathwise inequality
\[
f(x^{k+1})\le f(x^k)-\frac{|\nabla_{i_k}f(x^k)|^2}{2L_{i_k}}.
\]
The decrease holds for each realized coordinate, independently of how that coordinate was selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing the coordinate quadratic upper model yields an explicit objective decrease for every realized coordinate update.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable.
Coordinate \(i\) has smoothness constant \(L_i>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharp Coordinate Stepsize Boundary for Realized Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise descent range and its sharp scalar-quadratic failure boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the coordinate upper model with constant \(L_i>0\), the update \(x^+=x-\alpha_i\nabla_i f(x)e_i\) satisfies
\[
f(x^+)\le f(x)-\alpha_i\left(1-\frac{L_i\alpha_i}{2}\right)|\nabla_i f(x)|^2.
\]
Consequently strict decrease is guaranteed when \(\nabla_i f(x)\ne0\) and \(0<\alpha_i<2/L_i\). The range is sharp: for \(f(t)=L_it^2/2\), \(\alpha_i=2/L_i\) preserves the objective and \(\alpha_i>2/L_i\) increases it at every nonzero point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Realized coordinate descent is guaranteed below twice the reciprocal coordinate curvature, and a scalar quadratic shows that boundary is sharp.
assumptions_latex: The selected coordinate satisfies the quadratic upper model with constant \(L_i>0\).
The update uses a scalar stepsize \(\alpha_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0<\alpha_i<2/L_i\implies f(x^+)<f(x)\text{ whenever }\nabla_i f(x)\ne0,\text{ and the interval is sharp.}
knowledge_statements.title: Sharp Coordinate Stepsize Boundary for Realized Descent

knowledge_statements.title: Expected-Descent Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected objective decrease obtained by averaging realized coordinate descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^+=x-(\nabla_I f(x)/L_I)e_I\), where coordinate \(I\) is sampled with probabilities \(p_i>0\). If the coordinate-smooth upper model holds with constants \(L_i\), then conditioning on \(x\) and averaging the realized decrease yields
\[
\mathbb E[f(x^+)\mid x]\le f(x)-\frac12\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{p_i}{L_i}|\nabla_i f(x)|^2.
\]
Equivalently, with \(D=\operatorname{diag}(L_i/p_i)\), the decrement is \(\tfrac12\|\nabla f(x)\|_{D^{-1}}^2\). This converts pathwise coordinate progress into a deterministic conditional drift bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging coordinate-wise decrease produces a weighted squared-gradient decrement determined by sampling probabilities and coordinate smoothness.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable and coordinate-smooth.
\(\mathbb P(I=i)=p_i>0\) and \(\sum_i p_i=1\).

notation.meaning: Random coordinate selected for the update.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected Descent with General Coordinate Stepsizes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional expected decrease for coordinate-smooth updates using general scalar coordinate stepsizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbb P(I=i\mid x)=p_i>0\) and set \(x^+=x-\alpha_I\nabla_I f(x)e_I\). If \(f(x+he_i)\le f(x)+h\nabla_i f(x)+(L_i/2)h^2\), then
\[
\mathbb E[f(x^+)\mid x]\le f(x)-\sum_{i=1}^n p_i\alpha_i\left(1-\frac{L_i\alpha_i}{2}\right)|\nabla_i f(x)|^2.
\]
Thus \(0<\alpha_i<2/L_i\) gives a positive decrement coefficient, while \(\alpha_i=1/L_i\) recovers the seed's reciprocal-curvature formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging general coordinate-gradient steps weights each squared partial gradient by its sampling probability and quadratic-model decrease coefficient.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) satisfies the coordinate quadratic upper model with constants \(L_i>0\).
\(\mathbb P(I=i\mid x)=p_i>0\) and \(\sum_i p_i=1\).
\(\alpha_i>0\) for every coordinate.

notation.meaning: Stepsize used when coordinate i is selected.
Conditional probability of selecting coordinate i.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge 0}\) be a filtration. For each \(k\ge 0\), let \(V_k\), \(G_k\), \(a_k\), and \(\varepsilon_k\) be nonnegative \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable random variables, and let \(V_{k+1}\) be \(\mathcal F_{k+1}\)-measurable. Assume all displayed terms are integrable and
\[
\mathbb E[V_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]\le V_k-a_kG_k+\varepsilon_k
\]
almost surely. Taking expectations and summing from \(k=0\) to \(N-1\) gives, for every integer \(N\ge 1\),
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\mathbb E[a_kG_k]\le \mathbb E[V_0]-\mathbb E[V_N]+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\mathbb E[\varepsilon_k]\le \mathbb E[V_0]+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\mathbb E[\varepsilon_k].
\]
Thus the conditional inequality provides an interface between one-step sampling calculations and global expected-progress bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditional potential decrease separates one-step sampling analysis from global convergence: taking expectations and telescoping bounds cumulative expected progress by the initial potential and accumulated expected errors.

knowledge_statements.title: Quasi-Fejér Distance Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stochastic quasi-Fejér recursion with summable errors and residual decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed subset of a Hilbert space and let \((x^k)\) be adapted to \((\mathcal F_k)\). Suppose that for every \(z\in C\),
\[
\mathbb E[\|x^{k+1}-z\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le(1+\eta_k)\|x^k-z\|^2-c_kR_k+\varepsilon_k
\]
almost surely, where \(R_k\ge0\), \(c_k\ge0\), and \(\sum_k\eta_k<\infty\), \(\sum_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\). Then \(\|x^k-z\|^2\) converges almost surely for each \(z\in C\), and
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}c_kR_k<\infty
\]
almost surely. Additional cluster-point assumptions are required to conclude convergence of the iterates to a point of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A summably perturbed conditional distance decrease makes distances converge and forces the weighted residual decreases to be summable.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is nonempty and closed in a Hilbert space.
\(\sum_k\eta_k<\infty\) and \(\sum_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\) almost surely.
The conditional quasi-Fejér inequality holds for every \(z\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(z\in C\), \(\|x^k-z\|^2\) converges and \(\sum_k c_kR_k<\infty\) almost surely.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated conclusion is theorem-level quasi-Fejer/supermartingale knowledge even though property is a plausible container role. No source is supplied, and the record does not fully specify whether eta_k and epsilon_k are adapted random variables or deterministic sequences, nor the integrability conditions needed for the conditional supermartingale result. An authoritative theorem citation and a source-aligned formulation are required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed general cluster-point criterion for whole-sequence convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\) be nonempty and closed. If \((x^k)\) is bounded, \(\|x^k-z\|\) converges for every \(z\in C\), and every cluster point belongs to \(C\), then \(x^k\) converges to a point of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergent distances to every target point and admissibility of all cluster points force whole-sequence convergence in finite dimensions.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset\mathbb R^d\) is nonempty and closed.
\((x^k)\) is bounded and every target-point distance converges.
Every cluster point belongs to \(C\).

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Residual Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected residual decrease for uniform randomized block updates of an averaged operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=H_1\oplus\cdots\oplus H_n\), let \(T:H\to H\) be \(\alpha\)-averaged with \(0<\alpha<1\), and let \(Z=\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\). Given \(x\in H\), sample \(i\) uniformly from \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and set \(x^+=x+U_i(Tx-x)\), where \(U_i\) is the orthogonal projector onto block \(H_i\). Then, for every \(z\in Z\), \[\mathbb E[\|x^+-z\|^2\mid x]\leq \|x-z\|^2-\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha n}\|x-Tx\|^2.\] Thus summability of the expected distance decreases implies summability of the squared fixed-point residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform randomized block update of an averaged operator decreases expected squared distance to every fixed point by a multiple of the full residual squared.
assumptions_latex: \(H=\bigoplus_{i=1}^n H_i\) is a Hilbert-space orthogonal decomposition.
\(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged and \(\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
\(i\) is sampled uniformly and independently conditional on the current iterate.

children.top_down_role: Connections between distance control and fixed-point residual control.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual and Distance Need Not Be Linearly Equivalent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonexpansive scalar example showing failure of the reverse residual-distance inequality without metric subregularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be \(T(x)=x/(1+|x|)\). Then \(T\) is nonexpansive, \(\operatorname{Fix}T=\{0\}\), and \[|x-Tx|=\frac{|x|^2}{1+|x|},\qquad \frac{|x-Tx|}{\operatorname{dist}(x,\operatorname{Fix}T)}\to0\quad(x\to0).\] Thus \(I-T\) is not metrically subregular at zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonexpansiveness alone does not make residual size linearly equivalent to fixed-set distance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\text{ is nonexpansive, but }I-T\text{ is not metrically subregular at }0.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual and Distance Need Not Be Linearly Equivalent
Distance–Residual Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local equivalence between fixed-point distance and residual under metric subregularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be nonexpansive on a Hilbert space, let \(Z=\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\), and define \(R=I-T\). For every \(x\in H\), \(\|R(x)\|\leq 2\operatorname{dist}(x,Z)\). If, on a neighborhood \(U\) of \(Z\), the residual is metrically subregular in the form \(\operatorname{dist}(x,Z)\leq\kappa\|R(x)\|\), then \[\kappa^{-1}\operatorname{dist}(x,Z)\leq\|R(x)\|\leq2\operatorname{dist}(x,Z),\qquad x\in U.\] Hence residual convergence and distance-to-fixed-set convergence are locally equivalent, with explicit comparison constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonexpansive map, residual is at most twice fixed-set distance; metric subregularity supplies the reverse inequality and makes the two measures locally equivalent.
assumptions_latex: \(T:H\to H\) is nonexpansive and \(Z=\operatorname{Fix}T\neq\varnothing\).
\(\operatorname{dist}(x,Z)\leq\kappa\|(I-T)x\|\) holds for \(x\) in a neighborhood \(U\) of \(Z\).

children.title: Coordinate Error-Bound Mechanisms

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error bound using a block-scaled proximal-gradient residual for a separable composite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n g_i(x_i)\), \(D=\operatorname{diag}(L_1I,\ldots,L_nI)\succ0\), \(T_D(x)=\operatorname{prox}^{D}_{g}(x-D^{-1}\nabla f(x))\), and \(R_D(x)=D(x-T_D(x))\). A composite coordinate error bound on \(S\) is \[\operatorname{dist}_{D}(x,X^*)\le\kappa\|R_D(x)\|_{D^{-1}},\qquad x\in S.\] Moreover, \(R_D(x)=0\iff0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial g(x)\); for convex \(F\), this is equivalent to \(x\in X^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite coordinate error bound controls solution-set distance by a scaled proximal-gradient residual whose zeros are stationary points.
assumptions_latex: \(g=\sum_i g_i\) is proper, closed, and block separable.
\(D\succ0\) is block diagonal.
For equivalence with global optimality, \(F\) is convex and \(X^*\neq\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual vanishing at a nonoptimal stationary point cannot control distance to the global minimizer set there.

\(R(\bar x)=0\) for some \(\bar x\notin X^*\).

Coordinate Error-Bound Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Level-set error bound expressed through a weighted coordinate-gradient residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable with nonempty minimizer set \(X^*\), and partition the variables into \(n\) blocks. Given block constants \(L_i>0\), define \(D=\operatorname{diag}(L_1I,\ldots,L_nI)\). A coordinate error bound holds on a set \(S\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\) with modulus \(\kappa>0\) when \[\operatorname{dist}_{D}(x,X^*)\leq\kappa\|\nabla f(x)\|_{D^{-1}}\qquad\text{for every }x\in S.\] Equivalently, the distance to the solution set is controlled by the aggregate of the normalized coordinate residuals \(\sum_iL_i^{-1}\|\nabla_i f(x)\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordinate error bound controls weighted distance to the solution set by the weighted norm of all block gradients on a specified region.

\(L_i>0\) for every coordinate block.
\(S\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\) is the region on which the bound is asserted.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonquadratic order-p objective growth in a coordinate-weighted metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f^*=\min f\), \(X^*=\operatorname{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\), and \(D\succ0\) be block diagonal. The objective has quadratic growth on \(S\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\) with modulus \(\mu_g>0\) if \[f(x)-f^*\geq\frac{\mu_g}{2}\operatorname{dist}_{D}(x,X^*)^2\qquad\text{for every }x\in S.\] This condition separates objective value from its minimum at least quadratically in weighted distance, without requiring uniqueness of a minimizer or global strong convexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Growth-to-Rate Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-rate transfer from residual descent and an objective-residual domination inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Delta(x)=f(x)-f^*\geq0\), and let \(R(x)\) be a coordinate residual. Suppose iterates remain in a set \(S\) and satisfy \(\mathbb E[\Delta(x^{k+1})\mid x^k]\leq\Delta(x^k)-c\|R(x^k)\|^2\) with \(c>0\). If growth and an error bound yield \(\Delta(x)\leq\beta\|R(x)\|^2\) on \(S\), where \(\beta\geq c\), then \[\mathbb E[\Delta(x^{k+1})\mid x^k]\leq\left(1-\frac{c}{\beta}\right)\Delta(x^k),\qquad \mathbb E\Delta(x^k)\leq\left(1-\frac{c}{\beta}\right)^k\Delta(x^0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected residual descent becomes a geometric objective rate whenever objective error is uniformly bounded above by the squared residual.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb E[\Delta(x^{k+1})\mid x^k]\leq\Delta(x^k)-c\|R(x^k)\|^2\).
\(\Delta(x)\leq\beta\|R(x)\|^2\) on the invariant set \(S\).
\(0<c\leq\beta\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity boundary for convergence conclusions based on coordinatewise minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=[-1,1]^2\) and \(F(x,y)=\max\{x,y\}\), the point \((0,0)\) minimizes each one-block restriction with the other block fixed at zero, but \(F'(0,0;(-1,-1))=-1\). Hence it is coordinatewise minimal without being directionally stationary or locally minimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex nonsmooth objective can be minimal on every coordinate slice at a point while admitting strict joint-direction descent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (0,0)\text{ is coordinatewise minimal but neither directionally stationary nor locally minimal.}

Block Successive-Minimization Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity of cluster points for cyclic exact or majorizing surrogate block minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be continuously differentiable on the Cartesian product \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_n\), where each \(X_i\) is nonempty, closed, and convex. At iteration \(k\), cyclically replace block \(i\) by a minimizer of a continuous surrogate \(u_i(\cdot;x)\) that majorizes the corresponding block objective, agrees with it at the current block, and has the same block directional derivative there. Assume the initial lower level set is compact and every surrogate subproblem has a unique minimizer. Then \(F(x^k)\) converges, every cluster point \(\bar x\) is coordinatewise minimal, and regularity of \(F\) at \(\bar x\) implies \(0\in\nabla F(\bar x)+N_X(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under compactness, consistent majorizing surrogates, and unique block solutions, cyclic successive minimization has stationary cluster points and convergent objective values.

Each block surrogate is continuous, majorizing, value-consistent, and first-order consistent, with a unique minimizer.
\(\{x\in X:F(x)\leq F(x^0)\}\) is compact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every cluster point \(\bar x\) satisfies \(0\in\nabla F(\bar x)+N_X(\bar x)\), provided \(F\) is regular at \(\bar x\).

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Convex Coordinate Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected objective complexity of serial randomized coordinate descent for smooth convex objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be convex and differentiable, with block-coordinate Lipschitz constants \(L_i>0\), and let \(D=\operatorname{diag}(L_1I,\ldots,L_nI)\). At each iteration choose a block uniformly and set \(x_i^+=x_i-L_i^{-1}\nabla_i f(x)\). If \(R_D=\sup\{\operatorname{dist}_D(x,X^*):f(x)\leq f(x^0)\}<\infty\), then serial coordinate descent satisfies \[\mathbb E[f(x^k)-f^*]=O\!\left(\frac{nR_D^2}{k}\right).\] Consequently, \(O(nR_D^2/\varepsilon)\) coordinate-gradient evaluations suffice to make the expected objective error at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform serial coordinate descent reaches expected objective error epsilon in order n times the squared weighted level-set radius divided by epsilon updates.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex, differentiable, and has block-coordinate Lipschitz constants \(L_i>0\).
\(X^*=\operatorname{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\).
The weighted lower-level-set radius \(R_D\) is finite.

notation.meaning: Weighted radius of the initial lower level set relative to the solution set

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Coordinate Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric expected complexity under strong convexity in the block Lipschitz metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) have block-coordinate Lipschitz constants \(L_i>0\), and let \(D=\operatorname{diag}(L_1I,\ldots,L_nI)\). Suppose \(f\) is \(\mu_D\)-strongly convex in the norm \(\|\cdot\|_D\). Uniform serial coordinate descent, using \(x_i^+=x_i-L_i^{-1}\nabla_i f(x)\), admits a universal constant \(c>0\) such that \[\mathbb E[f(x^k)-f^*]\leq\left(1-\frac{c\mu_D}{n}\right)^k(f(x^0)-f^*).\] Therefore \(O((n/\mu_D)\log((f(x^0)-f^*)/\varepsilon))\) coordinate-gradient evaluations suffice for expected objective error at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity changes the smooth coordinate-descent rate from inverse-linear to geometric, requiring order n over weighted strong convexity times a logarithmic accuracy factor.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable with block-coordinate Lipschitz constants \(L_i>0\).
\(f\) is \(\mu_D\)-strongly convex in \(\|\cdot\|_D\).
Blocks are sampled independently and uniformly.

Uniform exact proximal-coordinate updates admit a universal \(c>0\) such that \[\mathbb E[F(x^k)-F^*]\le\left(1-\frac{c\mu_D}{n}\right)^k(F(x^0)-F^*).\] Thus \(O((n/\mu_D)\log((F(x^0)-F^*)/\varepsilon))\) block-gradient and block-proximal evaluations suffice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted strong convexity gives geometric expected convergence for uniform proximal-coordinate descent as well as for the smooth method.

The regularizer is proper, closed, convex, and block separable.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Convex Coordinate Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sublinear complexity for randomized block-proximal descent with a separable nonsmooth term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_i(x_i)\), where \(f\) is convex and differentiable with block-coordinate Lipschitz constants \(L_i>0\), and each \(\psi_i\) is proper, closed, and convex. Uniformly sample block \(i\) and minimize \[\langle\nabla_i f(x),u-x_i\rangle+\frac{L_i}{2}\|u-x_i\|^2+\psi_i(u).\] Let \(D=\operatorname{diag}(L_iI)\), let \(X^*=\operatorname{argmin}F\neq\varnothing\), define \(R_D=\sup\{\operatorname{dist}_D(x,X^*):F(x)\leq F(x^0)\}<\infty\), and set \(\Delta_0=F(x^0)-F^*\). Then \[\mathbb E[F(x^k)-F^*]=O\!\left(\frac{n(R_D^2+\Delta_0)}{k}ight).\] Consequently, \(O(n(R_D^2+\Delta_0)/\varepsilon)\) block-gradient and block-proximal evaluations suffice for expected objective error at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomized block-proximal coordinate descent for a separable convex composite objective has inverse-linear expected error, with its bound depending on both the weighted level-set radius and the initial objective gap.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex, differentiable, and block-coordinate smooth with constants \(L_i>0\).
Each \(\psi_i\) is proper, closed, convex, and block separable.
\(X^*=\operatorname{argmin}F\neq\varnothing\), and the initial lower level set has finite \(D\)-radius \(R_D\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Coordinate Stationarity Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected weighted-gradient stationarity for randomized coordinate descent on a smooth nonconvex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, bounded below by \(f_{\inf}\), and block-coordinate smooth with constants \(L_i>0\). Uniformly sample block \(i_k\) and set \(x_{i_k}^{k+1}=x_{i_k}^k-L_{i_k}^{-1}\nabla_{i_k}f(x^k)\), leaving other blocks unchanged. With \(D=\operatorname{diag}(L_iI)\), \[\min_{0\leq k<K}\mathbb E\|\nabla f(x^k)\|_{D^{-1}}^2\leq\frac{2n(f(x^0)-f_{\inf})}{K}.\] Hence \(O(n(f(x^0)-f_{\inf})/\varepsilon^2)\) coordinate-gradient evaluations suffice to obtain an iterate whose expected squared weighted gradient norm is at most \(\varepsilon^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform randomized coordinate descent finds an epsilon-stationary point in order n times the initial objective gap divided by epsilon squared coordinate updates.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and bounded below by \(f_{\inf}>-\infty\).
Each block gradient is Lipschitz along its block with constant \(L_i>0\).
Blocks are sampled independently and uniformly.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform-Sampling Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Policy-dependent linear complexity for uniform sampling of smooth strongly convex coordinate updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex in the Euclidean norm and have coordinate Lipschitz constants \(L_i>0\). Choose \(i_k\) uniformly from \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and update \(x_{i_k}^{k+1}=x_{i_k}^k-L_{i_k}^{-1}\nabla_{i_k}f(x^k)\). Writing \(L_{\max}=\max_iL_i\), the method has the policy-dependent bound \[\mathbb E[f(x^k)-f^*]\leq\left(1-\frac{\mu}{nL_{\max}}\right)^k(f(x^0)-f^*).\] Consequently, \(O((nL_{\max}/\mu)\log((f(x^0)-f^*)/\varepsilon))\) coordinate updates suffice for expected objective error at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform coordinate sampling yields a linear rate governed by n times the largest coordinate smoothness constant divided by strong convexity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and \(\mu\)-strongly convex in the Euclidean norm.
Coordinate \(i\) has Lipschitz gradient constant \(L_i>0\).
Coordinates are sampled independently with probability \(1/n\).

notation.meaning: Uniformly sampled coordinate at iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Importance-Sampling Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear complexity obtained by sampling coordinates proportionally to their smoothness constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be \(\mu\)-strongly convex in the Euclidean norm and have coordinate Lipschitz constants \(L_i>0\). Define \(S_L=\sum_{j=1}^nL_j\), sample coordinate \(i\) with probability \(p_i=L_i/S_L\), and update \(x_i^+=x_i-L_i^{-1}\nabla_i f(x)\). Then \[\mathbb E[f(x^k)-f^*]\leq\left(1-\frac{\mu}{S_L}\right)^k(f(x^0)-f^*).\] Thus \(O((S_L/\mu)\log((f(x^0)-f^*)/\varepsilon))\) coordinate updates suffice for expected objective error at most \(\varepsilon\), replacing the uniform-sampling factor \(nL_{\max}\) by \(\sum_iL_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampling coordinates proportionally to smoothness replaces the uniform condition factor n times maximum smoothness by the sum of coordinate smoothness constants.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and \(\mu\)-strongly convex in the Euclidean norm.
Coordinate \(i\) has Lipschitz gradient constant \(L_i>0\).
Coordinates are sampled independently with \(p_i=L_i/\sum_jL_j\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Policy Complexity Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Serial randomized coordinate descent under coordinate smoothness and Euclidean strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and \(\mu\)-strongly convex, with coordinate constants \(L_i>0\) satisfying \(f(x+t e_i)\le f(x)+t\nabla_i f(x)+L_i t^2/2\). At each iteration sample \(i\) with probability \(p_i>0\) and set \(x^+=x-(\nabla_i f(x)/L_i)e_i\). With \(\Lambda(p)=\max_i L_i/p_i\), \[\mathbb{E}[f(x^k)-f^*]\le \left(1-\frac{\mu}{\Lambda(p)}\right)^k(f(x^0)-f^*).\] Hence \(k\ge \Lambda(p)\mu^{-1}\log((f(x^0)-f^*)/\varepsilon)\) suffices. Uniform sampling gives \(\Lambda=n\max_iL_i\), whereas \(p_i=L_i/\sum_jL_j\) minimizes \(\Lambda\) and gives \(\Lambda=\sum_iL_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Importance probabilities proportional to coordinate smoothness improve the standard serial bound from n times the largest coordinate constant to the sum of all coordinate constants.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(\mu>0\).
Each coordinate derivative has finite smoothness constant \(L_i>0\).
The coordinate samples are independent with probabilities \(p_i>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharp Range of the Importance-Sampling Improvement Factor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Range of the certified serial complexity-factor improvement over uniform sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(n\ge2\) and \(L_i>0\). The certified factor improvement from uniform sampling to \(p_i\propto L_i\) is \[R=\frac{nL_{\max}}{\sum_{i=1}^nL_i}.\] Since \(L_{\max}\le\sum_iL_i\le nL_{\max}\), \(1\le R<n\). Equality \(R=1\) holds exactly when all \(L_i\) are equal, while the supremum \(n\) is approached when one coordinate constant dominates and the other positive constants tend to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Importance sampling gives no certified improvement for equal coordinate smoothness and can approach an n-fold improvement under extreme heterogeneity.
assumptions_latex: \(L_i>0\) for every coordinate.
Uniform and importance policies use the same per-update cost model.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Naive Simultaneous Coordinate Curvature Can Increase the Objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled quadratic showing that scalar coordinate curvatures need not be safe for a simultaneous minibatch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\ge3\) and \(\delta>0\), let \(f(x)=\tfrac12(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x)^2+\tfrac\delta2\|x\|_2^2\). Every scalar coordinate has curvature \(1+\delta\). Starting from \(x^0=c\mathbf1\), update all coordinates simultaneously by \(x_i^+=x_i^0-\nabla_i f(x^0)/(1+\delta)\). Then \(x^+=\rho x^0\), where \(\rho=(1-n)/(1+\delta)\), and \(f(x^+)=\rho^2f(x^0)\). Hence whenever \(0<\delta<n-2\), the simultaneous step strictly increases the objective although each scalar curvature is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a densely coupled quadratic, combining individually exact coordinate steps can increase the objective unless minibatch interaction is included in the curvature.
assumptions_latex: All coordinates are updated simultaneously using scalar curvature \(1+\delta\).

notation.meaning: Scalar factor relating the new iterate to the old iterate

knowledge_statements.title: Naive Simultaneous Coordinate Curvature Can Increase the Objective

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion structure for uniform sampling without replacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let S be uniform over all \tau-element subsets of \{1,\ldots,n\}, where 1\le\tau\le n. Then \mathbb P(i\in S)=\tau/n and, for n\ge2 and i\ne j, \mathbb P(i,j\in S)=\tau(\tau-1)/(n(n-1)).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform fixed-size minibatch has exchangeable marginal and pairwise inclusion probabilities determined by n and its size.
assumptions_latex: 1\le\tau\le n.
S is uniform over all subsets of cardinality \tau.
n\ge2 for the pairwise formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Fixed-Size Minibatch Inclusion Probabilities

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Minibatch Complexity for Separable Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-free fixed-size minibatch rate when selected separable coordinates are minimized exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_i(x_i)\), where each \(\phi_i\) attains its minimum \(\phi_i^*\). At every iteration sample uniformly a \(\tau\)-element subset \(S_k\), independently across iterations, and replace each selected coordinate by a minimizer of \(\phi_i\). Then \[\mathbb E[f(x^k)-f^*]=\left(1-\frac\tau n\right)^k(f(x^0)-f^*).\] Hence \(\left\lceil\log((f(x^0)-f^*)/\varepsilon)/[-\log(1-\tau/n)]\right\rceil\) minibatch iterations suffice when \(\tau<n\), while \(\tau=n\) solves the problem in one iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a separable objective, exact updates of a uniform fixed-size minibatch remove the selected coordinate gaps and yield an exact geometric rate.
assumptions_latex: \(1\le\tau\le n\).
The objective is separable by scalar coordinates.
Each selected coordinate is replaced by an exact component minimizer.
Minibatches are independent and uniform among all size-\(\tau\) subsets.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Minibatch Complexity for Separable Objectives

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strongly convex objective-error rate for a fixed-size minibatch with interaction-adjusted curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_k\) be independent and uniform over all \(\tau\)-element subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Suppose \[\mathbb E[f(x+h_{[S_k]})]\le f(x)+\frac\tau n\sum_i\nabla_i f(x)h_i+\frac\tau{2n}\sum_i v_i h_i^2.\] Update every \(i\in S_k\) by \(h_i=-\nabla_i f(x^k)/v_i\). Define \(w_i=nv_i/\tau\). If \(f\) is differentiable and \(\mu_w\)-strongly convex in \(\|\cdot\|_w\), where \(0<\mu_w\le1\), then \[\mathbb E[f(x^k)-f^*]\le(1-\mu_w)^k(f(x^0)-f^*).\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint and monotonicity properties of the standard partial-separability factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integers \(n\ge2\), \(1\le\tau\le n\), and \(1\le\omega\le n\), define \(\beta(\tau)=1+(\omega-1)(\tau-1)/(n-1)\). Then \(1\le\beta(\tau)\le\min\{\tau,\omega\}\), \(\beta(1)=1\), \(\beta(n)=\omega\), and \(\tau/\beta(\tau)\) is nondecreasing in \(\tau\). Moreover, \(\omega=1\) gives \(\tau/\beta(\tau)=\tau\), whereas \(\omega=n\) gives \(\tau/\beta(\tau)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard interference factor interpolates from ideal linear minibatch scaling for separable objectives to no iteration speedup for fully coupled objectives.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dense Coupling Attains the Full Minibatch Interference Factor
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic witness showing tightness of the dense-interaction endpoint \(\beta(\tau)=\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}x)^2\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), and let \(S\) be uniform over all \(\tau\)-element subsets. Every scalar coordinate curvature equals one. For \(h=\mathbf1\), \[\mathbb E\left[(\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}h_{[S]})^2\right]=\tau^2.\] An ESO quadratic term of the form \(\beta\,\mathbb E\|h_{[S]}\|_2^2=\beta\tau\) therefore requires \(\beta\ge\tau\). Since \((\sum_{i\in S}h_i)^2\le\tau\sum_{i\in S}h_i^2\), \(\beta=\tau\) is sufficient and sharp.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a rank-one densely coupled quadratic, the fixed-size minibatch interference factor equals the batch size, so worst-case iteration speedup disappears.

children.title: Cyclic-Ordering Complexity
children.top_down_role: Coordinate complexity under repeated deterministic traversal orders.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact epoch contraction characterization for repeated fixed-order coordinate minimization on a positive-definite quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx-b^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(Q\succ0\). Repeatedly update coordinates in the fixed order \(1,\ldots,n\) by \(x_i^+=x_i-(Qx-b)_i/Q_{ii}\). With \(T_i=I-e_ie_i^{\mathsf T}Q/Q_{ii}\), one epoch maps errors by \(x^+-x^*=T_{\mathrm{cyc}}(x-x^*)\), where \(T_{\mathrm{cyc}}=T_n\cdots T_1\). Setting \(q_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\|T_{\mathrm{cyc}}\|_Q^2<1\), \[f(x^{mn})-f^*\le q_{\mathrm{cyc}}^m(f(x^0)-f^*).\] Thus \(n\left\lceil\log((f(x^0)-f^*)/\varepsilon)/(-\log q_{\mathrm{cyc}})\right\rceil\) coordinate updates suffice.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an SPD quadratic, repeated cyclic coordinate minimization is governed exactly by the energy-norm contraction of its ordered sweep matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is symmetric positive definite.
Every coordinate update exactly minimizes along that coordinate.
The same fixed order is repeated every epoch.

notation.meaning: Squared energy-norm contraction of one fixed sweep

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-window deterministic generalization of repeated cyclic traversal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A coordinate sequence \((i_k)_{k\ge0}\) is essentially cyclic with window length \(M\ge n\) if, for every \(k\), \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\subseteq\{i_k,\ldots,i_{k+M-1}\}\). Ordinary traversal of one fixed permutation repeatedly is essentially cyclic with \(M=n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An essentially cyclic policy visits every coordinate within each bounded window; repeating a fixed permutation is the shortest-window case.
assumptions_latex: \(M\ge n\).
Every coordinate occurs in every consecutive window of \(M\) selections.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: A Coupled Quadratic Is Strictly Sensitive to Cyclic Order
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit SPD quadratic whose objective after one exact coordinate-minimization sweep depends on the fixed order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx\), where \[Q=\begin{pmatrix}2&1&0\\1&2&1\\0&1&2\end{pmatrix}\succ0,\qquad x^0=(1,1,1)^{\mathsf T}.\] Exact coordinate minimization in order \((1,2,3)\) gives \(x^+=(-\tfrac12,-\tfrac14,\tfrac18)\) and \(f(x^+)=27/64\). Order \((2,1,3)\) gives \(\widehat x^+=(\tfrac12,-1,\tfrac12)\) and \(f(\widehat x^+)=1/2\). Thus two complete fixed cyclic orders have different one-sweep progress on the same SPD quadratic and starting point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two cyclic coordinate orders produce different complete-sweep objective values on an explicit positive-definite quadratic.

children.title: Permutation Complexity
children.top_down_role: Coordinate complexity under fixed or randomized coordinate permutations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition needed to iterate a one-epoch expected contraction across permutation epochs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a permutation policy satisfies \(\mathbb E[\Phi(x^{r+1})\mid\mathcal F_r]\le q\Phi(x^r)\) for every epoch \(r\), with \(\Phi\ge0\) and \(q<1\), then \(\mathbb E\Phi(x^m)\le q^m\Phi(x^0)\). An inequality averaged only over one initially drawn permutation does not by itself imply this recursion when that same permutation is reused, because the required conditional inequality at later iterates has not been established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric reshuffling complexity requires an epochwise conditional contraction; a one-time average over an initially drawn order is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb E[\Phi(x^{r+1})\mid\mathcal F_r]\le q\Phi(x^r)\) holds at every epoch.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional-Contraction Boundary for Random Reshuffling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes complete-permutation policies by how the epoch order is sampled and reused.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Pi_n\) be the permutations of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let \(\pi_r\in\Pi_n\) be the order used in epoch \(r\). A one-time-randomized policy draws \(\pi_0\) once and sets \(\pi_r=\pi_0\) thereafter. An independently reshuffled policy redraws \(\pi_r\) independently from a fixed law each epoch. A deterministic fixed permutation is the degenerate reuse case and belongs to cyclic-order analysis. All three visit every coordinate exactly once per epoch but have different inter-epoch laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete-permutation policies differ according to whether an order is drawn once and reused or redrawn each epoch; deterministic reuse is the cyclic boundary case.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi_n\) is the set of complete coordinate permutations.
Every epoch applies each coordinate exactly once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\pi_r=\pi_0\) under one-time reuse, whereas independently reshuffled epochs redraw \(\pi_r\) each epoch.

notation.meaning: Set of permutations of n coordinates

Exact minimization of coordinate i sets x_i=b_i/q_i independently of all other coordinates. Hence applying every coordinate exactly once in any permutation produces x^* after one epoch.

Each coordinate is exactly minimized once.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed Permutation Reuse and Independent Reshuffling Are Not Equivalent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-coordinate quadratic separating the epoch laws of one-time randomization and independent reshuffling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x,y)=\tfrac12(x^2+2\rho xy+y^2)\), with \(0<\rho<1\), start from \((1,0)\), and exactly minimize each coordinate. Order \((1,2)\) reaches \((0,0)\) in one epoch, whereas order \((2,1)\) reaches \((\rho^2,-\rho)\). If a uniformly random first permutation is thereafter reused, then after two epochs \[\mathbb E f(x^2)=\tfrac14\rho^6(1-\rho^2).\] If an independent uniform permutation is drawn in each epoch, then \[\mathbb E f(x^2)=\tfrac18(\rho^4+\rho^6)(1-\rho^2).\] These values differ for \(0<\rho<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Drawing one random order and reusing it has a different two-epoch law from independently reshuffling every epoch, even on a two-dimensional SPD quadratic.
assumptions_latex: Each coordinate is minimized exactly once per epoch.
Each random permutation is uniform on the two possible orders.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Permutation Reuse and Independent Reshuffling Are Not Equivalent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete independently reshuffled epoch rate for exact coordinate minimization of a coupled SPD quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x,y)=\tfrac12(x^2+2\rho xy+y^2)\), where \(0<\rho<1\). In each epoch independently choose either coordinate order \((1,2)\) or \((2,1)\), each with probability \(1/2\), and exactly minimize each coordinate once. Then, conditionally on the current iterate, \[\mathbb E[f(x^{r+1},y^{r+1})\mid x^r,y^r]\le q_\rho f(x^r,y^r),\qquad q_\rho=\frac{\rho^2(1+\rho)}2<1.\] Consequently, \(\mathbb E f(x^m,y^m)\le q_\rho^m f(x^0,y^0)\), and \(2\lceil\log(f(x^0,y^0)/\varepsilon)/(-\log q_\rho)\rceil\) coordinate minimizations suffice for expected error at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform independent reshuffling has an explicit geometric epoch rate on the two-coordinate coupled quadratic.
assumptions_latex: Each epoch independently uses either complete order with probability \(1/2\).
Every selected coordinate is minimized exactly.

notation.meaning: Worst conditional expected contraction of one uniformly reshuffled epoch

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected Sweep-Matrix Certificate for Independent Reshuffling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable arbitrary-dimensional contraction certificate for exact coordinate minimization of an SPD quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx-b^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(Q\succ0\), and let \(T_\pi\) be the error-propagation matrix for one epoch of exact coordinate minimization in permutation \(\pi\). For a distribution \(\mu\) on complete permutations define \[M_\mu=\mathbb E_{\pi\sim\mu}[T_\pi^{\mathsf T}QT_\pi],\qquad q_\mu=\lambda_{\max}\!\left(Q^{-1/2}M_\mu Q^{-1/2}\right).\] Then \(0\le q_\mu<1\) and \[\mathbb E_{\pi\sim\mu}\|T_\pi z\|_Q^2\le q_\mu\|z\|_Q^2\quad\text{for every }z.\] If permutations are redrawn independently from \(\mu\) each epoch, \[\mathbb E[f(x^m)-f^*]\le q_\mu^m(f(x^0)-f^*).\] Consequently, \(n\left\lceil\log((f(x^0)-f^*)/\varepsilon)/(-\log q_\mu)\right\rceil\) coordinate minimizations suffice when \(q_\mu>0\); if \(q_\mu=0\), one epoch suffices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite generalized eigenvalue gives the exact worst conditional expected energy contraction of one independently reshuffled quadratic epoch and its geometric complexity.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is symmetric positive definite.
Every epoch exactly minimizes every coordinate once.
Epoch permutations are independently drawn from the fixed law \(\mu\).

notation.meaning: one-epoch error-propagation matrix for permutation pi
expected energy matrix after one permutation epoch

knowledge_statements.title: Expected Sweep-Matrix Certificate for Independent Reshuffling
Permutation Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent random-permutation epochs for exact coordinate minimization of a quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the quadratic setting \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx-b^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(Q\succ0\), let \(T_i=I-e_i e_i^{\mathsf T}Q/Q_{ii}\). At epoch \(r\), draw an independent permutation \(\pi_r\) and apply its coordinates once, so \(T_{\pi}=T_{\pi(n)}\cdots T_{\pi(1)}\). Define \[q_{\mathrm{perm}}=\sup_{z\ne0}\frac{\mathbb{E}_{\pi}\|T_{\pi}z\|_Q^2}{\|z\|_Q^2}<1.\] Then \[\mathbb{E}[f(x^{mn})-f^*]\le q_{\mathrm{perm}}^m(f(x^0)-f^*),\] and \(n\lceil\log((f(x^0)-f^*)/\varepsilon)/(-\log q_{\mathrm{perm}})\rceil\) coordinate updates suffice in expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Random-permutation complexity is governed by the worst expected energy contraction of one independently reshuffled epoch.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is symmetric positive definite.
Each epoch uses an independent permutation from a fixed distribution.
Each selected coordinate is exactly minimized once per epoch.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The expected epoch complexity is \(O(\!\log((f(x^0)-f^*)/\varepsilon)/(-\log q_{\mathrm{perm}}))\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic tail conversion proposed for a conditionally contracting epoch potential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Delta_r=f(x^r)-f^*\ge0\). If \(\mathbb E[\Delta_{r+1}\mid\mathcal F_r]\le q\Delta_r\) for every \(r\), where \(0<q<1\), then \(\mathbb P(\Delta_m>\varepsilon)\le q^m\Delta_0/\varepsilon\). Hence \(m\ge\lceil\log(\Delta_0/(\varepsilon\delta))/(-\log q)\rceil\) implies \(\mathbb P(\Delta_m\le\varepsilon)\ge1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative conditionally contracting potential admits a Markov-inequality tail bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Epochwise Ordering Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Like-for-like comparison using complete-sweep contraction factors and ordering overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any two epochwise coordinate policies \(A\) and \(B\) applied to the same positive-definite quadratic, let \(q_A,q_B\in(0,1)\) satisfy \(\mathbb{E}[f(x^{m+1})-f^*\mid x^m]\le q_A(f(x^m)-f^*)\) and the analogous inequality for \(B\). If their epoch costs are \(c_A,c_B>0\), their certified work bounds are \[W_A(\varepsilon)=c_A\left\lceil\frac{\log((f(x^0)-f^*)/\varepsilon)}{-\log q_A}\right\rceil,\qquad W_B(\varepsilon)=c_B\left\lceil\frac{\log((f(x^0)-f^*)/\varepsilon)}{-\log q_B}\right\rceil.\] Thus a smaller contraction factor implies fewer epochs, but not necessarily less work when permutation generation, synchronization, or coordinate-access costs differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ordering policies should be compared by both complete-epoch contraction and epoch cost; better contraction alone need not mean lower total work.
assumptions_latex: Both policies use the same objective gap and epoch convention.
Each policy has a uniform conditional epoch contraction factor.
All ordering overhead is included in the corresponding epoch cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Policy \(A\) has the smaller certified work bound exactly when \(W_A(\varepsilon)\le W_B(\varepsilon)\).

Greedy-Selection Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gauss–Southwell–Lipschitz selection with explicit coordinate-search overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable and \(\mu\)-strongly convex, with coordinate smoothness constants \(L_i>0\). knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Speedup Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wall-clock speedup accounting for convergence inflation and per-iteration coordination overhead.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a serial coordinate method require \(K_1(\varepsilon)\) iterations of cost \(c>0\). Suppose a \(P\)-worker implementation requires at most \(K_P(\varepsilon)\le(1+\delta_P)K_1(\varepsilon)\) iterations and each parallel iteration costs at most \(c/P+h\), where \(h\ge0\) is nonparallel overhead. Its speedup satisfies \[S_P(\varepsilon)=\frac{cK_1(\varepsilon)}{(c/P+h)K_P(\varepsilon)}\ge\frac{P}{(1+\delta_P)(1+Ph/c)}.\] Therefore speedup is within a constant factor of \(P\) whenever both the convergence inflation \(\delta_P\) and the overhead ratio \(Ph/c\) remain bounded independently of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel coordinate updates achieve near-linear wall-clock speedup only while convergence inflation and accumulated coordination overhead remain bounded.
assumptions_latex: Serial and parallel runs use the same accuracy criterion.
Parallel iteration count is inflated by at most \(1+\delta_P\).
The stated compute-plus-overhead timing model applies.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((E_k)_{k\ge-\tau}\) be nonnegative and satisfy \[E_{k+1}\le(1-a)E_k+b\max_{k-\tau\le j\le k}E_j\] for an integer delay bound \(\tau\ge0\), coefficients \(0\le b<a\le1\), and \(1-a+b>0\). Let \(q_\tau\in(0,1)\) be the unique root of \[q^{\tau+1}=(1-a)q^\tau+b.\] With \(M=\max_{-\tau\le j\le0}E_jq_\tau^{-j}\), one has \(E_k\le Mq_\tau^k\) for every \(k\ge0\). Thus any asynchronous coordinate method whose error quantity obeys this recurrence converges linearly despite bounded staleness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded-delay error recurrence converges linearly when its fresh-step contraction strictly dominates the delayed-error coefficient, apart from the excluded degenerate zero-factor case.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharpness of fresh-contraction dominance for the bounded-delay recurrence family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonnegative sequences satisfying \[E_{k+1}\le(1-a)E_k+b\max_{k-\tau\le j\le k}E_j,\] strict dominance \(b<a\) is necessary for a uniform convergence-to-zero conclusion over all admissible histories. If \(b=a\), every positive constant sequence is admissible and does not approach zero. If \(b>a\), already for \(\tau=0\) the equality recurrence \(E_{k+1}=(1-a+b)E_k\) grows geometrically from every \(E_0>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fresh contraction must strictly dominate delayed feedback: equality permits stagnation and reversed dominance permits geometric growth even without delay.
assumptions_latex: The conclusion is required uniformly over all sequences satisfying the displayed recurrence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b=a\) permits nonzero stagnation and \(b>a\) permits geometric growth; hence uniform convergence requires \(b<a\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Delay-induced inflation of sufficient update bounds for a standard scalar error recurrence.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the recurrence \(E_{k+1}\le(1-a)E_k+b\max_{k-\tau\le j\le k}E_j\), assume \(0\le b<a\le1\) and \(1-a+b>0\). Let \(q_\tau\in(0,1)\) solve \(q^{\tau+1}=(1-a)q^\tau+b\), and choose a common constant \(M>0\) that is a valid initial-error bound for both the delayed and zero-delay comparisons. A sufficient delayed-update bound for \(E_k\le\varepsilon\) is \[K_\tau(\varepsilon)=\left\lceil\frac{\log(M/\varepsilon)}{-\log q_\tau}\right\rceil.\] The zero-delay factor is \(q_0=1-a+b\), and \(q_\tau\) is nondecreasing in \(\tau\). Using the same \(M\) and ignoring ceilings, the ratio of these sufficient bounds is \[\frac{\log(M/\varepsilon)/(-\log q_\tau)}{\log(M/\varepsilon)/(-\log q_0)}=\frac{-\log q_0}{-\log q_\tau}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a common initial-error bound, bounded staleness weakens the contraction factor and inflates the corresponding sufficient update bound by the ratio of logarithmic rates.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the accepted recurrence assumptions, additionally suppose \(0<b<a\). For the root \(q_\tau\in(0,1)\) satisfying \[q_\tau^{\tau+1}=(1-a)q_\tau^\tau+b,\] one has \[q_\tau\uparrow1,\qquad \tau(1-q_\tau)\to\log(a/b),\qquad -\log q_\tau\sim\frac{\log(a/b)}{\tau}.\] Therefore, with a common delay-independent initial bound \(M\) and fixed \(\varepsilon<M\), the unrounded sufficient update count satisfies \[K_\tau(\varepsilon)\sim\frac{\tau\log(M/\varepsilon)}{\log(a/b)}.\] If \(b=0\) and \(a<1\), then \(q_\tau=1-a\) and this delay penalty is absent.

children.title: Convex Accelerated Coordinate Rates
children.top_down_role: Accelerated coordinate complexity in the general convex setting.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard smooth-convex accelerated coordinate upper rate under matched Euclidean geometry and square-root smoothness sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be convex and differentiable and satisfy \[f(x+te_i)\le f(x)+t\nabla_i f(x)+\frac{L_i}{2}t^2\] for \(L_i>0\). Let \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\), \(R=\lVert x^0-x^*\rVert_2<\infty\), and \(S=\sum_{i=1}^n\sqrt{L_i}\). There exists an accelerated randomized coordinate method, sampling coordinate \(i\) proportionally to \(\sqrt{L_i}\) and using one partial derivative per update, for which \[\mathbb E[f(x^k)-f(x^*)]\le \frac{C S^2R^2}{(k+1)^2}\] with an absolute method-dependent initialization constant \(C>0\). Hence \(O(SR/\sqrt\varepsilon)\) coordinate-gradient evaluations suffice for expected objective error at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Square-root importance sampling permits inverse-square expected objective decay, with coordinate-oracle complexity proportional to the sum of square roots of coordinate smoothness constants.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and coordinatewise smooth with constants \(L_i>0\).
A minimizer \(x^*\) exists and \(\lVert x^0-x^*\rVert_2<\infty\).
The accelerated method and its sampling and initialization conventions are matched to the displayed Euclidean geometry.

notation.meaning: sum of square roots of coordinate smoothness constants

knowledge_statements.title: Importance-Sampled Convex Accelerated Coordinate Rate
Convex Accelerated Coordinate Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected objective rate for smooth convex minimization with importance-sampled accelerated coordinate updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be convex and differentiable, with \(f(x+t e_i)\le f(x)+t\nabla_i f(x)+L_i t^2/2\) for every \(i\), \(x\), and \(t\). Let \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin} f\), \(R=\lVert x^0-x^*\rVert_2\), and \(S=\sum_{i=1}^n\sqrt{L_i}\). An accelerated randomized coordinate method using probabilities \(p_i=\sqrt{L_i}/S\) has an implementation satisfying \[\mathbb E[f(x^k)-f(x^*)]\le \frac{C S^2R^2}{(k+1)^2},\] where \(C>0\) is an absolute initialization constant. Consequently, achieving expected error at most \(\varepsilon>0\) requires \(k=\mathcal O(SR/\sqrt{\varepsilon})\) coordinate-gradient evaluations.

children.title: Strongly Convex Accelerated Coordinate Rates
children.top_down_role: Accelerated coordinate complexity under strong convexity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Importance-Sampled Strongly Convex Accelerated Coordinate Rate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard geometric accelerated coordinate upper rate under Euclidean strong convexity and matched coordinate smoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, coordinatewise \(L_i\)-smooth, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex in the Euclidean norm, with \(L_i>0\) and \(\mu>0\). Set \(S=\sum_{i=1}^n\sqrt{L_i}\) and \(\Delta_0=f(x^0)-f(x^*)\). There exists an accelerated randomized coordinate method using square-root importance sampling and one partial derivative per update such that \[\mathbb E[f(x^k)-f(x^*)]\le C\Delta_0\exp\!\left(-c k\frac{\sqrt\mu}{S}\right)\] for positive absolute method-dependent constants \(c,C\). Consequently, \[k=O\!\left(\frac{S}{\sqrt\mu}\log\frac{\Delta_0}{\varepsilon}\right)\] coordinate-gradient evaluations suffice for expected error at most \(\varepsilon\in(0,\Delta_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Euclidean strong convexity converts accelerated coordinate convergence to geometric decay with square-root dependence on the matched coordinate condition parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is coordinatewise \(L_i\)-smooth and Euclidean \(\mu\)-strongly convex.
The accelerated algorithm, square-root sampling rule, and Euclidean geometry are matched.
One coordinate partial derivative is charged per update.

notation.meaning: sum of square roots of coordinate smoothness constants

Thus the coordinate-oracle complexity for expected error at most \(\varepsilon\in(0,\Delta_0)\) is \(\mathcal O((S/\sqrt\mu)\log(\Delta_0/\varepsilon))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity converts the accelerated inverse-square rate into geometric decay, with a condition factor equal to weighted coordinate smoothness divided by the square root of strong convexity.

children.title: Convexity-Regime Transitions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact relation between simultaneously valid convex and strongly convex accelerated coordinate bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the same expected gap \(G_k\) satisfies \[G_k\le \frac{A}{(k+1)^2}\qquad\text{and}\qquad G_k\le B e^{-\alpha k},\] where \(A,B,\alpha>0\). Then \[G_k\le\min\!\left\{\frac{A}{(k+1)^2},Be^{-\alpha k}\right\}.\] Every crossover of the two displayed upper bounds is determined by \(A/(k+1)^2=Be^{-\alpha k}\), so it depends on \(A/B\) as well as \(\alpha\); the condition scale \(1/\alpha\) alone does not determine it. For accelerated coordinate bounds with \(\alpha\) proportional to \(\sqrt\mu/S\), the geometric complexity scale diverges as \(\mu\downarrow0\), while the convex inverse-square estimate remains valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The valid combined guarantee is the minimum of the matched convex and strongly convex bounds, and its crossover depends on constants and initial data as well as the condition scale.
assumptions_latex: Both displayed bounds apply to the same method output, expected gap, initialization, and oracle count.
\(A,B,\alpha>0\).
The identification \(\alpha\asymp\sqrt\mu/S\) is made only when supplied by a matched strongly convex coordinate theorem.
