children.title: Accelerated Arbitrary-Sampling Complexity
children.top_down_role: Accelerated complexity under general block-subset sampling.

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Arbitrary-Sampling Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: ESO-parameterized accelerated rate for random subsets of coordinate blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be a proper sampling with inclusion probabilities \(p_i=\mathbb P(i\in\widehat S)>0\). Suppose an expected separable overapproximation holds with constants \(v_i>0\), and define \(\Psi=\max_i v_i/p_i^2\). For a convex objective with a minimizer \(x^*\), an accelerated arbitrary-sampling coordinate method governed by this overapproximation has the canonical bounds \[\mathbb E[f(x^k)-f(x^*)]=\mathcal O\!\left(\frac{\Psi R^2}{k^2}\right),\qquad k=\mathcal O\!\left(\frac{R\sqrt\Psi}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\right),\] where \(R=\lVert x^0-x^*\rVert_2\). Sampling dependence therefore enters through both \(v_i\) and \(p_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For general random block subsets, accelerated complexity is controlled by the largest overapproximation constant divided by the square of that block’s inclusion probability.
assumptions_latex: \(p_i>0\) for every block.
The sampling satisfies an expected separable overapproximation with constants \(v_i\).
The accelerated method uses sampling-compatible steps and estimate-sequence weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(k=\mathcal O(R\sqrt\Psi/\sqrt\varepsilon)\) sampled-subset iterations suffice in the convex regime.

notation.meaning: Marginal probability that block i is sampled

children.title: Accelerated Parallel Complexity
children.top_down_role: Accelerated coordinate complexity under simultaneous block updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Parallel Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work-depth guarantee for conflict-free batches of accelerated coordinate updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an accelerated coordinate execution requiring \(K(\varepsilon)\) coordinate-oracle calls to reach expected error \(\varepsilon\). Suppose every consecutive group of at most \(\tau\) calls acts on mutually compatible blocks, so their read sets and write sets do not interfere and the grouped execution is algebraically identical to the serial trace. With \(\tau\) processors, the same trace has parallel depth \[D_\tau(\varepsilon)=\left\lceil\frac{K(\varepsilon)}{\tau}\right\rceil.\] In particular, if \(K(\varepsilon)=\mathcal O(SR/\sqrt\varepsilon)\), then \(D_\tau(\varepsilon)=\mathcal O(SR/(\tau\sqrt\varepsilon)+1)\). This ideal linear speedup requires compatibility; simultaneous conflicting updates are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conflict-free batches preserve the serial accelerated trace, dividing its coordinate-oracle depth by the processor count up to rounding and an additive constant.
assumptions_latex: At most \(\tau\) mutually compatible coordinate calls execute per parallel round.
Grouping compatible calls preserves the serial iterates exactly.
Communication and scheduling overhead are excluded from depth.

notation.meaning: Serial coordinate-oracle complexity at accuracy epsilon

children.title: Accelerated Asynchronous Complexity
children.top_down_role: Accelerated coordinate complexity under delayed or stale block updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Asynchronous Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional linear-rate complexity under bounded stale-update perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Phi_k\ge0\) be the potential of an accelerated asynchronous coordinate method. Assume the serial accelerated step contracts by \(\rho\in(0,1)\), while bounded staleness produces a relative perturbation satisfying \(\mathbb E[\Phi_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]\le(1-\rho+c\eta^2)\Phi_k\), with \(c>0\) and \(0\le\eta<\sqrt{\rho/c}\). Then \[\mathbb E\Phi_k\le(1-\rho+c\eta^2)^k\Phi_0,\] and reaching \(\mathbb E\Phi_k\le\varepsilon\) requires \(k=\mathcal O((\rho-c\eta^2)^{-1}\log(\Phi_0/\varepsilon))\) completed asynchronous updates. Thus stale reads reduce the effective accelerated contraction from \(\rho\) to \(\rho-c\eta^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If stale-update error remains below the accelerated contraction margin, asynchronous acceleration retains geometric convergence with a delay-degraded contraction factor.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi_k\) is nonnegative and adapted to \(\mathcal F_k\).
The stated conditional perturbation recursion holds uniformly.
\(c\eta^2<\rho\).

notation.meaning: Relative perturbation level induced by staleness

children.title: Acceleration–Asynchrony Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where delay or conflict limits the benefit of coordinate acceleration.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact boundary at which an asynchronous perturbation consumes the contraction margin of an accelerated potential recursion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a nonnegative accelerated potential satisfies \[\mathbb E[\Phi_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]\le q\Phi_k,\qquad q=1-\rho+c\eta^2,\] with \(0<\rho\le1\), \(c>0\), and \(\eta\ge0\). The recursion certifies geometric contraction exactly when \(c\eta^2<\rho\). At \(c\eta^2=\rho\) it certifies only nonincrease, and for \(c\eta^2>\rho\) it supplies no contraction guarantee. Equality recursions with \(q=1\) or \(q>1\) respectively permit a positive constant potential or geometric growth, so the boundary is sharp for this abstract recursion. If a separate algorithm-specific analysis proves \(\eta\le G(d,\Delta)\), then \(cG(d,\Delta)^2<\rho\) is sufficient, but no delay threshold follows without that estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceleration survives an asynchronous perturbation certificate only while the perturbation term remains strictly below the serial contraction margin; equality permits stagnation and larger perturbations permit growth in the abstract recursion.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi_k\ge0\) and the displayed conditional recursion holds.
Any conversion from \(\eta\) to delay or block interference is supplied by a separate algorithm-specific result.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c\eta^2<\rho\) is necessary and sufficient for contraction of the displayed certificate.

notation.meaning: optional algorithm-specific perturbation bound in terms of delay and interference

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Perturbation-Certificate Boundary
Acceleration–Asynchrony Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perturbation threshold separating accelerated contraction from loss of a geometric guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an asynchronous accelerated potential satisfying \(\mathbb E[\Phi_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]\le(1-\rho+c\eta^2)\Phi_k\), geometric contraction is certified precisely when \(c\eta^2<\rho\). If a delay analysis supplies \(\eta\le\gamma d\sqrt\Delta\), where \(d\) is the maximum delay, \(\Delta\) is a block-interference parameter, and \(\gamma\) is the step scale, then the sufficient acceleration region is \[d<\frac{1}{\gamma}\sqrt{\frac{\rho}{c\Delta}}.\] At or above this threshold the displayed recursion no longer yields contraction; this is failure of the certificate, not by itself a divergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceleration is certified only while delay-induced interference stays below the serial contraction margin; beyond that boundary the standard potential argument ceases to prove convergence.
assumptions_latex: The asynchronous potential obeys the displayed perturbation recursion.
The perturbation estimate \(\eta\le\gamma d\sqrt\Delta\) holds.
\(c,\gamma,\Delta>0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case query lower bound for deterministic one-coordinate-at-a-time derivative access.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(a\in\{-1,1\}^n\), let \(f_a(x)=\tfrac12\|x-a\|_2^2\) and \(x^0=0\). Suppose a deterministic algorithm adaptively queries one index \(i\) per call and receives only \(\nabla_i f_a(x)=x_i-a_i\). After \(k<n\) calls, there is a sign vector consistent with the transcript for which \[f_a(x^k)-f_a(a)\ge\frac{n-k}{2}.\] Thus worst-case relative error at most \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) requires at least \(n(1-\varepsilon)\) calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic one-coordinate oracle must reveal nearly every hidden coordinate even for a separable strongly convex quadratic.

A serial coordinate oracle queried at index \(i\) returns only \(\nabla_i f_a(x)=x_i-a_i\). After \(k<n\) distinct coordinate queries, an adversary may retain an unrevealed sign on every unqueried coordinate, so any deterministic algorithm has worst-case residual \[f_a(x^k)-f_a(a)\ge\frac{n-k}{2}.\] Since \(f_a(x^0)-f_a(a)=n/2\), attaining relative error at most \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) requires at least \(n(1-\varepsilon)\) serial coordinate queries.

children.title: Randomized Coordinate-Oracle Lower Bounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected query lower bound for randomized algorithms receiving one selected partial derivative per call.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a\) be uniform on \(\{-1,1\}^n\), let \(f_a(x)=\tfrac12\|x-a\|_2^2\), and start from \(x^0=0\). Suppose each adaptive query selects one coordinate \(i\) and returns only \(\nabla_i f_a(x)=x_i-a_i\). After \(k\le n\) calls, every randomized algorithm satisfies \[\mathbb E_{a,r}[f_a(x^k)-f_a(a)]\ge \frac{n-k}{2}.\] Consequently, some fixed \(a\) satisfies \(\mathbb E_r[f_a(x^k)-f_a(a)]\ge(n-k)/2\), and expected relative error at most \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) requires \(k\ge n(1-\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomization cannot avoid inspecting nearly every hidden coordinate when each query reveals only one partial derivative.
assumptions_latex: The internal random seed is independent of \(a\).
Each charged call returns information about only one selected coordinate.
The output is measurable with respect to the query transcript and internal randomness.
knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Hidden-Coordinate Lower Bound
Randomized Coordinate-Oracle Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributional lower bound for randomized single-coordinate derivative algorithms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Draw \(a\) uniformly from \(\{-1,1\}^n\) and let \(f_a(x)=\tfrac12\lVert x-a\rVert_2^2\), with \(x^0=0\). A coordinate query at index \(i\) reveals only \(a_i\). Conditional on any transcript containing \(k\) distinct queried coordinates, every unqueried sign remains independent and symmetric; hence every estimator \(x^k\) satisfies \[\mathbb E_a[f_a(x^k)-f_a(a)]\ge\frac{n-k}{2}.\] By the distributional principle, every randomized coordinate-oracle algorithm has a fixed instance with the same expected lower bound. Therefore expected relative error at most \(\varepsilon\) requires \(k\ge n(1-\varepsilon)\) queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomization cannot avoid learning almost all hidden coordinates on a separable quadratic: each unqueried sign contributes an unavoidable expected error.

A query reveals information about only its selected coordinate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous round lower bound with at most p nonadaptive coordinate queries per round.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a\) be uniform on \(\{-1,1\}^n\), let \(f_a(x)=\tfrac12\lVert x-a\rVert_2^2\), and take \(x^0=0\). Suppose a synchronous oracle permits at most \(p\) coordinate-gradient queries per round and queries in a round cannot depend on answers from that round. After \(T\) rounds, at most \(pT\) signs have been revealed, so every possibly randomized algorithm satisfies \[\mathbb E_{a,\mathcal A}[f_a(x^T)-f_a(a)]\geq\frac{(n-pT)_+}{2}.\] Hence any method guaranteeing expected relative error at most \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) for every instance requires \[T\geq\left\lceil\frac{n(1-\varepsilon)}p\right\rceil.\]

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Response-Delay Coordinate Information Lower Bound
Asynchronous Coordinate Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information lower bound combining worker throughput with mandatory oracle-response delay.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_a(x)=\tfrac12\lVert x-a\rVert_2^2\) with \(a\) uniform on \(\{-1,1\}^n\). Consider \(p\) workers issuing coordinate queries in rounds, where every answer is unavailable for exactly \(d\) subsequent rounds and at most \(p\) new coordinate signs can be returned per round thereafter. By round \(T\), at most \(p(T-d)_+\) signs are known, so \[\mathbb E[f_a(x^T)-f_a(a)]\ge\frac{(n-p(T-d)_+)_+}{2}.\] Consequently, expected relative error at most \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) requires \(T\ge d+n(1-\varepsilon)/p\). Delay and finite parallel information throughput therefore contribute additive barriers in this oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When coordinate answers arrive after d rounds, the hidden-sign quadratic imposes both a delay latency and the usual information-throughput lower bound.
assumptions_latex: There are at most \(p\) coordinate answers per round.
Every oracle response has fixed delay \(d\).
An unrevealed coordinate sign is independent of the transcript.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T\ge d+n(1-\varepsilon)/p\) rounds are necessary for expected relative error \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Maximum number of coordinate answers per round

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive delay bound is conditional on a fixed-response-delay oracle that may not represent standard stale-read asynchronous coordinate methods. A source and precise round/response convention are required.

children.title: Parallelism–Delay Barriers

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Response Latency Is Not Stale-Read Delay
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Model-transfer boundary for additive delay lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A lower bound that assumes an oracle answer is unavailable for \(d\) rounds does not automatically apply to a shared-memory stale-read method with read age at most \(\tau=d\). In the latter model a worker may immediately compute and commit from an old snapshot; the delay bounds information age rather than imposing response latency. Transferring an additive \(d\)-round term therefore requires an explicit reduction between the two execution models.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Response latency and stale-read age constrain different events, so an additive latency lower bound cannot be transferred merely by identifying their numerical delay parameters.
assumptions_latex: The response-latency model delays availability of oracle answers.
The stale-read model permits immediate computation from a snapshot up to \(\tau\) commits old.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d=\tau\ \text{alone does not imply transfer of a response-latency lower bound to a stale-read execution}.
knowledge_statements.title: Response Latency Is Not Stale-Read Delay

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Duplicate-Update Barrier under Common Stale Reads
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conflict-based obstruction to uniform parallel speedup when delay permits a common snapshot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\geq2\) workers minimize \(f(x)=x^2/2\) in one shared coordinate using overwrite commits. Suppose all workers read the same nonzero value, compute the exact coordinate minimizer \(0\), and subsequently overwrite the coordinate with \(0\). The \(p\) computations produce the same final state as one computation. When commits are indexed sequentially, the last update's read has age \(p-1\); thus the schedule satisfies a bounded-delay model only when \(\tau\geq p-1\). Under such a model, processor count and bounded delay alone cannot guarantee uniform \(p\)-fold useful-work speedup.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the delay allowance permits p workers to act on one common snapshot, conflicting overwrites can duplicate all but one worker's progress.
assumptions_latex: \(p\geq2\) workers use overwrite commits.
No rule prevents simultaneous selection of the same coordinate.
The delay allowance satisfies \(\tau\geq p-1\).
Useful progress is compared at visible commit boundaries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The final state after }p\text{ overwrites equals the state after one overwrite; uniform }p\text{-fold speedup is impossible from }(p,\tau)\text{ alone}.

notation.meaning: maximum read age measured in committed writes

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate-Update Barrier under Common Stale Reads
Parallelism–Delay Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A conflict-based obstruction to uniform parallel speedup under delayed coordinate updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an overwrite-based shared-memory coordinate method using \(p\) workers, with each update computed from a read delayed by at most \(\tau\) committed writes. For the one-coordinate quadratic \(f(x)=x^2/2\), embedded as one active coordinate in any dimension, suppose all workers read the same value \(x\), compute the same exact coordinate minimizer, and overwrite that coordinate. Then the \(p\) computations produce the same state change as one computation. Hence no worst-case guarantee can yield uniform \(p\)-fold speedup from parallelism and bounded delay alone; additional assumptions controlling coordinate conflicts, sampling, or interaction sparsity are necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Concurrent stale updates can duplicate one another, so processor count and bounded delay alone cannot guarantee linear speedup without conflict or sparsity control.
assumptions_latex: \(p\ge 2\) workers use overwrite semantics.
Read delays are bounded by \(\tau\ge 0\).
No restriction prevents simultaneous selection of the same coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform worst-case \(p\)-fold speedup is impossible under these assumptions alone.

notation.meaning: maximum read delay in committed updates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and local topic fit, but the example does not support the stated range of delay bounds: if p overwrites commit after a common read, the last such update can be delayed by p-1 committed writes, so the construction is incompatible with arbitrary tau, especially tau=0. A source must also specify the concurrency, work, and speedup model before the claimed worst-case barrier is reliable.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Gradient Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise first-order residuals for unconstrained smooth optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=X_1	imes\cdots	imes X_m\) be a finite-dimensional product Hilbert space and let \(f:X	o\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable. The coordinate gradient residual at \(x\in X\) for block \(i\) is \(r_i(x)=\lVert
abla_i f(x)Vert_{X_i}\). Its aggregate Euclidean residual is \(r(x)= igl(\sum_{i=1}^m r_i(x)^2 igr)^{1/2}=\lVert
abla f(x)Vert_X\), using the product norm. Thus \(r(x)=0\) if and only if every block gradient vanishes, equivalently \(
abla f(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coordinate residual is the norm of a block gradient; aggregating squared block residuals gives the full gradient norm and detects stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) is finite-dimensional.
\(f\) is differentiable at \(x\).

notation.meaning: gradient of f with respect to block i

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimization Meaning of a Zero Coordinate Gradient Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity and optimality meanings of the unconstrained smooth residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every unconstrained local minimizer \(x^*\) of a differentiable function satisfies \(r_i(x^*)=0\) for all \(i\). If \(f\) is convex, simultaneous vanishing is equivalent to global optimality. Without convexity it certifies only first-order stationarity; for example, \(f(t)=-t^2\) has \(r(0)=0\), although \(0\) is not a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Zero coordinate gradients are necessary at local minima and sufficient for global optimality under convexity, but not under general nonconvexity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable.
The domain is an unconstrained finite-dimensional product Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\text{ local minimum}\Rightarrow r(x^*)=0;\qquad f\text{ convex}\Rightarrow\bigl[r(x)=0\iff x\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\bigr].

notation.meaning: norm of the i-th block gradient

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Coordinate Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise gradient-mapping residuals for product-constrained smooth optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C=C_1	imes\cdots	imes C_m\) be a nonempty closed convex product set in a finite-dimensional product Hilbert space, let \(f\) be differentiable, and fix \(\alpha_i>0\). For \(x\in C\), define the projected coordinate residual vector by \(G_{i,\alpha_i}(x)=\alpha_i^{-1} igl(x_i-P_{C_i}(x_i-\alpha_i
abla_i f(x)) igr)\). Its norm is the block residual, and \(G_{i,\alpha_i}(x)=0\) exactly when \(-
abla_i f(x)\in N_{C_i}(x_i)\). All block residuals vanish exactly when \(0\in
abla f(x)+N_C(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected coordinate residual measures the scaled displacement of one projected-gradient step and vanishes exactly at blockwise constrained stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(C_i\) is nonempty, closed, and convex for every \(i\).
\(f\) is differentiable at \(x\in C\).
\(\alpha_i>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimization Meaning of Vanishing Projected Coordinate Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationarity and optimality meanings of projected block residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every local minimizer of a differentiable function over \(C=\prod_iC_i\) satisfies \(G_{i,\alpha_i}(x)=0\) for all \(i\). If \(f\) is convex, simultaneous vanishing is equivalent to global optimality over \(C\). Without convexity it is only a stationarity condition; with \(C=\mathbb R\) and \(f(t)=-t^2\), the residual vanishes at \(0\), which is not a local minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing projected block residuals are necessary at local minima and globally sufficient under convexity, but only stationary in general nonconvex problems.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_i\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(f\) is differentiable.
\(\alpha_i>0\) for every block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\text{ local minimum over }C\Rightarrow G_{i,\alpha_i}(x^*)=0\ \forall i;\quad f\text{ convex}\Rightarrow\bigl[G_{i,\alpha_i}(x)=0\ \forall i\iff x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{C}f\bigr].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stepsize Comparison for Projected Coordinate Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of a projected block residual on its positive stepsize.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(x_i\in C_i\) and \(g_i=\nabla_i f(x)\). If \(0<\alpha\leq\beta\), then the projected displacements and normalized residuals satisfy \[\alpha\lVert G_{i,\alpha}(x)\rVert\leq\beta\lVert G_{i,\beta}(x)\rVert,\qquad \lVert G_{i,\beta}(x)\rVert\leq\lVert G_{i,\alpha}(x)\rVert.\] In particular, every positive stepsize has the same zero set, although nonzero residual magnitudes depend on the stepsize.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A larger projected-gradient stepsize produces a no-smaller displacement but a no-larger normalized residual; all positive stepsizes have identical zeros.
assumptions_latex: \(C_i\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(x_i\in C_i\).
\(0<\alpha\leq\beta\).

\(x_i\in C_i\), \(f\) is differentiable at \(x\), and \(\alpha_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of raw and projected block-gradient residuals on convex product constraints.

source_refs.source_title: Optimization: Algorithms and Consistent Approximations

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(G_{i,\alpha_i}(x)=\alpha_i^{-1}\bigl(x_i-P_{C_i}(x_i-\alpha_i\nabla_i f(x))\bigr)\). Since \(P_{C_i}(x_i)=x_i\) and the metric projection \(P_{C_i}\) is nonexpansive, \(\lVert G_{i,\alpha_i}(x)\rVert_{X_i}\leq\lVert\nabla_i f(x)\rVert_{X_i}\). If \(C_i=X_i\), then \(P_{C_i}\) is the identity and equality holds. With an active constraint, the inequality can be strict because projection removes components of the proposed gradient step that point outside the feasible set. Thus a small projected residual is the constraint-sensitive stationarity measure, while a small raw block gradient is generally a stronger condition and is not necessary at a constrained solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection cannot enlarge the block-gradient residual. Equality holds without constraints, while an active constraint can remove infeasible components of the proposed gradient step and make the projected residual strictly smaller.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Sensitive Residual Comparisons

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constrained Optimum with Nonzero Raw Coordinate Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp separation between raw and projected residuals at a boundary solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=[0,\infty)\), \(f(x)=x\), and \(x^*=0\). Then \(x^*\) is the unique minimizer over \(C\), but \(|f'(x^*)|=1\). For every \(\alpha>0\), \(P_C(x^*-\alpha f'(x^*))=0\), and hence \(G_\alpha(x^*)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a boundary minimizer the projected residual can vanish while the raw gradient remains nonzero.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Proximal Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise composite stationarity residual for separable nonsmooth terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(x_i)\), where \(f\) is differentiable and each \(g_i\) is proper, closed, and convex. For \(\alpha_i>0\), define \(G^{\mathrm{prox}}_{i,\alpha_i}(x)=\alpha_i^{-1} igl(x_i-\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha_i g_i}(x_i-\alpha_i
abla_i f(x)) igr)\). This vector is the coordinate proximal residual. It vanishes if and only if \(0\in
abla_i f(x)+\partial g_i(x_i)\). Therefore every coordinate proximal residual vanishes if and only if \(0\in
abla f(x)+\partial(\sum_i g_i)(x)\), the composite first-order stationarity condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coordinate proximal residual is the scaled displacement of a block proximal-gradient step and vanishes exactly at composite block stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable.
Each \(g_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(\alpha_i>0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sampled Representation of the Aggregate Proximal Residual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inverse-probability reconstruction of the squared aggregate block proximal residual from one sampled block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G_i(x)=\alpha_i^{-1}(x_i-\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha_i g_i}(x_i-\alpha_i\nabla_i f(x)))\), let \(\mathbb P(I=i\mid x)=p_i>0\), and define \(\|G(x)\|^2=\sum_{i=1}^m\|G_i(x)\|^2\). Then
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\|G_I(x)\|^2}{p_I}\,\middle|\,x\right]=\|G(x)\|^2.
\]
A single sampled value is therefore an unbiased estimator, not a deterministic upper bound, for the full squared residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse-probability weighting makes one sampled block proximal residual an unbiased estimator of the full squared residual, but not a pathwise upper certificate.
assumptions_latex: The block proximal residuals are well defined.
\(\mathbb P(I=i\mid x)=p_i>0\) for every block.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Coordinate Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise residual interface for a block-decomposed fixed-point operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\) and let \(T:X\to X\) have block components \(T_i:X\to X_i\). Define the coordinate fixed-point residual by \(R_i(x)=x_i-T_i(x)\), with scalar magnitude \(r_i(x)=\lVert R_i(x)\rVert\). Under the product norm, the aggregate residual is \(r(x)=\bigl(\sum_{i=1}^m r_i(x)^2\bigr)^{1/2}=\lVert x-Tx\rVert\). Hence \(r_i(x)=0\) for every block if and only if \(x=Tx\). A coordinate fixed-point iteration replaces a selected block by \(T_i(x)\) and leaves all other blocks unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each coordinate residual is the discrepancy between a block and its operator image; all residuals vanish exactly at a fixed point.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite product Hilbert space.
\(T:X\to X\) is single-valued.

\[
\mathbb E\!\left[\frac{\|R_I(x)\|^2}{p_I}\,\middle|\,x\right]=\|x-Tx\|^2.

For the relaxed selected-block update \(x_I^+=x_I-\lambda R_I(x)\), with all other blocks unchanged and \(\lambda\ge0\), one also has \(\|x^+-x\|=\lambda\|R_I(x)\|\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel-gap certificate decomposed into block-maintainable contributions.

source_refs.source_title: First-Order Methods in Optimization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\), let \(A_i:X_i\to Y\) be linear, and define \(Ax=\sum_{i=1}^m A_ix_i\). For the convex primal objective \(F(x)=f(Ax)+\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(x_i)\), define the dual objective \(D(y)=-f^*(y)-\sum_{i=1}^m g_i^*(-A_i^*y)\). At any \(x\) and \(y\) for which these values are finite, set \(c_0(x,y)=f(Ax)+f^*(y)-\langle Ax,y\rangle\) and \(c_i(x_i,y)=g_i(x_i)+g_i^*(-A_i^*y)+\langle A_ix_i,y\rangle\). Fenchel-Young inequalities imply \(c_0(x,y)\geq0\) and \(c_i(x_i,y)\geq0\). The pairing terms cancel on summation, giving \(F(x)-D(y)=c_0(x,y)+\sum_{i=1}^m c_i(x_i,y)\geq0\). By weak duality, this primal-dual gap is an upper bound on primal suboptimality whenever the primal infimum is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Fenchel primal-dual gap decomposes into one nonnegative global term and nonnegative block terms. Their sum is a coordinate-compatible certificate that upper-bounds primal suboptimality by weak duality.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Coordinate Fenchel Gap as an Exact Optimality Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness criterion for the decomposed Fenchel-gap certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(F(x)\) and \(D(y)\) are finite. Then \(F(x)-D(y)=0\) if and only if \(y\in\partial f(Ax)\) and \(-A_i^*y\in\partial g_i(x_i)\) for every \(i\). In this event \(x\) and \(y\) are respectively primal and dual optimal. Conversely, any finite equal-valued primal-dual optimal pair makes every nonnegative contribution \(c_0,c_1,\ldots,c_m\) vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The decomposed coordinate gap is zero exactly when all component Fenchel equalities hold; this certifies primal and dual optimality.

\(F(x)\) and \(D(y)\) are finite.
\(Ax=\sum_iA_ix_i\).

children.title: Certificate Refresh Policies
children.top_down_role: Timing and selection policies for updating blockwise stopping information.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete baseline policy periodically recomputing all certificate contributions at one common iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an integer period \(q\ge1\). At iterations \(k\in q\mathbb N\), choose a declared snapshot \(x^k\), evaluate every contribution \(c_i(x^k)\), store \(\widehat c_i=c_i(x^k)\), and form \(\widehat C^k=\sum_i\widehat c_i\). An unqualified stopping decision based on \(\widehat C^k\) is permitted only at that refresh iteration. At intervening iterations the stored sum is labeled stale and is not treated as a certificate for the current iterate unless separately certified staleness bounds are applied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Periodic full refresh recomputes every block certificate at one snapshot and permits unqualified stopping only at refresh iterations.
assumptions_latex: The global certificate is separable as \(C(x)=\sum_i c_i(x)\).
All contributions can be evaluated at a common declared snapshot.
\(q\ge1\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: k\in q\mathbb N\implies \widehat C^k=C(x^k);\quad k\notin q\mathbb N\text{ gives no current-iterate guarantee without additional bounds.}

notation.meaning: Number of iterations between complete refreshes.
Aggregate certificate computed at a refresh snapshot.

knowledge_statements.title: Periodic Consistent-Snapshot Full Refresh
Certificate Refresh Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic policy for maintaining cached block-certificate values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given nonnegative block certificate functions \(c_i(x)\), cached values \(\widehat c_i\), refresh times \(t_i\), a refresh budget \(b\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\), initialize \(\widehat c_i=c_i(x^0)\) and \(t_i=0\). At iteration \(k\), form priorities \(q_i^k\) from certified staleness bounds or elapsed ages, select at most \(b\) indices with largest priorities, recompute their exact \(c_i(x^k)\), and update their caches and timestamps. Leave other caches unchanged. Stop only when an aggregation rule using the refreshed values and valid bounds for unrefreshed blocks certifies an aggregate residual or gap not exceeding \(\varepsilon\); output \(x^k\) and that certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refresh the highest-priority cached certificate blocks within a budget and stop only when exact values plus valid stale bounds meet tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Each refreshed value \(c_i(x^k)\) is exactly computable.
Unrefreshed blocks possess valid error or upper bounds.
\(1\leq b\leq m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is accepted only when the maintained aggregate upper certificate is at most \(\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: last refresh iteration for block i

children.title: Partial Certificate Aggregation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Delta Maintenance for Locally Changing Contributions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental maintenance of an additive certificate when all changed contributions are known.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(C^k=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i^k\) is stored exactly and only contributions in a known set \(S_k\) can change between iterations \(k\) and \(k+1\). If their old and new values are exact, update
\[
C^{k+1}=C^k+\sum_{i\in S_k}(c_i^{k+1}-c_i^k).
\]
This requires \(O(|S_k|)\) aggregation arithmetic after evaluating the changed contributions. If a contribution outside \(S_k\) can change through global state dependence, the maintained value need not equal the current aggregate and cannot by itself justify stopping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An additive certificate is maintained exactly by adding every changed contribution's delta; omitting a globally affected contribution invalidates exactness.
assumptions_latex: The aggregate is additive: \(C^k=\sum_i c_i^k\).
\(S_k\) contains every contribution changed by iteration k.
Old and new values are exact for all indices in \(S_k\).

notation.meaning: Set of all certificate contributions changed at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Delta Maintenance for Locally Changing Contributions

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotone Aggregation of Partial Certificate Intervals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rigorous aggregate bounds from exact refreshed contributions and certified intervals for unrefreshed contributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C(x)=\Phi(c_1(x),\ldots,c_m(x))\), where \(\Phi:\mathbb R_+^m\to\mathbb R_+\) is nondecreasing in every argument. For refreshed blocks set \(\ell_i=u_i=c_i(x)\); for every unrefreshed block suppose \(0\le\ell_i\le c_i(x)\le u_i\). Then
\[
\Phi(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_m)\le C(x)\le\Phi(u_1,\ldots,u_m).
\]
Consequently the upper aggregate being at most \(\varepsilon\) certifies success, while the lower aggregate exceeding \(\varepsilon\) certifies failure of the tolerance. Additive certificates use \(\Phi(v)=\sum_i v_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any coordinatewise monotone aggregate converts valid block intervals into rigorous global lower and upper certificates, including additive certificates as a special case.
assumptions_latex: \(C(x)=\Phi(c_1(x),\ldots,c_m(x))\) with \(\Phi\) coordinatewise nondecreasing.
Every unrefreshed contribution has a valid interval \([\ell_i,u_i]\).
Refreshed contributions are evaluated exactly at the declared current snapshot.

notation.meaning: Certified lower and upper bounds for contribution i.

Partial Certificate Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rigorous aggregate bounds from refreshed blocks and bounded unrefreshed contributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a nonnegative separable certificate satisfy \(C(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i(x)\). For a refreshed subset \(S\), suppose exact values \(c_i(x)\) are available for \(i\in S\), while valid bounds \(0\leq \ell_i\leq c_i(x)\leq u_i\) are available for \(i
otin S\). Then \(L_S=\sum_{i\in S}c_i(x)+\sum_{i
otin S}\ell_i\) and \(U_S=\sum_{i\in S}c_i(x)+\sum_{i
otin S}u_i\) satisfy \(L_S\leq C(x)\leq U_S\). Consequently, \(U_S\leq\varepsilon\) is a verifiable stopping certificate, whereas \(L_S>\varepsilon\) certifies that tolerance has not yet been reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact refreshed contributions and valid bounds on omitted blocks yield rigorous lower and upper aggregate certificates.
assumptions_latex: \(C(x)=\sum_i c_i(x)\) with \(c_i(x)\geq0\).
Bounds \(\ell_i\leq c_i(x)\leq u_i\) are valid for every unrefreshed block.

children.title: Certificate Staleness Control
children.top_down_role: Validity limits caused by delayed or uneven refresh of certificate components.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: False Stopping from an Unbounded Stale Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal failure example for reuse of a previously exact residual without a variation bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c(x)=|x|\). Refresh at \(z=0\), so \(\widehat c=c(z)=0\). If the current iterate is \(x=1\) and no displacement or variation bound is maintained, then \(c(x)=1\) although \(\widehat c=0\). Hence \(\widehat c\le\varepsilon\) falsely accepts every \(0\le\varepsilon<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate exact at its refresh point can falsely signal convergence after the iterate moves unless its variation is bounded or it is refreshed.
assumptions_latex: A cached value is reused after the state changes.
No certified bound relates the current contribution to its cached value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat c\le\varepsilon\not\Rightarrow c(x)\le\varepsilon\text{ for an uncontrolled stale cache.}
knowledge_statements.title: False Stopping from an Unbounded Stale Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Current-value uncertainty interval for a cached certificate contribution under certified state displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\widehat c_i=c_i(z_i)\) be a cached nonnegative contribution. Suppose a nondecreasing modulus \(\omega_i:\mathbb R_+\to\mathbb R_+\) satisfies \(\omega_i(0)=0\) and
\[
|c_i(x)-c_i(z)|\le \omega_i(\|x-z\|)
\]
on the relevant region. If \(\|x-z_i\|\le d_i\) is certified, then
\[
\max\{0,\widehat c_i-\omega_i(d_i)\}\le c_i(x)\le \widehat c_i+\omega_i(d_i).
\]
Thus \(\omega_i(d_i)\le\eta_i\) is a sufficient, not necessary, test that the cache error is at most \(\eta_i\). For an \(L_i\)-Lipschitz contribution one may take \(\omega_i(t)=L_it\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuity modulus evaluated at a certified displacement gives a sound stale-cache interval; meeting an uncertainty tolerance is sufficient but need not be necessary.
assumptions_latex: \(c_i\) obeys the stated modulus of continuity on the traversed region.
\(\|x-z_i\|\le d_i\) is certified.

notation.meaning: State at the last refresh of contribution i.
Certified displacement from the refresh state.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Modulus-of-Continuity Staleness Envelope
Certificate Staleness Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for cached coordinate certificates under intervening updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each block certificate \(c_i:X\to\mathbb{R}_+\), let \(z_i\) be the state at its last refresh and store \(\widehat c_i=c_i(z_i)\). Suppose \(c_i\) is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz on the region traversed by the iterates and a maintained displacement bound satisfies \(\lVert x-z_i\rVert\leq d_i\). Then the current value obeys \(\max\{0,\widehat c_i-L_id_i\}\leq c_i(x)\leq\widehat c_i+L_id_i\). A cache is admissible for tolerance \(\eta_i\) precisely when \(L_id_i\leq\eta_i\); otherwise block \(i\) must be refreshed or assigned a larger certified uncertainty interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lipschitz constant times displacement since refresh bounds cache error; exceeding the allowed uncertainty forces a refresh.
assumptions_latex: \(c_i\) is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz on the relevant iterate region.
\(\lVert x-z_i\rVert\leq d_i\) is certified.
\(\eta_i\geq0\) is the permitted block uncertainty.

notation.meaning: state at the last block refresh

However, calling the cache admissible precisely when L_i d_i is at most eta_i makes this chosen conservative test sound like a necessary condition; a cache could have smaller actual error even when the bound exceeds tolerance. A sourced definition of admissibility or a reformulation as a sufficient certified test is needed.

children.title: Quadratic Coordinate Descent

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unfair Selection Can Stall Away from the Minimizer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coordinate minimization need not converge if a coordinate is never selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=I_2\), \(b=(0,1)^{\mathsf T}\), and \(x^0=(1,0)^{\mathsf T}\). If every iteration selects coordinate \(1\), the first update gives \(x^1=(0,0)^{\mathsf T}\) and all later iterates remain there, although the minimizer is \(x^*=b=(0,1)^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly minimizing only one coordinate can stall at a point that is not the quadratic minimizer.
assumptions_latex: Only coordinate \(1\) is selected.
knowledge_statements.title: Unfair Selection Can Stall Away from the Minimizer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact realized decrease from one quadratic coordinate minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx-b^{\mathsf T}x\), let \(g_i=(Qx-b)_i\) and \(x^+=x-(g_i/Q_{ii})e_i\). Then \(f(x^+)=f(x)-g_i^2/(2Q_{ii})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact quadratic coordinate step decreases the objective by the squared coordinate gradient divided by twice its diagonal curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
Coordinate \(i\) is exactly minimized.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Coordinate Decrease Identity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global linear convergence under uniformly bounded coordinate-revisit gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) and apply exact coordinate minimization. If some finite \(M\) makes every consecutive \(M\) selections contain every coordinate, then \(x^k\to Q^{-1}b\), and constants \(C<\infty\), \(q\in(0,1)\) exist such that \(f(x^k)-f^*\le Cq^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact coordinate descent on an SPD quadratic converges linearly under essentially cyclic selection.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
Every consecutive \(M\) selections contain all coordinates for some finite \(M\).
knowledge_statements.title: Essentially-Cyclic Linear Convergence
Quadratic Coordinate Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact cyclic coordinate minimization for a strictly convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^TQx-b^Tx\) with symmetric positive-definite \(Q\), choose \(x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and an index sequence \(i_k\) that visits every coordinate, such as cyclic order. At iteration \(k\), compute the coordinate derivative \(g_{i_k}=(Qx^k-b)_{i_k}\) and set \(x^{k+1}=x^k-(g_{i_k}/Q_{i_ki_k})e_{i_k}\). This update exactly minimizes \(f\) along coordinate \(i_k\), leaving all other coordinates unchanged. Stop when a prescribed residual, such as \(\lVert Qx^k-b\rVert\), is at most \(\varepsilon\); output \(x^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact quadratic coordinate descent subtracts the coordinate gradient divided by the corresponding diagonal Hessian entry and cycles through all coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^T\succ0\).
Every coordinate is selected infinitely often.
\(\varepsilon\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each update exactly minimizes \(f\) over the selected coordinate line.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The update is the exact coordinate-line minimizer for a symmetric positive-definite quadratic, and algorithm is the correct kind for the leaf. The mathematical specification is standard, but no source with a specific locator is provided.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A generic SPD-quadratic certificate is not primarily a coordinate-descent claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx-b^{\mathsf T}x\), \(Q\succ0\), and \(g=Qx-b\), \(f(x)-f^*=\tfrac12g^{\mathsf T}Q^{-1}g\), with eigenvalue-based upper and lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full gradient gives an exact optimality-gap formula for any SPD quadratic, independently of the algorithm.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Gradient Optimality Certificate

children.title: Gauss–Seidel Relaxation
children.top_down_role: Sequential linear-relaxation interpretations of quadratic coordinate updates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonsingularity and a nonzero diagonal do not guarantee Gauss–Seidel convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\2&1\end{bmatrix}\) and \(b=0\), Gauss–Seidel has iteration matrix \(G_{\mathrm{GS}}=-(D+L)^{-1}U=\begin{bmatrix}0&-2\\0&4\end{bmatrix}\). Hence \(\rho(G_{\mathrm{GS}})=4\), so some initial errors grow geometrically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonsingular two-by-two system with nonzero diagonal can make Gauss–Seidel diverge geometrically.
assumptions_latex: \(A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\2&1\end{bmatrix}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsingularity Does Not Ensure Convergence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Iteration Matrix and Exact Convergence Criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stationary-iteration representation and exact convergence criterion for classical Gauss–Seidel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(A=D+L+U\) is nonsingular and \(D+L\) is nonsingular. For \((D+L)x^{k+1}=b-Ux^k\), let \(x^\star=A^{-1}b\). Then \(e^{k+1}=G_{\mathrm{GS}}e^k\), where \(G_{\mathrm{GS}}=-(D+L)^{-1}U\). Consequently, \(x^k\to x^\star\) for every \(x^0\) if and only if \(\rho(G_{\mathrm{GS}})<1\); its asymptotic factor is governed by that spectral radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gauss–Seidel converges from every starting point exactly when its iteration matrix has spectral radius below one.
assumptions_latex: \(A=D+L+U\) is nonsingular.
\(D+L\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.title: Iteration Matrix and Exact Convergence Criterion
Gauss–Seidel Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential component relaxation for a positive-definite linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Qx=b\), write \(Q=D+L+U\), where \(D\) is diagonal and \(L\) and \(U\) are strictly lower and upper triangular. Given \(x^0\), one Gauss–Seidel sweep computes, for \(i=1,\ldots,n\), \(x_i^{k+1}=Q_{ii}^{-1}\bigl(b_i-\sum_{j<i}Q_{ij}x_j^{k+1}-\sum_{j>i}Q_{ij}x_j^k\bigr)\). Equivalently, \((D+L)x^{k+1}=b-Ux^k\). Stop when \(\lVert Qx^k-b\rVert\leq\varepsilon\); output \(x^k\). If \(Q\) is symmetric positive-definite, the iterates converge to the unique solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gauss–Seidel solves each row sequentially using new lower-index values and old upper-index values; positive definiteness ensures convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(Q=Q^T\succ0\).
\(x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(\varepsilon\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k\to Q^{-1}b\), and each component update matches exact quadratic coordinate minimization.

notation.meaning: diagonal, strictly lower, and strictly upper parts of Q

The additional correspondence with exact quadratic coordinate minimization is also correct for the associated quadratic, but neither the algorithmic claim nor the correspondence has a cited source and locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic SPD residual bounds are not primarily Gauss–Seidel results.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), \(x^\star=A^{-1}b\), and \(r=b-Ax\). Then \(\|x-x^\star\|_2\le \|r\|_2/\lambda_{\min}(A)\) and \(f(x)-f(x^\star)=\tfrac12r^{\mathsf T}A^{-1}r\le \|r\|_2^2/(2\lambda_{\min}(A))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an SPD system, its residual bounds solution error and quadratic objective gap independently of the solver used.
assumptions_latex: \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.title: SPD Residual Error Certificate

children.title: Descent–Relaxation Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between quadratic coordinate updates and Gauss–Seidel sweeps.

assumptions_latex: \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
\(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Ax-b^{\mathsf T}x\).
Coordinates are visited cyclically using the newest available components.
The relaxation parameter \(\omega\) is fixed.

notation.meaning: current component residual using newest sweep values

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between relaxed exact-coordinate descent and SOR, including convergence and the sharp relaxation interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\widehat x_i\) is the exact coordinate minimizer from the current partially updated sweep state, then \(x_i^+=x_i+\omega(\widehat x_i-x_i)=x_i+\omega(b_i-(Ax)_i)/A_{ii}\), exactly the SOR component update. Its objective change is \(-\omega(2-\omega)(b_i-(Ax)_i)^2/(2A_{ii})\). Consequently, cyclic sweeps converge to \(A^{-1}b\) for every start when \(0<\omega<2\). For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\), the error satisfies \(e^+=(1-\omega)e\), so \(\omega=0,2\) is noncontractive and values outside \([0,2]\) are expansive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxing exact quadratic coordinate minimization is precisely SOR; cyclic sweeps converge for 0<omega<2, and a scalar quadratic shows the interval is sharp.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Descent-SOR Correspondence
Descent–Relaxation Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact cyclic coordinate descent on a strictly convex quadratic is Gauss–Seidel relaxation for its normal equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite, let \(b\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and define \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Ax-b^{\mathsf T}x\).\) During a cyclic sweep, exact minimization in coordinate \(i\), using already updated coordinates \(j<i\) and old coordinates \(j>i\), gives
\[
x_i^{k+1}=\frac{b_i-\sum_{j<i}A_{ij}x_j^{k+1}-\sum_{j>i}A_{ij}x_j^k}{A_{ii}}.
\]
These are precisely the component equations of the Gauss–Seidel iteration for \(Ax=b\). Hence one cyclic exact-coordinate-descent sweep and one Gauss–Seidel relaxation sweep produce the same iterate from the same starting point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive-definite quadratic, sequential exact coordinate minimizations generate exactly the same iterates as Gauss–Seidel relaxation applied to the associated linear system.
assumptions_latex: \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
Coordinates are visited cyclically and minimized exactly.
Both procedures start from the same iterate.

children.title: Parallel Quadratic Block Updates

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Quadratic Block Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous exact block-model updates for a partitioned strictly convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Partition \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_p)\) and conformally partition a symmetric positive-definite matrix \(A\), with block diagonal \(D=\operatorname{blkdiag}(A_{11},\ldots,A_{pp})\). For \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Ax-b^{\mathsf T}x\), initialize \(x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n\). At iteration \(k\), compute all blocks from the unchanged vector \(x^k\) in parallel:
\[
x_i^{k+1}=x_i^k-A_{ii}^{-1}(Ax^k-b)_i,
\qquad i=1,\ldots,p.
\]
Equivalently, \(x^{k+1}=x^k-D^{-1}(Ax^k-b)\). Stop when a prescribed residual or iterate-change tolerance is met, and output the last iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each block independently minimizes its quadratic block model using the same old iterate; the parallel updates combine into a block-diagonally preconditioned residual step.
assumptions_latex: \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
The blocks form a disjoint partition of the coordinates.
Each diagonal block \(A_{ii}\) is solved exactly.

notation.meaning: diagonal Hessian block for block i

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled cross-block spectrum exactly controls whether simultaneous exact block proposals decrease the joint objective.
assumptions_latex: \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
\(D=\operatorname{blkdiag}(A_{11},\ldots,A_{pp})\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Relaxed simultaneous block updates use \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\omega D^{-1}(Ax^k-b)\). With \(B=D^{-1/2}AD^{-1/2}\succ0\), they converge linearly from every starting point, and every nonstationary step decreases the quadratic, exactly when \(0<\omega<2/\lambda_{\max}(B)\). The worst-case factor is minimized at \(\omega_*=2/(\lambda_{\min}(B)+\lambda_{\max}(B))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled spectrum gives the exact relaxation boundary and optimal constant weight for simultaneous exact block minimization.

children.title: Jacobi Relaxation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SPD Does Not Guarantee Ordinary Jacobi Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive definiteness alone is insufficient for ordinary Jacobi convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A=(1-c)I+c\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}\), \(1/2<c<1\), the eigenvalues of \(A\) are \(1-c,1-c,1+2c\), so \(A\succ0\). Since \(D=I\), the Jacobi matrix \(I-A\) has spectral radius \(2c>1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A three-dimensional SPD matrix with strong equal coupling makes ordinary Jacobi diverge.
assumptions_latex: \(A=(1-c)I+c\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}\).
knowledge_statements.title: SPD Does Not Guarantee Ordinary Jacobi Convergence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted Jacobi and the SPD Parameter Interval
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted Jacobi and its exact SPD convergence interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Weighted Jacobi uses \(x^{k+1}=x^k+\omega D^{-1}(b-Ax^k)\). If \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) and \(B=D^{-1/2}AD^{-1/2}\), it converges from every initial vector exactly when \(0<\omega<2/\lambda_{\max}(B)\). Its factor is \(\max_j|1-\omega\lambda_j(B)|\), minimized at \(\omega_*=2/(\lambda_{\min}(B)+\lambda_{\max}(B))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For SPD systems, the scaled spectrum gives the exact weighted-Jacobi interval and optimal constant weight.
assumptions_latex: \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
\(D=\operatorname{diag}(A)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Jacobi and the SPD Parameter Interval

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient convergence condition for classical Jacobi relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonsingular \(A=D+L+U\) with nonsingular \(D\), Jacobi errors satisfy \(e^{k+1}=G_Je^k\), where \(G_J=-D^{-1}(L+U)=I-D^{-1}A\). Thus \(x^k\to A^{-1}b\) for every initial vector if and only if \(\rho(G_J)<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jacobi converges from every initial vector exactly when its iteration matrix has spectral radius below one.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is nonsingular.
\(D\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.title: Jacobi Spectral-Radius Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical checkable sufficient conditions for Jacobi convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(|A_{ii}|>\sum_{j\ne i}|A_{ij}|\) for every row, then \(\rho(I-D^{-1}A)<1\). The same conclusion holds for irreducible weak row diagonal dominance with at least one strict row.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict row diagonal dominance, and its irreducible weak variant with one strict row, guarantee Jacobi convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(A_{ii}\ne0\) for every \(i\).
A is strictly row diagonally dominant, or irreducibly weakly row diagonally dominant with at least one strict row.
knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal-Dominance Convergence Conditions
Jacobi Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical simultaneous component relaxation for a nonsingular linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A=D+L+U\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), where \(D=\operatorname{diag}(A)\) has no zero diagonal entries and \(L,U\) are the strict lower and upper parts. Given \(x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), Jacobi relaxation computes
\[
x^{k+1}=D^{-1}\bigl(b-(L+U)x^k\bigr)
=x^k+D^{-1}(b-Ax^k).
\]
Thus every component satisfies \(x_i^{k+1}=(b_i-\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}x_j^k)/A_{ii}\) and can be evaluated concurrently. Stop under a prescribed residual or iterate-change test and return the final iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jacobi relaxation updates every component simultaneously from the previous iterate by dividing its residual equation by the corresponding diagonal entry.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) and \(A_{ii}\ne0\) for every \(i\).
All component updates use the same previous iterate \(x^k\).

notation.meaning: strict lower and upper parts of A

children.title: Block–Jacobi Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between parallel block updates and Jacobi-type relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Block–Jacobi Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parallel exact block minimization of a quadratic equals block-Jacobi relaxation of its optimality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Ax-b^{\mathsf T}x\), where \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), and partition \(x\) into disjoint blocks. For every block \(i\), minimize \(f(x_1^k,\ldots,z_i,\ldots,x_p^k)\) over \(z_i\), with all other blocks fixed at their old values. The first-order equation gives
\[
x_i^{k+1}=A_{ii}^{-1}\left(b_i-\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}x_j^k\right).
\]
Collecting these simultaneous minimizers yields \(x^{k+1}=x^k-D^{-1}(Ax^k-b)\), exactly the block-Jacobi relaxation of \(Ax=b\), where \(D=\operatorname{blkdiag}(A_{11},\ldots,A_{pp})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneous exact minimization over quadratic coordinate blocks is identical, iterate for iterate, to block-Jacobi relaxation of the associated linear system.
assumptions_latex: \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
The coordinate blocks are disjoint and exhaustive.
Every block minimizer uses only blocks from \(x^k\).

notation.meaning: block of A coupling blocks i and j

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Coordinate Solvers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact or inexact minimization over one coordinate block while other blocks remain fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_p\) and let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable. Initialize \(x^0\in X\). At iteration \(k\), select a block \(i_k\) and compute \(z^k\in X_{i_k}\) satisfying either exact minimization,
\[
z^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in X_{i_k}}f(x_1^k,\ldots,z,\ldots,x_p^k),
\]
or a specified inexactness condition. Set \(x_{i_k}^{k+1}=z^k\) and \(x_j^{k+1}=x_j^k\) for \(j\ne i_k\). Stop according to a prescribed stationarity or iterate-change test and output the last iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-coordinate solver selects one block, solves the restricted optimization problem exactly or to a stated tolerance, and leaves all other blocks unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_p\).
Each selected block subproblem has an accepted exact or inexact solution.
The block-selection rule is specified.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error-propagation view of a sequential exact-subspace sweep.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Successive exact corrections in \(V_1,\ldots,V_p\) give \(e^{k+1}=E_{\mathrm{mult}}e^k\), where \(E_{\mathrm{mult}}=(I-\Pi_p^A)\cdots(I-\Pi_1^A\). The factors generally do not commute, so changing their order can change the sweep operator and its rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequential exact-subspace sweep propagates error by an ordered product of complementary A-orthogonal projectors.

notation.meaning: A-orthogonal projector onto the correction subspace

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A-orthogonal projection and exact energy-decrease representation of one correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(\Pi_i^A=P_i(P_i^{\mathsf T}AP_i)^{-1}P_i^{\mathsf T}A\). Then \(\Pi_i^A\) is the \(A\)-orthogonal projector onto \(V_i\). One exact correction satisfies \(e^+=(I-\Pi_i^A)e\), \(\|e^+\|_A^2=\|e\|_A^2-\|\Pi_i^Ae\|_A^2\), and \(f(x)-f(x^+)=\tfrac12\|\Pi_i^Ae\|_A^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact correction removes the A-orthogonal projection of the error and decreases energy by half the squared removed component.
knowledge_statements.title: Energy-Projection Representation

assumptions_latex: \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
All correction spaces are finite-dimensional.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp spanning and relaxation conditions for stationary multiplicative and additive exact-subspace iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Repeated multiplicative sweeps converge to \(x^*=A^{-1}b\) from every start if and only if \(V_1+\cdots+V_p=\mathbb R^n\), equivalently \(\rho(E_{\mathrm{mult}})<1\). A relaxed additive correction has error update \(e^+=(I-\omega T)e\), with \(T=\sum_i\Pi_i^A\), and converges from every start if and only if the spaces span and \(0<\omega<2/\lambda_{\max}(T)\). If the spaces do not span, every nonzero error in their common \(A\)-orthogonal complement is unchanged; at or beyond the additive relaxation boundary a top-eigenvalue mode is noncontractive or expansive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact subspace iterations converge precisely when the spaces cover every error direction, with additive corrections also requiring relaxation below the sharp spectral threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Additive and Multiplicative Convergence Boundary
Subspace Correction Views
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A quadratic block update represented as an energy-minimizing correction in an embedded subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Ax-b^{\mathsf T}x\), and let \(P_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d_i}\) have full column rank with correction space \(V_i=\operatorname{range}(P_i)\).\) The exact subspace correction from \(x^k\) is \(x^{k+1}=x^k+P_i s_i\), where
\[
s_i=\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in\mathbb{R}^{d_i}} f(x^k+P_i s)
=(P_i^{\mathsf T}AP_i)^{-1}P_i^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax^k).
\]
Equivalently, the new residual is orthogonal to \(V_i\): \(P_i^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax^{k+1})=0\).\)
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact quadratic subspace correction minimizes energy along an embedded subspace and makes the new residual orthogonal to that subspace.
assumptions_latex: \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
\(P_i\) has full column rank.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The subspace-correction formula and residual orthogonality condition are correct for an SPD quadratic and full-column-rank embedding, and representation fits the leaf. No citation is supplied, and the statement contains unmatched closing delimiters that must also be repaired.

Block–Subspace Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-block restriction matrices identify block minimization with exact subspace correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Ax-b^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).\) For a coordinate block \(I\subseteq\{1,
\ldots,n\}\), let \(E_I\) be the matrix whose columns are the corresponding coordinate vectors. Exact minimization over block \(I\), holding its complement fixed, has the form
\[
x^{k+1}=x^k+E_I(E_I^{\mathsf T}AE_I)^{-1}E_I^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax^k).
\]
This is exactly the subspace-correction update with \(P_i=E_I\) and \(V_i=\operatorname{range}(E_I)\). Conversely, every correction in a coordinate subspace has a unique block-coordinate representation through \(E_I\).\)
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic coordinate-block minimization is precisely an exact correction in the coordinate subspace spanned by that block’s basis vectors.
assumptions_latex: \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
\(I\) is a nonempty coordinate block.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected linear convergence under canonical squared-row-norm sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x^{k+1}=x^k+(b_{i_k}-a_{i_k}^{\mathsf T}x^k)a_{i_k}/\|a_{i_k}\|_2^2\) with \(\mathbb P(i_k=i)=\|a_i\|_2^2/\|A\|_F^2\), \(\mathbb E\|x^k-x^*\|_2^2\leq(1-(\sigma_{\min}^+(A))^2/\|A\|_F^2)^k\|x^0-x^*\|_2^2\). In particular, \(k\geq \|A\|_F^2(\sigma_{\min}^+(A))^{-2}\log(\|x^0-x^*\|_2^2/\varepsilon)\) is sufficient for expected squared error at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Squared-row-norm sampling gives geometric expected error decay governed by the Frobenius norm and smallest positive singular value.

assumptions_latex: Both rows are sampled independently with positive probability.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of unmodified randomized Kaczmarz on an inconsistent system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the inconsistent equations \(x=0\) and \(x=1\), projection onto the first row sets the iterate to \(0\), while projection onto the second sets it to \(1\). If both rows have positive sampling probability, each is selected infinitely often almost surely, so the iterates do not converge and in particular do not approach the least-squares solution \(1/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the inconsistent equations x=0 and x=1, randomized Kaczmarz repeatedly jumps between row solutions rather than converging to the least-squares point.

Randomized Kaczmarz Coordinate Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-row Kaczmarz projections are randomized coordinate-ascent steps on the minimum-norm problem’s dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have nonzero rows \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\), and assume \(Ax=b\) is consistent. The dual of \(\min_x\tfrac12\lVert x\rVert_2^2\) subject to \(Ax=b\) is
\[
\max_{y\in\mathbb{R}^m}\; b^{\mathsf T}y-	frac12\lVert A^{\mathsf T}y\rVert_2^2,
\qquad x=A^{\mathsf T}y.
\]
Selecting row \(i\) and exactly maximizing over coordinate \(y_i\) gives \(y_i^+=y_i+(b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x)/\lVert a_i\rVert_2^2\). Consequently,
\[
x^+=x+\frac{b_i-a_i^{\mathsf T}x}{\lVert a_i\rVert_2^2}a_i,
\]
which is the Kaczmarz projection onto \(\{z:a_i^{\mathsf T}z=b_i\}\).\) Random row selection therefore corresponds to randomized dual coordinate ascent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Randomized Kaczmarz is randomized coordinate ascent on the dual minimum-norm formulation, with each dual coordinate step inducing one row-hyperplane projection.
assumptions_latex: \(Ax=b\) is consistent.
Every sampled row \(a_i\) is nonzero.
The primal representative satisfies \(x=A^{\mathsf T}y\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection geometry and feasibility test for one exact block Kaczmarz correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_I=b_I-A_Ix\) and \(x^+=x+A_I^{\mathsf T}(A_IA_I^{\mathsf T})^\dagger r_I\). For every \(z\) satisfying \(Ax=b\), \(\|x^+-z\|_2^2=\|x-z\|_2^2-\|x^+-x\|_2^2\). Moreover, \(x^+=x\) if and only if \(A_Ix=b_I\), and \(P_I=A_I^{\mathsf T}(A_IA_I^{\mathsf T})^\dagger A_I\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{range}(A_I^{\mathsf T})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact block Kaczmarz projection decreases squared distance to every solution by the squared correction norm and is stationary exactly when the selected equations hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Block Projection Decrease and Feasibility
Block Kaczmarz Coordinate Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row-block projections are exact block-coordinate ascent steps in the minimum-norm problem’s dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Ax=b\) be consistent and consider the dual objective \(d(y)=b^{\mathsf T}y-	frac12\lVert A^{\mathsf T}y\rVert_2^2\), with \(x=A^{\mathsf T}y\).\) For a row block \(I\), exact maximization over \(y_I\), leaving \(y_{I^c}\) fixed, admits the minimum-norm increment
\[
\Delta y_I=(A_IA_I^{\mathsf T})^{\dagger}(b_I-A_Ix).
\]
The induced primal update is
\[
x^+=x+A_I^{\mathsf T}(A_IA_I^{\mathsf T})^{\dagger}(b_I-A_Ix),
\]
which is the Euclidean projection of \(x\) onto the affine set \(\{z:A_Iz=b_I\}\).\) Thus block Kaczmarz is dual block-coordinate ascent under this primal-dual identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block Kaczmarz projects onto several row equations at once and is exactly a dual block-coordinate ascent step using the corresponding row block.
assumptions_latex: \(Ax=b\) is consistent.
The selected block equations \(A_Iz=b_I\) are consistent.
\(x=A^{\mathsf T}y\).

notation.meaning: selected row block and corresponding right-hand side

Coordinate-Sketch Specializations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A one-column coordinate sketch specializes a sketched quadratic step to a scalar coordinate update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\) be symmetric positive definite and let \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\).\) For a full-column-rank sketch \(S\), define the sketched quadratic step
\[
x^+=x-S(S^{\mathsf T}HS)^{-1}S^{\mathsf T}g.
\]
Choosing the elementary sketch \(S=e_i\) gives
\[
x^+=x-\frac{g_i}{H_{ii}}e_i.
\]
Thus an elementary one-dimensional sketch changes only coordinate \(i\) and coincides with exact coordinate minimization of the local quadratic model \(g^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}Hd\) restricted to \(d\in\operatorname{span}\{e_i\}.\) Random coordinate selection is represented by sampling \(S\) from the elementary coordinate sketches.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking the sketch matrix to be one coordinate vector reduces the general sketched quadratic step to an exact scalar coordinate-model update.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
The sketch is \(S=e_i\) for some coordinate i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A coordinate-selection matrix specializes a sketched quadratic step to an exact block update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), let \(g\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(E_I\) contain the standard basis vectors indexed by a nonempty block \(I\).\) Substituting the block sketch \(S=E_I\) into
\[
x^+=x-S(S^{\mathsf T}HS)^{-1}S^{\mathsf T}g
\]
gives
\[
x^+=x-E_I(E_I^{\mathsf T}HE_I)^{-1}E_I^{\mathsf T}g.
\]
This update is supported only on block \(I\) and exactly minimizes the quadratic model \(g^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}Hd\) over \(d\in\operatorname{range}(E_I)\).\) Random block-coordinate selection is therefore a distribution over multidimensional coordinate sketches \(E_I\).\)

knowledge_statements.title: Random-Update Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized coordinate iteration represented by masking the residual of a deterministic fixed-point operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_p\) be a finite-dimensional product space, let \(T:X\to X\), and let \(U_i:X\to X\) denote the canonical projector onto block \(i\). Given \(x^0\in X\), sample \(i_k\) and define
\[
x^{k+1}=x^k+U_{i_k}\bigl(Tx^k-x^k\bigr).
\]
Equivalently, \(x_{i_k}^{k+1}=(Tx^k)_{i_k}\) and \(x_j^{k+1}=x_j^k\) for \(j\ne i_k\). If a random subset \(J_k\) is updated, replace \(U_{i_k}\) by \(U_{J_k}=\sum_{i\in J_k}U_i\). Every fixed point of \(T\) is unchanged by every such masked update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomized coordinate update applies a random block projector to the residual of a deterministic fixed-point map, changing only the sampled blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_p\) is finite-dimensional.
\(U_i\) is the canonical block projector.
The sampling rule for \(i_k\) or \(J_k\) is specified.

notation.meaning: random block selected at iteration k

For \[x^{k+1}=x^k+M_k(Tx^k-x^k),\] if \(x^k\) and \(Tx^k\) are \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable, then \[\mathbb E[x^{k+1}-x^k\mid\mathcal F_k]=D_k(Tx^k-x^k),\qquad D_k=\sum_{i=1}^m q_i^kU_i.\] Only the marginal activation probabilities enter this identity; independence among the indicators is unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The conditional mean masked update is the full residual scaled blockwise by marginal activation probabilities, without requiring independent block activations.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-coordinate representation of a fixed-point problem on a finite product Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=H_1\times\cdots\times H_m\) be a finite product Hilbert space, let \(T:H\to H\), and write \(S=I-T\) with block components \(S_i:H\to H_i\). For the canonical injection \(U_i:H_i\to H\), a coordinate update with relaxation \(\lambda_i>0\) is \[x^{+}=x-\lambda_iU_iS_i(x).\] The underlying problem admits the equivalent fixed-point and residual representations \[x^\star\in\operatorname{Fix}T\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad T(x^\star)=x^\star\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad S(x^\star)=0.\] Thus each update changes one block while targeting a zero of the full residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-coordinate fixed-point step modifies one component of the residual equation; fixed points of the operator are exactly zeros of its residual.
assumptions_latex: \(H=\prod_{i=1}^m H_i\) is a finite product Hilbert space.
\(T:H\to H\) is single-valued.
\(\lambda_i>0\) for every selectable block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Fix}T=\{x\in H:S(x)=0\}\), and block \(i\) is updated by \(x^{+}=x-\lambda_iU_iS_i(x)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the notation of the fixed-point representation, let \(i_k\) be a random block index and let \(P_i=U_iU_i^*\) denote the orthogonal projector onto block \(i\). Define \(T_i=I-\lambda_iP_i(I-T)\). Then the random block update has the two identical operator forms \[x^{k+1}=x^k-\lambda_{i_k}P_{i_k}(I-T)x^k=T_{i_k}x^k.\] If every block has positive selection probability, a point is fixed by every selectable coordinate operator exactly when it is fixed by \(T\): \[\bigcap_{i=1}^m\operatorname{Fix}T_i=\operatorname{Fix}T.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomized residual-coordinate step is application of a random coordinate operator, and their common fixed points equal the original operator's fixed points.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_i=I-\lambda_iP_i(I-T)\), where \(\lambda_i\ne0\), and let \(S=\{i:\mathbb P(i_k=i)>0\}\). Then \[\bigcap_{i\in S}\operatorname{Fix}T_i=\{x:P_i(I-T)x=0\text{ for every }i\in S\}.\] If \(S=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(\sum_iP_i=I\), this set equals \(\operatorname{Fix}T\). Without full support it can be strictly larger: for \(T=0\) on \(\mathbb R^2\), canonical coordinate projectors, and \(S=\{1\}\), \(\operatorname{Fix}T_1=\{0\}\times\mathbb R\supsetneq\operatorname{Fix}T=\{(0,0)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The selectable coordinate operators recover exactly the original fixed points under full block support; omitted blocks can create spurious common fixed points.

\(\lambda_i\ne0\) for every selectable block.
\(S\) is the support of the block-sampling law.

children.title: Residual State Maintenance

knowledge_statements.title: Residual State Maintenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact incremental residual maintenance for block updates in a linear prediction model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A=[A_1\ \cdots\ A_m]\), \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\), and \(b\), initialize the cached residual by \(r^0=Ax^0-b\). If iteration \(k\) changes only block \(i_k\) by \(x_{i_k}^{k+1}=x_{i_k}^k+d^k\), retain every other block and update \[r^{k+1}=r^k+A_{i_k}d^k.\] The invariant \(r^k=Ax^k-b\) is then maintained in exact arithmetic. A stopping test may use any prescribed residual criterion, such as \(\|A^*r^k\|\leq\varepsilon\), without recomputing \(Ax^k-b\) from scratch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After changing one variable block, add that block’s matrix contribution to the cached residual; the cache remains equal to the full residual.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is partitioned conformably with the blocks of \(x\).
Arithmetic is exact, or periodic recomputation separately controls numerical drift.

notation.meaning: columns of A associated with block i
increment applied to the selected block

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact incremental residual invariant is mathematically coherent and the algorithm kind fits the maintenance leaf, but no inspectable citation or source locator is supplied. The optional stopping example also requires source confirmation in this context.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed least-squares gradient-error claim duplicates the dedicated inconsistent-auxiliary-state failure leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r(x)=Ax-b\) and \(\widetilde r=r(x)+e\), a least-squares block gradient computed from the cache satisfies \(A_i^*\widetilde r-A_i^*r(x)=A_i^*e\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual-cache error propagates through the adjoint block operator into the computed least-squares block gradient.
assumptions_latex: The loss is \(\frac12\|Ax-b\|^2\).
