children.title: Prediction State Maintenance
children.top_down_role: Incremental tracking of predictions affected by selected coordinates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision boundary of recursive linear-prediction maintenance and its refresh remedy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\widetilde z^{k+1}=\widetilde z^k+A_{i_k}d^k+\eta^k\) and \(e^k=\widetilde z^k-Ax^k\), then \[e^{k+1}=e^k+\eta^k,\qquad e^k=e^0+\sum_{t=0}^{k-1}\eta^t.\] Recursive maintenance therefore has no uniform drift bound without additional error control. Recomputing \(\widetilde z^k\leftarrow Ax^k\) resets accumulated drift to the error of that matrix-vector evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arithmetic errors accumulate additively in a recursive prediction cache; a full refresh resets the accumulated inconsistency.
assumptions_latex: The authoritative iterate receives the declared block increments.
\(\eta^k\) contains the arithmetic error of the corresponding cache update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e^k=e^0+\sum_{t<k}\eta^t\), and a full refresh resets accumulated drift.
knowledge_statements.title: Prediction-Cache Roundoff Drift
Prediction State Maintenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact incremental maintenance of the linear predictor associated with block-coordinate changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a block-partitioned linear map \(A=[A_1\ \cdots\ A_m]\), initialize the prediction cache by \(z^0=Ax^0\). When only block \(i_k\) changes by an increment \(d^k\), set \[x_{i_k}^{k+1}=x_{i_k}^k+d^k,\qquad z^{k+1}=z^k+A_{i_k}d^k,\] leaving all other blocks unchanged. In exact arithmetic this preserves \(z^k=Ax^k\) for every iteration. Any loss term or derivative depending on \(Ax^k\) may therefore be evaluated from \(z^k\); termination follows the optimization method’s prescribed criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update the cached prediction by the selected block’s contribution, preserving equality with the full matrix-vector product.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is linear and partitioned conformably with \(x\).
Each iteration changes exactly one declared block.

children.title: Shared-State Coupling
children.top_down_role: Dependencies between residual state, prediction state, and coordinate modifications.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Visibility condition preserving coupled prediction and residual invariants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a visible state \((x,z,r)\) satisfy \(z=Ax\) and \(r=z-b\). A coupling-consistent block commit \((i,d)\) has one visible transition \[(x,z,r)\mapsto(x+U_i d,\ z+A_i d,\ r+A_i d).\] Readers observing only before or after such transitions see both invariants. If components become visible independently, an intermediate observation can violate \(z=Ax\) or \(r=z-b\), even if the final state is correct.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coordinate, prediction, and residual changes must be observed as one serializable transition, or through a consistent snapshot, to preserve coupled invariants at observation boundaries.
assumptions_latex: The pre-commit visible state satisfies both invariants.
All changes use the same accepted block increment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Serializable commits or consistent snapshots preserve \(z=Ax\) and \(r=z-b\) at visible boundaries.

notation.meaning: block injection into the authoritative iterate

knowledge_statements.title: Transactional Coupled-Cache Commit
Shared-State Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency invariant coupling prediction and residual caches under the same coordinate update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^k\) and \(r^k\) be shared caches initialized by \(z^0=Ax^0\) and \(r^0=z^0-b\). For a block increment \(d^k\) on block \(i_k\), update both caches using the same contribution \(q^k=A_{i_k}d^k\): \[z^{k+1}=z^k+q^k,\qquad r^{k+1}=r^k+q^k.\] In exact arithmetic the coupled invariants \(z^k=Ax^k\) and \(r^k=z^k-b=Ax^k-b\) hold simultaneously. Consequently, either cache may be reconstructed from the other and \(b\), so independent inconsistent updates are unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prediction and residual caches receive the same block contribution, preserving their exact relation and allowing either state to reconstruct the other.
assumptions_latex: The same accepted block increment is applied to both caches.
Arithmetic is exact.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The shared-state consistency property follows coherently from the declared initial conditions and common increment, and property fits the leaf. No source or inspectable locator supports the formal coupling claim.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision departure of an incrementally maintained linear-transform cache from a fresh transform evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the authoritative iterate update is exact and a computed cache update satisfies \(\widehat y^{k+1}=\widehat y^k+L_{i_k}d^k+\eta^k\), where \(\eta^k\) is its local arithmetic error. For \(e^k=\widehat y^k-Lx^k\), the cache error satisfies \[e^K=e^0+\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\eta^k,\qquad \|e^K\|\le \|e^0\|+\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\|\eta^k\|.\] Periodic full recomputation resets accumulated incremental error to the error of a fresh transform evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Roundoff in incremental transform updates can accumulate additively, motivating occasional full recomputation.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is fixed and linear.
The authoritative iterate updates are exact in the stated error model.
Each computed cache update has additive local error \(\eta^k\).

local arithmetic error in one cache update

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arithmetic crossover between incremental maintenance and fresh transform evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For changed blocks \(S\), let \(c_i(d_i)\) be the work to form \(L_i d_i\), \(c_{\mathrm{acc}}(S)\) the accumulation work, and \(C_L(x^+)\) the work of fresh evaluation. Then \[C_{\mathrm{inc}}(S)=\sum_{i\in S}c_i(d_i)+c_{\mathrm{acc}}(S),\] and incremental maintenance has lower arithmetic work exactly when \(C_{\mathrm{inc}}(S)<C_L(x^+)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incremental caching is cheaper exactly when touched block transforms and accumulation cost less than a fresh full transform.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is fixed and linear.
The cache is consistent and every changed block is reported.
Both costs use the same arithmetic model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_{\mathrm{inc}}(S)<C_L(x^+)\iff\text{incremental maintenance has lower per-update arithmetic work}.
review_flags: Per-update comparison only; it makes no claim about the enclosing method's iteration count.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Commutativity of exact incremental updates to a fixed linear-transform cache.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\) be linear, let \(y=Lx\), and let \(d=\sum_{r=1}^qU_{i_r}d_r\). If every increment is reported exactly once, then for every permutation \(\pi\), \[y+\sum_{r=1}^qLU_{i_{\pi(r)}}d_{\pi(r)}=L(x+d).\] Thus exact cache corrections may be batched or reordered. This does not extend generally to nonlinear or state-dependent transforms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed linear transform, reported additive block corrections commute and may be batched without changing the exact cache.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is fixed and linear.
The initial cache equals \(Lx\).
Every additive block increment is included exactly once.
Arithmetic is exact.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact incremental maintenance of a fixed linear transform after reported block updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L:X_1\oplus\cdots\oplus X_m\to Y\) be fixed and linear, let \(U_i\) inject block \(i\), and initialize \(y^0=Lx^0\). Whenever \[x^{k+1}=x^k+\sum_{i\in S_k}U_i d_i^k,\] update the cache by \[y^{k+1}=y^k+\sum_{i\in S_k}LU_i d_i^k.\] If every authoritative increment is reported exactly once, exact arithmetic preserves \(y^k=Lx^k\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain a fixed linear-transform cache by adding the transformed value of every reported block increment.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is fixed and linear.
Every authoritative increment is reported to the cache exactly once.
Arithmetic is exact for the invariant conclusion.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental cache rule for a fixed linear transform under a block-sparse argument update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L:X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\to Y\) be linear, with block restrictions \(L_i d=L(U_i d)\). Initialize \(y^0=Lx^0\). If iteration \(k\) accepts the block update \(x^{k+1}=x^k+U_{i_k}d^k\), update the transform cache by \[y^{k+1}=y^k+L_{i_k}d^k.\] Exact arithmetic preserves \(y^k=Lx^k\). The cached value is returned whenever the algorithm requests \(Lx^k\); full recomputation is required only at initialization, after an untracked modification, or as a numerical-drift safeguard.

The authoritative state changes from zero to one.

children.title: Matrix-Product Caching
children.top_down_role: Cached matrix or operator products used during block evaluation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of coordinate derivatives from a maintained forward or Gram matrix-product cache.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2\), partition \(A=[A_1\ \cdots\ A_m]\). If \(y=Ax\) is maintained exactly, then \[\nabla_i f(x)=A_i^*(y-b).\] After accepting \(x_i^+=x_i+d_i\), a consistent forward cache satisfies \(y^+=y+A_i d_i\). Alternatively, if \(g=A^*Ax\) is maintained exactly, then \(\nabla f(x)=g-A^*b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consistent forward or Gram matrix-product cache yields exact least-squares block gradients.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(b\) are fixed.
Each maintained product cache equals its defining matrix product.
The block partition agrees with the block columns \(A_i\).

notation.meaning: block column associated with block i

knowledge_statements.title: Cached Least-Squares Block Gradient

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Updating Gram-product blocks through precomputed block Gram operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[A_1\ \cdots\ A_m]\), \(G_{ji}=A_j^*A_i\), and \(g_j=A_j^*Ax\). After \(x_i^+=x_i+d_i\), \[g_j^+=g_j+G_{ji}d_i,\qquad j=1,\ldots,m.\] With precomputed \(G_{ji}\), only nonzero Gram blocks need be applied; dense Gram storage can eliminate the benefit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Precomputed block Gram operators update all Gram-cache blocks after one block change, but dense Gram storage can erase the advantage.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is fixed and block-column partitioned.
The Gram cache is initially consistent.
Every used \(G_{ji}\) equals \(A_j^*A_i\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Direct and Precomputed Gram-Cache Cost Comparison
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense arithmetic and storage costs after one block modification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\) and block \(i\) have width \(b_i\). Directly form \(u=A_i d_i\) and update \(g\leftarrow g+A^{\mathsf T}u\), costing \(O(pb_i+pn)\) dense arithmetic with \(O(pn)\) storage for \(A\). With precomputed \(G=A^{\mathsf T}A\), applying \(G_{:i}d_i\) costs \(O(nb_i)\), while dense Gram storage costs \(O(n^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct Gram-cache updates use a block forward product and full adjoint product; precomputation reduces repeated arithmetic but may require quadratic storage.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is dense.
Classical dense matrix-vector arithmetic is used.
Any Gram matrix is precomputed exactly and stored densely.

children.title: Cache Invalidation Scope
children.top_down_role: Dependency regions requiring refresh after a coordinate or block modification.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invalidation closure when cached quantities depend on other cached quantities as well as iterate blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite acyclic dependency graph have source vertices representing iterate blocks and cache vertices representing cached quantities, with an edge \(u\to v\) for every direct dependency of \(v\) on \(u\). After changing a source set \(S\), the conservative invalidation scope is the set of cache vertices reachable from \(S\). Revalidation proceeds in topological order, and a marked cache becomes valid only after its affected predecessors are current and it has been recomputed or exactly incremented. If every genuine dependency is represented, every unmarked cache remains valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invalidate the transitive dependency closure of modified blocks and refresh layered caches in topological order.
assumptions_latex: The dependency graph is finite and acyclic.
Every genuine direct dependency is represented by an edge.
All caches are initially consistent with their predecessors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal I(S)=\{v:\text{a directed path leads from some }s\in S\text{ to }v\}\text{ is a conservative invalidation scope.}
knowledge_statements.title: Transitive Cache Invalidation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating conservative over-invalidation from invalid cache retention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a cache \(c_j=F_j(x)\) is retained whenever its declared dependency set \(\widehat D_j\) is disjoint from the modified blocks. This rule is sound for all updates if and only if \(F_j(x)=F_j(x')\) whenever \(x\) and \(x'\) agree on \(\widehat D_j\). If an omitted block can change \(F_j\), modifying that block can leave a stale value marked valid. Supersets of the genuine dependency set cause conservative over-invalidation, whereas omissions can cause incorrect reuse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extra declared dependencies waste refresh work, while omission of a genuine dependency can leave a stale cache marked valid.
assumptions_latex: Cache validity means equality to \(F_j\) at the current iterate.
Retention is decided from the declared set \(\widehat D_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat D_j\text{ is sound if and only if }F_j\text{ is invariant under changes outside }\widehat D_j.

notation.meaning: declared dependency set of cache j

knowledge_statements.title: Unsound Dependency Omission
Cache Invalidation Scope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependency-based condition identifying exactly which cached quantities become stale after a block update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let cached quantities satisfy \(c_j=F_j(x)\), and let \(D_j\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) contain precisely the argument blocks on which \(F_j\) depends. After changing the block set \(S\), cache \(c_j\) is potentially invalid exactly when \(D_j\cap S\neq\varnothing\). It remains valid when \(D_j\cap S=\varnothing\). An invalid cache becomes valid only after recomputation from the current iterate or after an exact incremental update whose value equals \(F_j(x^{+})\). Thus the minimal conservative invalidation scope is \[\mathcal I(S)=\{j:D_j\cap S\neq\varnothing\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invalidate precisely the caches whose declared dependencies intersect the updated blocks; retain disjoint caches and revalidate stale ones by exact updating or recomputation.
assumptions_latex: Each cache has an explicit dependency set \(D_j\).
The modified block set \(S\) is known.
Dependency sets are conservative: omitted blocks cannot affect the cached function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal I(S)=\{j:D_j\cap S\neq\varnothing\}\) is the minimal conservative invalidation set.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dependency-intersection invalidation condition is coherent when each D_j is the precise dependency set. However, the claimed minimal conservative scope depends on that exactness and has no cited source or locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work and storage required to propagate a block-sparse increment through indexed nonzero block columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[A_1\ \cdots\ A_m]\), let \(q_i=\operatorname{nnz}(A_i)\), and store every block column in a sparse representation. For an update supported on \(S\), accumulating \(Ad=\sum_{i\in S}A_i d_i\) requires \(O(\!\sum_{i\in S}q_i)\) arithmetic operations under the standard sparse-matrix–vector cost model. The complete column index uses \(O(\!\operatorname{nnz}(A))\) storage. This advantage disappears when the selected columns collectively contain a constant fraction of all stored entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse propagation costs work proportional to the nonzeros in the updated block columns and loses its advantage when those columns are effectively dense.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has a fixed block-column partition.
Every stored nonzero of each \(A_i\) is accessible through its sparse index.
Sparse entry access and scalar arithmetic have constant unit cost.

notation.meaning: number of stored nonzeros in block column i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal failure witness for an omitted output dependency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[1]\), \(x=0\), \(y=Ax=0\), and \(d=1\). If the stored adjacency index is empty and propagation visits only indexed outputs, it returns \(\widehat y^+=0\), whereas \[A(x+d)=1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Omitting a nonzero matrix dependency can leave a changed transformed output stale.
assumptions_latex: Propagation visits only outputs in the stored adjacency index.
The sole nonzero dependency is omitted.
knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Sparse-Update Index Misses a Changed Output

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact verification condition for an output index used to propagate sparse linear updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[A_{ji}]\) be partitioned into output rows \(j\) and input blocks \(i\), and let \(\widehat N(i)\) be the stored output index for block \(i\). Index-driven propagation is exact for every block-sparse increment if and only if \[j\notin\widehat N(i)\implies A_{ji}=0\qquad\text{for every }i,j.\] Equivalently, \(\{j:A_{ji}\ne0\}\subseteq\widehat N(i)\) for every \(i\). Extra indexed outputs affect work but not correctness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse update index is complete exactly when every omitted transform block is zero; extra entries are harmless but costly.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is fixed with declared input-block and output-row partitions.
Propagation accumulates every indexed contribution exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Exact propagation for all block-sparse }d\iff \forall i,j,\ j\notin\widehat N(i)\Rightarrow A_{ji}=0.

notation.meaning: stored outputs adjacent to input block i
operator block from input block i to output row j

review_flags: This tests a proposed index and does not replace the deferred foundational support representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Adjacency-Index Completeness Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural support and output-dependency indexes for exact propagation of a block-sparse linear increment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[A_{ji}]\) have input blocks \(i=1,\ldots,m\) and output blocks \(j\). For an increment \(d\), define \(S(d)=\{i:d_i\ne0\}\) and \(N(i)=\{j:A_{ji}\ne0\}\). If \(y=Ax\), update \[y_j^+=y_j+\sum_{i\in S(d):\,j\in N(i)}A_{ji}d_i\qquad\left(j\in\bigcup_{i\in S(d)}N(i)\right),\] leaving every other output unchanged. Then \(y^+=A(x+d)\), and \(\operatorname{supp}(Ad)\subseteq\bigcup_{i\in S(d)}N(i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Index the changed input blocks and their structurally adjacent outputs; visiting their union propagates every contribution of a sparse linear update exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and its block partition are fixed.
Each \(N(i)\) contains every output block with \(A_{ji}\ne0\).
Every indexed contribution is accumulated exactly once.

notation.meaning: structurally adjacent output blocks of input block i
operator block from input block i to output block j

review_flags: The affected-output union is a safe structural superset and may be strict because of cancellation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Affected-Output Union Can Strictly Overestimate Actual Change
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cancellation boundary for adjacency-based sparse-update scopes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[1\;1]\), with its two columns treated as separate scalar blocks, and let \(d=(1,-1)\). Then \(N(1)=N(2)=\{1\}\) and \(S(d)=\{1,2\}\), but \[Ad=0,\qquad \operatorname{supp}(Ad)=\varnothing\subsetneq\bigcup_{i\in S(d)}N(i)=\{1\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structural adjacency finds every output that may change, but cancellation can make the actual changed support smaller.
assumptions_latex: The two columns form distinct input blocks.
Adjacency is determined by structural nonzeros of \(A\).

notation.meaning: structural output adjacency of input block i

knowledge_statements.title: Affected-Output Union Can Strictly Overestimate Actual Change
Sparse-Update Indexes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Index representation of block-sparse iterate changes and their affected transform coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a block vector \(x=(x_1,\\ldots,x_m)\), represent an update \(d\) by its support \(S(d)=\{i:d_i\neq0\}\) and the stored pairs \(\{(i,d_i):i\in S(d)\}\). For a sparse linear map \(A\), associate each block with the affected-output index set \(N(i)=\{j:A_{ji}\neq0\}\). Then \[A(x+d)=Ax+\sum_{i\in S(d)}A_i d_i,\] and only output indices in \(\bigcup_{i\in S(d)}N(i)\) can change. The support list and adjacency indexes therefore determine the complete incremental update scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store only changed blocks and their matrix adjacency lists; their union identifies every transformed coordinate that can change.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) has a fixed finite block partition.
\(d\) has finite block support.
\(N(i)\) records every nonzero output dependency of block i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The sparse-support representation and affected-output inclusion are mathematically plausible, but no source is supplied. In addition, the expression for x contains the malformed sequence \\ldots rather than \ldots and must be repaired once a sourced replacement is prepared.

children.title: Active-Coordinate Structures
children.top_down_role: Structures maintaining currently eligible or active coordinates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-update work for an exact active-coordinate structure under an exact dependency neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose only predicates indexed by \(N(S)\) can change after updating \(S\), each predicate evaluation costs at most \(T_a\), and each membership insertion or deletion costs at most \(T_Q\). Reevaluating \(N(S)\) and updating the exact active set costs \[O\bigl(|N(S)|(T_a+T_Q)\bigr).\] If \(N(S)\) is exactly the set of possibly changed predicates, no predicate outside it is evaluated. A bitset paired with an iterable set gives \(O(1)\) membership tests and \(O(|\mathcal A(x)|)\) enumeration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact active-set maintenance scales with the affected dependency neighborhood, while enumeration scales with the active-set size.
assumptions_latex: \(N(S)\) contains every possibly changed predicate; exactness is additionally required for the no-outside-evaluation claim.
Predicate and membership-operation costs are bounded by \(T_a\) and \(T_Q\).
The active-set invariant holds before the update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Maintenance costs \(O(|N(S)|(T_a+T_Q))\), with \(O(|\mathcal A(x)|)\) enumeration for the stated representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Localized Active-Set Maintenance Cost
Active-Coordinate Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact data-structure invariant for coordinates satisfying a declared activity predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_i(x)\in\{0,1\}\) be a declared activity predicate for each coordinate or block, and define \(\mathcal A(x)=\{i:a_i(x)=1\}\). An exact active-coordinate structure stores membership indicators and an iterable set \(Q\) satisfying \[i\in Q\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a_i(x)=1.\] After an update affecting the predicate-dependency neighborhood \(N(S)\), reevaluate \(a_i\) only for \(i\in N(S)\), insert newly active indices, delete newly inactive indices, and leave all other memberships unchanged. The structure is valid when \(Q=\mathcal A(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain a set equal to the coordinates satisfying an activity test, revising only predicates whose dependencies were affected by the latest update.
assumptions_latex: Every activity predicate \(a_i\) is explicitly defined.
\(N(S)\) contains every predicate whose value can change after updating \(S\).
Set insertions and deletions preserve unique membership.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q^{+}=\mathcal A(x^{+})\) after reevaluating all and only potentially affected predicates.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The active-set invariant is a reasonable representation, but it is unsupported by a citation. The assumptions say N(S) contains every affected predicate and may therefore be conservative, while the conclusion says all and only potentially affected predicates are reevaluated; exactness of N(S) would be needed for that wording.

children.title: Candidate-Pool Maintenance
children.top_down_role: Maintenance of coordinate candidates used by selective update policies.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness and sampling overhead of a conservative eligibility superset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\varnothing\ne E(x)\subseteq C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\). If candidates are drawn uniformly from \(C\) and executed only after exact current-eligibility screening, no ineligible coordinate is executed, each eligible coordinate is drawn with probability \(1/|C|\), and a draw passes screening with probability \[|E(x)|/|C|.\] For independent repeated draws, the expected number required to obtain an eligible coordinate is \(|C|/|E(x)|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: False positives do not compromise execution correctness when exact screening is used, but they reduce acceptance probability and increase sampling work.
assumptions_latex: \(\varnothing\ne E(x)\subseteq C\) at sampling time.
Sampling is uniform over finite \(C\).
Eligibility is screened exactly against the current state.
Repeated draws are independent for the expectation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Screening succeeds with probability \(|E(x)|/|C|\), and expected draws per eligible selection equal \(|C|/|E(x)|\).
knowledge_statements.title: Candidate-Pool False-Positive Tradeoff
Candidate-Pool Maintenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maintenance rule for a conservative pool containing every coordinate eligible for selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e_i(x)\in\{0,1\}\) define exact eligibility and let \(E(x)=\{i:e_i(x)=1\}\). Maintain a candidate pool \(C\) with invariant \(E(x)\subseteq C\). After updating blocks \(S\), identify a dependency neighborhood \(N(S)\) containing every index whose eligibility can change. Reevaluate \(e_i(x^{+})\) for \(i\in N(S)\), insert every newly eligible index, and optionally delete an index only after verifying its current ineligibility. Selection must test exact eligibility before executing an update. The output pool satisfies \(E(x^{+})\subseteq C^{+}\), so no eligible coordinate is lost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update a conservative candidate pool around affected dependencies, never deleting an index without checking it and testing eligibility again before selection.
assumptions_latex: \(N(S)\) covers all eligibility predicates affected by the update.
Every newly eligible affected index is inserted.
Deletion and final selection use the current exact predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E(x^{+})\subseteq C^{+}\), and every selected coordinate satisfies its current eligibility predicate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conservative candidate-pool invariant is coherent and algorithm fits the maintenance leaf, but eligibility, neighborhood maintenance, deletion, and final screening form an application-dependent policy with no supporting source or locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Calibrated Coordinate Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block stepsizes calibrated by coordinate-wise quadratic upper models of a differentiable objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) be differentiable and let \(U_i\) inject block \(i\). A number \(L_i>0\) is a valid block-curvature parameter when, for every \(x\) and admissible block displacement \(h\), \[f(x+U_i h)\leq f(x)+\langle
abla_i f(x),hangle+ rac{L_i}{2}\|h\|^2.\] The curvature-calibrated gradient step uses \(\alpha_i\in(0,2/L_i)\), with the model-minimizing choice \(\alpha_i=1/L_i\), and sets \(x^{+}=x-\alpha_iU_i
abla_i f(x)\). For \(\alpha_i=1/L_i\), the upper model yields \(f(x^{+})\leq f(x)-\|
abla_i f(x)\|^2/(2L_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose each block stepsize from a valid coordinate curvature bound; the reciprocal bound minimizes the quadratic upper model and guarantees blockwise descent.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable on \(\mathbb R^n\).
The displayed block quadratic upper bound holds with \(L_i>0\).
The selected displacement remains in the domain of \(f\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Known-curvature proximal coordinate parameterization for a block-separable composite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=f(x)+\sum_jg_j(x_j)\), where \(f\) satisfies the block quadratic upper bound with \(L_i>0\). Set \[x_i^+=\operatorname{prox}_{g_i/L_i}\!\left(x_i-\frac{1}{L_i}\nabla_i f(x)\right),\qquad d_i=x_i^+-x_i,\] and leave other blocks fixed. If \(g_i\) is proper, closed, and convex, then \[F(x+U_i d_i)\le F(x)-\frac{L_i}{2}\|d_i\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reciprocal block curvature calibrates the proximal coordinate step and guarantees decrease proportional to its squared displacement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Blockwise multiplicative curvature search for a smooth coordinate step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), block \(i\), trial curvature \(M_i>0\), and \(\gamma>1\), set \(d_i=-M_i^{-1}\nabla_i f(x)\). While \[f(x+U_id_i)>f(x)+\langle\nabla_i f(x),d_i\rangle+\frac{M_i}{2}\lVert d_i\rVert^2,\] replace \(M_i\leftarrow\gamma M_i\) and recompute \(d_i\). At the first successful trial, accept \(x^+=x+U_id_i\); the accepted \(M_i\) may be retained as the next trial estimate for block \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase the selected block's curvature estimate geometrically until its quadratic model validates the coordinate step, then accept the step and optionally reuse that estimate.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable.
\(U_i\) embeds block \(i\) into the ambient space.
\(M_i>0\) and \(\gamma>1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coordinate Backtracking Termination and Rejection Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination, accepted-curvature bound, and descent for multiplicative coordinate backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(L_i>0\) satisfies \[f(x+U_ih)\le f(x)+\langle\nabla_i f(x),h\rangle+\frac{L_i}{2}\lVert h\rVert^2\] for every trial displacement generated by the search. Starting from \(M_i^{(0)}>0\), multiplicative backtracking with factor \(\gamma>1\) terminates after at most \[r_i=\max\left\{0,\left\lceil\log_\gamma\frac{L_i}{M_i^{(0)}}\right\rceil\right\}\] rejected trials. Its accepted curvature satisfies \[M_i^{\mathrm{acc}}\le\max\{M_i^{(0)},\gamma L_i\},\] and its accepted gradient step satisfies \[f(x^+)\le f(x)-\frac{1}{2M_i^{\mathrm{acc}}}\lVert\nabla_i f(x)\rVert^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a valid block Lipschitz upper model, geometric coordinate backtracking terminates after logarithmically many rejections, accepts a controlled curvature estimate, and produces quantified descent.
assumptions_latex: A finite \(L_i>0\) validates the block quadratic upper model for every tested displacement.
The trial step is \(d_i=-\nabla_i f(x)/M_i\).

notation.meaning: valid block Lipschitz curvature bound over all tested displacements

While \(f(x+U_i d_i)>f(x)+\langle\nabla_i f(x),d_i\rangle+(M_i/2)\lVert d_i\rVert^2\), replace \(M_i\leftarrow\gamma M_i\) and recompute \(d_i\). Accept \(x^+=x+U_i d_i\) at the first successful trial and retain the accepted \(M_i\) as the next curvature estimate for block \(i\).

The selected block gradient is Lipschitz on the searched segment.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Actual-decrease consequence of an accepted smooth or separable-composite block model.

For the smooth model change \(m_i(d)=\langle
abla_i f(x),dangle+(M_i/2)\|d\|^2\), acceptance implies \(f(x)-f(x+U_i d)\ge -m_i(d)\). For \(F=f+\sum_jg_j\), define \(m_i^F(d)=\langle
abla_i f(x),dangle+(M_i/2)\|d\|^2+g_i(x_i+d)-g_i(x_i)\); composite acceptance implies \(F(x)-F(x+U_i d)\ge-m_i^F(d)\). Thus an accepted model change at most \(-\delta\) certifies actual decrease at least \(\delta\). In the smooth unconstrained case, \(d=-
abla_i f(x)/M_i\) gives \(f(x)-f(x+U_i d)\ge\|

\(M_i>0\), and the accepted trial uses the displayed model.

For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), block \(i\), displacement \(d_i\), and \(M_i>0\), the trial point \(x^+=x+U_i d_i\) passes local-model validation precisely when \[f(x^+)\leq f(x)+\langle
abla_i f(x),d_iangle+ rac{M_i}{2}\lVert d_iVert^2.\] For a composite objective \(F=f+g\) with block-separable \(g(x)=\sum_j g_j(x_j)\), replace the two sides by \(F(x^+)\) and \(f(x)+\langle
abla_i f(x),d_iangle+(M_i/2)\lVert d_iVert^2+g_i(x_i+d_i)+\sum_{j
e i}g_j(x_j)\), respectively.

children.title: Model-Rejection Regimes
children.top_down_role: Situations where local surrogate behavior triggers recalibration or rejection.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiable one-dimensional family showing that increasing trial curvature need not ensure acceptance without local Lipschitz gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(t)=|t|^{3/2}\), take the base point \(x=0\), and note that \(f'(0)=0\). For every finite \(M>0\), any nonzero displacement satisfying \(|d|<4/M^2\) obeys \[f(d)=|d|^{3/2}>\frac{M}{2}|d|^2=f(0)+f'(0)d+\frac{M}{2}|d|^2.\] Hence trials can remain rejected along a sequence \(M_k\to\infty\) if \(0<|d_k|<4/M_k^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Differentiability alone does not ensure eventual acceptance: a non-Lipschitz gradient permits rejected shrinking trials even while curvature estimates diverge.
assumptions_latex: The trial displacement may depend on the tested curvature.
No local Lipschitz-gradient assumption is imposed at the base point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(M_k\to\infty\) and \(d_k\to0\) for which every quadratic-model trial is rejected.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Rejection without Block-Lipschitz Smoothness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact inference, and its limit, from one rejected nonzero block trial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(d_i\ne0\), define \[\widehat L_i(x,d_i)=\frac{2\bigl(f(x+U_i d_i)-f(x)-\langle\nabla_i f(x),d_i\rangle\bigr)}{\|d_i\|^2}.\] Rejection at curvature \(M_i\) is equivalent to \(\widehat L_i(x,d_i)>M_i\). This statement concerns only the tested base point and displacement; it neither rules out a finite smoothness bound on another region nor implies rejection of another displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rejected nonzero trial certifies that its observed secant curvature exceeds the tested curvature, but supports no stronger global inference.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable at \(x\).
The objective and model use the same base point and displacement.
knowledge_statements.title: Trialwise Curvature Certificate from Rejection
Model-Rejection Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which a coordinate quadratic trial must be rejected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A trial \(x^+=x+U_i d_i\) is rejected whenever \[f(x^+)>f(x)+\langle\nabla_i f(x),d_i\rangle+\frac{M_i}{2}\lVert d_i\rVert^2.\] If \(\nabla_i f\) is \(L_i\)-Lipschitz along the segment from \(x\) to \(x^+\), rejection cannot occur for \(M_i\geq L_i\). Hence persistent rejection with unboundedly increasing \(M_i\) indicates failure of the required segmentwise block smoothness, an invalid objective evaluation, or a displacement inconsistent with the tested model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reject whenever the objective exceeds the coordinate quadratic model. Under block Lipschitz smoothness, curvature at least the block Lipschitz constant rules out rejection.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable at the tested points.
The trial uses the same \(d_i\) and \(M_i\) as the displayed model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For segmentwise block Lipschitz constant \(L_i\), the rejection region is empty whenever \(M_i\geq L_i\).

notation.meaning: segmentwise Lipschitz constant of the block gradient

knowledge_statements.title: Delay-Aware Coordinate Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative relaxation calibrated to a deterministic consistent-read delay bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(U_i:\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\to\mathbb{R}^n\) embed block \(i\), and let \(S_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^{n_i}\) be its update operator. Consider \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta(\tau)U_{i_k}S_{i_k}(\hat x^k)\), where \(\hat x^k=x^k+\sum_{h=k-\tau_k}^{k-1}(x^h-x^{h+1})\) and \(\tau_k\in\{0,\ldots,\min\{\tau,k\}\}\). Given a synchronous admissible limit \(\bar\eta>0\), a delay-aware parameter rule is a map \(\eta:\mathbb{N}_0\to(0,\bar\eta]\) satisfying \(\eta(\tau_2)\leq\eta(\tau_1)\) whenever \(\tau_2\geq\tau_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated bounded consistent-read model, choose a positive relaxation no larger than the synchronous limit and nonincreasing in the certified maximum delay.
assumptions_latex: \(x^k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(U_i\) and \(S_i\) have the stated compatible domains.
Each read has a consistent delay \(\tau_k\) bounded by \(\tau\).
\(\bar\eta>0\) is a valid synchronous relaxation limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The calibrated relaxation satisfies \(0<\eta(\tau)\leq\bar\eta\) and is nonincreasing in \(\tau\).

notation.meaning: embedding of block i into the ambient space

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Constant-Delay Stability Boundary for a Scalar Coordinate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp stepsize boundary for delayed gradient descent on a scalar quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta x^{k-\tau}\) with fixed \(\tau\in\mathbb N_0\), \[x^k\to0\text{ for every initial history}\iff0<\eta<2\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi}{4\tau+2}\right).\] At equality the characteristic polynomial \(z^{\tau+1}-z^\tau+\eta\) has unit-modulus roots; above it some histories diverge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a delayed scalar quadratic, convergence for every history holds exactly below 2 sin(pi/(4τ+2)); equality and larger steps admit failure.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau\in\mathbb N_0\) is fixed and used at every iteration.
\(\eta\) is constant.
review_flags: Specific to the scalar constant-delay recurrence; it cannot be transferred unchanged to multidimensional, variable-delay, or inconsistent-read models.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Constant-Delay Stability Boundary for a Scalar Coordinate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Delay Monotonicity Alone Does Not Guarantee Stability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a merely nonincreasing delay-aware relaxation rule on a delayed scalar quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\), \(\bar\eta=3/2\), and \(\eta(\tau)=3/2\) for every \(\tau\). With constant delay one, \[x^{k+1}=x^k-\tfrac32x^{k-1}.\] The roots of \(z^2-z+3/2\) have modulus \(\sqrt{3/2}>1\), so some initial histories diverge despite \(0<\eta(\tau)\le\bar\eta\) and delay monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rule can satisfy the abstract delay-aware interface and remain unstable.
assumptions_latex: The read delay is constantly one.
\(\eta(\tau)=\bar\eta=3/2\).
review_flags: This concerns delay-only calibration, not conflict-aware or joint calibration.
knowledge_statements.title: Delay Monotonicity Alone Does Not Guarantee Stability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Impossibility of choosing a universally stable positive stepsize from delay alone without an objective scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\tau\in\mathbb N_0\) and any proposed \(\eta(\tau)>0\). For \(f_a(x)=\tfrac a2x^2\), the constant-delay iteration \[x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta(\tau)a x^{k-\tau}\] is stable for every initial history only if \[0<\eta(\tau)a<2\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi}{4\tau+2}\right).\] Hence no positive rule depending only on \(\tau\) is uniformly stable over all \(a>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delay alone cannot determine a universally stable positive stepsize; calibration also needs a curvature or operator scale.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau\) is a fixed nonnegative integer.
\(\eta(\tau)>0\) is chosen independently of \(a\).
The delayed gradient is evaluated on \(f_a(x)=\tfrac a2x^2\).

children.title: Conflict-Aware Coordinate Parameters

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Aware Coordinate Parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxation calibrated to overlap among simultaneously active updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(\{1,\ldots,m\},E)\) be the block-conflict graph, with \((i,j)\in E\) when updates of blocks \(i\) and \(j\) can access a common state component and at least one access writes. For conflict measure \(\Delta=\max_i\deg_G(i)\) and synchronous admissible limit \(\bar\eta>0\), a conflict-aware rule selects \(\eta=\eta(\Delta)\) such that \(0<\eta(\Delta)\leq\bar\eta\) and \(\eta(\Delta_2)\leq\eta(\Delta_1)\) whenever \(\Delta_2\geq\Delta_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent interfering blocks by a conflict graph and choose a positive relaxation that does not increase as the graph’s maximum degree grows.
assumptions_latex: The conflict graph includes every pair of potentially interfering block updates.
\(\bar\eta\) is admissible when conflicting updates are serialized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation remains within \((0,\bar\eta]\) and is nonincreasing in the maximum conflict degree.

notation.meaning: maximum degree of the conflict graph

children.title: Joint Asynchrony Calibration
children.top_down_role: Parameter regimes accounting simultaneously for stale information and block interference.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Asynchrony Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous calibration against bounded delay and update conflict.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a delay bound \(\tau\), conflict measure \(\Delta\), and synchronous limit \(\bar\eta>0\), a joint asynchrony calibration is a map \(\eta:\mathbb{N}_0^2\to(0,\bar\eta]\) satisfying \(\eta(\tau_2,\Delta_2)\leq\eta(\tau_1,\Delta_1)\) whenever \(\tau_2\geq\tau_1\) and \(\Delta_2\geq\Delta_1\). A conservative composition of independently valid bounds is \[\eta(\tau,\Delta)=\min\{\eta_{\rm delay}(\tau),\eta_{\rm conflict}(\Delta)\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a relaxation nonincreasing in both delay and conflict; taking the smaller independently admissible parameter is a conservative joint calibration.
assumptions_latex: \(\eta_{\rm delay}(\tau)\) and \(\eta_{\rm conflict}(\Delta)\) are independently admissible upper bounds.
Both component bounds lie in \((0,\bar\eta]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The minimum rule satisfies both component restrictions and is coordinatewise nonincreasing in \((\tau,\Delta)\).

children.title: Adaptive Parameter-Free Coordinate Policy Family
children.top_down_role: Policies reducing prior dependence on coordinate curvature, growth, or delay information.

children.title: Adaptive Coordinate Scaling
children.top_down_role: Online adjustment of coordinate or block metrics.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smoothness condition on an adaptive block step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If block \(i\) has coordinate Lipschitz constant \(L_i\) and \(x^+=x-\eta_iU_i\nabla_i f(x)\), then \[f(x^+)\le f(x)-\left(\eta_i-\frac{L_i\eta_i^2}{2}\right)\|\nabla_i f(x)\|^2.\] Hence every nonstationary selected-block step decreases \(f\) when \(0<\eta_i<2/L_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adaptive block step is descent-safe while it remains below twice the reciprocal block curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and block-coordinate smooth with constant \(L_i\).
knowledge_statements.title: Per-Block Descent Safeguard

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adaptive Scaling as a Diagonal Metric
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Metric representation of online blockwise step multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_k=\operatorname{diag}(h_1^kI_{n_1},\ldots,h_m^kI_{n_m})\succ0\). A selected-block scaled-gradient update is \[x^{k+1}=x^k-U_{i_k}(h_{i_k}^k)^{-1}\nabla_{i_k}f(x^k).\] Thus online changes of the positive block scales are changes of a block-diagonal metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive coordinate denominators are the diagonal blocks of an online metric.
assumptions_latex: Every \(h_i^k>0\).
The block decomposition is fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Scaling as a Diagonal Metric

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online block-scale calibration through a coordinate quadratic-upper-model test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain positive block curvature estimates \(h_i^k\). After selecting \(i=i_k\), set \(h\leftarrow h_i^k\), form \(x^+(h)=x^k-h^{-1}U_i\nabla_i f(x^k)\), and while \[f(x^+(h))>f(x^k)+\langle\nabla_i f(x^k),x_i^+(h)-x_i^k\rangle+\frac h2\|x_i^+(h)-x_i^k\|^2\] replace \(h\leftarrow\beta h\), where \(\beta>1\). Accept \(x^{k+1}=x^+(h)\), set \(h_i^{k+1}=h\), and leave the other scales unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase the selected block's online curvature scale until its quadratic model upper-bounds the observed objective, then take the scaled step.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and evaluable at trial points.
The selected block has a finite coordinate Lipschitz constant \(L_i\).
Initial scales are positive and \(\beta>1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: h\ge L_i\ \text{passes the test, and }f(x^{k+1})\le f(x^k)-\frac{1}{2h}\|\nabla_i f(x^k)\|^2.

notation.meaning: Online block curvature or metric scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Backtracking Coordinate Metric Scaling

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Summable Adaptive Steps Can Stagnate Away from Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by inverse metric scales having finite total mass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For f(x)=\tfrac12x^2 with x^0=1, choose \eta_k=2^{-k-2} and update x^{k+1}=(1-\eta_k)x^k. Every step satisfies 0<\eta_k<2 and strictly decreases f while x^k\ne0, but x^k=\prod_{h=0}^{k-1}(1-\eta_h)\to\prod_{h=0}^{\infty}(1-\eta_h)>0. Hence \nabla f(x^k) does not converge to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Individually descent-safe adaptive coordinate steps can stagnate at a nonstationary point when their total length is finite.
assumptions_latex: f(x)=\tfrac12x^2 and x^0=1.
x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta_k\nabla f(x^k).

notation.meaning: Effective coordinate stepsize or inverse online metric scale.

knowledge_statements.title: Summable Adaptive Steps Can Stagnate Away from Stationarity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationarity Under Uniformly Bounded Adaptive Block Metrics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global stationarity for descent-safe variable block-diagonal scaling with bounded coordinate starvation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be bounded below and have globally Lipschitz gradient. At iteration \(k\), select block \(i_k\) and set \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\eta_{i_k}^kU_{i_k}
abla_{i_k}f(x^k)\). Suppose every block appears at least once in each \(B\) consecutive iterations and, whenever block \(i\) is selected, \(0<\underline\eta_i\le\eta_i^k\le\overline\eta_i<2/L_i\), where \(L_i\) is a valid block smoothness constant. Then \(\sum_k\|
abla_{i_k}f(x^k)\|^2<\infty\), \(\|x^{k+1}-x^k\|	o0\), and \(\|
abla f(x^k)\|	o0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive coordinate scaling converges to first-order stationarity when every inverse metric scale stays uniformly positive and descent-safe and every block is visited within a bounded window.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is bounded below and has globally Lipschitz gradient.
Each block satisfies a coordinate quadratic upper model with constant \(L_i\).
Every block is selected at least once in each \(B\)-iteration window.
\(0<\underline\eta_i\le\eta_i^k\le\overline\eta_i<2/L_i\) whenever block \(i\) is selected.

notation.meaning: Effective inverse metric scale used on block i.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Under Uniformly Bounded Adaptive Block Metrics

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Selected-Block Stationarity Complexity Under Bounded Adaptive Metrics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-time consequence of uniformly bounded descent-safe adaptive coordinate steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the block quadratic upper models and bounds \(0<\underline\eta_i\le\eta_i^k\le\overline\eta_i<2/L_i\) whenever block \(i\) is selected. Define \[c:=\min_i\underline\eta_i\left(1-\frac{L_i\overline\eta_i}{2}\right)>0,\qquad \Delta_0:=f(x^0)-\inf f.\] Then for every \(K\ge1\), \[\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\|\nabla_{i_k}f(x^k)\|^2\le\frac{\Delta_0}{c},\qquad \min_{0\le k<K}\|\nabla_{i_k}f(x^k)\|^2\le\frac{\Delta_0}{cK}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly positive descent-safe inverse metric scales give an inverse-linear bound for the smallest squared selected-block gradient.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is bounded below.
Every selected block satisfies a coordinate quadratic upper model with constant \(L_i\).
Whenever block \(i\) is selected, \(0<\underline\eta_i\le\eta_i^k\le\overline\eta_i<2/L_i\).

notation.meaning: Initial objective gap to the infimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Selected-Block Stationarity Complexity Under Bounded Adaptive Metrics

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Backtracking Trials for One Coordinate Metric Update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trial-evaluation bound for multiplicative coordinate backtracking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In Backtracking Coordinate Metric Scaling, let the selected block have valid curvature constant \(L_i\), initial trial scale \(h_0>0\), and multiplier \(\beta>1\). Since every \(h\ge L_i\) passes the quadratic-upper-model test, the number of rejected trials satisfies \[N_{\rm rej}\le\max\left\{0,\left\lceil\log_\beta\frac{L_i}{h_0}\right\rceil\right\}.\] Thus one accepted update uses at most \(1+N_{\rm rej}\) trial objective evaluations. If \(h_0<L_i\), the first accepted scale satisfies \(h_{\rm acc}<\beta L_i\), although it may be smaller than \(L_i\) when the local test succeeds early.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplicative coordinate backtracking terminates after logarithmically many rejected scales; local acceptance may occur below the global block-curvature bound.
assumptions_latex: The selected block has a finite coordinate quadratic-upper-model constant \(L_i\).
The initial trial scale satisfies \(h_0>0\).
The multiplier satisfies \(\beta>1\).
Each trial evaluates the declared upper-model test.

notation.meaning: First scale accepted by coordinate backtracking.

knowledge_statements.title: Backtracking Trials for One Coordinate Metric Update

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Core summation inequality for coordinatewise squared-gradient accumulators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v^0=\delta^2>0\) and \(v^{k+1}=v^k+a_k^2\). Then, for every \(K\ge1\), \[\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\frac{a_k^2}{\sqrt{v^{k+1}}}\le 2\bigl(\sqrt{v^K}-\delta\bigr).\] Applied separately to each block, this bounds the cumulative normalized squared gradients contributed when that block is selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Squared magnitudes divided by their updated cumulative root scale sum to at most twice the scale's total growth.
assumptions_latex: \(a_k\in\mathbb R\) and \(v^{k+1}=v^k+a_k^2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Accumulated-Gradient Scaling Summation Bound
Adaptive Coordinate Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online diagonal metric update from observed coordinate gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(v_i^0=\delta^2\) for every block, with \(\delta>0\). At iteration \(k\), after selecting \(i_k\) and observing \(g_{i_k}^k=\nabla_{i_k}f(x^k)\), set \(v_{i_k}^{k+1}=v_{i_k}^k+\lVert g_{i_k}^k\rVert^2\), leave \(v_j^{k+1}=v_j^k\) for \(j\ne i_k\), and update \[x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha U_{i_k}\frac{g_{i_k}^k}{\sqrt{v_{i_k}^{k+1}}}.\] Stop according to a prescribed iteration, stationarity, or objective criterion and return the last iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accumulate squared gradients separately by block and divide each selected block step by the square root of its accumulated statistic.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) is differentiable.
\(\alpha>0\) and \(\delta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method produces a positive, nondecreasing block scale \(\sqrt{v_i^k}\) using only gradients observed online.

notation.meaning: accumulated squared-gradient statistic for block i

children.title: Adaptive Sampling Refresh Interface
children.top_down_role: Online revision of selection policies and their supporting statistics.

children.title: Adaptive Coordinate Sampling
children.top_down_role: Online revision of coordinate selection probabilities or priorities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-support safeguard for adaptive coordinate probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a history-measurable probability vector \(q^k\) and fixed \(\varepsilon\in(0,1]\), define \(p_i^k=(1-\varepsilon)q_i^k+\varepsilon/m\). Then \(p_i^k\ge\varepsilon/m\), \[\mathbb P(i_k\ne i\text{ for }k=t,\ldots,t+T-1\mid\mathcal F_t)\le(1-\varepsilon/m)^T,\] and every block is selected infinitely often almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform exploration prevents starvation and exponentially bounds omission over a finite window.
assumptions_latex: Each draw uses \(p^k\) conditionally on the pre-draw history.
\(\varepsilon>0\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Exploration-Mixture Support Guarantee

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise optimal probabilities for an inverse-probability coordinate estimator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For block vectors \(g_i\), let \(I\sim p\) and \(G=U_Ig_I/p_I\), with \(p_i>0\) whenever \(g_i\ne0\). Then \[\mathbb E\|G\|^2=\sum_i\frac{\|g_i\|^2}{p_i}\ge\left(\sum_i\|g_i\|\right)^2,\] with equality exactly when \(p_i\propto\|g_i\|\) on the nonzero blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampling proportionally to current block norms minimizes the second moment of the unbiased coordinate estimator.
assumptions_latex: The vectors and probabilities are measurable before drawing \(I\).
Each nonzero block has positive probability.
knowledge_statements.title: Variance-Optimal Adaptive Coordinate Probabilities
Adaptive Coordinate Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online importance sampling from positive block statistics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain positive statistics \(s_i^k>0\) for blocks \(i=1,\ldots,m\). At iteration \(k\), define \[p_i^k=\frac{s_i^k}{\sum_{j=1}^m s_j^k},\] sample \(i_k\) conditionally on the history with probability \(p_{i_k}^k\), perform the chosen block update, and refresh at least the observed statistic \(s_{i_k}^k\) using information revealed by that update. The conditional estimator \(U_{i_k}g_{i_k}^k/p_{i_k}^k\) is used whenever an unbiased full-gradient estimate is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize positive online block scores into probabilities, sample accordingly, update the chosen block, and refresh its score from newly observed information.
assumptions_latex: Every statistic satisfies \(s_i^k>0\).
The block score at iteration \(k\) is measurable before drawing \(i_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The probabilities satisfy \(p_i^k>0\) and \(\sum_i p_i^k=1\); inverse-probability weighting yields conditional unbiasedness when \(g_i^k=\nabla_i f(x^k)\).

children.title: Selection-Policy Refresh
children.top_down_role: Timing and triggering of updates to the active selection policy.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Refresh driven by observed score drift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\tilde s\) underlie the active policy and let \(s^k\) be the currently available positive score estimate. For \(\tau>0\), retain the policy while \[\max_i\left|\log\frac{s_i^k}{\tilde s_i}\right|\le\tau.\] When the inequality fails, set \(\tilde s\leftarrow s^k\), rebuild the normalized distribution, and continue. A positive floor may be applied before normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Refresh the active policy when an available score changes by more than a prescribed multiplicative factor.
assumptions_latex: All compared scores are strictly positive.
The drift test occurs before the next random draw.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{between refreshes},\quad e^{-\tau}\tilde s_i\le s_i^k\le e^\tau\tilde s_i

notation.meaning: score vector underlying the active policy

review_flags: Requires all scores used by the trigger to be currently available; their acquisition cost is not included.
knowledge_statements.title: Event-Triggered Selection-Policy Refresh

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact normalization after changing selected score entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain positive weights \(w_i\) and \(W=\sum_iw_i\). If a refresh changes entries in \(S\) to \(w_i'\), set \[W'=W+\sum_{i\in S}(w_i'-w_i),\qquad p_i'=w_i'/W'.\] This equals complete renormalization, and updating the stored total costs \(O(|S|)\) arithmetic apart from maintaining the sampling data structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial score refresh maintains exact normalization by updating the stored total weight.
assumptions_latex: Every post-refresh weight is positive.
The stored pre-refresh total is exact.
knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Normalization Refresh

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Refresh Count Under Bounded Log-Score Variation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-triggered policy rebuild count controlled by cumulative multiplicative score drift.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Event-Triggered Selection-Policy Refresh, let \(u^k=(\log s_1^k,\ldots,\log s_m^k)\) and \[V_K=\sum_{k=1}^K\|u^k-u^{k-1}\|_\infty.\] If a refresh occurs only when \(\|u^k-u^{t_q}\|_\infty>\tau\), where \(t_q\) is the preceding refresh time, then the number \(Q_K\) of triggered refreshes after initialization obeys \[Q_K\le\left\lfloor\frac{V_K}{\tau}\right\rfloor.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The number of event-triggered policy rebuilds is bounded by cumulative log-score variation divided by the drift threshold.
assumptions_latex: Every score is strictly positive.
The active baseline is reset after every refresh.
The trigger threshold satisfies \(\tau>0\).
Refresh tests use the available score vector before the next draw.

notation.meaning: Cumulative infinity-norm variation of log scores.
Triggered refreshes after initialization through time K.

Selection-Policy Refresh
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Periodic reconstruction of coordinate probabilities from current scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix refresh times \(0=t_0<t_1<t_2<\cdots\), a floor \(\varepsilon>0\), and nonnegative observed scores \(r_i^{t_q}\). At each \(t_q\), set \[p_i^{t_q}=\frac{r_i^{t_q}+\varepsilon}{\sum_{j=1}^m(r_j^{t_q}+\varepsilon)}.\] For \(t_q\leq k<t_{q+1}\), sample coordinates using \(p^k=p^{t_q}\). At \(t_{q+1}\), recompute all available scores and renormalize; output is the updated probability vector and the resulting sampled block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At scheduled times, add a positive floor to current block scores, renormalize them, and hold the resulting sampling distribution until the next refresh.
assumptions_latex: Refresh times are strictly increasing.
Each observed score satisfies \(r_i^{t_q}\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every refreshed distribution has full support and remains constant between consecutive refresh times.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Exploration Under Refreshed Weight Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematically sound sampling-coverage property whose canonical home is Adaptive Coordinate Sampling rather than policy-refresh mechanics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(p_i^k=w_i^k/\sum_jw_j^k\), \(w_i^k\ge\varepsilon>0\), and \(\sum_jw_j^k\le\overline W\), then \(p_i^k\ge\varepsilon/\overline W\), the conditional probability of omitting block \(i\) for \(H\) draws is at most \((1-\varepsilon/\overline W)^H\), and every block is selected infinitely often almost surely.

Every active weight is at least \(\varepsilon>0\).
Every active total weight is at most \(\overline W\).

children.title: Sampling-Statistic Staleness
children.top_down_role: Validity limits caused by outdated statistics supporting adaptive selection.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure from retaining a zero cached score without exploration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a normalized cached-score policy has \(\tilde s_i^k=0\) for every \(k\ge k_0\), while the current update signal for block \(i\) later becomes nonzero, then \(\tilde p_i^k=0\) and the block is never selected after \(k_0\). Inverse-probability estimation of that nonzero block is undefined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stale zero score can permanently starve a block whose current importance becomes positive.
assumptions_latex: No positive exploration floor is used.
Probabilities are obtained by normalizing cached scores.
knowledge_statements.title: Stale-Zero Starvation Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of cached-score error to normalized probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p_i=s_i/\sum_js_j\) and \(\tilde p_i=\tilde s_i/\sum_j\tilde s_j\), where all scores are positive and \(\rho^{-1}s_i\le\tilde s_i\le\rho s_i\). Then \[\rho^{-2}p_i\le\tilde p_i\le\rho^2p_i,\qquad \sum_i\frac{\|g_i\|^2}{\tilde p_i}\le\rho^2\sum_i\frac{\|g_i\|^2}{p_i}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor-rho score staleness causes at most factor-rho-squared probability distortion and second-moment inflation.
assumptions_latex: All current and cached scores are strictly positive.
Both score vectors use the same normalization rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Score Distortion Implies Probability Distortion
Sampling-Statistic Staleness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Age and distortion criteria for cached coordinate scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_i^k\) be the current ideal score for block \(i\), and let \(\tilde s_i^k=s_i^{u_i(k)}\) be the cached score last refreshed at time \(u_i(k)\leq k\). Its age is \(a_i(k)=k-u_i(k)\). The cache is \((A,\rho)\)-controlled at iteration \(k\) when \[a_i(k)\leq A\quad\text{and}\quad \rho^{-1}s_i^k\leq\tilde s_i^k\leq\rho s_i^k\qquad\text{for every }i,\] where \(A\in\mathbb{N}_0\) and \(\rho\geq1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cached sampling score is controlled when its age is bounded and it remains within a prescribed multiplicative factor of the current ideal score.
assumptions_latex: All ideal and cached scores are strictly positive.
Each refresh time satisfies \(u_i(k)\leq k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed age and multiplicative-distortion inequalities define controlled sampling-statistic staleness.

notation.meaning: last refresh time of block i by iteration k

children.title: Adaptive Coordinate Restart
children.top_down_role: Restart policies for accelerated coordinate methods without fixed regime knowledge.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limitation of observable momentum-restart tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An observable rule specifying only when momentum is reset does not imply acceleration or linear convergence. Such a rate additionally requires a bound for the base coordinate method and quantitative control of epoch lengths or a restart potential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restart trigger is an execution safeguard, not by itself a convergence-rate certificate.
assumptions_latex: The trigger supplies no independent potential-decrease or epoch-length guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: Trigger-Only Rate Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rate inherited when restart epochs have certified sufficient length.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an accelerated coordinate method started at \(z\) satisfies \(F(x_K)-F_\star\le C\operatorname{dist}(z,X_\star)^2/K^2\), and \(F(z)-F_\star\ge(\mu/2)\operatorname{dist}(z,X_\star)^2\). If epoch \(r\) retains its endpoint and has length \(K_r\), then \[F(z_{r+1})-F_\star\le\frac{2C}{\mu K_r^2}\bigl(F(z_r)-F_\star\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sufficiently long accelerated epoch contracts the objective gap under quadratic growth.
assumptions_latex: The accelerated bound holds from every epoch start.
Each restart preserves the completed epoch endpoint.
review_flags: Applies only when the adaptive policy separately certifies the required epoch lengths.
knowledge_statements.title: Epochwise Contraction Under Quadratic Growth

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observable coordinate restart using rejection and complete momentum reset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an accelerated coordinate routine have accepted iterate \(z^k\) and complete auxiliary state \(a^k\). Form a tentative coordinate update and extrapolated state \((\widetilde z^{k+1},\widetilde a^{k+1})\). If \(F(\widetilde z^{k+1})\le F(z^k)\), accept the candidate. Otherwise reject it, retain \(z^{k+1}=z^k\), and reinitialize every acceleration state at \(z^k\) before the next non-extrapolated coordinate step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a coordinate-accelerated candidate only when it does not increase the objective; otherwise roll back and reset all momentum state.
assumptions_latex: The base accelerated coordinate recurrence and all auxiliary states are specified.
Comparable objective values are available at tested candidates.
A rejected candidate has no committed side effects.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(z^{k+1})\le F(z^k),\qquad \text{and rejection resets all acceleration states at }z^k.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Safeguarded Adaptive Coordinate Restart

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective Safeguard Can Restart Every Two Coordinate Attempts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-coordinate example showing systematic objective-triggered momentum resets without an epoch-productivity certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=\tfrac12x^2\) and consider the one-coordinate inertial recurrence \(y_k=x_k+\beta(x_k-x_{k-1})\), \(\widetilde x_{k+1}=y_k-\tfrac32\nabla F(y_k)=-\tfrac12y_k\), with \(\beta>1/3\). At each restart set \(x_{-1}=x_0=a\neq0\). The first candidate is \(x_1=-a/2\) and decreases the objective. The second candidate is \[\widetilde x_2=\left(\tfrac14+\tfrac34\beta\right)a,\] whose magnitude exceeds \(|x_1|=|a|/2\). An objective safeguard therefore rejects the second candidate and restarts. Reapplying the same policy repeats this pattern after every accepted first step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even on a one-dimensional strongly convex quadratic, an objective safeguard can repeatedly reject the second inertial coordinate candidate and reset momentum.
assumptions_latex: The gradient step length is \(3/2\).
The momentum parameter satisfies \(\beta>1/3\).
Rejected candidates are rolled back and all momentum state is reset at the current accepted point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(\widetilde x_2)>F(x_1)\quad\text{in every reset epoch, so the safeguard restarts after each second attempt}.
review_flags: The safeguarded sequence still converges in this example; the claim demonstrates systematic over-restart, not divergence.
The example uses a particular inertial recurrence and does not establish a lower bound for every adaptive restart rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Safeguard Can Restart Every Two Coordinate Attempts
Adaptive Coordinate Restart
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Observable restart rule for accelerated coordinate iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Run an accelerated coordinate method in epochs. At epoch start \(r\), set the momentum state to the current point: \(y^{r,0}=x^{r,0}\). After each coordinate update producing \(x^{r,k+1}\) and extrapolated point \(y^{r,k+1}\), restart whenever \[\langle y^{r,k}-x^{r,k+1},\,x^{r,k+1}-x^{r,k}\rangle>0\] or whenever an accepted objective evaluation satisfies \(F(x^{r,k+1})>F(x^{r,k})\). On restart, set \(x^{r+1,0}=x^{r,k+1}\), reset momentum, and begin a new epoch; otherwise continue the accelerated recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reset coordinate-method momentum when an observable direction test signals misalignment or when an accepted step increases the objective.
assumptions_latex: The accelerated scheme exposes current, previous, and extrapolated iterates.
Objective-based restarts are used only when comparable objective values are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each triggered restart preserves the current point while eliminating accumulated momentum.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Length Restart Complexity Under Quadratic Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A parameter-calibrated scheduled-restart bound, not an adaptive coordinate-restart result.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under an epoch bound \(F(x_K)-F_\star\le C\operatorname{dist}(z,X_\star)^2/K^2\) and quadratic growth with constant \(\mu>0\), choosing \(K\ge\lceil\sqrt{2C/(\mu q)}\rceil\) gives a per-epoch contraction at most \(q\in(0,1)\) and a corresponding geometric update bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Known quadratic-growth calibration turns fixed-length restart epochs into a geometric rate, but it is not an adaptive or parameter-free restart policy.
assumptions_latex: The accelerated epoch bound holds from every retained epoch start.
Quadratic growth holds with a known constant \(\mu>0\).
Every epoch has a fixed length calibrated from \(\mu\).

notation.meaning: Fixed coordinate-update count per restart epoch.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Length Restart Complexity Under Quadratic Growth

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns coordinate-specific observable momentum-reset policies and conditional consequences of genuinely productive restart epochs. The proposed fixed-length bound was deferred because it is calibrated from known quadratic growth and does not analyze adaptive restart. Scaling, sampling refresh, generic restart mechanics, and the underlying accelerated recurrence were excluded. Parameter-free trigger validation, a contraction certificate, complexity, and an over-restart example remain missing.

children.title: Parameter-Free Coordinate Calibration
children.top_down_role: Coordinate policies operating without prespecified curvature, growth, or delay constants.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: When geometric block validation need not terminate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If no finite curvature value majorizes the selected block along the backtracking trials, geometric growth of \(M_i\) has no finite acceptance guarantee. Accepting a trial that fails the model test also removes its certified descent inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameter-free block backtracking is finite only when a finite valid local model exists.
assumptions_latex: Acceptance is based on block quadratic majorization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \neg\exists L_i<\infty\text{ valid on the trials}\Rightarrow\text{finite acceptance is not guaranteed}

Parameter-Free Coordinate Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate step calibration without supplied block smoothness constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize positive block curvatures \(M_i^0>0\), factor \(\gamma>1\), and iteration \(k=0\). After selecting block \(i_k\), repeatedly compute \(d_{i_k}\) as the minimizer of the current block quadratic model with curvature \(M_{i_k}^k\); if the trial fails the local-model validation inequality, set \(M_{i_k}^k\leftarrow\gamma M_{i_k}^k\) and retry. Accept the first valid trial, optionally set \(M_{i_k}^{k+1}=M_{i_k}^k/\gamma\) for the next search, leave unselected curvatures unchanged, and stop by a prescribed observable criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Learn each block curvature online by rejecting invalid quadratic-model steps and geometrically increasing its estimate until validation succeeds.
assumptions_latex: Each selected block has a finite local Lipschitz-gradient bound along its backtracking trials.
Every block-model subproblem has a computable minimizer.
The stopping rule uses observable iterates or objective values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted step requires no supplied block Lipschitz constant and carries forward a data-derived curvature estimate.

children.title: Prior-Information Independence
children.top_down_role: Regimes distinguished by which problem or execution constants need not be supplied in advance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter-free status relative to a declared set of unavailable constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a declared set \(S\) of problem or execution constants, a coordinate policy is \(S\)-prior-independent when every action is generated from public inputs, the observed transcript, and internal randomness without receiving any element of \(S\). Independence is relative: a policy may exclude coordinate curvatures while using a delay bound, horizon, target accuracy, or growth constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordinate policy is parameter-free only relative to an explicit list of constants it is not given.
assumptions_latex: Public inputs and the observed transcript are specified.
The unavailable set \(S\) is declared.
knowledge_statements.title: Relative Prior-Information Independence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Implementation Independence Does Not Remove Parameter Dependence from Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes policy inputs from constants appearing only in analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A policy that never receives \(\theta\) may satisfy \(R_T\le B(T,\theta)\). Conversely, inserting a bound on \(\theta\) into a stepsize, distribution, restart period, or stopping rule makes the implementation dependent on that information even if \(\theta\) is not queried during execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parameter-free implementation may have parameter-dependent performance, while offline tuning by that parameter violates independence.
assumptions_latex: Algorithmic inputs are distinguished from quantities used only in analysis.
knowledge_statements.title: Implementation Independence Does Not Remove Parameter Dependence from Bounds
Prior-Information Independence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information condition for adaptive, possibly randomized coordinate-selection policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta\) denote problem parameters unavailable to the algorithm, \(H_k\) the observed history before iteration \(k\), and \(A_k\) the selected block and associated control parameters. A policy is prior-information independent with respect to \(\Theta\) when its stochastic kernel satisfies \[\mathbb P(A_k\in E\mid H_k=h,\Theta=\theta)=\mathbb P(A_k\in E\mid H_k=h,\Theta=\theta')\] for every iteration \(k\), measurable action set \(E\), feasible observed history \(h\), and parameters \(\theta,\theta'\) compatible with \(h\). Thus the policy may adapt to revealed oracle values and internal randomness, but not directly to unrevealed constants in \(\Theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given the same observed history, the policy has the same action distribution for every compatible value of each unavailable problem parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(H_k\) contains exactly the information revealed to the policy before iteration \(k\).
The compared parameter values \(\theta,\theta'\) can both produce the history \(h\).

notation.meaning: observed algorithmic history before iteration k
selected block together with policy controls

children.title: Partial-Oracle Complexity
children.top_down_role: Counts of coordinate-specific information requests made during optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Oracle Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts selected-block oracle evaluations needed to reach a prescribed expected accuracy when each iteration makes one such call.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the iterate space, let \(G:X\to[0,\infty)\) be the declared accuracy measure, and suppose iteration \(k\) makes exactly one call to the partial oracle \(\mathcal O_{i_k}(x^k)\). For \(\varepsilon>0\), assume that the set \(\{K\in\mathbb N_0:\mathbb E[G(x^K)]\le\varepsilon\}\) is nonempty and define \[N_{\mathrm{po}}(\varepsilon)=\min\{K\in\mathbb N_0:\mathbb E[G(x^K)]\le\varepsilon\}.\] If \(\mathbb E[G(x^K)]\le\Phi(K)\) for every \(K\in\mathbb N_0\), where \(\Phi:\mathbb N_0\to[0,\infty)\) is nonincreasing, then \[N_{\mathrm{po}}(\varepsilon)\le\min\{K\in\mathbb N_0:\Phi(K)\le\varepsilon\}\] whenever the set on the right is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When every iteration makes exactly one selected-block oracle call, partial-oracle complexity equals the first iteration count attaining the expected accuracy, and an iteration convergence bound gives the same call bound.
assumptions_latex: \(G:X\to[0,\infty)\) is the declared accuracy measure.
Each completed iteration makes exactly one partial-oracle call.
The requested accuracy is attainable for the definition, and the displayed bound is used only when its right-hand minimum exists.

notation.meaning: oracle information restricted to block i
partial-oracle calls needed for expected accuracy epsilon
