knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial-oracle call complexity when an iteration may request several selected blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_k\in\mathbb N_0\) be the number of partial-oracle calls made during iteration \(k\), including repeated calls, and set \(C_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}Q_k\). For \(G:X\to[0,\infty)\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), define \[N_{\mathrm{po}}^{\mathrm{batch}}(\varepsilon)=\inf\{\mathbb E[C_K]:K\in\mathbb N_0,\ \mathbb E[G(x^K)]\le\varepsilon\}.\] If \(q_-\le Q_k\le q_+\) almost surely for every \(k\), and \(K_\varepsilon=\min\{K:\mathbb E[G(x^K)]\le\varepsilon\}\) exists, then \[q_-K_\varepsilon\le N_{\mathrm{po}}^{\mathrm{batch}}(\varepsilon)\le q_+K_\varepsilon.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For batched iterations, partial-oracle complexity counts every selected-block request; uniform per-iteration call bounds convert first-attainment iteration complexity into call complexity.
assumptions_latex: \(Q_k\) counts every partial-oracle call, including repeated calls to the same block.
The declared expected-accuracy target is attained.
The two-sided bound assumes uniform almost-sure limits \(q_-\le Q_k\le q_+\).

children.title: Block-Update Complexity
children.top_down_role: Counts of selected coordinate or block updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Update Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts expected committed block changes rather than oracle calls or nominal full-vector iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the iterate space, let the block partition contain \(m<\infty\) blocks, and let \(U_k\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\) be the possibly random set of blocks committed at iteration \(k\). Define \(B_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}|U_k|\) for \(K\in\mathbb N_0\). For \(G:X\to[0,\infty)\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), define \[N_{\mathrm{bu}}(\varepsilon)=\inf\{\mathbb E[B_K]:K\in\mathbb N_0,\ \mathbb E[G(x^K)]\le\varepsilon\}.\] If \(|U_k|=b\) almost surely for every \(k\) and \(\mathbb E[G(x^K)]\le\Phi(K)\), then \[N_{\mathrm{bu}}(\varepsilon)\le b\min\{K\in\mathbb N_0:\Phi(K)\le\varepsilon\}\] whenever the minimum on the right exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block-update complexity is the least expected number of committed block changes sufficient for the target expected accuracy; with exactly b committed blocks per iteration, it is at most b times the iteration bound.
assumptions_latex: The block partition contains \(m<\infty\) blocks.
An update is counted only when its block state is committed.
The right-hand minimum in the fixed-batch bound is nonempty.

notation.meaning: possibly random set of blocks committed at iteration k
cumulative number of committed block updates
expected block-update complexity at accuracy epsilon

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates iteration complexity to committed-update complexity when batch cardinality is uniformly bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}|U_k|\), and suppose integers \(1\le b_-\le b_+\) satisfy \(b_-\le |U_k|\le b_+\) almost surely for every \(k\). If \[K_\varepsilon=\min\{K\in\mathbb N_0:\mathbb E[G(x^K)]\le\varepsilon\}\] exists, then the seed-defined block-update complexity satisfies \[b_-K_\varepsilon\le N_{\mathrm{bu}}(\varepsilon)\le b_+K_\varepsilon.\]

The first iteration attaining the declared expected accuracy exists.

children.title: Oracle-to-Update Cost Conversion
children.top_down_role: Relationships between partial information requests and completed block updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-to-Update Cost Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converts separate oracle-call and block-update counts into a common weighted work measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\in\mathbb N\) be the number of blocks. For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), suppose a run performs \(N_i^{\mathrm{po}},N_i^{\mathrm{bu}}\in\mathbb N_0\) partial-oracle calls and committed block updates, with fixed costs \(c_i^{\mathrm{po}},c_i^{\mathrm{bu}}\in[0,\infty)\). Under additive accounting, the modeled work is \[W=\sum_{i=1}^m\left(c_i^{\mathrm{po}}N_i^{\mathrm{po}}+c_i^{\mathrm{bu}}N_i^{\mathrm{bu}}\right).\] If, for every block \(i\), each committed update corresponds to exactly \(q_i\in\mathbb N_0\) calls to the same partial oracle, then \(N_i^{\mathrm{po}}=q_iN_i^{\mathrm{bu}}\) and \[W=\sum_{i=1}^m\left(q_ic_i^{\mathrm{po}}+c_i^{\mathrm{bu}}\right)N_i^{\mathrm{bu}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed nonnegative per-block costs convert oracle-call and update counts into total modeled work; an integer calls-per-update ratio gives an update-only expression.
assumptions_latex: \(m\in\mathbb N\) is finite.
Per-event costs are nonnegative, additive, and fixed over the modeled run.
Every counted event is assigned to exactly one block.

notation.meaning: number of partial-oracle calls for block i
number of committed updates of block i

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lower and upper bounds on calls per committed update yield corresponding two-sided bounds on weighted work.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Arithmetic Work
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar-operation accounting for computations attributable to selected coordinates or blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a set \(\mathcal P\) of counted scalar arithmetic primitives, such as addition, multiplication, division, and comparison. If iteration \(k\) selects block \(i_k\), let \(a_k(p)\) be the number of executions of primitive \(p\in\mathcal P\) used to form and apply that coordinate update. The coordinate arithmetic work through \(K\) iterations is \[W_{\mathrm{arith}}(K)=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}a_k(p).\] Oracle-internal work, communication, memory transfers, and state-maintenance operations are excluded unless their arithmetic primitives are explicitly included in \(\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate arithmetic work is the total number of declared scalar operations used to compute and apply the selected block updates.
assumptions_latex: The counted primitive set \(\mathcal P\) is fixed before comparing algorithms.
Each primitive execution is assigned to at most one accounting category.

knowledge_statements.title: Block Subproblem Work
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operation count for solving the local optimization problem associated with each selected block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be the iterate space and \(V_i\) the step space for block \(i\). For \(x\in X\), let \(D_i(x)\subseteq V_i\) be nonempty and let \(q_i(\cdot;x):D_i(x)\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) have finite infimum. Fix a deterministic inner solver and a primitive-operation convention. For \(\delta\ge0\), let \(C_i(x,\delta)\in\mathbb N_0\) be the operations used when that solver returns \(d\in D_i(x)\) satisfying \[q_i(d;x)-\inf_{z\in D_i(x)}q_i(z;x)\le\delta.\] For \(K\in\mathbb N_0\), if blocks \(i_0,\ldots,i_{K-1}\) are processed at iterates \(x^0,\ldots,x^{K-1}\) with tolerances \(\delta_0,\ldots,\delta_{K-1}\), define \[W_{\mathrm{sub}}(K)=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}C_{i_k}(x^k,\delta_k).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block-subproblem work totals the declared primitive operations used by a fixed inner solver to attain the specified local-model tolerances.
assumptions_latex: Each \(D_i(x)\subseteq V_i\) is nonempty and the local model has finite infimum on it.
The deterministic inner solver returns a point meeting the declared tolerance.
The solver and primitive-operation convention are fixed.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Maintenance Overhead
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work spent maintaining auxiliary algorithmic state outside the primary block computation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_k\) be auxiliary state immediately before coordinate step \(k\), including any residual cache, sampling table, priority structure, counters, or restart statistics. If \(M_k\) is the number of declared primitive operations and memory actions required to transform \(S_k\) into \(S_{k+1}\) after processing block \(i_k\), then state-maintenance overhead through \(K\) steps is \[W_{\mathrm{state}}(K)=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}M_k.\] Work used to evaluate the partial oracle or solve the block subproblem is excluded, preventing double counting with those categories.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State-maintenance overhead totals the work used to update auxiliary caches, samplers, priorities, counters, and restart statistics.

children.title: Coordinate Memory Traffic
children.top_down_role: Data movement generated by coordinate access and state modification.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Memory Traffic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Data movement caused by coordinate updates across a specified memory boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix two adjacent memory levels and a transfer unit of \(L\) bytes. For coordinate step \(k\), let \(r_k\) and \(w_k\) be the numbers of transfer units read across and written across that boundary, counting cache-line write allocation according to the declared machine model. Coordinate memory traffic through \(K\) steps is \[Q_{\mathrm{mem}}(K)=L\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}(r_k+w_k)\quad\text{bytes}.\] The boundary, cache policy, and treatment of prefetched or shared transfers must remain fixed when comparing implementations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate memory traffic is the total data read and written across a declared memory-level boundary by coordinate updates.

Every crossing is classified consistently as a read or write transfer.

children.title: Cache Locality
children.top_down_role: Spatial and temporal locality behavior of coordinate-update workloads.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reference-order example separating arithmetic work from locality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an initially empty fully associative LRU cache hold \(C\) lines and let \(a_0,\ldots,a_C\) be distinct. Repeating \((a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_C)^R\) makes every reference a miss, whereas \(a_0^R,a_1^R,\ldots,a_C^R\) makes the same number of references to each line but incurs only \(C+1\) misses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cycling over one more line than capacity thrashes, while grouping equal accesses yields only cold misses.
assumptions_latex: The cache is initially empty, fully associative, and LRU.
knowledge_statements.title: Schedule-Induced Cache Thrashing

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Associativity Boundary of Global Reuse Distance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit of fully associative locality predictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a set-associative or direct-mapped cache, a global reuse distance below total capacity does not guarantee a hit: lines mapping to the same undersized set can evict one another. Exact prediction then requires set mapping and per-set associativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global reuse distance does not capture conflict misses in set-associative caches.
assumptions_latex: The hardware cache is not fully associative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D_t<C\not\Rightarrow\text{cache hit under arbitrary set mapping}
knowledge_statements.title: Associativity Boundary of Global Reuse Distance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacity-miss guarantee for a fixed cache-line working set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a fully associative LRU cache of capacity \(C\), consider an interval referencing only a fixed set \(W\) with \(|W|\le C\). After each line of \(W\) has been loaded, every remaining reference in the interval is a hit, so the interval incurs at most \(|W|\) misses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A phase whose cache-line working set fits in a fully associative cache has no capacity misses after warm-up.
assumptions_latex: The cache is fully associative and uses LRU replacement.
No reference outside \(W\) occurs in the interval.
knowledge_statements.title: Working-Set Capacity Locality
Cache Locality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reuse-distance characterization under a fully associative least-recently-used cache model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a fully associative cache holding \(C\) cache lines and using least-recently-used replacement. For the coordinate-update reference sequence \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_T\), define the reuse distance \(D_t\) as the number of distinct lines referenced after the preceding reference to \(\ell_t\) and before time \(t\), with \(D_t=\infty\) for a first reference. Then reference \(t\) is a cache hit exactly when \(D_t<C\), and the miss count is \[M_T=\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbf 1\{D_t\ge C\}.\] Consequently, coordinate schedules that reduce reuse distances below \(C\) improve locality in this model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a fully associative LRU cache, an access hits exactly when fewer than C distinct cache lines have intervened since its previous access.
assumptions_latex: The cache is fully associative with least-recently-used replacement.
The sequence \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_T\) records cache-line addresses.

notation.meaning: number of cache misses in T references

children.title: Sparse-Access Costs
children.top_down_role: Memory-system costs associated with irregular sparse coordinate access.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work and stored-word touches for traversing selected columns in compressed sparse column storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\) be stored in compressed sparse column format, let \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\), and define \(s_B=\sum_{j\in B}\operatorname{nnz}(A_{:j})\). Reading the column-pointer interval for every \(j\in B\) and processing each represented entry once uses \(\Theta(|B|+s_B)\) primitive work and touches \(\Theta(|B|+s_B)\) stored words under a constant-work-per-entry convention. Realized cache-line or memory-boundary traffic is not determined by this count and depends on layout and cache state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Traversing selected CSC columns costs linear work and stored-word touches in the number of selected columns plus their represented nonzeros; actual memory traffic remains machine dependent.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is stored in valid compressed sparse column form.
Each selected column pointer interval is read and each represented entry is processed once.
Processing one represented entry requires bounded primitive work.

knowledge_statements.title: Compressed-Orientation Sparse Access

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of output-sensitive sparse access when a request is misaligned with the compressed orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A compressed sparse representation provides direct pointer intervals only in its compressed orientation. Thus CSC supports output-sensitive traversal of selected columns, but a direct scan answering a selected-row request without a row-oriented auxiliary index may examine every stored entry and costs \(\Theta(d+\operatorname{nnz}(A))\) in the worst case. Maintaining a CSR copy or another row index changes the access bound but incurs additional storage and maintenance cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CSC gives direct sparse access to columns, not rows; without a row index, direct row access can require scanning the entire representation.
assumptions_latex: Only the CSC representation and its column pointers are used for the direct-scan row request.
No row-oriented auxiliary index is available.
Each stored entry inspection has bounded cost.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work and traffic for accessing a block stored in compressed sparse form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times d}\) be stored by compressed columns, and let \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\) be the selected coordinate block. Write \(s_B=\sum_{j\in B}\operatorname{nnz}(A_{:j})\). A direct scan of the selected columns, including their values and row indices, uses \[W_B=\Theta(s_B+|B|)\] primitive operations and transfers \(Q_B=\Theta(s_B+|B|)\) stored words when the required entries are not already cached. children.title: Coordinate Communication Cost

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Communication Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Latency-bandwidth representation of communication charged to parallel coordinate updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\in\mathbb N_0\) be the number of communication rounds. For each \(r\in\{1,\ldots,R\}\), let \(m_r,w_r\in\mathbb N_0\) be the numbers of critical-path messages and transmitted machine words attributed to coordinate coordination. Given a message-startup charge \(\alpha\ge0\) and a per-word charge \(\beta\ge0\), define the latency-bandwidth communication cost by \[T_{\mathrm{comm}}^{\mathrm{model}}=\sum_{r=1}^R(\alpha m_r+\beta w_r).\] Reductions, broadcasts, and ownership transfers required to commit coordinate updates contribute to \(m_r\) and \(w_r\); purely local reads and arithmetic do not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The latency-bandwidth model charges each critical-path message by alpha and each transmitted word by beta across all coordinate-coordination rounds.
assumptions_latex: \(m_r\) and \(w_r\) count only communication assigned to the critical path of round \(r\).
The adopted model uses fixed additive charges \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\).

notation.meaning: modeled charge per transmitted machine word
critical-path messages and transmitted words in round r

children.title: Synchronization Cost
children.top_down_role: Coordination overhead associated with barriers, locks, or update ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronization Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical-path overhead exposed by mandatory barriers and per-round worker imbalance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p\in\mathbb N\) workers execute \(R\in\mathbb N_0\) synchronized coordinate-update rounds. For \(r\in\{1,\ldots,R\}\) and \(j\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\), let \(t_{rj}\ge0\) be worker \(j\)'s local computation time before the barrier ending round \(r\), and let \(\sigma_r\ge0\) be the barrier or commit latency after all workers arrive. With \(\bar t_r=p^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^p t_{rj}\), define the synchronization cost relative to ideal per-round balanced computation by \[T_{\mathrm{sync}}=\sum_{r=1}^R\left(\max_{1\le j\le p}t_{rj}-\bar t_r+\sigma_r\right).\] The corresponding synchronized elapsed time is \[\sum_{r=1}^R\bar t_r+T_{\mathrm{sync}}=\sum_{r=1}^R\left(\max_{1\le j\le p}t_{rj}+\sigma_r\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronization cost is the sum of each round's slow-worker imbalance relative to average local work plus its barrier or commit latency.
assumptions_latex: Every worker must finish its local work before the associated barrier releases.
The local times \(t_{rj}\) exclude the barrier latency \(\sigma_r\).
The baseline is ideal per-round balanced computation with duration \(\bar t_r\).

notation.meaning: local computation time of worker j in round r
mean local computation time in round r
barrier or commit latency in round r
synchronization overhead relative to ideal balanced computation

children.title: Wall-Clock Performance
children.top_down_role: Elapsed execution behavior combining computation, coordination, and load imbalance.

assumptions_latex: \(P,K\in\mathbb{N}\), \(c_{k,r},m_k,s_k\ge 0\), and \(T_{\mathrm{wall}}(K)>0\).
Computation, communication, and synchronization do not overlap.

notation.meaning: iteration-k computation time assigned to worker r
communication and synchronization times at iteration k
total serial computational work and realized speedup

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical-path cost model for synchronous parallel block-coordinate iterations.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(K\) synchronous iterations are executed by \(P\) workers. Iteration \(k\) assigns work of duration \(c_{k,r}\) to worker \(r\in\{1,\ldots,P\}\), incurs communication time \(m_k\), and incurs synchronization time \(s_k\). With no overlap between these phases, the wall-clock time is
\[T_{\mathrm{wall}}(K)=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\left(\max_{1\le r\le P}c_{k,r}+m_k+s_k\right).\]
Define the corresponding serial computational work by \(C_K=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}\sum_{r=1}^P c_{k,r}\). When \(T_{\mathrm{wall}}(K)>0\), the realized speedup is \(S_K=C_K/T_{\mathrm{wall}}(K)\). Thus an iteration-count improvement alone does not imply a wall-clock improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under this synchronous no-overlap model, elapsed time is the sum of critical-worker computation, communication, and synchronization. When elapsed time is positive, realized speedup compares the corresponding serial computational work with that elapsed time.
knowledge_statements.title: Wall-Clock Performance

source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Critical-path elapsed time required to attain a declared expected-accuracy target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_{\mathrm{wall}}:\mathbb N_0\to[0,\infty)\) be nondecreasing, let \(G:X\to[0,\infty)\), and suppose \(\{K\in\mathbb N_0:\mathbb E[G(x^K)]\le\varepsilon\}\neq\varnothing\). Define \[K_\varepsilon=\min\{K\in\mathbb N_0:\mathbb E[G(x^K)]\le\varepsilon\},\qquad T_\varepsilon=T_{\mathrm{wall}}(K_\varepsilon).\] Methods evaluated under the same accuracy criterion are compared by \(T_\varepsilon\), not solely by \(K_\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Wall-clock time to expected accuracy is the elapsed critical-path time at the first completed iteration attaining the declared expected-error target.
assumptions_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{wall}}(K)\) is nondecreasing in \(K\).
The declared expected-accuracy target is attained.

children.title: Parallel Load-Balance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Execution regimes distinguished by distribution of coordinate work across workers.

assumptions_latex: For each \(P\ge1\), \(\mathcal K_P\subseteq\mathbb N_0\) is nonempty and \(\sum_{r=1}^P c_{k,r}^{(P)}>0\) for every \(k\in\mathcal K_P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(1\le\rho_k^{(P)}\le P\); uniform balance means \(\sup_{P\ge1}R_P<\infty\), asymptotic imbalance means \(\sup_{P\ge1}R_P=\infty\), and \(\rho_k^{(P)}=P\) exactly characterizes concentration of all positive work on one worker.

notation.meaning: load assigned to worker r at iteration k in the P-worker system
worst imbalance in the P-worker member of the family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classification by critical-worker load relative to average assigned work across a family of worker counts.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.4 The Case of a Product Constraint Set: Parallel Implementations p. 217

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each worker count \(P\ge1\), let \(c_{k,1}^{(P)},\ldots,c_{k,P}^{(P)}\ge0\) be the worker loads at iteration \(k\in\mathcal K_P\), where \(\mathcal K_P\) is nonempty and the mean \(\bar c_k^{(P)}=P^{-1}\sum_{r=1}^P c_{k,r}^{(P)}\) is positive. Define
\[\rho_k^{(P)}=\frac{\max_{1\le r\le P}c_{k,r}^{(P)}}{\bar c_k^{(P)}}\in[1,P],\qquad R_P=\sup_{k\in\mathcal K_P}\rho_k^{(P)}.\]
The family is uniformly load-balanced when \(\sup_{P\ge1}R_P<\infty\), and asymptotically imbalanced when \(\sup_{P\ge1}R_P=\infty\). At a particular iteration, \(\rho_k^{(P)}=P\) if and only if all positive work is assigned to one worker.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each worker count, imbalance is maximum worker load divided by average load. A family is uniformly balanced when its worst factor is bounded independently of worker count, and asymptotically imbalanced when those factors are unbounded. Factor P means that one worker carries all positive work.

children.title: Coordinatewise Optimality Failures
children.top_down_role: Regimes where blockwise improvement does not imply the desired full-space conclusion.

children.title: Nonsmooth Nonseparable Stalling
children.top_down_role: Coordinatewise traps caused by coupled nonsmooth geometry.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Differentiability or Block Separability Restores the Coordinatewise Implication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary showing why coupled nonsmooth geometry is essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For unconstrained convex minimization, if \(f\) is differentiable at a coordinatewise minimum \(x\), every block gradient vanishes; hence \(\nabla f(x)=0\) and \(x\) is globally optimal. Likewise, on a product feasible set, if \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\) and each \(x_i\) globally minimizes its block term over \(X_i\), then \(x\) is globally optimal. Thus the convex nonglobal-stalling pathology requires a formulation outside these sufficient regimes, such as coupled nonsmooth geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Differentiability in the unconstrained convex case, or genuine block separability, makes coordinatewise minimality sufficient for global optimality.
assumptions_latex: The differentiable case is unconstrained and convex.
In the separable case, X=\prod_i X_i, f(x)=\sum_i f_i(x_i), and every block value globally minimizes its term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{coordinatewise minimum}+\bigl(\text{differentiable unconstrained convex or block-separable convex}\bigr)\Longrightarrow\text{global minimum}.
knowledge_statements.title: Differentiability or Block Separability Restores the Coordinatewise Implication

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subdifferential representation of coordinatewise stalling for coupled convex nonsmooth objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) be proper convex and finite near \(x\in\mathbb R^{n_1}\times\cdots\times\mathbb R^{n_m}\). Coordinatewise minimality is equivalent to \(0\in\partial f_i(\,\cdot\,;x_{-i})(x_i)\) for every one-block slice, whereas full-space optimality is equivalent to \(0\in\partial f(x)\). For a coupled nonsmooth function, the blockwise zero conditions may be witnessed by different ambient supporting subgradients and therefore need not yield one common zero vector in \(\partial f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each block slice may admit a zero partial subgradient even though the full subdifferential contains no common zero.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is proper, convex, and finite on a neighborhood of }x.

notation.meaning: subdifferential of the one-block slice at its current block value

knowledge_statements.title: Incompatible Partial Subgradients
Nonsmooth Nonseparable Stalling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex coupled nonsmooth objective with a nonglobal coordinatewise minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[-1,1]^2\) and define \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) by \(f(x,y)=\max\{x,y\}\). At \((0,0)\), each one-coordinate slice is minimized without moving: for every \(t\in[-1,1]\), \(f(t,0)=\max\{t,0\}\ge 0\) and \(f(0,t)=\max\{0,t\}\ge 0\). Hence \((0,0)\) is coordinatewise optimal, and exact block minimization may retain it under a stay-put tie rule. Nevertheless, \(f(-1,-1)=-1<0=f(0,0)\), so this stalled point is not globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex function max(x,y) can stall at the origin under one-coordinate minimization, although moving both coordinates to −1 strictly improves the objective.
assumptions_latex: The two scalar coordinates are updated one at a time by exact slice minimization.
When the current coordinate value is a slice minimizer, the tie rule may retain it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((0,0)\) is coordinatewise optimal but not globally optimal for \(f(x,y)=\max\{x,y\}\) on \([-1,1]^2\).

children.title: Cycling with Nonunique Block Solutions
children.top_down_role: Unstable iterate behavior under ambiguous block minimizers.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cycle of Set-Valued Exact Block Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formalization of cycling generated by nonunique exact block solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For blocks \(1,\ldots,m\), let \(T_i(x)\) be the set of points obtained by globally minimizing over block \(i\) while fixing all other blocks. A cyclic exact-minimization trajectory selects \(x^{k,i}\in T_i(x^{k,i-1})\), with \(x^{k,0}=x^k\) and \(x^{k+1}=x^{k,m}\). It has a nontrivial completed-sweep cycle of period \(q\ge2\) when \(x^{k+q}=x^k\) for every \(k\) and the \(q\) sweep iterates are not all equal. Nonunique visited subproblems make the corresponding \(T_i\) set-valued, permitting—but not guaranteeing—a cycling selection rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cycling is periodic motion of the completed-sweep iterates of a set-valued exact block-minimization map.
assumptions_latex: Every visited block subproblem attains a global minimizer.
Updates follow a fixed cyclic block order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Nonunique visited block minimizers can make the sweep map set-valued and permit a nontrivial periodic selection.}

notation.meaning: set-valued exact-minimization update for block i

knowledge_statements.title: Cycle of Set-Valued Exact Block Minimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating ambiguity-driven cycles from other cycling mechanisms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every visited exact block subproblem has a unique minimizer. If an update changes its block, the objective decreases strictly; if it does not change the block, the point is unchanged. Consequently, a cyclic exact block-minimization trajectory cannot contain a nontrivial finite cycle. A cycle caused solely by alternating choices among exact block minimizers therefore requires nonuniqueness at some visited subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unique exact block minimizers exclude nontrivial finite cycles caused by tie selection.
assumptions_latex: Each visited block subproblem has a unique attained global minimizer.
Every update selects that exact minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Unique exact block minimizers}\Longrightarrow\text{no nontrivial finite completed-sweep cycle}.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniqueness Excludes Tie-Induced Finite Cycles
Cycling with Nonunique Block Solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvergence of iterates caused solely by unrestricted minimizer selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[-1,1]^2\) and \(f(x,y)=0\) on \(X\). Every feasible value is an exact minimizer of either coordinate subproblem. Starting from \((x^0,y^0)=(1,1)\), use cyclic exact block minimization and the admissible tie rules \(x^{k+1}=-x^k\) on the first block and \(y^{k+1}=-y^k\) on the second block. At completed sweeps the iterates alternate between \((1,1)\) and \((-1,-1)\). Thus objective values are constant and optimal, but the iterate sequence cycles because block solutions are nonunique and selection is uncontrolled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even exact cyclic minimization can produce a nonconvergent iterate cycle when every block subproblem has multiple minimizers and the tie rule alternates selections.
assumptions_latex: Block subproblems permit arbitrary selection among exact minimizers.
The two coordinates are updated in fixed cyclic order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The completed-sweep sequence is a two-cycle although every update exactly minimizes its block subproblem.

children.title: Nonconvex Coordinatewise Traps
children.top_down_role: Coordinate-stationary points with inadequate full-space stationarity properties.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates global block-slice minimality from full-space local minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a product set \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_m\), a point \(x\in X\) is a coordinatewise minimum of \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) when, for every block \(i\), \[f(x)\le f(x_1,\ldots,x_{i-1},z_i,x_{i+1},\ldots,x_m)\qquad\forall z_i\in X_i.\] In a nonconvex problem this need not imply full-space local minimality because descent may require simultaneous changes in several blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordinatewise minimum globally minimizes every one-block slice but may still admit a coupled descent direction in a nonconvex problem.
assumptions_latex: X\text{ has the stated Cartesian-product block structure}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{coordinatewise minimum}\not\Rightarrow\text{full-space local minimum in general nonconvex problems}.

notation.meaning: alternative feasible value of block i

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Diagonal Block Curvature Does Not Detect Coupled Negative Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order geometry underlying smooth coordinatewise traps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) be twice differentiable near an interior coordinatewise local minimum \(x\). Then \(
abla_i f(x)=0\) and \(
abla^2_{ii}f(x)\succeq0\) for every block \(i\), but these diagonal-block conditions do not imply \(
abla^2 f(x)\succeq0\). Off-diagonal Hessian blocks can produce a direction \(d\) satisfying \(d^	op
abla^2 f(x)d<0\), so the point can be a saddle despite minimizing along each block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative curvature in every individual block does not rule out negative curvature in a coupled direction.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is twice differentiable near an interior coordinatewise local minimum }x.

notation.meaning: diagonal Hessian block for block i

knowledge_statements.title: Diagonal Block Curvature Does Not Detect Coupled Negative Curvature
Nonconvex Coordinatewise Traps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth nonconvex coordinatewise minimum that is a strict-saddle-type trap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(f:\mathbb{R}^2\to\mathbb{R}\) by \(f(x,y)=xy\). At \((0,0)\), both coordinate restrictions are constant: \(f(t,0)=f(0,t)=0\) for every \(t\in\mathbb{R}\). Consequently, \((0,0)\) is a global minimizer of each one-coordinate subproblem, and a stay-put exact coordinate-minimization rule can remain there indefinitely. However, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), \(f(\varepsilon,-\varepsilon)=-\varepsilon^2<0=f(0,0)\). Hence the coordinatewise minimum is not a local minimum of the full nonconvex problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For f(x,y)=xy, the origin minimizes every coordinate slice but is not a local minimum, since simultaneous opposite-sign perturbations decrease the objective.
assumptions_latex: Coordinates are minimized separately and ties may be resolved by retaining the current value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((0,0)\) is coordinatewise minimizing but fails full-space local optimality.

children.title: Cyclic Worst-Case Slowdown

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cyclic Quadratic Sweeps as Gauss–Seidel Iterations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sweep matrix governing exact cyclic coordinate minimization of a strictly convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx-b^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(Q\succ0\), and write \(Q=D+L+U\), where \(D\) is diagonal and \(L,U=L^{\mathsf T}\) are strictly lower and upper triangular. One exact cyclic coordinate-minimization sweep in the order \(1,\ldots,n\) satisfies \[(D+L)x^{k+1}=b-Ux^k.\] For \(e^k=x^k-Q^{-1}b\), \[e^{k+1}=G_{\rm cyc}e^k,\qquad G_{\rm cyc}=-(D+L)^{-1}U.\] Positive definiteness gives \(\rho(G_{\rm cyc})<1\); slowdown occurs along families for which \(\rho(G_{\rm cyc})\uparrow1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact fixed-order coordinate minimization on a positive-definite quadratic is Gauss–Seidel, with sweep slowdown governed by its spectral radius.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is symmetric positive definite.
Each coordinate is minimized exactly in the fixed order \(1,\ldots,n\).

notation.meaning: diagonal, strictly lower, and strictly upper parts of Q

review_flags: This does not establish a sharp cyclic-versus-randomized worst-case separation.
knowledge_statements.title: Cyclic Quadratic Sweeps as Gauss–Seidel Iterations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of exact quadratic coordinate sweeps on the selected cyclic order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\succ0\), let \(P\) be a permutation matrix, and decompose \(P^{\mathsf T}QP=D_P+L_P+U_P\) into diagonal, strictly lower, and strictly upper parts. Exact coordinate minimization in the order encoded by \(P\) has original-coordinate error matrix \[G_P=-P(D_P+L_P)^{-1}U_PP^{\mathsf T}.\] Different orders generally give different sweep matrices and may have different spectral radii.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing the cyclic order changes the Gauss–Seidel splitting and can change the completed-sweep convergence factor.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is symmetric positive definite.
Every coordinate is minimized exactly once per sweep in the order encoded by \(P\).

notation.meaning: permutation matrix encoding the cyclic order
completed-sweep error matrix for that order

review_flags: This establishes order dependence but not a sharp cyclic-versus-randomized complexity separation.
knowledge_statements.title: Permutation-Dependent Cyclic Sweep Matrix

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Real-Eigenmode Certificate for Cyclic Sweep Slowdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instance-level certificate converting a real cyclic-sweep eigenvalue into an exact lower bound on required sweeps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_P\) be the completed-sweep error matrix for an exact cyclic quadratic coordinate-minimization order. If \(G_Pv=\lambda v\) for a real eigenvector \(v\ne0\) and real eigenvalue \(0<|\lambda|<1\), initialize \(e^0=v\). Then \(e^k=\lambda^kv\), so \(\|e^k\|/\|e^0\|=|\lambda|^k\). Achieving \(\|e^k\|\le\varepsilon\|e^0\|\) requires \[k\ge\left\lceil\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon)}{-\log|\lambda|}\right\rceil.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real eigenvalue near one exactly certifies slow cyclic sweeps when the initial error is aligned with its eigenvector.
assumptions_latex: \(G_P\) is the completed-sweep error matrix of the declared cyclic order.
\(v\ne0\) is a real eigenvector with real eigenvalue \(0<|\lambda|<1\).
The initial error equals \(v\).

notation.meaning: Completed-sweep error matrix for cyclic order P.
Real witness eigenvalue of the cyclic sweep matrix.
Sweeps required for relative error reduction epsilon.

knowledge_statements.title: Real-Eigenmode Certificate for Cyclic Sweep Slowdown

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scalar-Normalization Invariance of Cyclic Quadratic Slowdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive scalar rescaling cannot remove an order-specific cyclic sweep factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx-b^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(Q\succ0\), and let \(G_P\) be the exact cyclic coordinate-minimization error matrix for order \(P\). For any \(c>0\), the rescaled objective \(\widetilde f=cf\) has Hessian \(cQ\), linear term \(cb\), the same minimizer and coordinate updates, and \[\widetilde G_P=G_P.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying an SPD quadratic by a positive scalar leaves exact cyclic coordinate iterates and their slowdown factor unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is symmetric positive definite.
Coordinates are minimized exactly in a fixed order.
The entire objective is multiplied by one scalar \(c>0\).

notation.meaning: Completed-sweep error matrix for order P.

knowledge_statements.title: Scalar-Normalization Invariance of Cyclic Quadratic Slowdown
Cyclic Worst-Case Slowdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic family whose cyclic sweep contraction approaches one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(0<\rho<1\), consider the strongly convex quadratic
\[f_\rho(x,y)=\tfrac12(x^2+2\rho xy+y^2).\]
Exact cyclic minimization in the order \(x\) then \(y\) gives \(x^{k+1}=-\rho y^k\) and \(y^{k+1}=\rho^2y^k\) after sweep \(k\). The completed-sweep iteration matrix therefore has spectral radius \(\rho^2\). As \(\rho\uparrow1\), this contraction factor approaches one, so arbitrarily many sweeps may be required for a fixed reduction. The Hessian condition number is \((1+\rho)/(1-\rho)\), identifying near-coupling singularity as the slowdown boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled two-variable quadratic makes exact cyclic coordinate sweeps contract by rho squared; convergence becomes arbitrarily slow as rho approaches one.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\rho<1\), so the Hessian is positive definite.
Each coordinate is minimized exactly in the fixed order \(x\), then \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sweep contraction has spectral radius \(\rho^2\to1\) as \(\rho\uparrow1\).

children.title: Coverage-Starvation Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Policies that fail to revisit necessary coordinates or blocks.

children.title: Coordinate Starvation
children.top_down_role: Persistent neglect of coordinates or blocks needed for effective progress.

assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\) and one block index \(i_k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is selected at every iteration \(k\in\mathbb N_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Block \(j\) is starved exactly when \(\sup_{k\ge0}w_j(k)=\infty\), equivalently when no finite window length guarantees a visit to \(j\).

notation.meaning: waiting time from iteration k to the next visit to block j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absence of a uniform bound on the delay until the next visit to a coordinate block.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((i_k)_{k\ge0}\) be a block-selection sequence with \(i_k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). For block \(j\), define its waiting time from iteration \(k\) by
\[w_j(k)=\inf\{t\in\mathbb N_0:i_{k+t}=j\},\]
with \(\inf\varnothing=\infty\). Block \(j\) is starved when \(\sup_{k\ge0}w_j(k)=\infty\). Equivalently, no finite \(B\) guarantees a visit to \(j\) in every window \(\{k,k+1,\ldots,k+B-1\}\). This definition includes both eventual abandonment and arbitrarily long inter-visit gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block is starved when the waiting time until its next visit has no uniform finite bound. This includes blocks that are eventually abandoned and blocks whose inter-visit gaps become arbitrarily long.
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate Starvation

source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Independent Positive-Probability Sampling Has Unbounded Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that probabilistic recurrence need not satisfy deterministic bounded-gap nonstarvation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((i_k)_{k\ge0}\) be IID block selections and fix a block \(j\) selected with probability \(p_j\in(0,1)\). Then \(j\) is selected infinitely often almost surely, but for every integer \(B\ge1\) there are almost surely arbitrarily late runs of at least \(B\) consecutive iterations in which \(j\) is not selected. Consequently, \(\sup_k w_j(k)=\infty\) almost surely, so \(j\) is starved under the seed's deterministic bounded-wait definition despite positive sampling probability and infinite visitation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: IID positive-probability sampling visits a block infinitely often but almost surely produces arbitrarily long gaps.
assumptions_latex: (i_k)_{k\ge0}\text{ are IID}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb P\!\left(j\text{ is visited infinitely often and }\sup_k w_j(k)=\infty\right)=1.

notation.meaning: probability of selecting block j at each iteration

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Positive-Probability Sampling Has Unbounded Gaps

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded-Gap Fairness Is Stronger Than Infinite Visitation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fairness hierarchy induced by the seed's starvation definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite block system, \(\sup_k w_j(k)<\infty\) implies that block \(j\) is visited infinitely often. The converse is false: \(j\) may be selected infinitely often while its inter-visit gaps are unbounded, in which case it is starved under the bounded-wait definition. Thus nonstarvation here means bounded-gap, or essentially cyclic, fairness rather than mere recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded waiting guarantees infinitely many visits, but infinitely many visits do not prevent starvation when gaps are unbounded.
assumptions_latex: The block system is finite and w_j(k) is the waiting time defined in the accepted seed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_k w_j(k)<\infty\Longrightarrow j\text{ is visited infinitely often},\qquad\text{but not conversely}.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Gap Fairness Is Stronger Than Infinite Visitation

children.title: Incomplete Visitation Coverage
children.top_down_role: Visitation policies that omit required portions of the coordinate or block system.

assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N\) and \(i_k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) for every \(k\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_\infty\subsetneq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) if and only if some block is never visited.

notation.meaning: set of blocks visited at least once

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection sequence omits at least one block over the entire run.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a block-selection sequence \((i_k)_{k\ge0}\) on \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), define its visitation support by
\[S_\infty=\{j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}: i_k=j\text{ for at least one }k\ge0\}.\]
Visitation coverage is incomplete precisely when \(S_\infty\subsetneq\{1,\ldots,n\}\). Equivalently, there exists a block \(j\) such that \(i_k\ne j\) for every \(k\ge0\). This is stronger than merely having unbounded inter-visit gaps: an omitted block receives no update during the entire run.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coverage is incomplete when at least one block is never selected during the run, a stronger defect than merely infrequent visitation.
knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete Visitation Coverage

children.title: Starvation-Induced Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Progress loss attributable to repeatedly excluded coordinates or blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Starvation-Induced Stagnation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Omitted coordinate prevents convergence on a separable strongly convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^n x_i^2\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and suppose exact coordinate minimization is used but coordinate \(j\) is never selected. Then every selected coordinate is set to zero, whereas \(x_j^k=x_j^0\) for all \(k\). If \(x_j^0\ne0\), after all visited coordinates have been minimized the method stagnates at an objective value at least \(\tfrac12(x_j^0)^2>0\), while the unique minimizer \(x^\star=0\) has value zero. Thus incomplete coverage alone can prevent convergence even for a separable strongly convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If one coordinate of a squared-norm objective is never visited, its nonzero initial value persists and exact updates of all other coordinates cannot reach the minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(n\ge2\), coordinate \(j\) is never selected, and \(x_j^0\ne0\).
Every selected coordinate is minimized exactly.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Separable Objective Stagnation Under Permanent Omission
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General separable-objective obstruction caused by retaining a nonoptimal omitted coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\), where every \(f_i\) has finite infimum. Suppose an iterative coordinate method changes only selected coordinates, coordinate \(j\) is never selected, and \(f_j(x_j^0)>\inf_t f_j(t)\). Then \(x_j^k=x_j^0\) for every \(k\), and
\[f(x^k)-\inf_x f(x)\ge f_j(x_j^0)-\inf_t f_j(t)>0.\]
Consequently, no behavior of the visited coordinates can make the objective values converge to the global infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a separable objective, permanently omitting a coordinate initialized above its component infimum leaves a fixed positive objective gap.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x_i)\) and each component has finite infimum.
Updates alter selected coordinates only.
Coordinate \(j\) is never selected and \(f_j(x_j^0)>\inf_t f_j(t)\).

notation.meaning: objective component associated with coordinate i

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Objective Stagnation Under Permanent Omission

children.title: Importance-Weight Miscalibration
children.top_down_role: Nonuniform sampling priorities that poorly reflect coordinate value or update cost.

assumptions_latex: \(p_i,q_i>0\), \(\sum_{i=1}^n p_i=1\), and \(I\) is sampled according to \(p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[G]=g\) exactly when \(p_i=q_i\) for every coordinate satisfying \(g_i\ne0\), and \(\mathbb E\lVert G\rVert^2=\sum_{i=1}^n p_i g_i^2/q_i^2\).

notation.meaning: actual probability of sampling coordinate i
positive value used in the importance weight for coordinate i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bias and second-moment effects from using weights inconsistent with sampling probabilities.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g=(g_1,\ldots,g_n)\in\mathbb R^n\), sample \(I\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with probabilities \(p_i>0\), and form \(G=(g_I/q_I)e_I\) using weights \(q_i>0\). Then
\[\mathbb E[G]=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{p_i}{q_i}g_i e_i.\]
Consequently, \(G\) is unbiased for \(g\) exactly when \(p_i=q_i\) for every coordinate with \(g_i\ne0\). Moreover,
\[\mathbb E\lVert G\rVert^2=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{p_i g_i^2}{q_i^2}.\]
Thus weights inconsistent with the actual sampling probabilities generally create bias, and small weights can amplify the estimator's second moment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordinate estimator weighted by values different from the probabilities actually sampled is generally biased, and undersized weights can greatly increase its second moment.
knowledge_statements.title: Importance-Weight Miscalibration

children.title: Adaptive-Sampling Staleness
children.top_down_role: Adaptive priorities that cease to represent the evolving optimization state.

assumptions_latex: Conditionally on the iteration-\(k\) history, \(g_i^k\ne0\), \(p_i^k>0\), and \(\sum_{i=1}^n p_i^k=1\).
The importance weight uses the actual conditional sampling probability \(p_i^k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stale-policy second moment is at least \((\sum_{i=1}^n|g_i^k|)^2\), with equality exactly when \(p_i^k=p_i^{\star,k}\) for every \(i\).

notation.meaning: current nonzero coordinate quantity to be estimated
conditional expectation given the iteration-k history

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact second-moment penalty when sampling probabilities use outdated coordinate magnitudes.

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), let \(g_i^k\ne0\) be current coordinate quantities, and conditionally sample \(I_k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with probabilities \(p_i^k>0\) that may have been computed from earlier information. The estimator \(G^k=(g_{I_k}^k/p_{I_k}^k)e_{I_k}\) is conditionally unbiased and satisfies
\[\mathbb E_k\lVert G^k\rVert^2=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{(g_i^k)^2}{p_i^k}.\]
Among all positive probability vectors, the minimum is \((\sum_{i=1}^n|g_i^k|)^2\), attained uniquely at \(p_i^{\star,k}=|g_i^k|/\sum_{j=1}^n|g_j^k|\). Therefore, relative to the current-information optimum, the exact nonnegative second-moment penalty is
\[\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{(g_i^k)^2}{p_i^k}-\left(\sum_{i=1}^n|g_i^k|\right)^2.\]
It is zero when the stale probabilities still equal the current optimum and is positive otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correctly weighted outdated probabilities preserve conditional unbiasedness. Relative to probabilities proportional to the current coordinate magnitudes, they cannot reduce the second moment and increase it unless they still coincide with the current optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Sampling Staleness

source_witnesses.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp multiplicative control, and absence of control, for correctly weighted stale sampling probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(g_i\ne0\), set \(S=\sum_i|g_i|\) and \(p_i^\star=|g_i|/S\), and let \(p\) be a positive sampling distribution. If \(p_i\ge\alpha p_i^\star\) for every \(i\), where \(0<\alpha\le1\), then
\[S^2\le\sum_i\frac{g_i^2}{p_i}\le\frac{1}{\alpha}S^2.\]
Without such ratio control no finite uniform factor exists: for \(g=(1,1)\) and \(p=(\delta,1-\delta)\), the ratio \(\bigl(1/\delta+1/(1-\delta)\bigr)/4\) diverges as \(\delta\downarrow0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every stale probability is at least an alpha fraction of its current optimum, second-moment inflation is at most 1/alpha; without ratio control it is unbounded.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i\ne0\) and \(p_i>0\) for every coordinate.
\(p_i^\star=|g_i|/\sum_j|g_j|\).
For the upper bound, \(p_i\ge\alpha p_i^\star\) with \(0<\alpha\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_i g_i^2/p_i\le\alpha^{-1}(\sum_i|g_i|)^2\), while no uniform factor is possible without probability-ratio control.

notation.meaning: uniform lower ratio between stale and current-optimal probabilities

knowledge_statements.title: Probability-Ratio Control of Staleness Inflation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Wall-clock accounting for constructing, maintaining, and sampling adaptive coordinate distributions.

source_refs.locator: 5.2 Coordinate and extended coordinate-friendly operators p. 117
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider an adaptive method requiring \(K_1\) randomized coordinate updates to meet a prescribed accuracy criterion. At adaptive iteration \(k\), let \(u_k\) be the time to refresh scores or probabilities, \(a_k\) the time to maintain and sample the distribution, and \(c_k\) the selected-coordinate update time. Without overlap, its wall-clock cost is
\[T_{\mathrm{adapt}}(K_1)=\sum_{k=0}^{K_1-1}(u_k+a_k+c_k).\]
Suppose a fixed-policy baseline requires \(K_0\) updates to meet the same criterion and has mean total wall-clock cost \(\bar t_0\) per update, including its sampling and coordinate-update costs. Under this accounting model, adaptation improves wall-clock time if and only if
\[\sum_{k=0}^{K_1-1}(u_k+a_k+c_k)<K_0\bar t_0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive sampling improves elapsed time exactly when its total score-refresh, distribution-maintenance, sampling, and coordinate-update cost is below the total cost of a fixed-policy baseline reaching the same accuracy.
knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Policy Maintenance Overhead

children.title: Strong Cross-Block Coupling
children.top_down_role: Block decompositions exposing severe interaction geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Cross-Block Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic model showing arbitrarily slow simultaneous exact block minimization under strong coupling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12 x^{\mathsf T}Q_\rho x\) on \(\mathbb R^2\), where \(Q_\rho=\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\ \rho&1\end{pmatrix}\) and \(0<\rho<1\), with singleton blocks. Simultaneously minimizing each block while holding the other at its old value gives \[x^{k+1}=-\rho\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}x^k.\] Hence \(\|x^{k+1}\|_2=\rho\|x^k\|_2\). Although \(Q_\rho\succ0\), the contraction factor tends to \(1\) as \(\rho\uparrow1\). Thus strong off-block Hessian coupling can remove the practical progress advantage of blockwise updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a coupled positive-definite quadratic, simultaneous exact coordinate minimization contracts only by the coupling parameter, becoming arbitrarily slow as coupling approaches its positive-definiteness boundary.
assumptions_latex: Both block updates are computed from the same iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x^{k+1}\|_2=\rho\|x^k\|_2\), so the contraction factor approaches \(1\) as \(\rho\uparrow1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cyclic Exact Coordinate Minimization under Strong Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential counterpart to the seed's simultaneous-update example.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Q_\rho x\), where \(Q_\rho=\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}\) and \(0<\rho<1\). One cyclic sweep first exactly minimizes over \(x_1\) with \(x_2\) fixed and then over \(x_2\) with the new \(x_1\) fixed, giving \[x_1^{k+1}=-\rho x_2^k,\qquad x_2^{k+1}=\rho^2x_2^k.\] After the first sweep, successive iterates satisfy \(x^{k+1}=\rho^2x^k\). Thus the asymptotic per-sweep contraction factor approaches one as \(\rho\uparrow1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the standard coupled two-coordinate quadratic, cyclic exact coordinate minimization contracts asymptotically by rho squared per sweep and becomes arbitrarily slow near the positive-definiteness boundary.
assumptions_latex: Coordinates are minimized exactly in the fixed order \(1,2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The asymptotic per-sweep contraction factor is \(\rho^2\to1\) as \(\rho\uparrow1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Cyclic Exact Coordinate Minimization under Strong Coupling

children.title: Oversized or Imbalanced Blocks
children.top_down_role: Blocks whose solution cost or load imbalance removes partial-update benefits.

knowledge_statements.title: Oversized or Imbalanced Blocks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Work-model boundary at which block updates lose their computational advantage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition \(n\) variables into blocks \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\). Let \(c_i\) be the execution cost of computing and applying an update on \(B_i\), and let \(C_{\mathrm{full}}\) be the cost of one comparable full-gradient update. For a serial randomized block method selecting block \(i\) with probability \(p_i\), the expected update cost is \(\bar c=\sum_{i=1}^m p_i c_i\). For a synchronous parallel round that processes every block once and cannot finish before its slowest block task, the latency is at least \(c_{\max}=\max_{1\le i\le m}c_i\). Thus the per-update or per-round cost advantage is absent when \(\bar c\ge C_{\mathrm{full}}\) in the serial model or \(c_{\max}\ge C_{\mathrm{full}}\) in the synchronous model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block design loses its cost advantage when the expected serial block cost, or the slowest task in a synchronous all-block round, matches the cost of a comparable full update.
assumptions_latex: Costs include all computation required to apply an update and are measured on the same platform.
The synchronous comparison processes every block once per round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar c\ge C_{\mathrm{full}}\) or \(c_{\max}\ge C_{\mathrm{full}}\) eliminates the corresponding per-update or per-round cost advantage.

notation.meaning: execution cost of updating block i
cost of a comparable full-gradient update

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Synchronous Utilization Loss from Block Imbalance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact work–span measure of load imbalance for one synchronous all-block round.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a synchronous round assigns block tasks of costs \(c_1,\ldots,c_m>0\) to \(m\) processors, one task per processor, with no overlap or migration. Its total work is \(W=\sum_{i=1}^m c_i\), makespan is \(T=c_{\max}=\max_i c_i\), and average processor utilization is \[\eta=\frac{W}{mT}=\frac{\sum_i c_i}{m\max_i c_i}\le1.\] Its speedup over serial execution of the same tasks is \(W/T\le m\). If \(c_j/\sum_i c_i\to1\) for some task, then \(\eta\to1/m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronous utilization equals total block work divided by the processor count times the slowest-block cost; one dominant block drives utilization toward one over the processor count.
assumptions_latex: \(m\) block tasks are released simultaneously on \(m\) processors.
Each processor executes one task, and the barrier completes after the slowest task.
Communication and other overhead are excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\eta=(\sum_i c_i)/(m\max_i c_i)\), and \(\eta\to1/m\) when one block asymptotically contains all work.

notation.meaning: total block-task work in one round

knowledge_statements.title: Synchronous Utilization Loss from Block Imbalance

children.title: Redundant Overlap Work
children.top_down_role: Duplicated computation arising from variables shared across multiple blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Overlap Work
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Overlap multiplicity quantifies repeated coordinate processing in a full block sweep.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be blocks whose union contains every coordinate, and define \(r_j=|\{i:j\in B_i\}|\). If one sweep processes every entry of every block once, its entry-processing work is \[W_{\mathrm{block}}=\sum_{i=1}^m|B_i|=\sum_{j=1}^n r_j.\] In the same unit-cost model, processing each coordinate exactly once has work \(W_{\mathrm{full}}=n\). Hence the redundant work is \[W_{\mathrm{red}}=W_{\mathrm{block}}-W_{\mathrm{full}}=\sum_{j=1}^n(r_j-1).\] Therefore an overlapping full block sweep has no raw entry-count advantage over a full coordinate pass.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full sweep over overlapping blocks processes each coordinate according to its overlap multiplicity, and its work beyond one processing per coordinate is redundant.
assumptions_latex: \(\bigcup_{i=1}^m B_i=\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
Each processed block entry and each coordinate in the comparison pass have the same unit cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_{\mathrm{red}}=\sum_{j=1}^n(r_j-1)\ge0\), so an overlapping full block sweep cannot use fewer raw entry-processing operations than one full coordinate pass.

notation.meaning: number of blocks containing coordinate j

children.title: Conflicting Overlap Updates
children.top_down_role: Incompatible changes targeting variables shared by concurrently or sequentially updated blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflicting Overlap Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar replicated-block example where stale additive aggregation destroys descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\) and let the same coordinate belong to \(r\ge2\) concurrently updated blocks. From a common stale value \(x^k\), every block computes its exact minimizing displacement \(\delta_i=-x^k\). If the displacements are combined additively without conflict resolution, then \[x^{k+1}=x^k+\sum_{i=1}^r\delta_i=(1-r)x^k,\qquad f(x^{k+1})=(r-1)^2f(x^k).\] Thus \(r=2\) produces no decrease, while every \(r\ge3\) strictly increases the objective for \(x^k\ne0\), despite each isolated update being an exact minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Several blocks can each propose a correct update to one shared coordinate, yet additive aggregation stagnates with two proposals and diverges with three or more.
assumptions_latex: All blocks read the same nonzero stale value and their displacements are added.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x^{k+1})=(r-1)^2f(x^k)\); descent fails for \(r=2\) and the objective increases for \(r\ge3\).

notation.meaning: number of concurrent blocks containing the coordinate

children.title: Overlap-Resolution Overhead

knowledge_statements.title: Overlap-Resolution Overhead
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost boundary for locking, reduction, or reconciliation of overlapping updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For one parallel round, let \(C_{\mathrm{upd}}\) be useful block-update work, \(C_{\mathrm{res}}\) the cost of detecting and resolving overlapping writes, and \(C_{\mathrm{full}}\) the cost of an equivalent full update. The realized round cost is \(C_{\mathrm{round}}=C_{\mathrm{upd}}+C_{\mathrm{res}}\). Hence overlap handling removes the per-round computational advantage whenever \[C_{\mathrm{res}}\ge C_{\mathrm{full}}-C_{\mathrm{upd}},\] equivalently \(C_{\mathrm{round}}\ge C_{\mathrm{full}}\). If resolution serializes every pair of conflicting updates, its critical-path contribution must be included in \(C_{\mathrm{res}}\), not counted as parallel work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Locking or reconciliation eliminates the block advantage once its cost fills the gap between useful block work and a full update.
assumptions_latex: All costs refer to the same execution platform and one comparable optimization round.

notation.meaning: cost of the comparable full update

children.title: Excessive or Adversarial Staleness
children.top_down_role: Delayed information overwhelming useful coordinate progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Excessive or Adversarial Staleness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Delayed-gradient recurrence showing failure within the synchronous stable stepsize range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\) and apply a delayed gradient update with one-step staleness, \[x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha x^{k-1}.\] Its characteristic polynomial is \(z^2-z+\alpha\). For \(1<\alpha<2\), the two roots have modulus \(\sqrt{\alpha}>1\), so generic nonzero initial conditions yield an unbounded sequence. In contrast, the synchronous update \(x^{k+1}=(1-\alpha)x^k\) converges for every \(0<\alpha<2\). Therefore even a fixed delay of one can invalidate a stepsize that is admissible without staleness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a scalar quadratic, one-step delayed gradients diverge for stepsizes between one and two, although the corresponding synchronous method converges.
assumptions_latex: The delayed recurrence is initialized with generic nonzero \(x^{-1}\) and \(x^0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The delayed iteration has spectral radius \(\sqrt{\alpha}>1\), whereas the synchronous iteration converges.

notation.meaning: characteristic root of the delayed recurrence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact stability interval for the canonical scalar one-step delayed-gradient recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the recurrence \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha x^{k-1}\) with constant real \(\alpha\), convergence to zero for every initial history occurs if and only if \(0<\alpha<1\). At \(\alpha=1\), characteristic roots lie on the unit circle; outside the open interval, at least one characteristic root lies on or outside the unit circle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scalar one-step delayed-gradient method is stable exactly for stepsizes between zero and one, half the upper synchronous interval.
assumptions_latex: The recurrence uses a constant real stepsize \(\alpha\).
Convergence is required for every initial pair \((x^{-1},x^0)\).

children.title: Dense-Interaction Parallel Failure
children.top_down_role: Concurrent updates interfering across many coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Dense-Interaction Parallel Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense quadratic for which simultaneous exact coordinate updates diverge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\ge3\), let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx\), where \(Q=(1-\rho)I+\rho\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}\) and \(1/(n-1)<\rho<1\). Then \(Q\succ0\), and every coordinate interacts with all others. Simultaneous exact minimization of all singleton coordinates from the common iterate gives \[x^{k+1}=-\rho(\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}-I)x^k.\] Along \(x^k=c_k\mathbf1\), the multiplier is \(-\rho(n-1)\), whose modulus exceeds \(1\). Thus the parallel Jacobi-style coordinate scheme diverges although the objective is strongly convex and each isolated coordinate minimization is well defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense strongly convex quadratic can make simultaneous exact coordinate minimizations diverge because all updates react to the same interacting coordinates.
assumptions_latex: All coordinate minimizers are computed simultaneously from one iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration has eigenvalue \(-\rho(n-1)\) with modulus greater than \(1\), so it diverges along \(\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1\}\).

notation.meaning: all-ones vector in the ambient dimension

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convergence boundary for simultaneous exact singleton-coordinate minimization of a strictly convex quadratic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Qx-b^{\mathsf T}x\) with \(Q\succ0\), and write \(Q=D+R\), where \(D=\operatorname{diag}(Q)\). Simultaneous exact singleton-coordinate minimization from a common iterate has the form \[x^{k+1}=D^{-1}(b-Rx^k),\qquad x^{k+1}-x^\star=-D^{-1}R(x^k-x^\star).\] It converges to \(x^\star=Q^{-1}b\) for every initial point if and only if \(\rho(D^{-1}R)<1\). If \(\rho(D^{-1}R)>1\), some initial errors diverge; at spectral radius one, convergence for every initial point fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel exact coordinate minimization of a positive-definite quadratic converges globally exactly when its Jacobi iteration matrix has spectral radius below one.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is symmetric positive definite.
All singleton-coordinate minimizers use the same old iterate.
All coordinate updates are committed simultaneously.

knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistent Auxiliary-State Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure condition for cached quantities used to form coordinate derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=	frac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2\), and suppose an implementation maintains a cache \(s\) intended to equal \(Ax\). The derivative used for coordinate \(i\) is \(g_i=A_{:i}^{\mathsf T}(s-b)\), while the true derivative is \(
abla_i f(x)=A_{:i}^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)\). Their error is \[e_i=g_i-
abla_i f(x)=A_{:i}^{\mathsf T}(s-Ax).\] If updates to \(x\) and \(s\) are not consistent, then \(e_i
e0\) may occur; consequently any descent rule whose guarantee assumes \(g_i=
abla_i f(x)\) is inapplicable unless the cache error is explicitly bounded and absorbed by its stepsize condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stale residual cache produces a computable partial-derivative error; exact-gradient descent guarantees fail unless that error is controlled.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
The coordinate rule uses the maintained cache \(s\) in place of \(Ax\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_i=A_{:i}^{\mathsf T}(s-Ax)\); an uncontrolled nonzero cache inconsistency invalidates exact-coordinate-gradient descent conditions.

notation.meaning: error in the computed partial derivative

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar least-squares example where failure to update an auxiliary product cache makes iterates unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12x^2\), initialize \(x^0=s^0=1\), and use \(s^k\) as a cache for \(x^k\) in \(x^{k+1}=x^k-\alpha s^k\), while never propagating accepted changes to the cache, so \(s^{k+1}=s^k\). For every \(\alpha>0\), \[x^k=1-k\alpha,\qquad s^k=1,\qquad f(x^k)\to\infty.\] If instead \(s^k=x^k\) is maintained, the update is ordinary gradient descent and converges for \(0<\alpha<2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even on a scalar quadratic, an unpropagated cache can turn a convergent gradient update into an unbounded iteration.

The cache is not updated after accepted iterate changes.

children.title: Coordination-Overhead Dominance
children.top_down_role: Execution regimes where synchronization or communication outweighs saved computation.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordination-Overhead Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Runtime crossover where parallel coordination exceeds the computation saved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1\) be the serial cost of a fixed amount of useful coordinate work. With \(p\) workers, let \(C_p^{\mathrm{comp}}\) be its parallel computation time and let \(H_p\) be synchronization, communication, scheduling, and contention time. The parallel elapsed time is \(T_p=C_p^{\mathrm{comp}}+H_p\). Parallel execution provides no runtime improvement whenever \[H_p\ge C_1-C_p^{\mathrm{comp}},\] equivalently \(T_p\ge C_1\). In particular, even under ideal computation scaling \(C_p^{\mathrm{comp}}=C_1/p\), speedup is at most one when \(H_p\ge C_1(1-1/p)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parallel coordinate work is not faster once synchronization, communication, scheduling, and contention consume all computation saved by parallelization.
assumptions_latex: Serial and parallel costs represent the same useful optimization work.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_p\ge C_1-C_p^{\mathrm{comp}}\) implies \(T_p\ge C_1\) and hence no positive speedup.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-System Misalignment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rotated separability showing dependence of coordinate friendliness on parameterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(z)=\sum_{j=1}^n\phi_j(z_j)\) and set \(f(x)=g(Ux)\), where \(U\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is orthogonal. In the \(z\)-coordinates, changing \(z_j\) affects only one summand. In the \(x\)-coordinates, changing coordinate \(x_i\) by \(t\) changes every transformed component for which \(U_{ji}\ne0\), since \[(U(x+te_i))_j=(Ux)_j+tU_{ji}.\] Thus if column \(i\) of \(U\) is dense, an axis update generally touches all \(n\) component functions. The separable coordinate advantage is therefore not invariant under an orthogonal reparameterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rotation can turn a separable objective into one where changing a single coordinate affects every component, destroying coordinate-friendly evaluation.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\phi_j:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is differentiable.
\(U^{\mathsf T}U=I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A dense column of \(U\) makes one \(x_i\)-update affect all corresponding component functions, despite separability in \(z=Ux\).

notation.meaning: univariate component of the separable transformed objective

children.title: Ill-Conditioned Coordinate Geometry
children.top_down_role: Coordinate-scaled geometry that produces highly uneven or weak progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioned Coordinate Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate condition number governing randomized coordinate-descent iteration growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable and \(\mu\)-strongly convex in the Euclidean norm. Suppose each coordinate derivative is Lipschitz with constant \(L_i>0\). Randomized coordinate descent selecting \(i\) with probability \(L_i/S\), where \(S=\sum_{j=1}^nL_j\), and updating \(x_i^+=x_i-\nabla_i f(x)/L_i\), satisfies the standard linear estimate \[\mathbb E[f(x^k)-f^*]\le\left(1-\frac{\mu}{S}\right)^k(f(x^0)-f^*).\] Consequently achieving expected error at most \(\varepsilon\) requires at most \(\left\lceil(S/\mu)\log((f(x^0)-f^*)/\varepsilon)\right\rceil\) coordinate updates; the bound deteriorates as \(S/\mu\) grows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Importance-sampled coordinate descent has iteration scale equal to the sum of coordinate smoothness constants divided by strong convexity, so poor coordinate conditioning slows it.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(\mu>0\).
\(|\nabla_i f(x+te_i)-\nabla_i f(x)|\le L_i|t|\) for every \(i\), \(x\), and \(t\).
Coordinates are sampled independently with probabilities \(L_i/S\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sharp Slow Coordinate under Lipschitz Importance Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal quadratic attaining the seed rate on a low-probability coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12\sum_{i=1}^n L_i x_i^2\), where \(L_i>0\), \(\mu=\min_iL_i\), and \(S=\sum_iL_i\). Sample coordinate \(i\) with probability \(L_i/S\) and apply \(x_i^+=x_i-\nabla_i f(x)/L_i=0\). If \(j\) satisfies \(L_j=\mu\) and \(x^0\) is supported only on coordinate \(j\), then the objective remains unchanged until \(j\) is first sampled. Consequently, \[\mathbb E[f(x^k)]=(1-\mu/S)^k f(x^0).\] Thus the factor in the seed's upper bound is attained exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a diagonal quadratic initialized on its least-curved coordinate, Lipschitz-importance sampling exactly attains the geometric factor one minus mu over the sum of coordinate smoothness constants.
assumptions_latex: \(L_i>0\) and \(\mu=\min_iL_i\).
Coordinates are sampled independently with probabilities \(L_i/S\).
The initial point is supported on a coordinate whose curvature equals \(\mu\).

children.title: Axis-Restricted Progress Loss
children.top_down_role: Efficiency loss caused by restricting updates to poorly aligned coordinate directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Axis-Restricted Progress Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies one-step loss when descent directions are restricted to coordinate axes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\tfrac12 x^{\mathsf T}Qx-c^{\mathsf T}x\), where \(Q\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}\) is symmetric positive definite, and put \(g=\nabla f(x)\neq0\). Exact minimization along coordinate \(e_i\) decreases the objective by \(g_i^2/(2Q_{ii})\), whereas exact minimization along the steepest-descent direction \(-g\) decreases it by \(\lVert g\rVert_2^4/(2g^{\mathsf T}Qg)\). Consequently, the best axis-restricted progress ratio is \[\rho(x;Q)=\frac{\max_i g_i^2/Q_{ii}}{\lVert g\rVert_2^4/(g^{\mathsf T}Qg)}.\] For \(Q=I_d\) and \(|g_1|=\cdots=|g_d|\), one has \(\rho(x;Q)=1/d\); thus even perfectly conditioned geometry can impose a factor-\(d\) one-step loss solely through axis restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an isotropic quadratic with equal gradient components, the best exact coordinate step achieves only one-dth of the decrease achieved by an exact steepest-descent line search.
assumptions_latex: \(d\ge2\) and \(Q\succ0\).
Coordinate and steepest-descent steps use exact line minimization.

notation.meaning: the gradient at the current point
best-coordinate decrease divided by steepest-descent decrease
